coreItems.name: Serylda's Grudge
coreItems.note: The slow keeps a target inside the sweet spot of his next Q swing. The armor penetration keeps that swing hurting against bruisers.

coreItems.name: Death's Dance

coreItems.name: Spear of Shojin

situationalItems.name: Serpent's Fang
situationalItems.note: Build this when shields absorb Aatrox's gank damage. His wide Q sweet spots can reduce shields across several targets before the next knock-up and passive-enhanced attack land.

situationalItems.name: Guardian Angel
situationalItems.note: Build this when Aatrox must start a late fight he cannot walk out of. The revive forces enemies to wait near his body, giving Q and Umbral Dash time to return for a healing second rotation.

situationalItems.name: Maw of Malmortius
situationalItems.note: Build this when the enemy has heavy magic burst that kills him faster than he can heal.

situationalItems.name: Sundered Sky
situationalItems.note: The first-hit crit and heal stack neatly with Aatrox's passive-enhanced attack after a Q sweet spot, giving him a heavy hit and enough sustain to keep the combo going.

situationalItems.name: Goredrinker
situationalItems.desc: Fighter sustain item with AoE healing
situationalItems.note: Build this when the enemy team has several melee champions, since they fight close enough together for one active to catch more than one of them. It heals more for each enemy it hits, and his Q already wants him standing next to several of them.

situationalItems.name: Stridebreaker
situationalItems.desc: Juggernaut bruiser item with a dash
situationalItems.note: Build this when you cannot keep targets still long enough to land all three Q swings. The dash and slow fix that.

situationalItems.name: Mercurial Scimitar
situationalItems.note: Build this when a crowd-control chain stops Aatrox before he can finish his Q sweet-spot sequence. Cleansing the first disable lets him keep World Ender moving toward its takedown extension.

keystoneRune.name: Conqueror
keystoneRune.desc: Gain stacks by damaging enemy champions. At maximum stacks, gain bonus damage and healing.
keystoneRune.note: He wants long fights, and the healing at max stacks adds to the healing his E already gives him.

primaryRunes.desc: Immobilizing enemy champions grants a defensive shield for frontline engages.
primaryRunes.note: His Q sweet spot knocks up, which triggers the shield on the same cast he opens trades with.

primaryRunes.name: Second Wind
primaryRunes.desc: After taking damage from a champion, regenerate health over time.
primaryRunes.note: His E already heals him off damage dealt, and this covers the poke he takes when there is nothing to hit back.

primaryRunes.note: His healing scales off a bigger pool, so extra max health is extra damage healed back per fight.

secondaryRunes.note: His E is a dash, so the bonus true damage lands on his first swing after closing.

spells.name: Flash

goodAgainst.note: Shen's block stops your empowered auto but does nothing against the Q sweeps that carry most of your damage, so you win the trades.
Sion is big and slow, so your sweet spots land freely, your passive chunks his huge health pool, and a knockup interrupts his charging Q.

Deathbringer Stance and Aatrox's sweet-spot knockups punish the maximum health Mundo stacks, while World Ender can sustain through the return damage. Open with the first Darkin Blade edge to consume Goes Where He Pleases, then use Infernal Chains and the later sweet spots after Mundo's crowd-control immunity is down.
His blind turns off your empowered attack but not your Q sweeps, which carry most of your damage, and he is too squishy to survive your all-in once World Ender is up.

weakAgainst.note: Fiora heavily punishes a predictable sweet spot: a riposted swing leaves you stunned, slowed and chunked. Vary your Q timing and spacing so she cannot reserve Riposte, since she out-duels you once she is even on items.
Counter Strike dodges your autos and blunts your sweeps, his stun starts trades on his terms, and he out-scales you hard in the 1v1.

Bladesurge resets let Irelia cross Aatrox's Darkin Blade sweet spots instead of standing at their edges, and a fully stacked Ionian Fervor wins the sustained auto-attack fight. Do not spend Umbral Dash on the first swing: hold it to realign a later sweet spot after her dash, and back off while her passive is stacked on the wave.
Constant poke and his stun chain ruin your combo timing, and you can only walk up when his energy is low or his stun mark is not loaded.
She kites you and slips out of your Q wind-ups with ease, then shreds you with percent-health true damage that neither armor nor a bigger health bar blunts.

gamePlan.overview:
Aatrox is one of the strongest bruisers in the Baron lane. He is a drain tank who wins long fights by landing the sweet spots on The Darkin Blade and healing back the damage he takes. Each of his three Q casts has a sweet spot: the far end of the first slash, the edge of the second, and the center of the third slam. Hitting one deals bonus damage plus a short knockup, and landing all three usually wins the trade outright.

His plan runs on two early timings: his passive empowered attack, which deals bonus damage based on the target's max health, and World Ender at level 5, which adds damage, speed, and much stronger healing. Win a trade, crash the wave, and be first to Rift Herald.

He is not a late-game split pusher. Aatrox does his best work in skirmishes and teamfights, where every sweep hits multiple enemies and every hit heals him.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Levels 1 to 3 are about short, sharp trades. Walk up with your passive attack ready, start with Q1 at max range so the tip lands, and weave the empowered auto between casts since it both damages and heals. The full combo is Q1 into W, Q2, E, then Q3 with an auto at the end. You can also use E in the middle of a Q to slide a sweet spot onto a dodging enemy. Level 5 is your first real all-in window: World Ender plus Ignite kills most Baron laners who are not near full health. In ranged matchups, save E to dodge their key spell instead of using it to attack.
gamePlan.midGame: Your first core item flips close trades into wins, and that is your cue to play the map. Crash the wave, walk to river, and set up Rift Herald, since few champions contest it as well as Aatrox with World Ender. In skirmishes, remember that takedowns extend your ult: commit where a kill is likely, then carry the extension into the next target. Your W pull punishes anyone who face-checks a river brush, so play around vision and use it to threaten the enemy jungler's path through river.
gamePlan.lateGame: Late game Aatrox is a teamfighter, not a side laner. He falls off in pure 1v1s against scaled duelists, so ignore advice that tells you to split push. Group with your team, look for flanks, and save W for a carry instead of wasting the pull on a tank. Track enemy anti-heal: once their carry buys it, you are much less tanky in practice and need to fight around their cooldowns instead of face-tanking. Use World Ender as the fight commits, not before, so the bonus damage and healing cover the real fight.
gamePlan.teamfights: Activate World Ender right as the fight starts, then position so your Q sweeps hit two or three enemies, since every target hit means more healing. Use E, or even Flash mid-cast, to drag sweet spots onto the enemy carry: the knockups set up your team's follow-up and the bonus damage is what actually kills. If their front line blocks your path, do not force it. Sweep the tanks, heal off them, and let your passive chip at their big health pools. One takedown extends your ult, and an extended World Ender Aatrox usually decides the rest of the fight.

Kha'Zix depends on isolated Taste Their Fear burst, but Aatrox can survive that opener and heal back through Darkin Blade sweet spots and World Ender. Lillia never stands still long enough for a sweet spot to land, kiting you while her burn stacks from range. Her sleep sets up burst you cannot heal through, and you cannot catch her alone.

gamePlan.overview:
Aatrox in the jungle is a drain-tank brawler who brings a lane bully's all-in to the whole map. Everything runs through The Darkin Blade: three swings, each with a sweet spot that knocks up and hits harder, plus a passive that turns one auto into a big chunk of health. His clear is quick once you learn to overlap the sweeps, and his ganks usually end in kills, because a clean combo with World Ender up heals back everything the enemy deals.

His plan is to win the long fight. He is not a power-farmer and not a one-shot assassin. He walks into skirmishes over scuttle or dragon, lands a sweet spot, and outlasts everyone while his health keeps climbing. Once his ultimate is up, ganks turn into kills far more often, and the longer a fight runs the better it gets for him.

The downside is real. All his damage is skillshots, so a missed sweet spot is a wasted gank, and once his dash is spent, one stun chain can kill him before any healing matters. Anti-heal ruins his plan, and he loses pure duels to scaled carries late. His power is front-loaded, so take your fights while your combo still threatens to kill and close the game before the enemy carries finish scaling.
gamePlan.earlyGame:
Your first clear is steady, not fast. Start where all three Q sweeps can cover the camp and weave normal attacks between casts. Deathbringer Stance periodically empowers an attack and its cooldown is reduced by Aatrox's attacks and ability hits; it does not itself reset the attack timer. Umbral Dash does reset the attack timer, so use E deliberately when that reset improves the clear rather than describing every passive attack as a reset.

Contest scuttle when a lane can back you up, and skip it against junglers who win the straight fight, since your early duel is decent but loses to the strongest early duelists. Hold E to dodge their key spell instead of using it to engage, and ward behind you, because a slow brawler without his dash is easy to collapse on.
gamePlan.midGame:
The first grouped objective is where World Ender starts paying for the farm you invested. World Ender makes you one of the better objective contesters in the game, so if your team is winning the early fights, take one: every sweep that hits two enemies heals you twice, and the pit is exactly where they have to stand. If the game is even, trade one objective for the other instead of forcing a fight you do not clearly win, and take Herald, since it converts straight into a tower without asking your team to hold a five on five. Play for dragon instead when your team fights well enough to want soul later.

Between objectives keep the loop going: clear your camps, gank while they respawn, and invade the slow farmers when you know where their jungler is. Takedowns extend your ultimate, so commit when a kill is on and ride the extra time into the next fight.
gamePlan.lateGame: Late game you are a durable teamfighter, not a side laner. Do not split push, because you lose the clean duel to anyone who scaled. Group, look for flanks through fog, and pop World Ender as the fight starts rather than walking in with it already running. Save your W for a carry instead of pulling a tank, since it is your one real pick tool and it is wasted on the front line. Watch for enemy anti-heal on the scoreboard, because once their carry finishes it you can no longer face-tank and have to fight around their cooldowns instead of through them. At Baron and the late dragons, you are the front line that keeps the fight going long enough for your team to finish it.
gamePlan.teamfights: Flank if you can, and time your engage with your team's, since a sweet spot knockup is worth much more when someone follows up on it. Use World Ender right as the fight commits, then swing where your Q hits two or three enemies, because every extra body means more healing and the fight tilts your way the longer it runs. Use E, or even Flash mid-cast, to land a sweet spot on their carry: the knockup chains into your team's lockdown and the bonus damage is what actually kills. If their front line blocks the backline, do not force it. Sweep the tanks, heal off them, and let your passive punish their health stacking. One takedown extends your ultimate, and an extended World Ender usually decides the rest of the fight.

startingItem.name: Amplifying Tome
startingItem.note: Early ability power for her kunai poke. She uses energy instead of mana, so Five Point Strike is limited by both its cooldown and her current energy; Twilight Shroud restores 100 energy for a committed rotation.

boots.name: Spellslinger's Shoes

coreItems.name: Infinity Orb

coreItems.name: Void Staff

situationalItems.desc: AP engage item with a dash

Choose it when enemies have not built much magic resist, so trading Void Staff's extra damage for more ability haste and an area heal after takedowns is worthwhile.

spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

goodAgainst.note: Her whole game is ball position, and the shroud stops her single-target casts from picking you out, though her ground-targeted and Ball-centred areas still hit you inside it, so move as well as hide; her early poke priority is the only edge she has on you.
One missed binding removes Lux's only hard crowd control. She can still shield herself and slow Akali with Lucent Singularity, but she has no dash or blink to escape the follow-up all-in.

Akali can cross Ziggs's artillery range and use Twilight Shroud to deny targeted follow-up. Respect Satchel Charge's displacement and Hexplosive Minefield's slow, because those are his real tools for creating space once she arrives.

Mel has no dash, but Solar Snare and its expanding slow zone can still stop a careless approach. Bait Rebuttal before committing the full combo: its brief invulnerability prevents non-turret damage even when there is no projectile to reflect.

weakAgainst.note: You bully him early, but he scales past you: his post-five blinks match your mobility, and his magic shield absorbs your burst, so your lead only lasts until his spike.

She beats you in extended exchanges: Bladesurge heals her and resets when it kills a target or consumes a mark, while her stacked passive increases her attack speed. Her stun can also catch a predictable dash, so avoid fighting through a prepared minion wave.

Galio is built to stop magic-damage assassins: Shield of Durand periodically grants him a magic-damage shield, while his crowd control punishes Akali's landing point. He can charge W around a predictable commit, though Akali can still space the radius or time her movement around the channel.
Kennen's ranged poke punishes every step toward him, his stun chain connects even through your shroud plays, and his teamfight ultimate beats yours when it lands first.
His ultimate reveals you even inside Twilight Shroud, stripping your safest engage and cleanest escape at once, and the gold card locks you down for his team's follow-up.

gamePlan.overview:
Akali is a mid laner who cares more about the map than the lane itself. Twilight Shroud hides her inside the cloud, restores 100 energy, and temporarily raises her maximum energy, her kunai fan chips at range, and her ultimate's two-part dash gives her kill threat from very far away. She is an assassin who happens to start in a farming lane, and she spends the laning phase waiting for the moment she can leave it.

Her plan is tempo, not lane dominance. Survive a weak early phase against mids who out-stat you, hit your first item, then turn wave priority into roams: an Akali who can shove is a threat to the side lanes and the river. Her full combo kills a squishy carry through most of their peel, and the shroud makes almost every gank easy to escape. You are not there to win a poke war; you are there to win the map around it.

The cost is the lane itself. She is very squishy, her energy bar limits how often she can fight, and harder mid duelists beat her when she has to stand still. Hard crowd control still catches her around the shroud, and against frontlines she cannot one-shot, her kit does very little. Akali wins by refusing fair fights and only taking the ones she sets up herself.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Play the early lane patiently and gather information. Chip with the kunai fan and its empowered follow-up, watch your energy bar, and spend the shroud only on things that matter: dodging the matchup's key spell, resetting a trade that went wrong, or surviving a gank. Most mids beat you before your first item, so do not pretend the lane is yours when it is not. Hold a healthy wave, match their roams, and treat farm, chip, and survival as the whole job until your spike arrives.
gamePlan.midGame: Your first item flips the lane in your favor, and the roaming starts. The full combo kills a squishy target, so shove the wave hard and leave: a kill on a side laner who never saw you coming is worth more than the minions you gave up. Use that same priority to fight over scuttle, show up at dragon or herald with your jungler before the enemy mid does, and find picks in unwarded river brush. In skirmishes, go in after the enemy uses their crowd control, burst the priority target, and use the second ultimate dash or the shroud to leave before anyone reacts. Hunt isolated targets and stay out of messy five-man fights.
gamePlan.lateGame: Stay outside the frontline and commit after the enemy uses the lockdown that can stop your first dash. If the map stalls, clear a side wave when the next objective is not exposed, then look for a rotating target who has separated from peel. Use Twilight Shroud to wait out targeted damage and preserve the second ultimate dash for the exit when possible. If no isolated carry is reachable, keep applying side-lane pressure instead of forcing a dive through the enemy frontline.
gamePlan.teamfights: Pick one target and ignore the other four. Wait on the flank while the fight uses up its crowd control, then enter from the side: ultimate dash, burst rotation, empowered auto, then the shroud or final dash to get out. Never open a fight and never trade with the frontline, because your entire value is killing their carry. The shroud can also save you from a bad collapse, buying the moment you need to move and find a cleaner angle. Patience is the difference between carrying the fight and dying for nothing.

situationalItems.note: Build this when the enemy team has multiple crit champions. Headbutt-Pulverize puts Alistar beside their carry, and the crit reduction keeps him alive there until his next crowd-control rotation.

keystoneRune.note: Every engage he makes immobilizes, and his Q into W gives two triggers in one combo.

primaryRunes.desc: Immobilizing enemy champions grants a defensive shield for frontline engages.
primaryRunes.note: His knock-up triggers the shield, so it arrives on the same button he engages with.

primaryRunes.name: Second Wind
primaryRunes.desc: After taking damage from a champion, regenerate health over time.
primaryRunes.note: He soaks poke for his carry all lane, and this pays that health back between engages.

primaryRunes.desc: Gain tenacity and bonus defenses while immobilized.
primaryRunes.note: Take this against teams whose crowd control prevents the champion's key follow-up. Its tenacity shortens most disables and grants temporary defenses while immobilized. The shorter disable lets Alistar continue from Headbutt-Pulverize into peel or activate his ultimate before the return burst.

secondaryRunes.name: Hexflash

spells.name: Flash

goodAgainst.note: Sona is immobile, but she can peel with Crescendo, an empowered Song of Celerity slow, or Diminuendo's damage reduction. Unbreakable Will can cleanse Crescendo from Alistar himself, so engage when her passive chord is unprepared and use the cleanse after the stun lands.

Current Yuumi casts her main spells while attached, so waiting for a routine detach is not the lane plan; Alistar instead attacks the host she cannot body-block for. Headbutt into Pulverize the host after Zoomies is spent, then use Unbreakable Will to ignore Final Chapter's stacking slow while your carry finishes the all-in.
His cage is his entire defense, and your ultimate lets you walk straight through it, leaving an immobile mage with no peel: exactly the target your combo kills.
You are the worst target his hook can catch: a tank who wanted to be close anyway. A grab onto you just starts your combo next to his own carry.

weakAgainst.note: Braum can dash to your target and grant both of them resistances, then turn Unbreakable toward Alistar's allies to intercept their follow-up damage. His passive stun and ultimate also punish the extended brawl after you commit.
Her tornado and monsoon cancel your combo outright, and you have no second engage to fall back on, so every all-in you start she ends with a knockback.
Lux pokes the walk-up your whole kit needs, and her binding holds you off the carry the moment you commit, so a snare mid headbutt stops the combo and leaves you stranded in the open.

gamePlan.overview:
Alistar is an engage and displacement support. His reliable all-in is Headbutt followed by a Pulverize recast during the dash, which carries him to the target and knocks nearby enemies up before Headbutt can fling its target away. He can also Pulverize first and then Headbutt one airborne enemy toward his team, but Headbutt always knocks the target away from Alistar rather than pulling them.

In the Dragon lane he is a pure all-in support. He has no poke and no waveclear, so the lane is a patience game: bait the enemy support forward, soak a trade with your sustain, then commit the combo the moment they step out of position. Triumphant Roar heals you and your carry through the damage you take walking in, and Unbreakable Will makes him nearly impossible to kill while removing the crowd control meant to stop him.

The catch is that everything he does happens at melee range with no exit. Before his combo is up he is a slow body the enemy can poke freely, and once Headbutt is spent he has nothing left to start or escape a fight.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Play the early lane patiently and wait for your engage window. Triumphant Roar triggers automatically to heal Alistar and nearby allies when they are wounded, and displacing or stunning enemy champions reduces its cooldown, so there is no heal button to hold. When an enemy steps too far forward, cast Headbutt and recast Pulverize during the dash to arrive with the knock-up. Use Pulverize first only when you are already in range and positioned so the following Headbutt sends the target toward your carry. Track the enemy jungler before every commit, because a missed combo leaves you in melee range with no escape.
gamePlan.midGame: Mid game your engage threat matters across the map. Leave Dragon lane after your duo crashes the wave or your carry recalls, then look for an overextended mid laner or move with your jungler into river. Around dragon and Herald, establish vision before the contest and engage only when your team is close enough to follow the displacement. A successful pick creates a numbers advantage, but a roam without a safe wave can cost your carry farm and turret pressure.
gamePlan.lateGame: Late game your combo either starts the teamfight or peels for your carry, and you have to pick which before the fight begins. Against a poke or pick comp, hold the combo to peel: knock the diver off your carry and headbutt them back where they came from. Against a grouped enemy, look for the flank that knocks their backline into your team before they can react. Your ultimate is the cooldown that matters. With Unbreakable Will up you can walk into anything and live; without it you are a slow body waiting to be kited. Commit your engage where the most valuable target stands.
gamePlan.teamfights: Pick a target and commit, because half-engages get you killed and do nothing. The best case is a knockup that catches two, or a headbutt that knocks their carry into your team before the fight starts. If you are the only frontline, peel instead: body the diver, fling them off your ADC, and pop your ultimate as the crowd control comes in so it cleanses off you. You are not there for damage and should not want to be. Your fight ends with their carry out of position and yours untouched.

goodAgainst.note: His sweet spots assume you stand still, and your dashes make them hard to line up. Public Execution suppresses and then stuns Aatrox, but it does not cancel World Ender; it only spends part of the form's remaining duration while keeping him from attacking or healing.

Mordekaiser is slow, committed, and built for a long brawl you keep refusing. Your dashes slide out of his big slam, and your chained bursts land faster than his shield can build up.

Counterstrike is built to blank autos, but most of your damage rides on abilities, so the dodge buys him little, and your suppression pins him straight through it. He gets much stronger with items, so your advantage is early.

weakAgainst.note: Jayce chunks your approach from a range you cannot answer and knocks you back the moment you finally arrive, so his poke wins the lane by default.

Irelia matches your mobility and answers your commitment with her own: her dashes reset off low minions and slip your cleaves, and her stun lands after your dash, punishing a predictable endpoint. Messy extended brawls are hers.

Armor and an unstoppable targeted dash ultimate answer your physical, movement-heavy plan: Malphite shrugs off trades, his passive shield absorbs poke, and Unstoppable Force can catch the endpoint of Ambessa's dash chain. It is aimed and cast, not charged over time.

Camille's kit answers yours directly: the hookshot stun pins your arrival, her true damage skips the resistances you trade behind, and her shield blanks the burst you committed. Even with items her duel beats yours.
Renekton wins the early brawl your whole game is built on: fury-empowered trades beat your chains, his stun starts fights on his terms, and his dash both engages and escapes.

gamePlan.overview:
Ambessa is a mobile skirmisher built around constant repositioning. For a brief window after every ability, an attack or movement command triggers a dash in that direction and grants a Medarda Maxim stack; the dash does not happen automatically. Her fights become one continuous chain: cleave, direct the dash, sweep, dash again, then weave an empowered attack to restore energy.

Her kit rewards planned aggression. Dash-chaining turns short trades into full combos, Repudiation provides a 0.5-second crowd-control immunity window followed by a shield and ground slam, and her ultimate is a long-range suppression that pins the one target she picks. Few champions punish a single positioning mistake this hard.

The cost is commitment. Once her combo is spent she has no exit, and ranged poke, parry duelists, and hard crowd control all make her pay for chained engages. She wins by choosing her fights and ending them fast.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Trade in chained bursts without spending every passive dash forward. Open with a cleave, move to the flank, weave a Medarda Maxim attack for energy, and keep the final movement command for the retreat. Save Repudiation's brief crowd-control immunity and shield for the spell that defines the matchup instead of using it on reflex. Against ranged poke, farm patiently and use the wave or brush to shorten the approach. Against melee opponents, stop the trade after your energy falls too low to continue the dash chain safely.
gamePlan.midGame: Your first item and Public Execution create strong pick pressure. Crash the Baron wave before the first objectives, then favor Herald when both sides offer an even trade. Use the ultimate on a target your team can reach after the suppression, and keep enough energy to continue the dash chain when it ends. Repudiation can absorb a key response, but it does not make an unsupported dive safe. In the side lane, fight when vision shows the likely collapse and disengage as soon as several enemies leave the map.
gamePlan.lateGame: Late game, use a side wave to create a flank without arriving after the objective starts. Public Execution is strongest on a carry who has spent mobility, but suppressing a fed diver or isolated jungler can be the better decision when it protects your backline or secures Baron. Chain passive dashes around the edge of the formation, weave attacks to restore energy, and save Repudiation for the control or burst that follows your landing. If the target cannot be finished, use the remaining movement to leave instead of extending through the full team.
gamePlan.teamfights: Enter from the side after identifying the target and the control spell that can stop your follow-up. Public Execution can pin a carry, remove a jungler from an objective moment, or interrupt a diver threatening your own damage dealer. Chain cleaves and Medarda Maxim attacks through the target, using Repudiation's timed immunity and shield against the response. Do not spend every dash on entry, and switch to the closest safe target when the backline remains protected. Ambessa needs enough energy and space to leave after the first commitment.

gamePlan.overview:
Ambessa is a dive bruiser whose abilities chain into each other. Every ability slides her into the next one, so a gank plays out as one sequence: cleave out of the brush, dash onto the target, sweep, dash again, and the laner is often dead before help arrives. Her clear is average and her ganks before the ultimate are plain, but once her ultimate can pin the most important enemy in place, she becomes a threat the enemy team has to path around.

She wins through tempo and picks, not by farming toward a teamfight ultimate. You skirmish, invade the junglers you out-duel, and turn the mid game into small fights where one of your dashes always reaches the target that matters. Her ultimate is the centerpiece: a long-range suppression that holds a carry or jungler still while their team scrambles, which turns a contested dragon into a free one. She converts an early lead into constant backline access.

The cost is commitment. Mid-combo Ambessa has spent her whole kit, so hard crowd control, a parry, or kiting punishes every dash she commits. She is squishier than the juggernauts she trades with, her clear loses a race, and her early ganks need a lane that can hold the target for her. Pick your fights, end them fast, and do not get caught in the open with your combo spent.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Your first clear is fine but not fast, so run it cleanly and do not pretend you win the scuttle race against the real early junglers. Take the crab on your side and give up the one a faster skirmisher already reached. That scuttle is what puts you on level five, and your ultimate is the difference between a gank that needs a lane to set it up and one that does not, so treat the clear as the route to it rather than a phase to rush. Once it is up, spend the camp respawn timer on a lane, ideally one with its own crowd control to hold the target still while you cleave in and chain through. Then clear again and look for the next one while the camps come back. Ward your own entrances, since a committed clear is exactly what an invader wants to catch.
gamePlan.midGame:
Public Execution turns the first objective rotation into a pick opportunity. A gank now converts most of the time: glide in, chain your cleaves through the target, and the suppression means nobody arrives in time to save them. Take that same threat to the pit. Suppressing the enemy jungler the instant they reach dragon or Herald removes them from the contest and usually hands you the objective and the fight after it, so contest whenever your team is ahead in the early skirmishes. In an even game take Herald and let the other side have dragon, unless your team comp actually wants to hold fights for soul.

This is your counter-jungle window too, because you out-skirmish most junglers in a straight duel once your combo is real. Invade their clear, steal the camp they were walking to, and force them to path scared.
gamePlan.lateGame: Late game you are a flanking assassin, not a frontliner, so stay out of the front line and let the fight develop until their carry steps too far forward. When that happens, come in from an angle nobody warded and spend the ultimate on the player whose death decides the game, because the suppression holds them through every peel their team throws back. Dash along the edges of the fight instead of through the middle, and keep the defensive window for the lockdown aimed at you, since one hard chain with your combo spent kills you. At Baron and dragon, your threat shapes the fight as much as your damage: an Ambessa waiting on a flank makes five people position wrong, and one of those mistakes is all your combo needs.
gamePlan.teamfights: Come in from the side and pin the priority target; never be the first body into the fight. The plan is simple: wait for the fight to commit, suppress their carry as the teams collide, chain your cleaves through the kill, and glide out while your defensive window absorbs whatever they fire back. Do not spend the ultimate on a frontliner, because it is a single-target tool and the tank is not the target that matters. Do not chase a peeled target through their whole team when a cleaner angle opens a moment later. Judge your fight by one question: did their best player get to take part.

Before Viktor reaches level five, his zone is a nuisance rather than a wall, and your range wins the boomerang-for-autos trade; his only real threat is scaling if he farms freely.

Akshan can pressure the gaps between Lux's casts, but Light Binding passes through minions and Lucent Singularity automatically detonates and slows when he swings into its area. Wait for Q and E before committing Heroic Swing, and account for Prismatic Barrier's outward and returning shields.

Avengerang and Akshan's ranged passive trade punish Yone whenever he walks up to prepare Mortal Steel, while Soul Unbound always marks the body he must return to. Harass that body rather than chasing the spirit, save Heroic Swing for Yone's final dash, and leave before his repeated knockups turn the trade into an extended melee fight.

Fizz's pole-vault hops over your boomerang and he is too slippery to kite, so you cannot poke him and cannot escape the all-in once his shark lands.
Irelia's dashes reset through the wave and arrive with a stun attached; she out-sustains your poke, out-trades you once her passive is stacked, and shreds your squishy frame at melee.
Ryze's targeted root cannot be sidestepped: it controls you once the swing ends, or denies the next cast, and his low-cooldown poke plus sustain out-trades the boomerang chip you rely on.

gamePlan.overview:
Akshan is a ranged marksman who plays mid with an assassin's game plan. His boomerang chips on the way out and again on the way back, Heroic Swing hooks terrain and fires as he circles it, and Comeuppance charges a long-range barrage whose bullets deal much more damage to missing-health targets. The bullets execute minions, not champions, and stop on the first enemy or turret hit. Dirty Fighting adds a delayed second shot, and consuming three stacks on a champion grants an immediate shield when that shield is off cooldown.

His game is tempo and pressure. Shove the wave with the boomerang, swing around river terrain to set up picks, and use Going Rogue's terrain-linked camouflage to threaten roams. His W has a larger payoff too: if Akshan scores a takedown on a Scoundrel within three seconds of damaging them, every currently dead ally that Scoundrel killed is resurrected after one second. Claiming one Scoundrel removes the marks from all others.

The price for all that movement is a thin body and a plan that fails under lockdown. Akshan has no hard crowd control, and immobilizing him cancels Heroic Swing. Dirty Fighting's shield only appears after consuming three stacks on a champion and has its own cooldown, so he cannot count on it for every engage.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Play the early lane as an aggressive poke carry. Throw Avengerang so it clips the enemy on both passes, then land enough attacks or ability hits to consume three Dirty Fighting stacks for bonus damage and the champion-only shield. Decide whether to let the delayed second shot fire or cancel it for movement speed. Heroic Swing is both trade and escape, so only hook terrain that leaves a safe arc.
gamePlan.midGame: Once your ultimate and first item are online, shift from laning to hunting picks. Shove the wave, move into the river brush with your stealth, and look for a swing onto a mispositioned enemy mid or a charged barrage onto someone limping out of a skirmish. Mid priority wins objectives, so crash the wave before scuttle, help your jungler contest it, and rotate to dragon or herald with the tempo you built. Roams to the side lanes work very well here, since the camouflage hides your angle. Keep the boomerang chipping and keep an escape route in mind, because the mobility that gets you in is the only thing that gets you out.
gamePlan.lateGame: Clear a side wave only when you can return before Baron or Elder is contested, then hold terrain near your team rather than remaining alone in lane. Comeuppance scales with missing health, but enemy units and turrets can intercept every bullet. Charge from an angle where a wounded carry has limited cover and allied vision protects the channel. Stay near useful terrain so Heroic Swing has both an entrance and an exit if the target survives.
gamePlan.teamfights: Wait for the fight to start, then come in from a flank. Swing from terrain, build three Dirty Fighting stacks for the immediate shield, and use Comeuppance on a wounded backliner only when enemies and turrets cannot body-block the bullets. A champion takedown resets Heroic Swing, which is what can provide the second exit. If a marked Scoundrel killed multiple allies, a qualifying takedown can resurrect all of those currently dead allies; not merely one teammate.

situationalItems.note: The alternative to Void Staff. Less penetration, but the ability haste and healing on takedown help when she fights with her team. Choose it when enemies have not built much magic resist, so trading Void Staff's extra damage for more ability haste and an area heal after takedowns is worthwhile.

keystoneRune.name: Electrocute
keystoneRune.desc: Deal bonus damage after hitting an enemy champion with 3 separate attacks or abilities.
keystoneRune.note: The outward Twofold Hex, its returning energy, and The Weirding are separate hits, so her normal rotation triggers it without inventing a champion pull her kit does not have.

primaryRunes.name: Sudden Impact
primaryRunes.desc: Deal bonus true damage after using mobility or exiting stealth.
primaryRunes.note: Her hop and her rift dash both count, so the bonus true damage lands on the damage that follows.

primaryRunes.name: Chain Assault
primaryRunes.desc: Reward chained attacks and abilities on the same target with stronger combo pressure.
primaryRunes.note: She commits her full combo to a single target, and this rewards every hit of it.

primaryRunes.name: Eyeball Collector
primaryRunes.desc: Gain adaptive force by collecting takedown stacks from enemy champions and epic monsters.
primaryRunes.note: Her whole pattern is isolating one target and killing it, and each takedown feeds the burst that gets the next.

secondaryRunes.name: Bone Plating
secondaryRunes.desc: After taking damage from a champion, the next 3 instances of champion damage are reduced.
secondaryRunes.note: Her damage comes from staying in range, and blunting the first exchange is what lets her finish the rotation.

spells.name: Flash
spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

goodAgainst.note: Orianna's damage follows the ball, so Across the Veil can cross its control zone and The Weirding can recoil Aurora away before Command: Dissonance answers. Engage when the ball is on the wave rather than on Orianna, land both passes of Twofold Hex, and leave before she recalls it for the shield and Shockwave threat.

Rebuttal can turn Aurora's incoming projectile pressure back during its brief window, but it cannot cover Mel again once the barrier expires. Bait it with the first bolt instead of committing the whole hex, then use Aurora's blink and slow to change the return angle and pull the marked spirit while Mel is immobile and Rebuttal is on cooldown.
He out-ranges your bolts and his knockup combo hurts early, but an immobile artillery mage with no escape is exactly the target your slow and blink were built to delete.

Twofold Hex does not slow Akali or prevent her from using shroud. The Weirding supplies Aurora's strong slow, and a Q mark already applied can still recall energy through Akali's position, but Aurora must predict her movement when invisibility removes direct targeting.

weakAgainst.note: Zed matches your mobility and out-bursts you: his shadow gives him a blink to trade for yours, and once you spend your dash he picks an all-in your squishy frame loses.
Katarina thrives in the messy fights your kit invites, and her resets punish you the moment your combo is on cooldown; blink in without killing her and she snowballs off your health bar.
Kassadin survives your early aggression and then outscales you completely, with a blink of his own that ignores your zone and chases your exits.

Across the Veil makes Aurora invisible after its dash completes; Twisted Fate's global reveal exposes her through that invisibility. Gold Card can also stop the follow-up before she reaches the border tricks of Between Worlds.

gamePlan.overview:
Aurora is a mobile burst mage built around three-hit passive procs and a two-pass Q. Twofold Hex fires one bolt that can mark multiple enemies; recasting recalls spiritual energy from every marked target back to Aurora, damaging enemies it passes through and hitting wounded targets harder. Her attacks and abilities apply Spirit Abjuration, and consuming three stacks on a champion deals max-health magic damage and frees a Spirit that follows Aurora and heals her over time, up to four active Spirits.

In lane she marks with the outward Q, repositions so the returning bolts cross the enemy again, and uses The Weirding's line blast, heavy decaying slow, and backward recoil to control distance. Across the Veil is a short dash followed by invisibility and movement speed; it has no forced snapback and resets on a qualifying champion takedown. Her ultimate creates a circular rift: Aurora teleports to the opposite side when she touches its border, while enemies that touch the border are slowed. Allies do not teleport through it.

Her weakness is the same as every burst mage who has to step forward: if Across the Veil and The Weirding are down, she is a low-health caster with limited spacing. Wind Wall can block the outward Twofold Hex projectile, but Aurora's ultimate shockwave and rift are area effects rather than an ally portal or champion pull.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Start by learning return paths. Hit the enemy and wave with the outward Twofold Hex, move so the recalled energy passes through the champion again, and use The Weirding to slow them while recoiling away. Across the Veil can reposition for the return line or hide an exit, but hold it against ganks because the invisibility only begins after the dash completes. Trade until the third Spirit Abjuration stack releases a healing Spirit, then back away while that sustain works.
gamePlan.midGame: The mid game is your strongest window. Shove, then roam with Across the Veil and The Weirding ready. Between Worlds leaps forward with displacement immunity, sends out a slowing shockwave, and leaves the circular rift. Fight near its edge so touching the border sends Aurora to the diametrically opposite side while enemies colliding with it are slowed; close the rift early if the reposition would become dangerous.
gamePlan.lateGame: Late game your job is finding a return-Q angle and using the rift without trapping your own pathing. Mark several enemies with Twofold Hex, move before the recast so all returning bolts share a useful line, and use Between Worlds to threaten the backline while its border gives Aurora repeated cross-circle dashes. Your allies move normally through the rift; position it for Aurora's movement and enemy slows, not as team transportation.
gamePlan.teamfights: Wait for the engage to commit, then mark the reachable targets with Twofold Hex and recoil from danger with The Weirding. Between Worlds can carry Aurora into the fight with displacement immunity during its leap, but it does not pin enemies or transport allies. Use the border teleport to cross the rift and become untargetable during the travel, then recall Q through the marked formation. If lockdown is waiting, keep Across the Veil for its dash and post-dash invisibility rather than spending every movement tool on entry.

startingItem.name: Relic Shield
startingItem.note: Turns the wave into gold and health for a support whose job is standing in front of his carry.

boots.name: Armored Advance
boots.note: Armor and health for a champion whose whole plan is being the thing the enemy has to shoot through.

coreItems.name: Bulwark of the Mountain
coreItems.note: Quest income. His gold turns directly into how long his carry survives.

coreItems.name: Locket of the Iron Solari
coreItems.note: His shield only covers one direction, so build this when damage is coming from everywhere at once.

coreItems.name: Knight's Vow
coreItems.note: His W dashes him to one ally, so pick that same carry and he takes their damage while healing off their output.

coreItems.name: Frozen Heart
coreItems.note: Build this when the enemy team has a lot of attack speed dependent champions. It stacks with his shield, which already blocks the first hit from that direction.

coreItems.name: Force of Nature
coreItems.note: Build this when the enemy team has two or more AP champions. The move speed also helps him reach an ally in time.

situationalItems.name: Thornmail
situationalItems.note: Build this against healing. The Grievous Wounds applies from your own damage as well as when they attack you, and the armor is a bonus against a team that has to shoot through him anyway.

situationalItems.name: Randuin's Omen
situationalItems.note: Build this when the enemy team has multiple crit champions. He is standing directly in front of their marksman by design.

situationalItems.name: Chainlaced Crushers
situationalItems.note: Boot swap against heavy magic damage and crowd control. Tenacity helps Braum resume guarding his carry, while magic resistance covers the spells Unbreakable cannot fully prevent.

situationalItems.name: Redemption
situationalItems.desc: Active AoE heal and enemy true-damage burn
situationalItems.note: Build this when you keep needing to help a fight you cannot physically reach.

situationalItems.name: Warmog's Armor
situationalItems.note: Health and regeneration so he can keep soaking poke through his shield without recalling.

keystoneRune.name: Guardian
keystoneRune.desc: Protect nearby allies with a reactive shield and movement burst when they are threatened.
keystoneRune.note: He is already standing next to the ally he protects, which is exactly what this keystone needs.

primaryRunes.name: Font of Life
primaryRunes.desc: Damaging enemy champions heals you and the lowest-health nearby ally after a short cooldown.
primaryRunes.note: Winter's Bite can trigger Font of Life from range, healing Braum and his lowest-health nearby ally while also starting the Concussive Blows stack his lane wants to follow.

primaryRunes.name: Second Wind
primaryRunes.desc: After taking damage from a champion, regenerate health over time.
primaryRunes.note: He puts his shield between his carry and the poke, and this covers the damage that goes around it.

primaryRunes.name: Perseverance
primaryRunes.desc: Gain tenacity and bonus defenses while immobilized.
primaryRunes.note: Take this against teams whose crowd control prevents the champion's key follow-up. Its tenacity shortens most disables and grants temporary defenses while immobilized. The shorter disable helps Braum return to his carry and raise Unbreakable before the next projectile arrives.

secondaryRunes.name: Ingenious Hunter
secondaryRunes.desc: Gain item ability haste, then stack even more through champion and epic monster takedowns.
secondaryRunes.note: His build is item actives, so shorter cooldowns on Locket and Redemption mean more shields and heals per fight.

spells.name: Flash
spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

goodAgainst.note: His entire lane is one grab, and your shield blocks it, leaving a slow melee body with no lane control while the hook sits on cooldown.
Your shield eats Death Sentence, and once the hook is denied the rest of his kit has little threat, since his pairing needs a caught target to all-in and you refuse to be caught.
A squishy melee engage who needs his hook and his all-in to function, and you out-tank both, so nobody on your side ever ends up isolated enough for him to reset on.
His hook is a projectile your shield denies, and his engage walks straight into the frontline brawl you want, so denying one throw removes his pairing's whole opener.
She has to walk into you to start anything, which is the brawl you were built for: her engage lands on your shield and your peel instead of your ADC.

weakAgainst.note: Her plants and skillshots fill the lane with more damage sources than one projectile block can answer, and she zones you off the wave from a range you cannot reach.
Karma pokes harder than you and shields her carry through your slow, blunting both halves of your kit, while her empowered bolt chunks you before you reach mark range.

Howling Gale interrupts Braum's walk-up before Concussive Blows can stack, and Monsoon pushes him away from the carry after he commits with Stand Behind Me. Preserve Unbreakable for her allies' projectile follow-up, but stop forcing the 2v2 while Monsoon is ready because Janna's disengage resets all four passive stacks.

Polymorph shuts off the engage your kit lives on, her pix poke chips you all lane, her shields blunt the stun trades your passive builds toward, and Wild Growth knocks your engage away right as it lands.

gamePlan.overview:
Braum is the support who blocks damage with his own body. He stands between your carry and everything trying to kill them, points Unbreakable toward the threat to intercept incoming projectiles, and completely negates the first champion damage that reaches him from that direction.

His 2v2 is about slowly building stun stacks. Winter's Bite chips and slows from range while marking the target, and once enough marks land (from his poke or his carry's autos) the target gets stunned, which is how a calm lane turns into a kill. Stand Behind Me dashes to an ally and grants both of them bonus armor and magic resistance, Unbreakable blocks hooks and poke from one direction, and Glacial Fissure knocks enemies up before leaving a slowing zone for four seconds.

What he cannot do is fight from a distance or carry a lane with his own damage. He is short ranged, his stun needs setup to come online, and a duo that pokes from outside his reach chips him down without a clean answer.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Use Winter's Bite when it will not push the wave into an unsafe position, and coordinate attacks with your carry to finish Concussive Blows. When a target is one stack from the stun, step forward only if the enemy duo cannot punish the approach. Save Unbreakable for the hook, projectile, or burst sequence that would decide the trade. Hold Stand Behind Me for peel or a planned engage with follow-up instead of dashing forward without an exit.
gamePlan.midGame: As lanes loosen, your kit matters across the whole dragon side of the map. Set deep vision around dragon and the river before your team commits, because your slow poke and ultimate turn a contested pit into a fight your side wins on positioning. Roam only when your carry is safe and the wave is shoved, and look for picks on anyone crossing the river without vision: a passive stun followed by Glacial Fissure's knock-up and persistent slow can keep a target from escaping. When Herald or dragon goes live, soak the opening projectile with Unbreakable and save Glacial Fissure for a clump or a choke the enemy must cross.
gamePlan.lateGame: Late game you are a full-time bodyguard. Stay glued to your carry, keep Unbreakable ready for the projectile burst everyone can see coming, and use Stand Behind Me to reach them and grant both of you resistances when a flanker commits. Glacial Fissure is now a fight-changing knock-up followed by a four-second slow zone; place it through a choke or across the route a diver must use. Do not chase and do not duel, because your damage was never the point.
gamePlan.teamfights: Aim Glacial Fissure through as many enemies as possible, then use the slowing ground it leaves to make their follow-up difficult. Stand between their damage and your carry with Unbreakable facing whoever is firing. When a diver leaps at your ADC, use Stand Behind Me to dash to them and grant both of you armor and magic resistance; the ability does not provide a shield. Keep attacking the nearest target so Concussive Blows can reach four stacks and stun them.

startingItem.name: Relic Shield
startingItem.note: Turns minions he is not last-hitting into gold, and gives him the health to walk up and threaten a hook.

boots.name: Armored Advance

coreItems.name: Yordle Trap
coreItems.note: His hook and knock-up both displace, so the armor and magic resist shred triggers on his normal combo.

coreItems.name: Warmog's Armor
coreItems.note: Health and out-of-combat regeneration, so a missed hook no longer means recalling.

coreItems.name: Force of Nature
coreItems.note: Build this into repeated magic damage. The movement speed helps Blitzcrank find Power Fist or hook angles, while the magic resistance protects the position where Rocket Grab pulls an enemy to him. Blitzcrank does not travel with the hook.

coreItems.name: Frozen Heart
coreItems.note: Build this when the enemy team has a lot of attack speed dependent champions. The mana is not wasted on him either, since his passive shield is a percentage of maximum mana.

situationalItems.name: Thornmail
situationalItems.note: Build this against healing. The Grievous Wounds applies from your own damage as well as when they attack you, so the carry he hooked is cut off from healing even while they focus someone else.

situationalItems.name: Randuin's Omen
situationalItems.note: Build this when the enemy team has multiple crit champions. He pulls their marksman next to himself, so he is the one taking that damage.

situationalItems.name: Chainlaced Crushers
situationalItems.note: Boot swap against heavy magic damage and crowd control. Tenacity lets Blitzcrank use Power Fist or retreat after a failed hook instead of losing the entire trade to one disable.

situationalItems.name: Abyssal Mask
situationalItems.note: Shreds magic resist on everyone near him, which works because a landed hook pulls the enemy next to his mages.

keystoneRune.name: Ice Overlord
keystoneRune.desc: Immobilizing an enemy champion creates icy beams and a frozen zone that slows enemies inside.
keystoneRune.note: His hook, knock-up and pull all immobilize, so almost every engage drops the zone on the target.

primaryRunes.name: Courage of the Colossus
primaryRunes.desc: Immobilizing enemy champions grants a defensive shield for frontline engages.
primaryRunes.note: His hook immobilizes, so the shield arrives on the same button he starts the fight with.

primaryRunes.name: Second Wind
primaryRunes.desc: After taking damage from a champion, regenerate health over time.
primaryRunes.note: He stands in range waiting for a hook and eats chip for it, and this heals that back between attempts.

primaryRunes.name: Overgrowth
primaryRunes.desc: Gain permanent maximum health when nearby minions or monsters die.
primaryRunes.note: He is the one walking forward for hooks, so the health is what lets him survive being the target.

secondaryRunes.name: Hexflash
secondaryRunes.desc: While Flash is on cooldown, it is replaced by Hexflash.
secondaryRunes.note: Flash into hook is his main engage, and Hexflash keeps a version of it while Flash is down.

spells.name: Flash
spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

goodAgainst.note: No dash, no escape, and very little health make Sona exactly the profile your grab punishes, and her duo has to sit at a range your hook can still reach.
Pulling her out of position nets a kill and cuts the healing that keeps her lane alive, and she has to step up to poke, which hands you grab windows.

Yuumi is normally untargetable while attached and vulnerable when detached, but her current kit does not force a detach on a fixed schedule. Track passive attacks, warding, and host swaps rather than assuming she must step out.
Immobile artillery with no dash, and your hook ignores every shield she stacks, so the grab threat alone shrinks her comfortable poke range to nothing.
He has to walk into range to drop his cage, and that walk up is a hook window before he ever sets up, so his stun into burst combo never gets started.

weakAgainst.note: Grabbing her pulls a tank into your lap and starts a fight on her terms, since she wants the all-in as much as you do and brings a crowd control chain that survives it.

Death Sentence contests the same pick line as Rocket Grab, but Flay can cancel Blitzcrank's Overdrive approach and Dark Passage can extract whichever carry he hooks. Do not grab Thresh's frontline body for him; pressure the lantern landing point and engage only after Flay or the lantern has been spent.

Braum can intercept Rocket Grab by standing in front, but Unbreakable does not leave him untouched: Braum becomes the hit target and can be pulled. That often still favors him because he wanted to enter the brawl and can stack Concussive Blows afterward.
Black Shield makes your grab bounce off the exact target you want, and her bind out-ranges your engage to lock you down first.
Zyra zones you out of grab range with plants and poke before you ever reach it, and your immobile frame takes all of that damage on the walk in.

gamePlan.overview:
Blitzcrank is built around one ability on a big, slow body. Rocket Grab is one of the most feared abilities in the Dragon lane: a single hook that pulls an enemy out of position and into your duo, and the threat of it alone changes how the other lane can stand. He does not poke, shield, or heal. He looks for picks and turns one mistake into a kill before the enemy carry can react.

The win condition in the 2v2 is the pick. Land a grab on the enemy support or ADC, follow with the Power Fist knockup and the Static Field silence, and your marksman cleans up a target who never got to act. Even a missed hook does work, since an enemy dodging grabs is not last hitting, trading, or warding. Overdrive also makes him a real roam threat, so a quiet lane can turn into a roam toward river or mid the moment a kill opens up.

Whiffing Rocket Grab removes the safe, long-range engage, but Blitzcrank still has a riskier fallback: use Overdrive to run into Power Fist range. Recasting Overdrive gives more speed and then ends in a 99% self-slow, so that approach is punishable if the knockup does not create a kill.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Lane as a visible hook threat. Use brush or the side of the wave to make the enemy carry respect Rocket Grab while your marksman farms and trades. Cast when the support steps away from minion cover or the carry commits to a last-hit, then follow with Power Fist and Static Field. Do not spend the hook into a blocked line, because its cooldown removes most of your pressure. Ward your flank before holding an aggressive position, since Blitzcrank has no clean exit from a gank.
gamePlan.midGame: Overdrive matters most in the mid game. Shove the wave with your duo, then walk the river looking for a grab on a mid laner or jungler who thinks the fog is empty. A single pick here wins dragon or herald before the contest even starts, so time your roams to the objective timer instead of wandering at random. Keep vision tight around the pit: a hook from a warded brush onto whoever steps in first hands your team the numbers fight. One grab that starts an objective fight is worth more than several landed in lane.
gamePlan.lateGame: One grab still wins fights, but now target choice is everything. You want the enemy carry or their key backline threat, and a hook that drags one of them out of formation usually decides the fight on the spot. Position on the flank or just off your frontline, where you threaten an angle their squishies have to respect, and hold the engage instead of spending it on the nearest tank. A wasted grab late is not just a missed pick: your team starts the fight a man short while your hook sits on cooldown.
gamePlan.teamfights: Your contribution often happens before the fight begins. The best case is a grab from fog onto their carry, followed by Power Fist and Static Field. If the clean angle is not there, keep Rocket Grab and Power Fist for the diver reaching your backline; Blitzcrank has no ally shield or heal, but those two crowd-control tools can peel when they were not already spent on engage.

startingItem.note: Early ability power for his beam, which is weak until his stacks build up.

boots.name: Spellslinger's Shoes
boots.note: Magic penetration keeps his beam relevant in the levels before his stacks arrive, which is his weakest stretch.

coreItems.name: Rylai's Crystal Scepter
coreItems.note: His beam damages continuously, so the slow reapplies constantly and targets cannot walk out of it.

coreItems.name: Liandry's Torment
coreItems.note: His beam ticks constantly, so the max health burn stays applied for as long as he holds it on someone.

coreItems.name: Rabadon's Deathcap
coreItems.note: Multiplies his ability power, which raises his beam, his black hole and his ultimate at the same time.

coreItems.name: Void Staff
coreItems.note: Cuts the magic resist that lets a frontline stand in his beam and ignore it. Choose it over Cryptbloom when enemies are stacking magic resist and maximum personal damage matters more than ability haste and team healing.

coreItems.name: Banshee's Veil
coreItems.note: Build this when the enemy has crowd control ready for his channel, since interrupting it stops his damage completely.

situationalItems.name: Morellonomicon
situationalItems.note: Build this when enemies heal while standing in Aurelion Sol's breath and singularity. Both persistent zones keep Grievous Wounds refreshed across the frontline; buy Oblivion Orb early and complete the item later.

situationalItems.name: Oceanid's Trident
situationalItems.note: Build this when the enemy has shields that keep absorbing his beam damage.

situationalItems.name: Zhonya's Hourglass
situationalItems.note: Build this when assassins reach him mid-channel. Buy Seeker's Armguard early for the armor and ability power.

situationalItems.name: Cryptbloom
situationalItems.note: Choose this when enemies have only moderate magic resist. Compared with Void Staff, Aurelion Sol trades some beam damage for haste on his control spells and an area heal when his sustained damage earns a takedown.

keystoneRune.name: Dark Harvest
keystoneRune.desc: Damaging low-health champions harvests a soul and empowers your next harvest proc.
keystoneRune.note: His E executes low health targets, so the souls come from kills his black hole was already going to get.

primaryRunes.name: Manaflow Band
primaryRunes.desc: Hitting an enemy champion with an ability permanently increases your maximum mana.
primaryRunes.note: His beam is expensive to channel, and the extra mana lets him hold it for full rotations.

primaryRunes.name: Absolute Focus
primaryRunes.desc: While above 70% health, gain bonus adaptive force.
primaryRunes.note: He should be poking from range at full health rather than trading, so the bonus is live when he casts.

primaryRunes.name: Gathering Storm
primaryRunes.desc: Gain increasing adaptive force every few minutes as the game goes on.
primaryRunes.note: His whole champion is permanent stacking, so a rune that grows over the game fits the plan.

secondaryRunes.name: Bone Plating
secondaryRunes.desc: After taking damage from a champion, the next 3 instances of champion damage are reduced.
secondaryRunes.note: He needs uninterrupted time to stack, and this buys him through the burst that would otherwise end the cast.

spells.name: Flash
spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

goodAgainst.note: A scaler-versus-scaler race played around zones: Veigar's Event Horizon can stop Astral Flight, while a large Singularity drags his immobile frame inward. Stardust improves the black hole and beam burst damage, not the beam's cast range.
Annie needs you standing still inside Tibbers range, and her burst window is brief; once you scale she has no answer to your range or your zone control.

Breath of Light eventually reaches beyond Orianna's command range, while Singularity forces her to move herself instead of controlling the fight only through the ball. Respect her earlier Command: Attack and Dissonance poke, then use Astral Flight to change the beam angle after the ball is committed away from her and scale the Stardust race.

Mistral Bolt and Looming Darkness are telegraphed, but Personal Space hits immediately around Vex and Shadow Surge can deliver a prepared Doom fear from range. Aurelion Sol's reach and scaling still favor long fights, but he must respect the ultimate mark instead of treating every Vex cast as a slow windup.
Yasuo leans on Wind Wall against mages, but it does not block your first ability, Breath of Light, so the beam keeps burning him through the wall while your range and scaling grind him down.

weakAgainst.note: Living Shadow lets Zed place Razor Shuriken damage beyond Aurelion Sol's early Breath of Light range, and Death Mark punishes the stationary channel before Stardust has improved it. Keep Singularity on the shadow return point, hold Astral Flight until Zed commits his swap, and give up early lane priority rather than feeding the assassin his snowball timing.

Katarina can use units and ground Daggers as Shunpo targets, but minion deaths do not trigger Voracity's champion-takedown cooldown reduction. She can still dive while Astral Flight is unavailable and snowball through Aurelion Sol's weak phase.
Fizz's pole-vault makes him untargetable through your key spells, so he chunks you, hops over the black hole, and all-ins once his ultimate lands the shark.
A scaling race you lose on timing: once his ultimate is online he blinks through your range over and over, and his magic shield blunts the beam.

Charm interrupts Aurelion Sol's stationary Breath of Light channel and can stop Astral Flight, while Spirit Rush crosses Singularity before its pull controls Ahri. Keep Singularity between yourself and her before level five, hold Astral Flight as an exit, and concede the wave after Charm lands instead of giving her the early kill that delays Stardust scaling.

gamePlan.overview:
Aurelion Sol is a scaling mid laner who collects Stardust to upgrade different parts of his kit. Stardust increases Breath of Light's burst damage, Astral Flight's travel range, Singularity's radius and execute threshold, and Falling Star's impact radius. It does not directly extend Breath of Light's beam range. Every 65 Stardust also empowers the next Falling Star into The Skies Descend, a larger delayed knockup with a map-spreading shockwave.

In lane he is the purest scaling control mage. Channeling Breath of Light on the same champion produces periodic max-health bursts and Stardust, while enemies that remain inside Singularity and units that die within it add more stacks. As Singularity and Falling Star grow, objective entrances become much harder for the enemy team to cross.

The catch is how long the scaling takes. Before your stacks and first items land, you are short-ranged, mana-hungry, and slow to answer a committed dive, so early laning is about discipline, not aggression. Assassins who close the gap and fighters who walk you down both kill you before your stacks come online. Get there intact and he is one of the best teamfight mages in Wild Rift; get caught early and you contribute almost nothing.
gamePlan.earlyGame: The opening levels are about staying alive and stacking, not winning trades. Use the beam to last-hit and chip when the enemy steps into the wave, but watch your mana, because with an empty bar you are just a slow target. Drop the black hole to peel a gank or punish anyone who walks a straight line at you, and hold your flight as an escape rather than an entry until your stacks make committing worth it. Against the lane bullies who own this phase, give a little ground, soak the wave under tower, and let the stacks climb; every minion moves you closer to taking over.
gamePlan.midGame: Your first item and a healthy Stardust count flip the lane from survival to control. Breath of Light's cast range is not growing with Stardust, but its same-target bursts hit harder, Singularity covers more ground, and Astral Flight reaches farther. Shove with those tools, then arrive early enough to place Singularity where the enemy must cross for dragon or Herald.
gamePlan.lateGame: Late game is where the stacking pays off. Singularity remains stationary after placement; it does not move; but its larger radius drags enemies inward and executes non-epic targets beneath its Stardust-scaled threshold. Keep Breath of Light on one safe target long enough to trigger repeated max-health bursts, and track whether your next Falling Star has transformed into The Skies Descend before committing to an objective fight.
gamePlan.teamfights: In a teamfight you are area control, not a target diver. Place Singularity on a choke or beneath a controlled target so its inward drag keeps enemies in the zone, then channel Breath of Light on the nearest safe target instead of constantly changing targets and losing the one-second burst cadence. Astral Flight resets the beam and lets Aurelion Sol channel it without a cooldown during the dash, but any immobilizing crowd control knocks him out of the flight.

startingItem.name: Long Sword
startingItem.note: Simple early attack damage, which makes her headshot chunk instead of chip.

boots.name: Gunmetal Greaves
boots.note: Attack speed builds her headshot stacks faster, so the empowered shot is up more often.

coreItems.name: The Collector
coreItems.note: Its execute complements Ace in the Hole's role as a long-range finisher, helping Caitlyn convert the low-health targets she creates through poke into kills.

coreItems.name: Magnetic Blaster

coreItems.name: Lord Dominik's Regard
coreItems.note: Build this against armor stackers, so her poke still threatens a frontline that itemized against it. Choose it over Mortal Reminder when enemies are stacking health rather than healing, since Giant Slayer increases Caitlyn's damage against high-health targets.

coreItems.name: Bloodthirster
coreItems.note: Physical vamp that increases on critical strikes helps her recover from chip damage without leaving lane.

coreItems.name: Soul Transfer
coreItems.note: Her headshot scales with crit chance, and each crit summons a clone that keeps attacking from where she is not standing.

situationalItems.name: Mortal Reminder
situationalItems.note: Build this against armor stackers or enemies who heal, since either will outlast her poke. Choose it over Lord Dominik's Regard when enemy healing is the bigger problem, since Grievous Wounds stops targets from recovering Caitlyn's damage.

situationalItems.name: Blade of the Ruined King
situationalItems.note: Percent current health damage and omnivamp, for the games where she has to fight instead of zone.

situationalItems.name: Guardian Angel
situationalItems.note: Build this when assassins keep reaching her. Her net repositions her but does not save her once it is spent.

situationalItems.name: Infinity Edge
situationalItems.note: A crit spike pays her twice, since her headshot damage also scales with crit chance.

situationalItems.name: Mercurial Scimitar
situationalItems.note: Build this when one stun or root is what kills her. Her net is a repositioning tool, not a cleanse.

keystoneRune.name: Lethal Tempo
keystoneRune.desc: Attacking champions grants attack speed. At maximum stacks, also gain attack range.
keystoneRune.note: Attack speed and eventually more range on a champion built around hitting from further away than anyone.
