primaryRunes.desc: Attacks deal bonus adaptive damage to enemy champions.
primaryRunes.note: Bonus damage on every autoattack, which turns her range advantage into an actual health lead.

primaryRunes.name: Cut Down
primaryRunes.desc: You deal bonus adaptive damage (except true damage) to enemy champions above 60% health.
primaryRunes.note: She wins by attacking safely for a long time, and this makes those attacks count against the tank standing in front.

primaryRunes.name: Legend: Alacrity
primaryRunes.desc: Gain permanent attack speed by taking down champions, monsters, and minions.
primaryRunes.note: Faster attacks build headshot stacks quicker, so the empowered shot is up for more of each trade.

secondaryRunes.name: Bone Plating
secondaryRunes.desc: After taking damage from a champion, the next 3 instances of champion damage are reduced.
secondaryRunes.note: Her whole plan is out-ranging the lane, so the thing that kills her is a support who closes the gap and commits.

spells.name: Flash
spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

goodAgainst.note: Zeri's mobility only matters once she gets inside your range, and your headshots and traps control the lane from outside her reach, so her dashes never get the chance to work.
Kai'Sa needs farm to hit her evolutions, and your range denies it. Behind on items she contributes little in teamfights, and this lane puts her behind.

Caitlyn's basic-attack range and Piltover Peacemaker punish Vayne before she can apply three Silver Bolts, while Yordle Snap Traps restrict the Tumble angles around the wave. Push the early lane, keep 90 Caliber Net for Vayne's approach, and convert turret pressure before her items turn the isolated duel around.

weakAgainst.note: Jhin's fourth shot hits much harder than your headshots, and his root turns your forward steps into trades you lose. You both poke at long range, but his hits are heavier.
Ezreal pokes through the minions your headshot game hides behind, and his blink ignores the traps that anchor your control. His kit is built to cancel your range advantage.
Sivir's Spell Shield eats your net and even your ultimate, so your pick tools bounce off her, and her boomerang and Ricochet shove the wave into you, denying the controlled lane you want.

gamePlan.overview:
Caitlyn controls the Dragon lane with the longest range in the role. Her rifle out-reaches every other carry, her headshot passive turns every few attacks into a free chunk of damage, and brushes charge that passive faster, so brush control is a core part of her lane. Laning against her means constantly giving up ground.

The rest of her kit locks down space: traps that guard objectives and chokes, a piercing shot for poke and waves, and a hop-back net for the rare escape she needs. Her ultimate is a long-range targeted shot with fixed physical damage, so it can finish someone who leaves a fight low, but another enemy champion can intercept the bullet.

Her pattern is strong early, awkward middle, scary late. Her lane bullying is elite and her late-game siege is miserable to face, but in the mid game she has to survive on range and traps while other carries hit their spikes first.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Use your range to control the wave without standing in the enemy support's engage line. Pressure the carry when they last-hit, enter brush when it is safe to accelerate Headshot, and place traps where an engage or retreat must step rather than scattering them randomly. Crash only when your river vision is ready, then convert the window into turret plating, a recall, or a rotation. Save 90 Caliber Net for the enemy jungler or committed engage unless spending it forward secures the kill.
gamePlan.midGame: This is a weaker relative stretch, so convert lane control instead of forcing even all-ins. At six minutes, push before moving and help your team take the objective it can reach first. Herald is usually the stronger first conversion, while dragon is worth prioritizing when your composition can keep winning grouped fights toward soul. Place traps across the approach your team controls, use Piltover Peacemaker to chip enemies before they enter, and siege only while the flanks are warded. Keep Ace in the Hole for a target whose allies cannot easily block it.
gamePlan.lateGame: Your range matters most when the objective area is prepared before the enemy arrives. Build a trap line through the entrances your team controls, then attack the closest safe target without stepping beyond your peel. Headshots and Piltover Peacemaker can force health or defensive cooldowns before Baron or Elder begins. Hold 90 Caliber Net for the diver who crosses the trap line, and cast Ace in the Hole only after checking who can block it or reach Caitlyn during the channel.
gamePlan.teamfights: Fight from maximum useful range, with traps already covering the main engage and one flank. Attack the frontline while looking for a trapped carry that enables the longer Headshot range, and move sideways with your peel rather than chasing through the fight. 90 Caliber Net creates one burst of distance and another Headshot, so aim it through the diver instead of firing it only as movement. When the fight breaks apart, use Ace in the Hole on a low target only if the channel and shot cannot be punished.

startingItem.name: Amplifying Tome
startingItem.note: Early ability power for her Q, which refunds its own cost when it kills, so more damage also means more mana.

boots.name: Spellslinger's Shoes
boots.note: Magic penetration matters because her damage arrives in one stunned window that either kills or does not.

coreItems.name: Malignance
coreItems.note: Her game runs on Tibbers, so the ultimate haste brings him back for more fights. The burn adds damage on whoever he lands on.

coreItems.name: Hextech Rocketbelt
coreItems.desc: AP engage item with a dash
coreItems.note: Her stun only works at short range, so the dash is what closes the gap once she has four stacks.

coreItems.name: Rabadon's Deathcap
coreItems.note: Multiplies her ability power, and everything she does lands inside one stunned window, so all of it goes up at once.

coreItems.name: Cryptbloom
coreItems.note: Cuts the magic resist that lets a stunned target survive. The healing on takedown also helps the team that followed Tibbers in. Choose it when enemies have not built much magic resist, so trading Void Staff's extra damage for more ability haste and an area heal after takedowns is worthwhile.

coreItems.name: Infinity Orb
coreItems.note: Her burst often leaves squishies at a sliver, and the crit against low health targets closes that gap.

situationalItems.name: Zhonya's Hourglass
situationalItems.note: Build this for when the stun is spent and she is standing in their team. Buy Seeker's Armguard early for the armor and ability power.

situationalItems.name: Stormsurge
situationalItems.note: One stunned rotation already does enough damage to trigger the mark, so it works on the combo she casts anyway.

situationalItems.name: Void Staff
situationalItems.note: The raw penetration alternative to Cryptbloom. Build it when the enemy stacks magic resist and the team heal matters less. Choose it over Cryptbloom when enemies are stacking magic resist and maximum personal damage matters more than ability haste and team healing.

keystoneRune.name: Electrocute
keystoneRune.desc: Deal bonus damage after hitting an enemy champion with 3 separate attacks or abilities.
keystoneRune.note: Her stun window is three casts in a row, so the bonus damage lands on the combo she was doing anyway.

primaryRunes.name: Hexflash
primaryRunes.desc: While Flash is on cooldown, it is replaced by Hexflash.
primaryRunes.note: Flash into stun range is her main engage, and Hexflash keeps a version of it while Flash is down.

primaryRunes.name: Transcendence
primaryRunes.desc: Gain ability haste, then reduce a basic ability's cooldown after it hits at level 9.
primaryRunes.note: Ability haste means more Q casts, which is how she builds the four stacks her kill pattern needs.

primaryRunes.name: Nimbus Cloak
primaryRunes.desc: After casting a summoner spell, gain movement speed and slow resistance.
primaryRunes.note: The move speed after a summoner spell carries her the last few steps into stun range.

secondaryRunes.name: Bone Plating
secondaryRunes.desc: After taking damage from a champion, the next 3 instances of champion damage are reduced.
secondaryRunes.note: She has to step up to last hit with no escape, so the burst that punishes her walk-up is what this cuts down.

spells.name: Flash
spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

goodAgainst.note: His strength is the gold card and the global roam, not the 1v1: in lane a loaded stun beats his slow card windup every time he steps up to farm.

Mistral Bolt and Looming Darkness are telegraphed, but Personal Space hits immediately around Vex and Shadow Surge can carry a prepared Doom fear into the engage. Track her fear bar and hold Annie's loaded stun for the dash arrival instead of treating every Vex basic ability as a slow projectile.

Taliyah must stand near the wave to cast Threaded Volley and set up Seismic Shove, which brings her into Flash or Tibbers range despite her longer poke. Arrive with Pyromania already loaded, avoid walking through Unraveled Earth, and spend the stun only after she has used Seismic Shove so the burst cannot be displaced.

Vladimir's sustain means nothing if you delete him in one loaded-stun rotation, and his early levels are weak before Transfusion ranks and items strengthen his healing. Sanguine Pool can still dodge the spell carrying Pyromania if he reads the cast.

weakAgainst.note: Akali's shroud hides her from your walk-up and her dashes cover the gap your combo depends on, so the all-in that beats immobile mages misses here, and she wins any extended trade.
Zed out-ranges your walk-up with shurikens and all-ins your immobile frame the moment your stun is on cooldown; only a loaded stun turns his shadow engage against him.
Orianna out-ranges you badly and her whole plan is staying out of stun range: her shield blunts your one combo and the ball zones the exact ground you need to stand on.

Rebuttal can reflect Annie's projectile Disintegrate and makes Mel briefly invulnerable to the non-projectile parts of the combo, but it does not copy Incinerate or Tibbers back at Annie. Draw out the 0.75-second window before committing the loaded stun and full burst.

Galio's Shield of Durand passive grants a magic-damage shield after its refresh condition, and the active adds damage reduction plus a taunt. Combined with his knockup and tank build, that makes Annie's single burst rotation unreliable; it is not a generic magic-resistance passive.

gamePlan.overview:
Annie is a burst mage who carries her crowd control on a passive instead of a single dedicated ability. Every fourth spell loads a free stun onto the next one, and her whole laning pattern is building to that fourth cast, then spending it on a Tibbers summon that stuns everyone standing in the landing zone. The stun itself never misses once the spell connects, and Tibbers covers enough ground that a target already inside her range rarely walks out in time.

In mid lane she plays the all-in instead of the poke. Farm with Disintegrate to keep your mana steady, stack the passive so the stun is always a button-press away, and wait for the enemy mid to misjudge how close is too close. Hit your item spike with the stun loaded and you kill a target before they can react. The same package makes her one of the scarier roamers in Wild Rift, because a loaded stun is just as lethal on a side laner who never warded the river.

The catch is range and mobility. Annie has very short range and no dash, so anyone who out-distances her or escapes her one big button is safe from everything she does. Without the stun ready she is a short-range mage with a slow walk-up, and a wasted Tibbers leaves her standing in the open with every cooldown spent.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Lane around the passive counter, not the health bar. Last-hit with Disintegrate when the mana refund is up, chip with Incinerate only when it also stacks you toward a stun, and always know whether your next spell is the loaded one, because that decides whether you can walk up or have to wait. Against shorter-range mages, shove and bully, daring them to contest a wave you can stun-burst them off. Against anyone with reach or a dash, sit further back, farm patiently, and save the stun for one big moment instead of spending it on poke. Ward the river the moment you push, since an immobile mid with no escape is exactly the gank the enemy jungler is hoping to find.
gamePlan.midGame: Your ultimate coming online changes everything: a loaded stun plus Tibbers is a kill on any squishy who lets you reach combo range, in lane or anywhere else. Shove the wave with Disintegrate and Incinerate, then leave with the stun stacked and go hunt, because Annie roams as well as she lanes and her lockdown is just as lethal on a side laner. Mid priority lets you join scuttle fights, where Tibbers dropped on a clustered jungle duo flips the contest before it starts, and it lets you zone the enemy off dragon and herald with the simple threat of a loaded stun. The trade-off is that every roam leaves your immobile frame stranded if you misjudge the timing, so push with a plan and an escape path, not just a hunch.
gamePlan.lateGame: By now the combo kills a carry, so the late game is entirely about getting the stun to the right target without dying on the way. Keep Tibbers ready and the stun always stacked before a fight, and look for the flank or the flash-stun that catches their backline off guard. Molten Shield is your only defensive tool, so keep it for the burst and the dives aimed at you. The situation never changes: you are a short-range mage in a fight full of people who want to reach you first. The skill is patience, spotting the moment their carry steps half a step too far, and turning it into the lockdown that wins the fight.
gamePlan.teamfights: Annie does not poke a teamfight; she starts one or ends one. Best case is a Flash-stun Tibbers that catches two or three enemies. If the clean multi-stun is not there, hold the loaded cast for their carry. Tibbers remains as a controllable pet for up to 20 seconds, but the current Wild Rift description does not give him the old persistent burn aura. After two seconds, recast the ultimate to make Tibbers pounce onto a champion for damage and a one-second knockup, and save that leap for a target trying to leave.

coreItems.name: Liandry's Torment
coreItems.note: His W never stops ticking, so the max health burn stays applied to everyone standing near him.

coreItems.name: Thornmail
coreItems.note: Build this against healing. The Grievous Wounds applies from your own damage as well as when they attack you, so his aura keeps it on everyone he stunned.

coreItems.name: Amaranth's Twinguard
coreItems.note: Build this when you are fighting in the middle of the enemy team and need both armor and magic resist. Amumu's W and ultimate already require him to stay surrounded, which reliably activates Twinguard during the fight.

coreItems.name: Abyssal Mask
coreItems.note: His passive already makes cursed targets take more magic damage, and this shreds their magic resist on top of it.

situationalItems.name: Randuin's Omen
situationalItems.note: Build this when the enemy team has multiple crit champions. Bandage Toss and Curse of the Sad Mummy place Amumu in their firing line, so reducing incoming crits protects the exact position his engage requires.

situationalItems.name: Chainlaced Crushers
situationalItems.note: Boot swap against heavy magic damage and crowd control. Tenacity gets Amumu back to moving and casting after the first disable, while magic resistance protects the Bandage Toss entry his kit requires.

situationalItems.name: Frozen Heart
situationalItems.note: Build this when the enemy team has several attack-speed carries. Amumu already stands beside them with Despair active, so Frozen Heart's aura remains on the targets caught by his ultimate.

keystoneRune.name: Ice Overlord
keystoneRune.desc: Immobilizing an enemy champion creates icy beams and a frozen zone that slows enemies inside.
keystoneRune.note: He has two bandage charges and a teamfight stun, so he immobilizes enemies more often than almost anyone.

primaryRunes.desc: Gain bonus armor and magic resist, increasing further when surrounded by enemies.
primaryRunes.note: His job is standing surrounded, which is when this rune gives the most.

primaryRunes.name: Bone Plating

primaryRunes.note: He walks into the middle of a team to land his ultimate, so the first rotation aimed at him is the one worth blunting.

primaryRunes.name: Overgrowth
primaryRunes.desc: Gain permanent maximum health when nearby minions or monsters die.
primaryRunes.note: He initiates and gets focused for it, and the extra health is what carries him through the answer.

secondaryRunes.name: Sudden Impact
secondaryRunes.desc: Deal bonus true damage after using mobility or exiting stealth.
secondaryRunes.note: His Q pulls him to the target, which counts as a dash and sets up the bonus true damage.

spells.name: Smite
spells.note: Required for Jungling. Secures objectives and sustains through camp clears.

goodAgainst.note: Talon's burst does little against your resists, and your ultimate pins him the moment he blinks in. He has no health bar to trade with you, so a failed gank near you becomes his death.
Rengar's leap-and-burst combo needs a squishy target, and you are not one. His damage bounces off your frame while your multi-target stun holds him in place with no reset to escape.
Viego lives on resets, but your Bandage Toss and group lockdown stop him before he secures the kill that keeps him alive, and his weak early duel cannot break a tank.

weakAgainst.note: Her spears poke you down before you get close, and her fast clear lets her invade your mana-hungry start. A straight-line engage rarely lands on a champion built to kite and reposition.
Lillia drifts out of Bandage Toss range while her burn wears you down from a distance. If the bandage misses you are an immobile tank with nothing to do, and her sleep starts fights on her terms.

A missed Bandage Toss strands you inside his Crowstorm, feared and silenced while his drain ticks you down. His fear lasts longer than your stun, and he out-zones your ultimate in the cramped objective fights you want to start.

gamePlan.overview:
Amumu is the jungler who turns one good throw into a won teamfight. Bandage Toss is a line skillshot that stuns and pulls him to whatever it hits, Despair drains health from everyone nearby, Tantrum cuts the physical damage he takes and deals area damage, and Curse of the Sad Mummy locks down everyone caught in it at once. He is a tank whose ultimate starts the fight whenever he decides, on his terms.

He wins through patience. His early clear is steady, his ganks depend on landing one skillshot, and before items he mostly just soaks damage in duels. None of that matters much, because the moment his ultimate is up he can jump into three or four people and lock the whole group while his team deletes them. Amumu does not snowball lanes; he waits for the first real objective fight and decides it.

His weakness is that same skillshot. Bandage Toss is slow and straight, and if it misses he is a melee tank with no gap closer, standing in the open and often out of mana. He is mana-hungry early, weak in early skirmishes, and easy to invade before he comes online. Protect that window and he is one of the most reliable engage junglers in Wild Rift.
gamePlan.earlyGame:
Your first clear is steady rather than fast, so route for mana rather than racing a timer you will lose. Despair and Tantrum clear camps comfortably, but watch your mana, because an empty bar means no gank and no escape. Finish the rotation and take scuttle, which puts you on level five with your ultimate up. Once the camps are respawning, that is your window to walk at a lane: the gank is real the moment Bandage Toss lands, and the stun chain usually finishes it. Clear again when the camps are back and repeat.

Be careful at scuttle, since a strong early duelist will simply out-damage you over the crab, so contest with your laners nearby or give it up and farm. Track the enemy jungler, ward your own buffs, and accept that this phase is about surviving until you matter.
gamePlan.midGame:
Curse of the Sad Mummy changes your role as soon as teams begin grouping. A clean Bandage Toss onto their carry, then the ultimate landing on the whole group, is the cleanest objective trade there is, so contest when your team can follow up. If the fight looks even, take Herald and trade away the dragon rather than throwing your ultimate into a coin flip, though a team built to hold long fights is a reason to play for soul instead.

You can also invade, because your percent-health aura and area damage win a counter-jungle skirmish when you bring a teammate. Path toward whatever spawns next, since your tempo comes from setting up fights rather than out-clearing anyone.
gamePlan.lateGame: Late game Amumu exists for teamfights, so stop hunting solo plays and position for the one engage that wins the fight. You cannot catch anyone in a footrace and you do not want to duel a fed carry alone, so play around vision and find the angle where your ultimate hits the most people. Baron and the late dragons are ideal: the space is cramped, the enemies are clumped, and one engage into their backline can end the game on the spot. Hold the engage until your team can actually follow it, because a wasted ultimate usually means dying and watching the rest from the death timer. Build to survive the burst long enough to land the throw, and let your team do the killing.
gamePlan.teamfights: You are the engage, and almost nothing else matters until you commit it. Find the flank or the choke where their carries are stacked, go in with Bandage Toss or Flash plus ultimate, and lock the whole group while your team collapses. Despair keeps draining everyone standing next to you, Tantrum keeps hitting the cluster, and your damage reduction lets you hold the middle of the fight instead of melting in it. The hard part is timing: engage a beat too early and you are alone, a beat too late and the carries have scattered. Get it right and Curse of the Sad Mummy is the most decisive single button a jungler can press.

coreItems.name: Rylai's Crystal Scepter

coreItems.name: Void Staff

coreItems.note: Multiplies his spell damage, the AP-scaling portion of Blaze's three-stack explosion, and his bouncing ultimate. Blaze's ordinary percentage maximum-health burn has no AP ratio, so Deathcap does not increase that component directly.

situationalItems.name: Morellonomicon
situationalItems.note: Build this when the enemy heals through his burn. Buy Oblivion Orb early, since the anti-heal works from the component and the full item can wait.

situationalItems.name: Oceanid's Trident
situationalItems.note: Build this when shields absorb Brand's burn. His passive and area spells keep the reduction active across several targets while the blaze stacks toward its explosion.

situationalItems.name: Zhonya's Hourglass
situationalItems.note: Build this against assassins, which are the main thing that beats an immobile mage. Buy Seeker's Armguard early for the armor and ability power.

situationalItems.name: Banshee's Veil
situationalItems.note: Build this when the enemy has a hook or point-and-click stun, since a caught Brand dies before his stacks reach three.

situationalItems.name: Bloodletter's Curse
situationalItems.note: Brand's passive keeps applying Wicked Decay after his first hit and spreads it across grouped enemies. The Magic Resistance reduction benefits the whole team, making Bloodletter especially strong when your composition has multiple magic-damage threats.

situationalItems.name: Infinity Orb
situationalItems.note: His burn leaves targets low without finishing them, and the crit against low health turns those into kills.

keystoneRune.name: Aery
keystoneRune.desc: Your attacks and abilities send Aery to a target, dealing damage to enemies or shielding allies.
keystoneRune.note: Every ability he casts already reaches an enemy, so Aery adds free damage to the poke that wins his lane.

primaryRunes.desc: While in combat with an enemy champion, gain stacking basic ability damage amplification.
primaryRunes.note: Brand's passive burn keeps him in champion combat after the first spell, allowing Battle Zeal to amplify the later abilities and passive explosion in his rotation.

primaryRunes.name: Cut Down
primaryRunes.desc: You deal bonus adaptive damage (except true damage) to enemy champions above 60% health.
primaryRunes.note: Blaze really does deal a percentage of maximum health over time, and its three-stack explosion deals another, larger percentage. Cut Down adds damage against high-health champions on top of those built-in ratios.

primaryRunes.name: Legend: Bloodline
primaryRunes.desc: Gain permanent omnivamp by taking down champions, monsters, and minions.
primaryRunes.note: His burns tick constantly, and the Omnivamp turns that steady damage into staying power.

secondaryRunes.name: Transcendence
secondaryRunes.desc: Gain ability haste, then reduce a basic ability's cooldown after it hits at level 9.
secondaryRunes.note: Ability haste means more casts, so his passive reaches three stacks more often.

spells.name: Flash
spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

goodAgainst.note: Annie has to walk into your range to do anything with Tibbers, and your fire chunks her every time she steps up to farm, so your spreading damage beats her short range all lane.

Her shroud hides her from targeted spells, but Pillar of Flame still hits its ground area and Blaze keeps burning after she vanishes. Save the empowered Sear stun for the moment she reveals herself to attack rather than describing her shroud as a reset mechanic.
Swain needs long fights where his drain out-heals you, but your burst lands all at once, faster than his sustain can answer, and his root is his only way to force that fight.

You never dash, so Vex never collects a Gloom mark off you, though Doom still empowers her next ability on its own timer, and W lands instantly around her rather than travelling. You stack your stun faster than she builds her combo, and her squishy, immobile frame folds to the all-in.

weakAgainst.note: Irelia dashes through the wave and past your stun, with every low minion giving her another reset, and once she has items she can all-in you whenever she wants.
Early he struggles against your burst and faster clear, but once his ultimate is online he blinks through your combo, closes the distance, and out-scales you outright.
Your stun is a skillshot he can dodge behind a shadow, and the instant your combo is on cooldown he deletes a mage with no escape. A fair fight here is one you lose.
Viktor out-ranges your fire and out-scales you, his shield soaks the chip you do land, and his gravity field zones the ground you need while setting up a combo your squishy body cannot survive.

gamePlan.overview:
Brand is a burst mage who spreads fire between targets. His stun only works on a target that is already burning, his pillar of flame erupts where you place it, his conflagration jumps between clustered enemies and minions, and his ultimate bounces between anyone standing too close together. Land the opener and the rest of the combo follows, which is why one mistake against him often costs a whole health bar.

In mid he plays a burst-and-bully game. He shoves the wave with his spreading fire, chips immobile and short-range mages who have to stand in his zone to farm, and punishes any clump of minions and champions with a combo that hits all of it. Priority buys him roams: his burst does not need a lead, just a target standing still, and a stunned, burning enemy usually dies before they can react. He never turns into a hypercarry, but he stays a reliable source of burst that deletes squishies all game, and his damage chains through grouped enemies in a way single-target mages cannot match.

The catch is mobility. Brand has no dash and no blink, and his whole combo depends on landing a skillshot stun on a burning target. Miss the opener and he is a stationary mage with everything on cooldown, and any assassin who reaches him in that window kills him.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Play the early lane aggressively around your wave clear. Your fire spreads through the wave, so you clear fast, hold priority against most mids, and chip the enemy every time they step up to last-hit. The stun only lands on a burning target, so tag them with conflagration first, then drop the pillar where they have to stand and confirm the stun into the rest of the combo. Save that full rotation for the moment they overstep instead of spending it on the wave, because a clean all-in chunks most mids close to kill range. You have no escape, though, so ward the river: an immobile mage who shoves carelessly is the easiest gank on the map.
gamePlan.midGame: Mid game is shove, move, and control the entrance before the enemy arrives. Clear the wave with your spreading fire, then walk with your jungler toward river or a side lane and threaten a stun from fog. Both first objectives spawn at six minutes. Herald is usually the stronger even conversion, while dragon becomes attractive when your composition can use Brand's area damage to win repeated pit fights toward soul. Cast onto grouped enemies only after checking which target can spread the passive and ultimate effectively, and keep enough distance that an assassin cannot trade one flank for the mage controlling the whole choke.
gamePlan.lateGame: At full items, one clean stun can kill a squishy caught within your spell range. Find that opener from the edge of the fight, let the combo finish the kill, then look for the next target while your cooldowns come back. You never become a frontline threat; you stay a source of burst that decides whether their carry survives the opening exchange. Stand behind your frontline like the fragile mage you are, because the only way you lose a won fight is dying before your combo goes out. Hold your ultimate for a moment when the enemy clumps, since a fireball bouncing through grouped bodies does far more than one spent on a single target.
gamePlan.teamfights: You are the team's area burst, and the job is finding the angle where your fire hits the most people. The best case is a stun onto a clustered enemy, conflagration spreading to everyone nearby, and your ultimate bouncing between enemies who grouped too tight. Open from the back, burn whoever fronts the fight, and read the grouping before you spend the ultimate: a panicked early cast catches one stray, a patient one bounces through their whole back line. Stay close to your frontline so a diver has to go through them first, because once an assassin reaches you, you have no escape. Get the angle right and your fire decides the fight almost on its own.

gamePlan.overview:
Brand is a support who brings raw damage instead of shields or heals. Every spell sets enemies ablaze with a percent health burn, three stacks of Blaze detonate for a chunk of maximum health, and his ultimate bounces through clumped fights like a pinball made of fire. He protects his carry the same way artillery protects infantry: by making the other side of the lane unlivable.

In the 2v2 he is a kill-lane engine. Conflagration is targeted damage that spreads to nearby enemies, with doubled spread range when its main target is already Ablaze. Pillar of Flame punishes the wave, and Sear only stuns an Ablaze target if its fireball still connects.

The cost is durability and mobility. Brand has no sustain or dash, but he does have conditional peel: an Ablaze target hit by Sear is stunned for 1.75 seconds. If Sear misses, is intercepted, or the diver was not marked first, he has no second defensive control tool.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Stand beside the minion wave rather than directly behind it so Sear has a line when the enemy carry steps forward. Open short trades with Conflagration, place Pillar of Flame on the target's retreat path, and save Sear until the target is Ablaze. The mark enables the stun but does not let the projectile pass through another enemy. Avoid using Pillar on the wave without a reason, because repeated area damage pushes the lane and exposes an immobile support to ganks. The full three-ability detonation is not available at level one, so play the opening levels around poke and positioning rather than forcing an incomplete combo.
gamePlan.midGame: At level five, Pyroclasm makes close 2v2s and narrow river fights much more dangerous for a grouped enemy. Rotate after the Dragon-lane wave is safe, establish vision with a teammate, and apply Blaze before both teams enter the same choke. Hold Sear for a marked diver when your carry needs peel; use it aggressively only when the stun can create a real numbers advantage. Between objectives, pressure defenders with Conflagration from behind your frontline, but do not walk into hook range just to add one more poke cast.
gamePlan.lateGame: Move with your team before Baron and Elder because Brand cannot check dark vision alone. Fight around chokes where Conflagration can spread and Pyroclasm can bounce, then keep Sear for the marked assassin who reaches your backline. Against a spread formation, damage the nearest safe target and wait for the enemy to group before committing the ultimate. Pyroclasm can bounce to Brand, so spacing near a lone target can create return bounces, but standing too far forward to force that interaction is rarely worth the risk.
gamePlan.teamfights: Apply Blaze with Conflagration or Pillar of Flame before using Pyroclasm on a grouped formation. Place Pillar on the space enemies must move through rather than their current position. If a diver reaches your carry, mark that target and use Sear for the stun instead of spending it on the frontline. Brand contributes damage first, but preserving the conditional stun often determines whether he and his carry survive long enough to finish the rotation.

gamePlan.overview:
Ahri is a mobile mid laner who creates picks with Charm and follows them with a short burst rotation. Landing Charm gives Orb of Deception, Fox-Fire, and Spirit Rush a clear target. Missing it removes most of her pressure until the cooldown returns, so holding the spell can be more useful than throwing a low-percentage attempt.

She is strongest when mid priority lets her move first. Clear a wave, enter river with vision, and threaten Charm from an angle that is not blocked by minions. Spirit Rush can create that angle or cover the exit, but spending every charge to enter leaves her exposed to the response.

Ahri is still fragile, and her damage is less reliable when Charm misses or the first target is too durable to burst. Longer-range mages can make her spend health to reach the wave, while mobile assassins can attack during Charm's cooldown. She needs clean angles and disciplined Spirit Rush usage rather than repeated forced engages.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Use Orb of Deception through the wave when you need priority, but avoid pushing automatically when the enemy jungler is missing. Build Essence Theft with safe ability hits and use the empowered cast to recover health without stepping into a losing trade. Hold Charm while minions block the line, then use it after the opponent spends a dash, walks beside the wave, or enters a narrow river angle. If Charm misses, back away until it returns instead of trading without your main setup tool.
gamePlan.midGame: Once Spirit Rush and the first item are available, crash the wave before moving toward river. Roam when a side lane is extended, your jungler is contesting space, or an objective is close enough that arriving first matters. If none of those conditions exists, place vision, threaten the move, and return for the next wave instead of losing farm to a speculative gank. Enter from fog when possible, use Spirit Rush to improve the Charm angle, and preserve a charge for the exit unless the takedown is already secure.
gamePlan.lateGame: Clear side waves only when you can return before Baron or Elder is contested. In grouped fights, stay outside the enemy's reliable crowd control and look for a carry who has separated from peel. Commit after a key defensive spell or dash is used, then route at least one Spirit Rush charge toward safe terrain. If the backline is protected, use Charm to peel a diver or control a choke rather than forcing a low-value dash into the enemy team.
gamePlan.teamfights: Choose between a pick and peel before spending Spirit Rush. From a flank, wait until the enemy uses the crowd control that can stop your first dash, then Charm a reachable carry and move sideways between casts to avoid the return damage. From your own backline, hold Charm for the diver who commits onto your carry. Do not spend every dash entering unless the target will die and the remaining enemy cooldowns cannot punish the position.

Nautilus's hook removes the spacing your poke and roam game needs, and Bard's shrines heal rather than block crowd control. One landed hook can start a chain that a conditional Cosmic Binding stun may not interrupt in time.
Pyke out-roams you, threatens picks faster than you set them up, and his grey health sustain recovers your poke damage while his execute punishes any chip on your ADC.
Rakan engages on demand with a charged knockup and a dash your conditional stun cannot reliably answer, and he is mobile enough to dodge the Q you need to land.

gamePlan.overview:
Bard is a support who spends much of the game roaming. He wanders the map collecting chimes, builds meeps that empower his autos, and can threaten a wall stun in the Dragon lane at any moment. The enemy can never fully track him: a roam becomes a kill mid, a healing shrine turns a lost trade into a won one, a portal puts your jungler somewhere they did not account for.

In the 2v2 he plays a poke and pick game rather than sitting still to peel. His Q stuns when it pins a target against terrain or hits a second body, his shrines heal your duo and give a movement speed burst for the engage or the escape, and the meeps add real damage to his harass. Tempered Fate, his stasis ultimate, is the swing tool: it can freeze a diver, save your carry, or zone a whole pit at dragon.

The catch is the same thing that makes him exciting. His stun needs a wall or a second target, so a sloppy Bard whiffs the fight. He is squishy, his roams leave your ADC alone in dangerous windows, and a bad stasis can strand an ally or save an enemy you wanted dead.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Read the lane before leaving for chimes. Poke with Cosmic Binding when the enemy lines up with terrain or another unit, then add a meep-empowered attack only if the return trade is safe. Place shrines early enough to charge and collect nearby chimes without leaving your carry in a long 1v2. Roam after the wave is safe or your carry recalls, ping the movement, and avoid entering an unwarded river alone while the enemy jungler is missing.
gamePlan.midGame: Mid game is when your roaming pays off. With chimes banked you move faster than anyone expects, so look for picks: a wall stun on an enemy walking through river without vision, or a portal that lands your jungler behind their backline at dragon. Ward objectives early and stun the first body that walks into the pit, since one landed Q before a dragon fight tilts the numbers your way. Keep shrines stocked near the objective so your team contests at full health with a speed burst ready. Hold stasis for the moment the fight actually turns: it can freeze the enemy engage mid-commit or save your ADC from a dive.
gamePlan.lateGame: Late game Bard is a roaming control piece who sets up ambushes. Keep chiming on the way to grouping so your speed stays high, scout the flanks, and look for the stun that catches a stray carry before the teamfight forms. Around Baron and dragon, your portals and walls let you flank or move your whole team into an angle the enemy cannot see coming. Tempered Fate is your biggest contribution now: stasis the enemy hypercarry out of a fight you are losing, freeze a diver off your backline, or split their team in half so yours cleans up the stranded side. The risk scales with you, since one greedy roam or one stasis on the wrong target loses the game as fast as a good one wins it.
gamePlan.teamfights: Your job is to start the fight from a flank or break theirs in two. Open with a wall stun on a high value target if the terrain lets the Q connect, then drop a shrine so your team can collapse with the speed burst. Hold Tempered Fate as the swing it is: a good stasis can cut their engage off from their carries, save your ADC from focus, or buy the exact second your team needs to turn. Read the angles, because your stun needs terrain or a clustered body to land, and a Bard who whiffs the opener is a squishy with nothing left. Between roams, position to peel for your carry. An alive Bard threatening the next pick is worth more than a dead one who gambled a stasis.

secondaryRunes.note: Her poke is the outer half of her W thrown from the edge of their range, and Scorch adds damage to every one of those.

spells.name: Flash
spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

goodAgainst.note: Adaptive Defenses helps Camille absorb Garen's return trade, while the readied second Q converts more of its damage to true damage as Camille levels. Early it is only partial conversion, so do not treat armor as irrelevant from level one.

Yone does not take damage merely because Soul Unbound snaps him back; instead, the return deals stored true damage to champions he hit. Punish the body location he must return to with a timed second Q or Hookshot, rather than expecting the snapback itself to hurt him.
Too slow to threaten you. He cannot match your split push or escape your R in fights, and both his pillar and the brittle combo are avoidable.
Wind Wall does not stop Camille's melee Q attacks or Tactical Sweep. The readied second Q increasingly converts damage to true damage with level, but it is not fully true damage throughout the lane.
Her melee phase has no answer to your early Q trades, and her whole game depends on farm you keep taking away. Even if she scales, your true damage cuts through the armor she buys.

weakAgainst.note: He is strongest exactly when you are weakest: his stun interrupts your trade pattern and his burst goes through your shield in the early levels. He falls off; you do not.
Everything in his lane kit is built to kill you before items: the pull, the stacking bleed, the all-in. You can only really fight him once you reach two items.
She out-duels you, her parry answers your Hookshot stun with a stun of her own, and her vitals out-heal you in extended fights.
His Counter Strike dodges your Q autos and stuns you mid-combo, and once items arrive he out-trades your shield cycle, so the extended brawl is his.

gamePlan.overview:
Camille is a pick-focused Baron laner who dashes from terrain and traps one target inside The Hextech Ultimatum. The second Precision Protocol attack, readied after 1.6 seconds, converts 40% to 100% of its damage to true damage based on level; it is not fully true damage at every stage.

Camille starts slow, so lane around precise trades: land the first Q, wait for the readied second attack and its level-scaled true-damage conversion, hit Tactical Sweep's outer half to slow and heal from champion damage, and let Adaptive Defenses absorb the dominant damage type that target has dealt.

With items, she splits a side lane no single defender can hold, and in fights she has one clear job: hook in, ult their best player, and make the teamfight a four versus five.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Respect the first few levels until you know which spell wins the matchup's trades. Use the outer half of Tactical Sweep to thin the wave, slow the opponent, and heal without committing Hookshot. When you do trade, trigger the adaptive shield, use Q1, wait through the 1.6-second readiness window, and land Q2 after the enemy's defensive tool expires. Keep the wave on your side against strong gank setup, because a Hookshot spent forward leaves no clean retreat. The passive shield adapts to the target's prior physical or magic champion damage rather than blocking both types.
gamePlan.midGame: First item plus The Hextech Ultimatum gives Camille side-lane control and a reliable pick for river fights. Crash before moving to the first Herald, approach from terrain, and use Hookshot's champion hit to gain the attack-speed window before locking the target inside R. The initial cast knocks other nearby enemies away, but it does not stop them from attacking or casting back into the zone afterward. If the enemy sends multiple defenders to your side lane, disengage through terrain and let your team convert the pressure elsewhere.
gamePlan.lateGame: Late game, keep a side wave moving without disappearing from the next major objective. Duel isolated defenders when vision shows the rest of the enemy team, then rotate early enough to find a terrain flank onto the carry. The Hextech Ultimatum grounds its target and knocks other champions away on arrival, but the trapped carry can still fight and teammates can still assist from outside. Choose a target you can survive inside the zone, and remember that it ends early if Camille becomes untargetable, leaves it, or dies.
gamePlan.teamfights: Hold your engage until the frontline commits or a carry steps away from peel. Hookshot from an unseen terrain angle, land the stun if possible, and use R to dodge a key spell or contain the priority target. The initial knockback disrupts nearby peel, but enemies can still damage or control Camille inside the zone. Time Q2 after its conversion is ready, use the adaptive shield against the target's main damage type, and keep Flash or Hookshot available when the duel will not end immediately.

startingItem.name: Long Sword

boots.name: Gunmetal Greaves

coreItems.name: Kraken Slayer

coreItems.note: Her crit rate becomes on-hit magic damage, which stacks with the rest of the build. Terminus and Blade of the Ruined King ride the same attacks, and Runaan's spreads all of it.

coreItems.name: Runaan's Hurricane
coreItems.note: The bolts hit two extra enemies and apply on-hit effects, so her passive slow lands on all of them.

coreItems.name: Terminus
coreItems.note: Stacking penetration and resistances the longer she attacks, which suits a champion who wants fights to stay at range and go long.

situationalItems.name: Guardian Angel
situationalItems.note: Revives her once after dying. Build this when assassins keep reaching her, since she has no dash at all.

situationalItems.name: Magnetic Blaster
situationalItems.note: Extra attack range on a champion with no escape, so she can hold her line without entering danger.

situationalItems.name: Mercurial Scimitar
situationalItems.note: Build this when one root or stun is what kills her. She has no dash, so the cleanse is her closest thing to an escape.

keystoneRune.name: Lethal Tempo
keystoneRune.desc: Attacking champions grants attack speed. At maximum stacks, also gain attack range.
keystoneRune.note: Attack speed lets her complete four Focus attacks and fire Ranger's Focus flurries more often, while the later bonus range improves her kiting. Each flurry is still one attack for on-hit and on-attack effects.

primaryRunes.name: Brutal
primaryRunes.desc: Attacks deal bonus adaptive damage to enemy champions.
primaryRunes.note: Bonus damage on attacks makes her lane poke land harder before her crit items exist.

primaryRunes.name: Cut Down
primaryRunes.desc: You deal bonus adaptive damage (except true damage) to enemy champions above 60% health.
primaryRunes.note: Her attacks are her damage, and this is what makes them matter against the frontline she cannot walk away from.

primaryRunes.name: Legend: Alacrity
primaryRunes.desc: Gain permanent attack speed by taking down champions, monsters, and minions.
primaryRunes.note: More attack speed builds her Q stacks faster, so the flurry is up for more of the fight.

secondaryRunes.name: Bone Plating
secondaryRunes.desc: After taking damage from a champion, the next 3 instances of champion damage are reduced.
secondaryRunes.note: She has no dash, so the enemy engage always lands, and this turns the opening hits into something she can walk out of.

spells.name: Flash
spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

goodAgainst.note: Samira has to fight in melee, and your slows punish every step of her approach. Blade Whirl blocks Volley but not the slow on your autos, so she rarely reaches the combo her snowball needs.
Kai'Sa needs isolation and gap-closing to work, and your slow punishes both, while your Volley poke denies the farm she needs for her evolutions.
Kalista's whole game is hop spacing, and your slow ruins every hop. She is fragile in the early 2v2 and loses most of her mobility advantage against you.

weakAgainst.note: Caitlyn simply out-ranges you, which breaks your slow-and-control game before it starts. You lose the lane phase and only come back in teamfights, where your arrow matters more than her poke.

Tristana all-ins your immobile frame in one jump, and your slows do little against a dash that commits instantly and resets on a kill. You out-control her everywhere except the 2v2 all-in she is built for.
Lucian's dash trades burst harder than your slows can answer, and his early levels bully your immobile frame. You out-scale him late if you leave lane without a big deficit.

gamePlan.overview:
Ashe is a marksman built around utility. Every attack she lands slows its target, her volleys spread that slow across the wave, her hawk gives vision across the map, and her ultimate is a global stun arrow that can start a fight from anywhere. No other carry gives their team this much control while still dealing carry damage.

In the Dragon lane she plays a steady, controlling game: poke with Volley, keep the enemy duo slowed, and turn every skirmish into a chase they cannot escape. She has no escape and no burst, so she wins with discipline rather than big plays.

Her famous weakness is her own positioning. She is immobile and slow, so she is the first target of every dive and an easy kill for assassins. Her support pairing and her spacing decide her games.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Keep a steady trading pattern. Use Volley on cooldown when it hits both the wave and the enemy carry, keep your slow on whoever steps forward, and let your support play off it. Check the enemy jungler with your hawk before every long trade, because you have no escape and every gank is dangerous. You win this phase by being annoying and hard to kill, not by forcing risky trades your kit does not support.
gamePlan.midGame: Level five gives Ashe a long-range way to start a pick. Check the map after clearing the Dragon-lane wave and use Enchanted Crystal Arrow when allies are close enough to convert the stun. Before objectives, scout the river route with Hawkshot and use Volley to pressure the entrance. Catching the enemy jungler or mid laner can create a safe dragon window, but firing without follow-up only gives away the cooldown.
gamePlan.lateGame: Your late game is built around repeated slows and Enchanted Crystal Arrow. Stay behind your frontline, kite so divers must keep walking through damage, and hold the ultimate for an opening pick or an assassin after the dash lands. Ashe needs time to apply steady damage, so prioritize survival over stepping forward for one extra attack. If no pick is available, the threat of the arrow can still control how the enemy approaches an objective.
gamePlan.teamfights: Start the fight or slow it. The best opening is an arrow from fog onto their carry or engage tank, with your team collapsing before the stun ends. In the fight, attack whatever is closest and keep your slow on the biggest threat to your position: every slowed diver is one your support can answer. Hawk the flanks before the fight so nothing hits you from the side. Your slows set the pace of the whole fight, so staying alive matters more than your damage.

startingItem.name: Long Sword
startingItem.note: Simple early attack damage, which matters most in the levels where Darius is already strongest.

boots.name: Chainlaced Crushers
boots.note: Boot swap against heavy magic damage and crowd control. Being kited is what actually beats him, not being out-damaged.

coreItems.name: Trinity Force
coreItems.note: His W is an empowered attack, so Spellblade triggers on it. The move speed also helps a champion with no gap closer reach people.

coreItems.name: Stridebreaker
coreItems.desc: Juggernaut bruiser item with a dash
coreItems.note: Build this when you cannot reach anyone. The dash and slow fix the fact that his whole kit needs enemies standing next to him.

coreItems.name: Sterak's Gage
coreItems.note: Lifeline fires when damage drops him below the item's health threshold, which is usually the moment he is deep in a fight with his bleed stacked, and the shield buys the seconds he needs to finish and reset.

coreItems.name: Spear of Shojin
coreItems.note: Ability haste means more axe swings, so his bleed reaches five stacks faster.

coreItems.name: Guardian Angel
coreItems.note: Revives him once after dying. Noxian Guillotine resets and refunds its mana when its target dies within 0.15 seconds after the hit, so a second life gives Darius another chance to reach a valid finisher rather than guaranteeing a reset by itself.

situationalItems.name: Mortal Reminder
situationalItems.note: Build this against enemies who heal, since out-sustaining his bleed is the main way to survive five stacks.

situationalItems.name: Randuin's Omen
situationalItems.note: Build this when the enemy team has multiple crit champions. Darius must stay in melee long enough to reach five Hemorrhage stacks, so reducing crit damage protects the setup for Noxian Guillotine.

situationalItems.name: Armored Advance
situationalItems.note: Boot swap against heavy physical damage. Darius needs time in melee to stack Hemorrhage, so reducing the attacks taken during his approach protects the entire reset pattern.

situationalItems.name: Dead Man's Plate
situationalItems.note: Momentum builds while he walks someone down, and triggers on the swing that pulls them back into range.

situationalItems.name: Thornmail
situationalItems.note: Build this against healing. The Grievous Wounds applies from your own damage as well as when they attack you, so it stacks with his bleed on anyone he has pulled in.

situationalItems.name: Mercurial Scimitar
situationalItems.note: Build this when crowd control stops Darius from reaching five Hemorrhage stacks. The cleanse preserves his approach so he can pull the target back and unlock Noxian Guillotine resets.

keystoneRune.name: Conqueror
keystoneRune.desc: Gain stacks by damaging enemy champions. At maximum stacks, gain bonus damage and healing.
keystoneRune.note: His fights are long by design, so he reaches max stacks while stacking bleed, and the healing adds to his Q healing.

primaryRunes.name: Unshakeable
primaryRunes.desc: Gain bonus armor and magic resist, increasing further when surrounded by enemies.
primaryRunes.note: He wins by staying in the middle of the fight, which is when this rune gives the most.

primaryRunes.name: Second Wind
primaryRunes.desc: After taking damage from a champion, regenerate health over time.
primaryRunes.note: He has no way to close on a poke laner, so this refunds the health he spends waiting for his hook.

primaryRunes.name: Perseverance
primaryRunes.desc: Gain tenacity and bonus defenses while immobilized.
primaryRunes.note: Take this against teams whose crowd control prevents the champion's key follow-up. Its tenacity shortens most disables and grants temporary defenses while immobilized. The shorter disable preserves Darius's Hemorrhage stacks and his chance to reach Noxian Guillotine before the target escapes.

secondaryRunes.name: Nimbus Cloak
secondaryRunes.desc: After casting a summoner spell, gain movement speed and slow resistance.
secondaryRunes.note: Casting Ghost or Flash triggers the movement speed and slow resistance Darius needs to reach Apprehend range and keep Hemorrhage stacks from falling off.

spells.name: Flash
spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

goodAgainst.note: Garen wants Decisive Strike into Judgment, then to leave and regenerate with Perseverance before Darius can build Hemorrhage. Catch that exit with Apprehend or Crippling Strike, land the outer edge of Decimate for healing, and extend the trade until five bleed stacks turn Noxian Guillotine into the winning execute.
Windwall does nothing against your kit, his shield breaks on one Q edge, and the bleed kills him before his crits matter; he is only dangerous in the middle of a big minion wave.
A perfect bleed target: big, slow, and stacked with health, and his zombie passive cannot catch anyone who walks away from it.
Shen has no kill pressure on you and loses the brawl: his block shrugs off your autos for a moment, not your bleed or your pull, though his dash answers your engage with a taunt of its own.

weakAgainst.note: Shock Blast lets Jayce tax Darius before Apprehend can reach, and Thundering Blow knocks Darius away before Hemorrhage reaches five stacks. Preserve your health instead of chasing through ranged poke, then hold Apprehend for the moment Jayce uses To the Skies in hammer form and has committed inside your range.
His shotgun trades out-damage your bleed at the edge of your range, his shield blunts your burst, and once you drop low his execute threatens you instead.
The clone and dash slip your pull, so he only takes the fights he wants: he bursts in, drops the decoy when you commit, and leaves before your bleed matters.
Regen and a huge health pool outlast your bleed, the cleaver chips you before you ever land a clean pull, and his ultimate lets him walk away from your all-in.

gamePlan.overview:
Darius is the most straightforward threat in the Baron lane: anyone who walks into his axe range is in danger. His bleed builds toward Noxian Might, which adds huge bonus damage to everything he does. Noxian Guillotine deals true damage that increases with Hemorrhage stacks; it has no fixed health threshold, and resets with a mana refund when the target dies within 0.15 seconds after the hit. That reset is how one enemy mistake turns into a chain of kills.

In lane he is dominant. The outer edge of Decimate heals him based on how hurt he is, Apprehend drags escapees back in with built-in armor penetration, and Crippling Strike slows anyone trying to leave. Most melee laners cannot even last-hit without stepping into his range.

His weakness is just as simple: no dash, no jump, and no answer to a champion who refuses to fight him. Every Darius game comes down to whether his early dominance wins the game before the enemy team learns to stay away from him.
gamePlan.earlyGame: This is your strongest phase. Look for a trade whenever the enemy steps up for a last hit: pull with E or walk them down, hit the outer edge of Q for the heal, and let the bleed stack while W keeps them in range. Once the bleed is high, Noxian Guillotine's stack-scaled true damage kills from health totals that surprise people, but there is no automatic execute threshold. If they hug their tower, freeze the wave just outside yours and starve them, since they cannot walk up to a frozen wave without dying. Just watch the enemy jungler: everyone knows where you are, and you cannot run.
gamePlan.midGame: Turn lane dominance into map dominance before enemy scaling erodes it. Shove and force Rift Herald fights, where your pull and a lethal Noxian Guillotine turn a messy skirmish into a reset chain. With your first items you are sticky enough to actually catch people, so look for picks on anyone crossing river without vision. Your power compared to theirs peaks here, so play with urgency; the advantage shrinks every minute you spend passive.
gamePlan.lateGame: You will not outrun anyone, so stop trying. Play around your team's engage and arrive second: once the enemy spends their cooldowns on your frontline, walk in, pull the most dangerous target you can reach, and start a Noxian Guillotine reset chain when its true damage is lethal. Your E is also great peel, pulling a diver off your carry and into your whole team. Stay relevant by finishing low-health targets, not by chasing enemies you will never catch.
gamePlan.teamfights: You are a zone, not an assassin. Stand between their divers and your carries, or follow your engage into the middle of their team. Pull the highest-value target in reach, slow them with W, and swing Q at max range so the heal keeps you standing. Watch health bars and Hemorrhage stacks together: cast Noxian Guillotine only when its current true damage is lethal or when allied damage will kill the target within the 0.15-second reset window.

startingItem.name: Long Sword
startingItem.note: Simple early attack damage for his first clear and the river fights that follow it.

boots.name: Chainlaced Crushers
boots.note: Magic resistance and tenacity help Darius keep moving through the control used to stop his approach. Swap to Armored Advance against physical-heavy teams.

coreItems.name: Trinity Force
coreItems.note: Crippling Strike is an empowered attack that delivers Spellblade, while the movement speed helps Darius stay close enough to preserve Hemorrhage stacks.

coreItems.name: Dead Man's Plate
coreItems.note: Momentum builds while Darius moves between camps and lanes. The speed improves his approach, and the empowered hit helps begin a gank without spending Apprehend too early.

coreItems.name: Sterak's Gage
coreItems.note: The Lifeline shield buys time after Darius enters the fight, which is usually when he is close to five Hemorrhage stacks and one Noxian Guillotine reset.

coreItems.name: Amaranth's Twinguard
coreItems.note: Mixed defenses suit the long teamfights Darius needs. It has time to activate while he stacks Hemorrhage in the middle of the enemy team.

coreItems.name: Guardian Angel
coreItems.note: A late revive gives Darius another chance to reach a target and start a reset chain. It does not preserve Hemorrhage stacks or guarantee an ultimate reset.

situationalItems.name: Galeforce
situationalItems.note: Rush this instead of Trinity Force when stronger gank access matters more than normal bruiser scaling. Use Gale Volley's dash to enter Apprehend range, then grab the target after they commit to escaping. Galeforce and Stridebreaker are alternative active items, so choose one rather than planning to equip both.

situationalItems.name: Stridebreaker
situationalItems.desc: Juggernaut bruiser item with a dash
situationalItems.note: Build this when ranged champions keep escaping before Apprehend can reach. Its dash and slow give Darius a direct way to start the fight.

situationalItems.name: Armored Advance
situationalItems.note: A boot swap against heavy physical damage. The armor and defensive effect protect Darius while he walks through basic attacks to reach the backline.

situationalItems.name: Mortal Reminder
situationalItems.note: Build this against armor stacking or strong healing. Darius still deals substantial physical damage before Noxian Guillotine becomes lethal.

situationalItems.name: Spear of Shojin
situationalItems.note: Ability haste brings back Decimate and Apprehend sooner, giving Darius more healing, control, and chances to maintain his bleed stacks.

situationalItems.name: Force of Nature
situationalItems.note: Build this against repeated magic damage and slows. The defenses and movement speed help him survive the approach against AP-heavy teams.

situationalItems.name: Thornmail
situationalItems.note: Build this when physical attackers also have heavy healing. It adds armor and applies Grievous Wounds while Darius holds them in an extended fight.

keystoneRune.name: Conqueror
keystoneRune.desc: Gain stacks by damaging enemy champions. At maximum stacks, gain bonus damage and healing.
keystoneRune.note: Darius stacks it during the same extended fights that build Hemorrhage, adding damage and sustain before the ultimate finisher.

primaryRunes.name: Triumph
primaryRunes.desc: Champion takedowns restore missing health, max mana or energy, and grant movement speed.
primaryRunes.note: The heal after a takedown helps Darius survive long enough to use a Noxian Guillotine reset on the next target.

primaryRunes.name: Last Stand
primaryRunes.desc: Deal more damage to champions while you are low on health.
primaryRunes.note: Darius often reaches five bleed stacks while low on health, so the extra damage is active during the most important part of the fight.

primaryRunes.name: Legend: Alacrity
primaryRunes.desc: Gain permanent attack speed by taking down champions, monsters, and minions.
primaryRunes.note: Attack speed helps Darius weave basic attacks between abilities and reach five Hemorrhage stacks before the target escapes.

secondaryRunes.name: Nimbus Cloak
secondaryRunes.desc: After casting a summoner spell, gain movement speed and slow resistance.
secondaryRunes.note: Ghost or Smite triggers movement speed and slow resistance, helping Darius enter Apprehend range and stay attached after the pull.

spells.name: Smite
spells.note: Required for Jungling. Secures objectives and sustains through camp clears.

goodAgainst.note: Amumu has to enter Darius's preferred range to deal damage, and his early dueling is weaker before defensive items. Invade only with lane priority, space Decimate so the outer blade lands after Bandage Toss, and save Noxian Guillotine until Hemorrhage has raised its true damage.

Darius can pressure Fiddlesticks before Crowstorm controls objective entrances, and Apprehend interrupts Bountiful Harvest when Darius reaches him. Track vision before invading, pull him out of the drain, and keep Ghost for the chase after Terrify creates distance.

Shyvana wants uninterrupted farming and has no hard control to stop Darius in an early river fight. Contest her camps only when nearby lanes can move, hold Apprehend until she tries to leave, and convert the early advantage before Dragon Form and completed items improve her teamfighting.

weakAgainst.note: Lillia builds movement speed while clearing and can keep Darius outside Apprehend range with repeated Blooming Blows. Do not chase her through open jungle; force fights in a pit or narrow entrance, use Ghost after she commits close, and keep Smite available for the slow when she tries to create space.

Kindred attacks from outside Darius's range, hops away from Apprehend, and can use Lamb's Respite to deny a lethal Noxian Guillotine. Contest marks with lane priority instead of arriving alone, hold the ultimate until the zone ends, and use Apprehend after Dance of Arrows rather than before it.

Nidalee clears quickly, crosses walls, and weakens Darius with Javelin Toss before he can begin an extended fight. Ward her approach, avoid entering objectives at low health, and fight around closed terrain where Ghost and Apprehend can punish her after Pounce is spent.

gamePlan.overview:
Darius is an early brawling jungler who turns prolonged contact into a lethal advantage. Attacks and damaging abilities apply Hemorrhage, and reaching five stacks grants Noxian Might. Decimate supplies area damage for camps, Crippling Strike resets his attack and slows a target, and Apprehend pulls enemies back when they try to leave. Noxian Guillotine deals true damage that increases with Hemorrhage stacks and can reset when its target dies at the right moment.

Jungle removes the oppressive lane phase that normally defines Darius, but it gives him access to more fights and better approach angles. He clears toward lanes with reliable setup, contests melee junglers in the river, and uses Ghost to stay close long enough to build five stacks. His ganks are strongest when an ally has already forced the target to spend a dash or walk away from safety.

The weakness is still mobility. Darius has no natural dash, and walking directly into a lane rarely works against targets with vision and an escape ready. If the early map stays quiet, faster farming junglers reach their item spikes while ranged carries gain enough damage and movement to keep him outside Apprehend range.
gamePlan.earlyGame:
Start with Decimate and position the outer blade through as much of each camp as possible. Weave attacks and Crippling Strike between casts instead of cancelling them by moving too early. Clear toward the lane with the best crowd control or the enemy most likely to push, because Darius needs help creating the first contact.

At scuttle, fight melee junglers when your nearby lanes can move first. Begin with attacks and Crippling Strike, then hold Apprehend for their retreat rather than opening with the only tool that brings them back. Against a ranged jungler, do not cross the river without priority just because Darius wins a close fight. If no gank or invade is clearly available, finish the clear and protect your tempo.
gamePlan.midGame:
Play around Dragon and Rift Herald before enemy carries become difficult to reach. Darius is strongest when the opposing jungler has to enter a fixed area, since the pit removes much of the space normally used to kite him. Establish vision first, stand between the enemy and the objective, and save Smite for the secure rather than spending it only to trigger Nimbus Cloak.

Between objectives, approach lanes through fog and let an ally start when possible. Once a target spends its escape, use Ghost, apply Crippling Strike, and hold Apprehend until the pull prevents the final step back to safety. Convert kills into camps, towers, or neutral objectives instead of chasing a second target across the map.
gamePlan.lateGame:
Darius cannot start every late fight by walking through five enemies. Stay near the teammate who can engage, then enter after important control and movement spells have been used. Hit the nearest safe target until Noxian Might is active, then pressure the backline with full Hemorrhage stacks and look for a lethal Noxian Guillotine.

Around Baron and Elder, control entrances rather than disappearing into a side lane. Apprehend can pull an enemy away from the pit edge, but Darius still relies on Smite to secure the objective. If the enemy composition can kite him indefinitely, protect your carry with Apprehend and punish the diver who has already entered your range.
gamePlan.teamfights:
Use Ghost before Hemorrhage stacks begin falling off, not after the target has already escaped. Start on the closest champion you can hit safely, land the outer edge of Decimate for damage and healing, and use Crippling Strike between attacks. Apprehend should stop an escape, interrupt a channel, or peel a diver rather than add damage to a target already trapped beside you.

Track health and Hemorrhage together. Noxian Guillotine has no fixed execute marker, so cast it when its current stack-scaled true damage is lethal or allied damage will finish the target inside the reset window. One correct reset can decide the fight, while an early ultimate leaves Darius with no reliable way to finish the next target.

startingItem.name: Amplifying Tome

boots.name: Spellslinger's Shoes

coreItems.name: Dusk and Dawn
coreItems.note: Q or W opens Diana's passive attack-speed window and primes Spellblade for the next attack. Time it for her third Moonsilver Blade hit and the extra on-hit repeats the cleave's magic damage, giving her short all-in a much sharper finish.

coreItems.name: Rabadon's Deathcap
coreItems.note: Multiplies her ability power. All her damage lands in one all-in, so all of it goes up at once.

coreItems.name: Zhonya's Hourglass
coreItems.note: Her ultimate pulls their team on top of her, and stasis turns that into a setup instead of a death. Buy Seeker's Armguard early for the armor and ability power.

coreItems.name: Void Staff
coreItems.note: Cuts the magic resist that turns her all-in into a chunk instead of a kill. Choose it over Cryptbloom when enemies are stacking magic resist and maximum personal damage matters more than ability haste and team healing.

coreItems.name: Infinity Orb
coreItems.note: Crits against low health targets, which finishes what her cooldowns cannot.

situationalItems.name: Oceanid's Trident
situationalItems.note: Build this when shields absorb Diana's gank damage. Crescent Strike applies the reduction before Lunar Rush and Moonfall commit her to the target.

situationalItems.name: Morellonomicon
situationalItems.note: Build this against a drain laner who heals back everything her all-in takes off. Buy Oblivion Orb early, since the anti-heal works from the component.

situationalItems.name: Banshee's Veil

gamePlan.overview:
Diana is an assassin whose engage does not depend on landing a skillshot. She leaps a huge distance onto whoever she marked, pulls nearby enemies together with Moonfall, and deletes the softest target while her shield soaks the damage coming back. There is nothing to dodge on her engage: she farms quietly, hits her level, then all-ins all at once.

In mid she is a melee burst skirmisher who plays for the all-in, not the lane. Early you last-hit, shield through poke, and stack your passive on minions so the third hit cleaves for bonus damage. Once your ultimate is online the lane flips: shove, leap, pull, and the immobile mage who was poking you gets locked down and killed. That same package makes her one of the better roamers in Wild Rift, because a gap-close that pulls does not need the enemy to misplay, only to be standing somewhere you can reach.

The cost is range and timing. Before her ultimate she is a short-range farmer that lane bullies push around, and once she leaps she is fully committed. Whiff the dive, waste the shield on chip, or jump into a Galio who was waiting, and the strongest all-in in the lane becomes a melee champion stuck in the open with her best button on cooldown.
gamePlan.earlyGame: The first levels are about reaching your spike without giving anything up. Stack Moonsilver Blade so every third attack cleaves, use Crescent Strike as your ranged farming and poke tool, and time Pale Cascade to absorb trades. Diana does have ranged pressure before Moonfall; what she lacks is the ultimate's area slow, pull, and fresh Moonlight application that make a committed all-in much harder to escape.
gamePlan.midGame: Your ultimate coming online changes everything. A loaded leap plus the pull kills any squishy who lets you reach combo range, and most immobile mids cannot stop you reaching it. Shove the wave with your passive cleave, then leave with the dive ready and go hunt, because Diana roams as hard as she lanes and the pull works just as well on a sidelaner as it does in lane. Mid priority lets you collapse on scuttle fights, where leaping into a clustered jungle duo and pulling them together flips the contest, and it lets you zone the enemy off dragon and herald, since anyone who steps wide gets picked. Every roam can strand you if you misjudge it, so push out with an escape path in mind.
gamePlan.lateGame: By now the full combo removes a carry, so late game is patient work: get the leap onto the right target without dying while you look for the angle. Keep your ultimate ready and your shield saved for the moment you commit, and watch the edges of the map for the flank or the flash-pull that catches their back line out of position. The danger never changes: you are a short-range diver in fights full of lockdown, so timing your entry and exit is everything. Commit only to targets you know will die, land Crescent Strike on the next body so the Moonlight refunds your leap and chains you into them, and never open a fight by leaping into their whole front line because the pull looked tempting. A Diana who survives and picks her dives wins fights; a dead one wastes her team's best engage.
gamePlan.teamfights: Diana does not chip a teamfight; she either starts it with a dive or pulls the enemy into one spot and bursts the middle. The best case is landing among their carries and dragging two or three of them together with Moonfall, which is both your damage setup and lockdown your team follows up on. If the clean multi-pull is not there, save the engage for their back line, since leaping onto a Moonlight-marked target refunds the dash almost instantly and turns a good fight into a chain of kills rather than one trade. Your shield is what keeps you alive through the first wave of peel, so time it with the leap, not before. Find the carry, jump, pull, and keep Crescent Strike landing so the refunded dash decides how many targets you reach.
