gamePlan.overview:
Diana in the jungle is a diving AP fighter who clears safely and finishes fights like an assassin. Everything runs through Crescent Strike: the arc marks targets with Moonlight, and Lunar Rush resets onto anyone carrying that mark. Pale Cascade is the engine underneath, an orbiting shield that explodes for area damage and refreshes when every blade hits. Moonfall is what makes her a real jungler: a vortex that pulls a whole group into one spot so the rest of her kit lands on all of it.

Her plan is to reach her item spike intact, then turn every skirmish into one combo that erases the squishiest target in it. She is not a level-three predator. She farms clean camps, takes the fights her shields win, and comes online hard once Moonfall and her first item exist together. From there a gank is Q to mark, R to pull them off their escape, dash through, and detonate the shield. She can power-farm to a spike or punish a sloppy lane, and in teamfights she folds a backline together and deletes the middle of it.

The catch is that Crescent Strike sets up her reliable Lunar Rush reset. Miss the arc and the gank loses most of its reach. Once the dash is spent, crowd control can hold her inside the enemy team before her next shield matters. She has no independent escape, so tracked approaches and warded entrances make her commitments much easier to punish.
gamePlan.earlyGame:
Your first clear looks slow because you are melee, but the Pale Cascade detonations and the refreshing shield carry you through it. Open where the shield ring can chunk a camp, weave Crescent Strike to keep your dash reset available, and finish the rotation into scuttle, which puts Moonfall in your hands at level five. That is the point your ganks become real, so use the camp respawn timer to find a lane where an enemy has stepped too far: mark from a brush, pull them off their escape, and detonate the shield before they react. Clear again when the camps are back and go looking for the next one.

Your early duel is fine, not free: you beat the slow farmers over the crab and lose to junglers who out-damage you before your stacks matter, so read the matchup before you walk in. Remember you have no exit button. Ward behind you, keep the dash to dodge a key spell instead of engaging with it, and never get caught mid-clear by a jungler who can lock you down.
gamePlan.midGame:
Moonfall and your first completed item make clustered river fights your preferred battleground. Take that fight when your team is winning skirmishes. When it is even, Herald is the safer trade because it becomes a tower without needing a won teamfight, and you should only prioritise dragon when your team is built to fight for soul.

Between objectives, power-farm the camps and gank while they respawn, since every camp brings the next spike closer. Invade the slow scaling junglers, steal what they cannot defend, and punish anyone who face-checks river without vision, because a marked target in the fog is a free dash and a dead body.
gamePlan.lateGame: Late game you are a diver, not a frontliner, and scaled carries beat you in a clean extended duel. Look for a flank through fog and reach the backline after the enemy peel has committed elsewhere. Hold Moonfall for a valuable cluster rather than a single runner, and keep Pale Cascade and Lunar Rush ready for the entry. Track the control spells that can stop your dash, then enter after one is spent or when your team can follow immediately. At Baron and Elder, threaten the contest from an unseen angle instead of standing with the frontline and revealing the approach.
gamePlan.teamfights: Your teamfight is one decisive jump, so make it the right one. Wait for the enemy to clump, flank through fog, then Moonfall the cluster to drag their backline into one spot and detonate your whole combo on all of it at once. Reaching their carry is the dream, but the vortex is worth more when it catches two or three people, so pick the angle that folds the most of them together over the one that reaches a single target. Time it with your team, since a pull is far better when someone follows the lockdown, and a solo dive into set peel just trades you away for nothing. Save your dash and shield for the entrance, not for poke, because once you commit there is no exit and the fight comes down to whether the all-in lands before their crowd control answers. If the clump never forms, wait at the edge and threaten the jump, since a Diana in the fog changes how five people stand.

gamePlan.overview:
Ekko is a jungler built around short burst trades and Chronobreak's return point. The third passive hit deals bonus damage and grants movement speed, while Timewinder slows on the outward pass and damages again on its return. Parallel Convergence rewards predicting where a fight will move, and Chronobreak returns Ekko to his earlier position while healing him and damaging enemies near the arrival point. Those tools let him commit deeply when the return position remains safe.

Ekko is vulnerable to stronger early duelists and becomes more reliable after completing items and unlocking Chronobreak at level five. His early clear leans on abilities and can drain mana quickly, so choose river contests according to lane priority. After the first spike, use Timewinder's slow and a prepared Parallel Convergence to improve gank setup, while Chronobreak lets him commit deeper when the return point is safe.

His weakness is simple: take the slipperiness away and he is a soft AP carry with no resists. Hard crowd control that lands before he can W or rewind ends him, and early junglers who invade him kill the version that has not come online yet. Win the mid game and he is very hard to kill. Fall behind it and the rewind only delays death.
gamePlan.earlyGame:
Your first clear is functional, not fast, so route for a full clear instead of a race: lead with Q to soften camps, weave the passive third hit, and use W on the bigger camps. Take scuttle after it, since that is what brings your ultimate online, and an aggressive dive stops being a gamble the moment you have the rewind behind you. Use the camp respawn timer to hunt: land the W stun from fog, drop the Q slow, and commit knowing you have a way out. Clear again when the camps are back, then look for the next lane.

You reach scuttle with real dueling tools, since your Q slow and a landed W stun win most early contests, so take the crab your pathing favors and do not be shy about it. Watch your own jungle in this phase, because early junglers want to catch you mid-clear with no escape ready.
gamePlan.midGame:
Parallel Convergence makes pit walls and narrow entrances unusually valuable. A clean W stun on the enemy jungler at the dragon pit or against the Herald wall flips the contest before it starts, and your burst plus Smite wins most coin-flip steals, so contest whenever your team is ahead on early fights. In an even game take Herald and let dragon go, unless your team wants the soul and can hold the fights that come with it.

Between objectives, keep hunting rather than farming: gank while your camps respawn, then slip into their jungle behind that pressure, steal what you can, and rewind out before the collapse arrives. Every snowballed lane is another lane that lets you keep hunting.
gamePlan.lateGame: Late game Ekko is the one assassin who can survive a failed dive each fight. You are the pick threat their backline checks the map for, the flank that arrives from a wall nobody warded, the diver who kills a carry and rewinds home before the peel matters. Baron and Elder Dragon fights come down to starting with a stunned target or punishing anyone who strays from their group, so hold the flanks and let your W set up the pick. Keep the ultimate as your real escape, not your opener: rewinding out of a lost dive is what keeps you in the game late, and dying wastes the best reset in the match. Do not commit on the first body you see; the fight is yours when the carry becomes reachable.
gamePlan.teamfights: Your job in a teamfight is to remove their most important player and survive doing it. Wait for the engage to commit, then flank in, land your passive and W stun on the carry, dump your combo, and rewind out of the collapse while restoring part of the health lost recently. The rewind is what makes the dive sane, so do not spend it as an entry tool: it is the part that turns a suicide run into a clean trade. If their frontline stands between you and the target, do not wade in, because you die fast to focus fire and the reset cannot save you from a stun chain. Reposition, wait for the angle, and use your slow and stun to peel for your own carry in the meantime. One clean pick and a healthy rewind usually decides the rest.

Shove with Timewinder, bait the cage before committing, then place Parallel Convergence behind Veigar and preserve Chronobreak in case Primordial Burst turns the dive back on you.

Once Light Binding misses, Lux has no hard crowd control, but Lucent Singularity still slows and detonates automatically on Ekko's entry while Prismatic Barrier can shield twice. Approach outside E's area and use Chronobreak for the committed burst or reposition, not as proof that every dive is free.
Syndra punishes targets who stand still, which your kit never has to do: your dash dodges the scatter stun, and once it is spent she cannot escape your all-in.

Phase Dive crosses Singularity before its pull matures, and Chronobreak restores the health lost while Aurelion Sol channels Breath of Light. Pressure his Stardust stacking before the beam gains range, place Parallel Convergence behind his retreat, and save the final dash until Astral Flight is committed so he cannot simply leave the all-in.

Chronobreak can heal damage Zed dealt during the preceding few seconds and move Ekko back to his afterimage, but it does not cleanse Death Mark. Time it after absorbing meaningful burst, and do not assume rewinding before the mark detonates removes it.

weakAgainst.note: Galio shrugs off your magic burst with his passive and shield, and his taunt can be charged around your landing point and holds you through the combo, so you can neither kill him nor all-in through the crowd control.
Time favors him, not you: he suffers early, but once his ultimate is stacked he blinks around every commit you make and out-scales the tempo game you depend on.
The mirror dive favors her: Diana's pull plus shield out-trades your burst in a straight all-in, and her pull catches you the instant you dash in.
Irelia chains dashes off your minions and runs you down the moment your blink is spent, and the extended brawl is hers whenever she wants it.

Every dash you take marks you with Gloom, and the ability she lands cashes it in for bonus damage and a faster Doom, so the fear that interrupts your combo keeps coming back sooner than it should. The mobility that beats most mids works against you here.

gamePlan.overview:
Ekko is a mid laner built around his rewind. He chunks waves and champions with Timewinder, slows targets when it expands, and can shield himself and stun enemies inside Parallel Convergence when he enters its delayed zone. Chronobreak returns him to the afterimage marking where he was four seconds earlier, damages nearby enemies, and heals him with an amount that increases according to health recently lost. It can rescue a committed dive, but it is not a guaranteed full-health reset.

His game runs on tempo and roams. Ekko shoves fast with his Q, and between his dash and his ultimate he is rarely in lane when you check the map. He wants priority, river control, and squishy enemies who cannot punish the windows where his blink is down. He is not a poke-and-scale mage and not a pure one-shot assassin: he is a skirmisher who burst-trades, snowballs side lanes, and turns picks into objectives.

His weakness is the gap before his items arrive. Early Ekko is a melee-range caster with a thin health bar, and once his key cooldowns are spent he has no escape. Lane bullies punish him before his first item, hard crowd control punishes his entry and landing, while displacement or a Knockdown effect interrupts the dash itself, and scalers who survive his window outgrow him. Get him through that early stretch and he becomes the most slippery threat on the map.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Laning is about surviving to your spikes without giving up kills. Use Timewinder to last-hit and chip from a step back, since the return trip does more damage, and hold Parallel Convergence instead of throwing it as poke. Your real trade comes at level three: let Timewinder's expanding field slow the target, use Phase Dive to add another passive stack, and position so the faster returning grenade hits them a second time before you back away.
gamePlan.midGame: Once your first item lands and your ultimate is up, Ekko stops laning and starts pressuring the whole map. Shove the wave with a Q or two, then leave: a dash onto a mid who walked too far up, a flank on a side lane, a free scuttle for your jungler. Your stun field plus Chronobreak means you can commit to a river skirmish and rewind out if it goes wrong, which is exactly the pressure that takes an early dragon or herald. This is your strongest window, so use it hard, because scalers take over if you wait.
gamePlan.lateGame: Late game you have two jobs and you swap between them by reading the map. When your team groups, you flank; when they do not, you push a side lane and threaten to one-shot anyone who rotates alone, with Chronobreak as insurance against the collapse. Your damage stays scary into squishies, but the blink is the resource that keeps you alive, so never spend it on the escape until you have secured the kill you saved it for. Teams beat you by never giving you an isolated target, so create the isolation yourself with vision and patience.
gamePlan.teamfights: Your job is the back line, not the brawl. Wait for the enemy stuns to land on your frontline, then enter from the side: place Parallel Convergence ahead of their carry and step into the zone to trigger its shield and stun, hit Timewinder, dash through for the burst, and keep Chronobreak as the exit. If the first dive trades badly, the ultimate can return you to your afterimage and restore health based on recent damage, but it will not automatically refill your health bar. Open the fight yourself and you may die before the rewind matters. Arrive a moment late, on the target their team forgot to peel, and you decide the fight.

startingItem.name: Long Sword
startingItem.note: Simple early attack damage. His Q applies on-hit effects at full value, so it carries into his main trade.

boots.name: Immortal Treads
boots.note: The omnivamp keeps him healthy while poking from the front of his range, which is where he has to stand.

coreItems.name: Manamune
coreItems.note: Turns his mana pool into attack damage, and the refund lets him keep casting without running dry.

coreItems.name: Trinity Force
coreItems.note: Spellblade triggers on the attack after every Q, and the move speed helps a champion with one blink hold his spacing.

coreItems.name: Serylda's Grudge
coreItems.note: All four of his abilities are damaging actives, so every one of them applies the slow. He also wants the ability haste more than most marksmen.

coreItems.name: Spear of Shojin
coreItems.note: Ability haste is the stat his kit uses best, since more Q casts also reduce the cooldowns on everything else.

coreItems.name: Guardian Angel
coreItems.note: Revives him once after dying. His blink is usually spent repositioning, so this covers the fight he could not leave.

situationalItems.name: Blade of the Ruined King
situationalItems.note: Percent current health damage and omnivamp, for the games where he has to fight up close instead of poking.

situationalItems.name: Maw of Malmortius
situationalItems.note: Build this against heavy magic burst, which punishes a marksman standing as far forward as his poke needs.

situationalItems.name: Serpent's Fang
situationalItems.note: Build this when the enemy has shields that keep erasing the poke he has landed.

situationalItems.name: Iceborn Gauntlet
situationalItems.note: Its Spellblade leaves an icy zone on the attack after a Q, which adds area control and gives him armor he otherwise lacks.

situationalItems.name: Mercurial Scimitar
situationalItems.note: Build this when one stun catches him with his blink down, which is the only moment he has no answer.

keystoneRune.name: Conqueror
keystoneRune.desc: Gain stacks by damaging enemy champions. At maximum stacks, gain bonus damage and healing.
keystoneRune.note: His damage is a steady stream of casts and attacks, so he reaches max stacks and the healing pays for standing forward.

primaryRunes.name: Brutal
primaryRunes.desc: Attacks deal bonus adaptive damage to enemy champions.
primaryRunes.note: Bonus damage on attacks props up his weak laning before his first item.

primaryRunes.name: Cut Down
primaryRunes.desc: You deal bonus adaptive damage (except true damage) to enemy champions above 60% health.
primaryRunes.note: His poke is repeatable but low per hit, and this is what makes it register on health stackers.

primaryRunes.name: Legend: Bloodline
primaryRunes.desc: Gain permanent omnivamp by taking down champions, monsters, and minions.
primaryRunes.note: Sustain suits a marksman who wins by outlasting a poke war rather than winning one all-in.

secondaryRunes.name: Bone Plating
secondaryRunes.desc: After taking damage from a champion, the next 3 instances of champion damage are reduced.
secondaryRunes.note: His blink is his only escape, and this keeps him alive through the burst thrown the moment it is down.

spells.name: Flash
spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

goodAgainst.note: Draven has to juggle axes inside your Mystic Shot range, so every catch he reaches for is a free poke for you, and Arcane Shift escapes the all-in he needs. His window closes while yours opens.

Caitlyn can hide behind the minion wave because Mystic Shot stops on the first enemy hit, so use gaps in the wave rather than firing through it. Arcane Shift can avoid her net and reposition around traps, but spending it aggressively leaves you exposed to her range and follow-up.
Samira has to reach melee range to do anything, and your whole kit keeps her out of it: poke stops her style stacks, and Arcane Shift escapes the dash her snowball needs.

weakAgainst.note: Kalista's mobility matches your blink, and her early damage out-paces your poke before you have items, so the early 2v2 is hers. You out-range her once items land.
Tristana jumps straight onto you and baits out your one blink before committing. Her point-blank burst beats your poke, and a reset kill snowballs the lane.

Corki's full rotation lands more damage in one window than your Mystic Shot rhythm can answer, and trading with him drains your mana faster than his. Your blink answers his dive but not the burst that opens it.

gamePlan.overview:
Ezreal is a spell-focused carry whose damage and safety depend on landing Mystic Shot. Each hit lowers his other cooldowns and builds Rising Spell Force, while Arcane Shift lets him reposition across short walls or away from an engage. The blink makes him difficult to catch, but spending it aggressively removes that safety.

His lane is hit-and-run. He pokes from outside trade range, farms with spells when walking up is unsafe, and answers every gank and dive with Arcane Shift. The trade-off is a kit with no crowd control, weak wave-clear, and heavy mana costs.

His default plan is to farm through pressure, build an item advantage through safe uptime, and reach objective fights with enough space to land repeated shots. He still needs to adapt his positioning to the enemy engage instead of relying on Arcane Shift to correct every mistake.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Poke through gaps in the wave and keep farming through pressure. Mystic Shot stops on the first enemy hit, so clear or angle around minions before aiming at a champion. Each hit reduces the cooldowns of Ezreal's other abilities and grants a stack of Rising Spell Force for attack speed; it does not make the next Mystic Shot itself travel faster. Do not contest hard shoves your wave-clear cannot answer; take the safe farm and poke out the difference. Your blink is for safety, not engage, and most Ezreal deaths start with an aggressive Arcane Shift.
gamePlan.midGame: Crash the Dragon-lane wave before rotating, then arrive early enough to aim Mystic Shot through open river angles rather than into a full minion wave. Use Trueshot Barrage on a grouped approach or across a narrow objective entrance when it will soften several targets, but do not delay your rotation just to search for a cross-map cast. During skirmishes, weave basic attacks when the nearest target is safe to hit so Rising Spell Force produces real damage instead of treating every fight as poke only.
gamePlan.lateGame: Stay behind the teammate who can absorb the first engage and damage the closest safe target. Hold Arcane Shift until an enemy commits a gap closer or control spell, then blink to a position that still gives you a clear Mystic Shot line. Use Trueshot Barrage on grouped enemies, a narrow retreat, or a distant wave only when the next objective does not require your immediate presence. Preserve health before Baron and Elder, because Ezreal is strongest when he can keep firing through the full setup and fight.
gamePlan.teamfights: Begin at Mystic Shot range and attack the closest target you can reach without crossing the enemy frontline. Weave basic attacks between hits when it is safe, and use Arcane Shift only after a threat commits or to cross terrain into a clearly protected position. Trueshot Barrage is strongest through a clump or choke, but it does not need to open every fight. If the enemy has several divers, position near allied peel so the blink creates distance instead of leaving you isolated.

startingItem.name: Long Sword
startingItem.note: Simple early attack damage, which makes each caught axe hit harder.

boots.name: Immortal Treads
boots.note: The omnivamp keeps him healthy while holding the forward position catching axes requires.

coreItems.name: Bloodthirster
coreItems.note: Physical vamp that increases on critical strikes helps him recover while following axe landing spots through a fight.

coreItems.name: Magnetic Blaster
coreItems.note: The extra range helps Draven reach the next Spinning Axe catch without giving up an attack, while movement speed preserves the path between successive landing markers.

coreItems.name: Lord Dominik's Regard
coreItems.note: Build this against armor stackers, so his axes still hurt the frontline. Choose it over Mortal Reminder when enemies are stacking health rather than healing, since Giant Slayer increases Draven's damage against high-health targets.

coreItems.name: Infinity Edge
coreItems.note: His damage comes in a few very large hits, which is what a crit spike multiplies best.

coreItems.name: Guardian Angel
coreItems.note: Revives him once after dying. He has no escape at all, so this is what lets him keep holding a forward position.

situationalItems.name: Mortal Reminder
situationalItems.note: Build this against armor stackers or enemies who heal through his axe damage. Choose it over Lord Dominik's Regard when enemy healing is the bigger problem, since Grievous Wounds stops targets from recovering Draven's damage.

situationalItems.name: Essence Reaver
situationalItems.note: Ability haste improves Blood Rush and Stand Aside uptime. Casting an ability readies Spellblade for the next attack; catching an axe is not itself an attack and does not cash in the proc.

situationalItems.name: The Collector
situationalItems.note: Executes low health targets. His axes chunk in single large hits, so this converts those into kills and Adoration gold.

situationalItems.name: Armorcrusher Boots
situationalItems.note: Boot swap when the enemy stacks early armor and his axes stop chunking.

situationalItems.name: Mercurial Scimitar
situationalItems.note: Build this when one stun prevents him from following the landing marker. Draven can and should move while juggling; the next axe's landing location is determined by his movement when the current attack hits.

keystoneRune.name: Conqueror
keystoneRune.desc: Gain stacks by damaging enemy champions. At maximum stacks, gain bonus damage and healing.
keystoneRune.note: His trades are a steady stream of large attacks, so he stacks quickly and the healing pays for standing forward.

primaryRunes.name: Brutal
primaryRunes.desc: Attacks deal bonus adaptive damage to enemy champions.
primaryRunes.note: He wins lane on raw early damage, which is exactly what this adds.

primaryRunes.name: Cut Down
primaryRunes.desc: You deal bonus adaptive damage (except true damage) to enemy champions above 60% health.
primaryRunes.note: His axes hit hard but not for percent health, and this is what makes them cut through a frontline.

primaryRunes.name: Legend: Alacrity
primaryRunes.desc: Gain permanent attack speed by taking down champions, monsters, and minions.
primaryRunes.note: Attack speed lets Draven throw empowered attacks more often, but each axe still takes two seconds to land. The benefit is more attack throughput, not a faster individual return arc.

secondaryRunes.name: Bone Plating
secondaryRunes.desc: After taking damage from a champion, the next 3 instances of champion damage are reduced.
secondaryRunes.note: Axe landing markers are predictable and can pull Draven toward dangerous ground, so Bone Plating covers the engage aimed at the catch without implying he must stand still.

spells.name: Flash
spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

goodAgainst.note: Sivir's spell shield blocks one spell, and your damage is mostly axes. She plays for farm while you play for kills, and kills win this lane.

Twitch gives up lane pressure while Ambush is unavailable and needs several Deadly Venom stacks before Contaminate becomes a meaningful trade, while Draven's first Spinning Axe already hits at full strength. Push him off the early wave, use Stand Aside when he reveals to attack, and cash the lead before Spray and Pray turns later grouped fights into his preferred range.
Kalista's hops look flashy, but her early damage loses the direct exchange with your axes. Only her Fate's Call all-in is a real threat when your axes are down.

weakAgainst.note: Miss Fortune punishes the rhythm your axes force on you: every catch you reach for eats a Double Up, her burst wins the windows where you cannot reposition, and her ultimate zones your all-in.
Ashe's constant slows punish the movement your axe-catching requires, and her arrow punishes the all-in that solves most lanes. Your damage still leads if you keep catching cleanly.
Caitlyn out-ranges your axes by a wide margin and zones the catch spots your juggling depends on. You cannot collect axes under her poke, and her traps punish the all-in.

gamePlan.overview:
Draven is the highest-risk, highest-reward carry in the game. His spinning axes hit like a champion two items ahead, but every throw must be caught where it lands, so he manages catch positions through every trade. Played clean, no carry bullies a lane harder; played sloppy, he drops his axes and his damage with them.

His passive stacks adoration with every catch and cashes it in as bonus gold on kills, so a snowballing Draven earns extra gold doing it. The whole champion is a bet on early dominance: bully the lane, cash the stacks, and end the game before late-game carries get their items.

His weaknesses are built into the kit. The catch positions are predictable, he has no real escape, and a Draven who falls behind loses most of his threat.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Use the early damage advantage without making every axe a forced trade. Start Spinning Axe before the wave meets, pressure the carry when they walk up to farm, and move each catch marker toward a safe next position. If the marker lands inside the enemy support's engage range, let the axe drop. Stand Aside can interrupt a dash or create space for one more attack, so keep it available when the enemy still has an all-in. Adoration rewards a kill, but protecting the stacks is often worth more than chasing one through a bad wave.
gamePlan.midGame: Spend the lead on waves, structures, and objectives while your axes still dominate equal-item fights. At six minutes, crash Dragon lane before rotating and follow the objective your team can reach first. Herald is usually the stronger even trade because it converts directly into turret pressure. Dragon is the better commitment when your composition excels in grouped fights and can realistically continue toward soul, especially when Infernal is part of the payoff. Keep both axes active through the rotation, and use Stand Aside to stop the enemy's first approach rather than chasing a low target away from the pit.
gamePlan.lateGame: You still hit hard, but late fights punish predictable catch markers. Stand beside your peel, attack the closest safe target, and guide each marker sideways or backward so the next catch does not expose you. Use Whirling Death through a grouped formation or across an objective only when the return path is also useful, and watch the enemy jungler's secure rather than relying on a blind steal. A dropped axe costs damage; walking into crowd control to catch it costs the fight.
gamePlan.teamfights: Maintain two axes only while their landing spots remain safe. Attack the frontline from beside your support, step toward catch markers that preserve spacing, and let an axe expire when a diver controls the landing area. Save Stand Aside to interrupt a dash or push a threat off its line, then use Blood Rush after a catch to reposition. Whirling Death can soften a grouped team or finish retreating targets, but check both its outward and returning lines before casting.

startingItem.name: Ruby Crystal
startingItem.note: Early health, which is the only stat that matters to a champion who pays for all three of his basic abilities with his own health.

boots.name: Armored Advance
boots.note: Armor and health, which let him keep casting through a lane trying to punish the health he spends.

coreItems.name: Heartsteel
coreItems.note: Stacks permanent health from trades. Maximum health directly increases Mundo's passive regeneration and the size of percentage-health healing, while also giving him a larger pool for health-cost abilities; not every damage number in his kit scales from his own maximum health.

coreItems.name: Sunfire Aegis
coreItems.note: The burn scales with bonus health, so the stat he was buying anyway becomes constant area damage.

coreItems.name: Thornmail
coreItems.note: Build this against healing, which is what stops a sustain champion outlasting his ultimate. The Grievous Wounds applies from his own damage as well as when they attack him.

coreItems.name: Mantle of the Twelfth Hour
coreItems.note: The lifeline gives bonus maximum health when he drops low, expanding the pool his regeneration can refill. Maximum Dosage does not gain a special stronger coefficient merely because Mundo cast it at lower health.

coreItems.name: Amaranth's Twinguard
coreItems.note: Build this when you are fighting in the middle of the enemy team and need both armor and magic resist. Mundo's healing keeps him in combat long enough to activate Twinguard, whose mixed defenses make every restored health point harder to remove.

situationalItems.name: Randuin's Omen
situationalItems.note: Build this when the enemy team has multiple crit champions, since sustained damage is what beats his regeneration.

situationalItems.name: Chainlaced Crushers
situationalItems.note: Boot swap against heavy magic damage and crowd control, since magic burst outruns his healing.

situationalItems.name: Unending Despair
situationalItems.note: Damages nearby enemies and heals him for it. He is permanently standing in the middle of them, so it is always active.

situationalItems.name: Gargoyle Stoneplate
situationalItems.note: The shield scales with maximum health and grows for each nearby enemy champion, so it is far larger on him than on most champions.

keystoneRune.name: Grasp of the Undying
keystoneRune.desc: Every 4 seconds in combat, your next attack against a champion deals bonus damage and heals you.
keystoneRune.note: Permanent health growth, and his kit converts maximum health into damage and sustain.

primaryRunes.name: Unshakeable
primaryRunes.desc: Gain bonus armor and magic resist, increasing further when surrounded by enemies.
primaryRunes.note: He wins by standing in the middle of the fight and refusing to die, which is when this gives the most.

primaryRunes.name: Second Wind
primaryRunes.desc: After taking damage from a champion, regenerate health over time.
primaryRunes.note: His passive already runs on health, and this keeps the pool topped up between the trades he wants.

primaryRunes.name: Overgrowth
primaryRunes.desc: Gain permanent maximum health when nearby minions or monsters die.
primaryRunes.note: Everything he does runs on health, so a bigger pool is more damage, more healing, and more time.

secondaryRunes.name: Last Stand
secondaryRunes.desc: Deal more damage to champions while you are low on health.
secondaryRunes.note: He spends his own health to cast, so he is in this health range for most of every fight.

spells.name: Flash
spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

goodAgainst.note: Jax needs long duels and you are unkillable in them. His dodge stops autos, not cleavers, and his burst windows barely dent a health pool your size.
Both of you stack health, but yours regenerates, and his engage matters more than his lane, so the scaling contest quietly goes your way.
His combo stings but cannot keep pace with your sustain over a full lane, so his whole trading pattern loses to your regeneration.

Shen's Spirit's Refuge blocks Mundo's attacks, while Shadow Dash passes through and taunts rather than dragging its target. Mundo can ignore one immobilizing effect when his passive is ready, but the canister can be destroyed before he recovers it.
All his damage is front-loaded fury, and you are built to eat a burst and keep walking. He spikes first and falls off, while your sustain keeps growing.

weakAgainst.note: Percent-health true damage skips your armor and grows with the health you stack, which is the whole build. She kites your walk-up, shreds that health bar, and wins the late game your kit was aiming for.
Her whole kit deals percent-health damage, so stacking health only feeds her, and her mist blocks the cleavers that would otherwise chip her down.
Vitals scale off your max health, so everything you build feeds her damage, and her parry answers the one slow you can aim. No item count makes that duel winnable.
True damage on her Q, percent-health on her W, and a wall dash that ignores your spacing: her kit skips the armor and punishes the health your build is made of.

gamePlan.overview:
Dr. Mundo's whole design is a bet that he can stack more health than the enemy team can remove, then regenerate the difference. Infected Bonesaw costs health, deals damage based on its target, slows, and refunds part or all of its health cost when it hits. Goes Where He Pleases periodically ignores the next hostile immobilizing effect specifically; not every form of crowd control; then drops a recoverable canister at a health cost.

His lane starts slow because his abilities spend health before his regeneration and items are established. Maximum Dosage enhances him for ten seconds with increased base health, attack damage, movement speed, and health regeneration; it is sustained recovery, not an instant rewind of all damage taken in a fight.

His counters are famous: Grievous Wounds, percent-health damage, and kiting. Everything else only delays him.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Every cleaver spends health, so throw it when the hit secures a minion, meaningful poke, or the slow needed to leave a trade. Stand behind the wave against skillshots, use the health refund from a successful hit to manage costs, and collect the canister from Goes Where He Pleases only when the path is safe. Bait the opponent's first immobilizing spell into the passive before extending the trade. Mundo has no dash, so keep the wave close and stop pushing when the enemy jungler is missing.
gamePlan.midGame: Health items and Maximum Dosage let you take longer trades, but check for percent-health damage and Grievous Wounds before walking forward. Push the side lane with vision, then arrive early enough to stand between your team and the objective entrance. At six minutes, Herald is usually the stronger even conversion and Mundo can absorb the poke around its pit. Play for dragon when your composition wants repeated front-to-back fights toward soul. Cast Maximum Dosage after meaningful damage lands, not while the enemy can simply disengage and wait it out.
gamePlan.lateGame: Late game, stand where your team can use the space your health bar creates. Slow a reachable carry with Infected Bonesaw, but switch to the frontline if chasing would separate you from your damage dealers. Save Maximum Dosage for the enemy's committed burst and leave room to retreat while the healing catches up. Grievous Wounds, percent-health damage, and repeated control can still bring Mundo down, so track those threats instead of assuming durability replaces positioning.
gamePlan.teamfights: Front the fight and make the enemy spend time moving around you. Use Infected Bonesaw to slow whichever threat is reachable, activate Heart Zapper before the heaviest exchange, and recover its grey health with the recast while still near champions. Maximum Dosage belongs near the peak of incoming damage, but it is not a reason to walk beyond allied follow-up. If the enemy ignores you, peel back toward your carry or block the route to the objective instead of chasing harmlessly through their backline.

startingItem.name: Amplifying Tome
startingItem.note: Early ability power, since her clear and her first gank both come entirely from her abilities.

boots.name: Spellslinger's Shoes
boots.note: Magic penetration is what makes her opening burst kill instead of chunk.

coreItems.name: Lich Bane
coreItems.note: Spellblade triggers on the attack after her dash, which is the exact moment she comes out of stealth.

coreItems.name: Rabadon's Deathcap
coreItems.note: Multiplies her ability power. Her damage is one charmed rotation, so all of it goes up at once.

coreItems.name: Infinity Orb
coreItems.note: Crits against low health targets. Her ultimate already does more than double damage below that threshold, so the two stack.

coreItems.name: Void Staff
coreItems.note: Cuts magic resist. Her charm already shreds some, so this leaves the target with almost nothing. Choose it over Cryptbloom when enemies are stacking magic resist and maximum personal damage matters more than ability haste and team healing.

coreItems.name: Zhonya's Hourglass
coreItems.note: Build this for the moment after her ultimate blinks her out with cooldowns spent. Buy Seeker's Armguard early for the armor and ability power.

situationalItems.name: Oceanid's Trident
situationalItems.note: Build this when the enemy has shields that keep absorbing the burst she set up with a full charm.

situationalItems.name: Stormsurge
situationalItems.note: Her charmed rotation already does enough damage to trigger the mark, and the move speed carries her back into stealth.

situationalItems.name: Banshee's Veil
situationalItems.note: Build this when the enemy has crowd control ready for the instant she becomes visible, which is her only vulnerable moment.

situationalItems.name: Cryptbloom
situationalItems.note: The alternative to Void Staff. Less penetration, but the ability haste and healing on takedown help when she picks targets alongside her team. Choose it when enemies have not built much magic resist, so trading Void Staff's extra damage for more ability haste and an area heal after takedowns is worthwhile.

keystoneRune.name: First Strike
keystoneRune.desc: Deal bonus damage for the first 3 seconds of combat with champions and gain gold.
keystoneRune.note: She always opens the trade from stealth, so the condition is met on every engage.

primaryRunes.name: Sudden Impact
primaryRunes.desc: Deal bonus true damage after using mobility or exiting stealth.
primaryRunes.note: Her empowered dash sets up the bonus true damage right as she arrives.

primaryRunes.name: Hubris
primaryRunes.desc: Champion takedowns after damaging an enemy grant a temporary burst of adaptive force.
primaryRunes.note: Her picks convert into kills, and stacking power off takedowns builds the snowball her ambushes want.

primaryRunes.name: Eyeball Collector
primaryRunes.desc: Gain adaptive force by collecting takedown stacks from enemy champions and epic monsters.
primaryRunes.note: Takedowns are the point of her ganks, so the stacks build faster on her than on a farming jungler.

secondaryRunes.name: Transcendence
secondaryRunes.desc: Gain ability haste, then reduce a basic ability's cooldown after it hits at level 9.
secondaryRunes.note: Ability haste means more abilities and a faster charm cycle, so she finds more picks between objectives.

spells.name: Flash
spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

spells.name: Smite
spells.note: Required for Jungling. Secures objectives and sustains through camp clears.

goodAgainst.note: Graves cannot fight what he cannot see: your charm from camouflage takes away his dash, and your burst deletes him before his shotgun ever finds you.

Demon Shade camouflage lets Evelynn open with Allure before Talon can choose an Assassin's Path escape wall. The charm holds him through the first Noxian Diplomacy burst, and Last Caress finishes while avoiding Shadow Assault's return damage.
Nidalee wins open fights with poke and kiting, but none of that matters against a threat she cannot see. Her fragile frame dies to your burst once the charm lands from fog.

weakAgainst.note: Early on, Rengar plays your own game better: a camouflage hunter who jumps isolated targets and bursts you down before your charm matters. His ambush beats yours while you are both weak, though you outscale him.
Vi's lock-on ultimate punches through the stealth your escape depends on and pins your squishy frame for her team. Her charged knockup also interrupts your burst rotation.

Pantheon punishes your weak early game, invading before camouflage comes online and stunning you out of any play with his point-and-click combo. Aegis blocks your opening burst, and your fragile frame melts once you are visible.

gamePlan.overview:
Evelynn is the jungler whose ganks come with no warning. Once she hits level five and Demon Shade grants camouflage, she goes unseen at range, walks up to a lane, and opens with a charm that locks a target down completely. Her whole identity is the ambush: the lane that felt safe a second ago suddenly is not.

She wins through scaling. Her early clear is average and her early dueling is worse, so the start of the game is about farming safely and avoiding fights until her ultimate is online. After that, one charm into her empowered burst usually deletes a carry before their team reacts, and Last Caress lets her dive, kill, and vanish again.

Everything before that spike is a weakness. She has no strong early gank without setup, she loses to anyone who catches her mid-clear, and one sweeper or control ward in the right brush turns her ambush into a death. Her payoff comes in the second half of the game, and the weak early window is the price.
gamePlan.earlyGame:
Your first clear is about survival, not speed. Take a safe full clear and accept that you are slower and squishier than most junglers right now. Do not contest scuttle against a real early jungler and do not invade, because almost everyone beats you in that fight. Take the safe crab, finish the rotation, and get to level five, because your ultimate and camouflage arrive together and that is when you become a jungler instead of a farmer.

From that point you can start looking for ganks rather than waiting on items. Use the camp respawn timer to walk at whichever lane has pushed too far, come in from an angle nobody is watching, and let the charm do the setup. Clear again when the camps are back and repeat. Until camouflage is up, farm, track the enemy jungler so you never get counter-ganked, and walk away from every early skirmish instead of joining it.
gamePlan.midGame:
Treat the first objectives as ambush sites rather than front-to-back fights. Clear or avoid enemy vision, then hold a side angle near the route into the pit. Begin Allure early enough to complete the charm on an isolated contesting target, and convert the takedown into the objective only after checking the enemy jungler and nearby lanes. If both teams arrive together, trade for Herald or camps unless your composition can protect Evelynn's flank and win the grouped fight.

Between objectives, roam invisible and charm whoever stepped too far, then let the empowered hit do the rest. Keep farming between picks so your items keep up, and let your map threat make enemy carries play scared even in lanes you are nowhere near.
gamePlan.lateGame: Late game your job is to kill whoever the enemy cannot afford to lose. Find their main carry, charm them, delete them, then vanish before the rest of the fight can punish you. Camouflage lets you sit on a flank while Baron or Elder is being set up, so you can pick someone off before the objective starts and turn the fight into five versus four. Your damage is huge and your health bar is not, so patience is the real skill: wait for the carry to step out of position, take the angle, and never throw your charm at a tank just because the fight started. One clean kill on the right target ends most late fights before they begin.
gamePlan.teamfights: Wait on a flank until the enemy formation and key control spells are visible. Begin Allure on the highest-value target you can reach, then enter only when the charm can complete and Last Caress has a safe retreat direction. If the carry remains beside heavy peel, threaten the angle or charm the protecting champion instead of forcing the dive. Evelynn should finish a weakened or isolated target after the fight begins, not start a grouped fight from the front.

boots.name: Immortal Treads

coreItems.note: Ability haste means more Q casts, and hitting a target already halves its cooldown, so the two compound.

coreItems.name: Death's Dance
coreItems.note: Spreads burst damage out over a few seconds, which gives her Vital healing time to catch up in a duel she opened losing.

coreItems.name: Amaranth's Twinguard

keystoneRune.note: Her trades are repeated short walk-ups onto a Vital rather than one long fight, which is the rhythm this rewards.

primaryRunes.note: Winning a side lane duel only matters if the tower follows, and her Q makes reaching it easy.

primaryRunes.note: Her parry answers one spell, and this covers the poke thrown at her the rest of the time.

primaryRunes.desc: Gain tenacity and bonus defenses while immobilized.

secondaryRunes.name: Sudden Impact

secondaryRunes.note: Her Q is a dash, so the bonus true damage lands on the strike that follows.

spells.name: Flash
spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

goodAgainst.note: Sion's maximum-health build increases Fiora's Vital damage, and the long charge on Decimating Smash gives Riposte a readable crowd-control window that can stun him. Step around the shield instead of wasting the full combo into it, then use Grand Challenge during his committed charge or ultimate recovery when all four Vitals are accessible.
Everything he builds makes your vitals hit harder, his cleavers are easy to sidestep, and outlasting you is the only threat he has.

Yone's spirit form gives him a predictable return point but does not deal snapback damage to himself. Use that position to line up a Vital, and save Riposte for the telegraphed knockup from Mortal Steel or Fate Sealed rather than assuming Soul Unbound wins the trade for you.
Mordekaiser is slow, his big health pool makes your vital procs hit harder, and his shield melts faster than he can bank it; only his death realm catching you low is a real threat.

Riposte can negate Aatrox's knockups or the delayed pull from Infernal Chains and stun him if the return strike connects, but blocking only the chain's initial hit does not create a stun. Read the delayed crowd control carefully, because his World Ender sustain wins a sloppy extended brawl.

weakAgainst.note: Malphite's armor and Ground Slam attack-speed reduction weaken the attacks between Vitals, while repeated Seismic Shard poke pressures Riposte without committing. Riposte can negate the damage and crowd control from Unstoppable Force, but Malphite himself remains unstoppable during the dash, so the timing is less forgiving than against a normal engage.
A mind game between his Counter Strike and your Riposte: whoever reads the other wins the exchange, and he out-scales you in a pure extended duel.
A pure early-game counter: his fury-empowered stun and front-loaded burst beat you flat through the first levels, but the duel flips hard your way once your items come online.
Grit turns the damage you deal into a true damage punch handed right back, the pull restarts fights you tried to leave, and he heals off the grit you keep filling.

gamePlan.overview:
Fiora is a Baron-lane duelist who becomes extremely difficult to answer in a side lane once her items come in. Her passive marks Vitals on nearby enemy champions, and hitting one deals percentage maximum-health true damage while healing and speeding her up. Armor does not reduce that true damage, but Fiora still needs clean access to each Vital. With a prepared wave, she can force the enemy to send a strong duelist or several champions to stop her pressure.

Riposte is what separates good Fioras from great ones. For 0.75 seconds she prevents non-turret damage and ignores debuffs and crowd control, then strikes in the chosen direction. If it blocked an immobilizing effect, the first enemy champion hit by that return strike is stunned; the stun does not automatically jump back to whoever cast the crowd control. One good parry can turn a gank, while one wasted parry leaves her with no defensive tool at all.

Her laning phase is her weakest point. Take short Vital trades, preserve Riposte for the opponent's important control spell, and avoid giving away the farm she needs for her side-lane item spikes.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Trade only when a vital sits in a good spot. Q onto the marked side, take the proc and the heal, and step away before minion damage adds up. Save your parry for the spell that defines the matchup (a stun, a pull, a knockup), because a clean parry stun is the biggest swing available in lane. Against bullies and ranged matchups, give ground and farm: your power is in items, and every minion you farm safely brings your spikes closer.
gamePlan.midGame: Your first big item turns side-lane duels into your win condition, and Grand Challenge reveals all four Vitals on one champion. Triggering all four creates a Victory Zone, and the zone also appears if the marked target dies after you triggered at least one of those Vitals; Fiora and allies standing inside are healed. Shove your lane and split on the opposite side from your team's next objective, forcing a defender you can kill or a free tower. Join the Herald fight only if your team needs you; a Fiora trading one-for-one on the map is usually worth more than a Fiora grouping early.
gamePlan.lateGame: You are the reason the enemy cannot group. Keep a side lane permanently pushed, duel whoever they send (with items, that fight is yours against almost anyone), and ult the tank if they send one, since vitals plus true damage cut straight through big health bars. The map math is simple: they send one, you kill them; they send two, your team plays four against three at the objective. Just do not get caught between waves with your parry down.
gamePlan.teamfights: Hunt one target and make it count. Flank, Q onto the carry or ult the frontliner blocking your path, and parry the scariest answer they throw back. Triggering all four Grand Challenge Vitals, or helping kill the marked target after triggering at least one, drops a heal zone that can win a long fight for allies standing inside it. If they are too grouped to enter, do not force it. Stand at the edge, threaten the flank, and remember that pressuring a side lane often helps your team more than joining the fight.

goodAgainst.note: Draven has to catch axes and all-in, and your kit makes both expensive: the bomb punishes every axe reach, and Valkyrie dashes out of the dive he commits to.
Tristana's all-in needs a target with no exit, and Valkyrie gives you one. She loses the trading war on the way to a scaling fight that is roughly even.

Phosphorus Bomb and Gatling Gun give Corki a stronger early rotation before Kog'Maw has items to amplify Bio-Arcane Barrage, and Valkyrie avoids the return slow from Void Ooze. Push the early wave, trade while Barrage is inactive, and use that priority before Living Artillery turns the lane into a range contest Corki no longer controls.

weakAgainst.note: Caitlyn's basic-attack range and Headshot punish Corki before Phosphorus Bomb can begin a full rotation, while Yordle Snap Traps constrain his Valkyrie path. Farm with missiles instead of spending health on each minion, preserve Valkyrie for the trap-free exit, and contest her only after a Big One or item spike gives the return trade enough reach.
Constant slows from Ashe make it hard to space around Valkyrie, and her volleys cost less mana than the rotations you answer with.

Smolder advances Dragon Practice through Q last-hits while Corki's strongest Missile Barrage and Gatling Gun window is tied to earlier items and stored missiles. Pressure the stack walk-ups with Phosphorus Bomb, spend the Package spike at an objective, and end the quiet farm pattern before Smolder's burn and execute upgrades outgrow Corki's rotation.

gamePlan.overview:
Corki is a burst marksman whose basic attacks and Spellblade hits add true damage equal to a portion of his attack damage. That bonus does not apply to every ability hit. Phosphorus Bomb and Valkyrie's burning patches still deal magic damage, Gatling Gun deals physical damage while shredding both armor and magic resistance, and Missile Barrage deals physical damage.

Missile Barrage stocks up to four missiles and every third cast is a Big One with double damage, more range, and a larger explosion. Hitting champions with six missiles drops a Package at Corki's location; collecting it grants four Big Ones and pauses new package-stack generation until those missiles are spent or the Package expires.

His costs are heavy mana use, zero crowd control, and a reliance on spell rotations. Corki wins by catching a target inside one full rotation, then spending his missiles in the mid-game fights Valkyrie lets him survive.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Trade when the enemy carry steps up for a last-hit and your support can cover the response. Land Phosphorus Bomb, face Gatling Gun through the target, and add basic attacks while the resistance reduction builds. Watch your mana and avoid using Missile Barrage only to hit the wave when a Dragon-lane trade is likely. Keep Valkyrie for an engage or gank unless a forward cast clearly secures the takedown.
gamePlan.midGame: Your spike opens once you have items and missiles banked. Missiles explode on the first enemy hit, so they do not pass over a frontline; use their area explosion or a flank angle to reach a carry. Track the six champion-hit package requirement and collect the dropped Package before an objective when four consecutive Big Ones will matter most.
gamePlan.lateGame: You are a burst carry who still has to keep attacking. Face Gatling Gun through the frontline so its four resistance-reduction stacks improve the whole team's follow-up, and track whether the next R is the normal missile or Big One instead of saving an undefined special shot. Valkyrie remains the escape unless a forward dash clearly secures the fight.
gamePlan.teamfights: Start behind allied peel and damage the closest target while Gatling Gun reduces armor and magic resistance. Use Missile Barrage through open angles, tracking whether the next shot is a Big One. Hold Valkyrie until an enemy commits a gap closer or until a protected forward position clearly secures the fight. Corki has no control to stop a diver, so preserve enough distance for the dash to create a real escape route.

startingItem.name: Amplifying Tome

boots.name: Spellslinger's Shoes

coreItems.name: Rabadon's Deathcap
coreItems.note: Multiplies Fizz's AP across Chum the Waters and the dash sequence that follows, making the single untargetable dive much more likely to finish its target.

coreItems.name: Void Staff
coreItems.note: Cuts the magic resist that would let a target survive Chum the Waters and Fizz's one committed dive. Choose it over Cryptbloom when enemies are stacking magic resist and maximum personal damage matters more than haste and team healing.

coreItems.name: Zhonya's Hourglass
coreItems.note: Build this for when his E and ultimate are spent and he is standing in their team. Buy Seeker's Armguard early for the armor and ability power.

situationalItems.name: Oceanid's Trident
situationalItems.note: Build this when shields absorb Fizz's gank or all-in. Chum the Waters can apply the shield reduction before his dash sequence arrives, preserving the damage of his committed burst.

situationalItems.name: Morellonomicon
situationalItems.note: Build this when a target heals through Fizz's shark and dash combo. Grievous Wounds must be applied before that healing can erase his one burst window, so buy Oblivion Orb early and finish the item later.

situationalItems.desc: AP engage item with a dash
situationalItems.note: Build this when reaching a backline carry is the problem. It is a second gap closer next to his dash and E.

situationalItems.name: Banshee's Veil
situationalItems.note: Build this when the enemy has crowd control ready for the moment his untargetable window ends.

situationalItems.name: Stormsurge

situationalItems.name: Cryptbloom

keystoneRune.note: Heals him through a laning phase he loses on stats, keeping him alive to the levels where his dive works.

primaryRunes.note: His whole game is picking off targets, so the stacks build faster on him than on a farming mid.

spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

goodAgainst.note: Playful can make Fizz untargetable as Twisted Fate commits Gold Card, denying the stun that normally sets up Wild Cards and a gank. Respect the card timing instead of assuming every trade is free, and pressure him before he can finish Gate's channel to escape or influence another lane.

Playful can dodge Light Binding, but Lux still has Lucent Singularity's automatic detonation and slow plus Prismatic Barrier's shield for the landing. Bait Q, avoid landing inside E, and preserve enough damage to finish through the returning shield.

Syndra can cast Scatter the Weak through a Dark Sphere to stun a moving target, so Fizz is not safe simply because he keeps moving. Playful can dodge the line, and once Scatter is spent Syndra has no dash to escape the follow-up.
Norra controls space with poke from range, and your hop ignores that control completely: you vault over her projectile and the dog, and a squishy yordle with no dash cannot survive what lands on her.

Playful can dodge a key bomb, but Ziggs can still slow the landing area with Hexplosive Minefield and use Satchel Charge to knock Fizz away or hop to safety. Approach around his ground control and wait for Satchel before committing Chum the Waters.

weakAgainst.note: Early he is an easy kill, but once his ultimate is online his silence cancels your combo mid-commit, his blink matches your mobility, and his scaling wins the race from there.

Diana cannot pull Fizz while Playful makes him untargetable, but she can charge Moonfall and release it as he lands. Her shield absorbs part of his burst, and once Playful is spent he has no second defensive tool for the follow-up.
Her dashes match your mobility and her stun plus sustain outlast your short trades, since she resets off minions and the all-in runs longer than your cooldowns can cover.
A tank you cannot burst, with a taunt that catches you the moment you land, a magic shield that soaks your combo, and an ultimate that follows the roams meant to be your edge.

Lissandra can answer Fizz's landing point with her area root and reserve her targeted ultimate for the follow-up. Track the two controls separately, since Ring of Frost is centred on her and Frozen Tomb is the targeted stun.

gamePlan.overview:
Fizz is an assassin who ignores the spacing rules other champions live by. His pole-vault lifts him out of targeting at the exact moment your spell arrives, Playful/Trickster makes him harder to lock down than almost any other melee, and his ultimate throws a fish that pulls a shark out of the ground to knock your carry into the air.

His game is the snowball. Fizz is at his best against the immobile poke mage whose one panic button his untargetable hop dodges, and the rest of his combo deletes what is left. Get a lead, shove the wave, and convert it across the map: a Fizz with priority does not sit mid, he picks a side lane and kills whoever is standing in it. The shark is a low-risk commitment that turns a skirmish into a kill before peel can react.

The cost is melee range and cooldowns. Before items his trades are real but not lethal, and he farms under threat from anyone who out-ranges him. Hard crowd control that does not need aiming, tanky mids he cannot burst, and scalers who outgrow his kill window all shut him down. Fizz wins by ending the game early, not by reaching the late game.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Play the early lane on short, cheap trades: chip with the trident on the way past, weave in your on-hit passive, and bait the enemy's key spell before you ever commit the pole-vault. The hop is both your engage and your only escape, so do not burn it dodging minor poke when the matchup-defining cooldown is the thing you actually fear. Against ranged poke you will eat some chip while you farm, and that is fine: you are not built to win the level-two trade war, you are built to win the all-in once your ultimate and first item arrive. Track the enemy jungler, because a melee assassin pushed past the river is exactly the gank every jungler wants.
gamePlan.midGame: Your first item turns Fizz's empowered melee attacks and full rotation into a kill threat, and the roaming starts. Shove the wave hard, then spend the priority: a committed dive onto a mid who never respected your burst is worth more than the minions you left, and a side-lane roam usually comes back with a kill or a Flash. Around dragon and Herald, hold mid pressure and arrive first, because a fish onto a carry in front of your team can decide the objective. Preserve Playful/Trickster when possible to dodge the counter-engage or escape after the kill.
gamePlan.lateGame: By now you are the reason the enemy carry checks the minimap before every step. Stay off the front, hold the edges, and pick your moment: fish onto the priority target, let the shark knock them up, and burst them out of the fight before their team turns. The hop gives you exactly one escape, so commit on a target you know will die, not the first one you see. Split push when fights are not happening, since few mids can beat you in a true side-lane duel, but the second a fight starts you should be flanking it, not farming a wave two screens away.
gamePlan.teamfights: Pick one target and ignore everyone else. Wait on the flank while their stuns and engage get spent, then throw Chum the Waters onto the carry and follow its delayed knockup with Urchin Strike, Rending Wave, and attacks. Never duel the frontline, because your value is killing their carry. Preserve Playful/Trickster when possible to dodge the answer or escape; if you spend it to enter, you no longer have the same button available for the exit. Overstay that window and you are a squishy melee standing in the open with nothing left.

situationalItems.note: Build this when shields absorb Fizz's gank or all-in. Chum the Waters can apply the shield reduction before his dash sequence arrives, preserving the damage of his committed burst.

situationalItems.name: Morellonomicon

situationalItems.name: Banshee's Veil

situationalItems.name: Cryptbloom

keystoneRune.desc: Moving and attacking builds Energy. At 100 stacks, your next attack heals you and grants movement speed.

goodAgainst.note: Taliyah's ground control and poke mean nothing to a target that goes untargetable on reaction. She is a squishy mage with no dash to escape once you are on top of her.
Kha'Zix commits everything to one leap, and Playful Trickster turns that all-in into a whiff that leaves him stranded mid-combo. As a squishy assassin himself, he cannot survive your burst afterward.
Nidalee's spears do nothing to a target that hops untargetable on reaction, and once you close the gap she cannot kite your dash. Her fragile frame has no answer to your all-in.

weakAgainst.note: Rammus turns your dive against you: his taunt drags you into his reflected damage, and once your E is spent your squishy frame cannot survive sitting on top of him.
Warwick heals through your burst, and his suppressing ultimate lands the moment your E drops, pinning you with no way out. He wins the long fight because his sustain tops him back up after one combo.
Nunu is a tank you cannot burst, and his snowball and bite chunk you while your combo barely dents him. Your hop dodges one bite, not his percent-health damage and sustain.

gamePlan.overview:
Fizz is a jungler who ignores your front line entirely. He is a slippery melee assassin who hops over danger with Playful/Trickster, dashes onto the backline with his trident, and drops his shark on whichever carry stepped wrong. His clear speed is nothing special; his value is the dive.

He wins by turning ganks and skirmishes into picks. He clears first like everyone else, but the moment the rotation is done he is hunting: find an overextended lane, jump in, and delete whoever did not respect the hop. Once he has an item or two and his ultimate, he can force a pick in any river fight, because the shark is an engage that positioning alone cannot solve once the fish connects.

His weakness is what every diver shares, plus a little extra. His clear is steady rather than fast, so early predators can out-pace and out-trade him before his first item. He has one real defensive button: once Playful/Trickster is spent, he is a squishy melee target standing in the middle of five people. Bait the hop, or lock him before he presses it, and the dive fails.
gamePlan.earlyGame:
Your first clear is steady rather than fast, so take the full rotation and plan it to end near whichever side is pushing into your jungle. Take scuttle after it and get to level five, because your ultimate adds the delayed slow and knockup that make a gank much harder to escape. With the clear behind you, use the camp respawn timer to find lanes where Playful crosses terrain or dodges a key spell, then use Urchin Strike to reach the target; Urchin Strike itself does not slow. Clear again when the camps are back.

The scuttle fight is winnable when you arrive first, because the hop dodges most of what the enemy jungler throws at the crab, but do not gamble a scuttle against an early bruiser who out-trades you standing still. Counter-jungling is fine with vision, since E lets you dip into their camps and pop back out, but get caught with it down and an even jungler ends your game on the spot.
gamePlan.midGame:
Fizz controls early objectives by removing the isolated champion who tries to establish vision. Kill the support warding the pit and the fight is over before it starts. Hunt the side lanes that pushed up, ult the carry from fog so the shark lands before they react, and save the hop for the follow-up rather than the entry when your team is already collapsing. Contest properly when your team is ahead on early fights; when it is even, take Herald and trade dragon away, unless your team comp is built to hold fights for soul.

Keep your tempo high and pressure both sides of the map between objectives. A Fizz farming quietly through mid game is wasting the exact phase his kit was built for.
gamePlan.lateGame: Late game you are an execution threat, not a frontline. Sweep a side entrance, stay out of vision, and wait for the enemy carry to separate from peel or spend a movement spell. Cast Chum the Waters from enough distance to build a larger fish, then enter only when your team can follow or the target has no clean escape. Preserve Playful/Trickster when possible to dodge the response or leave after the kill. If the backline remains protected, keep threatening the flank instead of crossing the frontline alone.
gamePlan.teamfights: Approach from a side angle and identify the carry you can reach without crossing every control spell. Use Chum the Waters when your team can follow its knockup, then hold Playful/Trickster to avoid the stun or burst reserved for your dive. If the carry stays beside heavy peel, wait for that protection to be used or help damage the reachable target. Entering later is better than spending both movement tools before the enemy response is visible.

Zyra is fragile if Galio reaches her, but Grasping Roots still snares at close range, her plants continue attacking, and Stranglethorns can knock up the engage. Force those cooldowns before using Justice Punch rather than treating them as useless in melee.

weakAgainst.note: Janna is built to undo exactly what you do: your dash commits, then her tornado and ultimate blow your team back off the engage you just spent, while her shield and speed keep her carry slippery.

Four parts of his kit lock you down and the fifth is the shield that keeps him alive through your answer, so he pins you before your combo ever resolves: one hook and he is on you while your dash sits useless.

Whimsy breaks your taunt channel and stops you casting Justice Punch at all if it lands first, her shields blunt your magic poke, and Wild Growth's knockup interrupts the dash once it is already travelling.

gamePlan.overview:
Galio is the support who absorbs magic damage and then engages on the people dealing it. Shield of Durand reduces damage while he charges it, then taunts nearby enemy champions when released. Justice Punch is the straight-line dash that knocks enemies up. Hero's Entrance targets an allied champion within a long but limited range, shields allies around the selected area, then lands at the location chosen when Galio began channeling and knocks nearby enemies back.

In the Dragon lane he starts as a brawler with a damage-reduction charge, using Winds of War to chip the enemy duo off the wave. Once his engage comes online, Justice Punch can knock up a carry and Shield of Durand can taunt nearby champions into the follow-up. His biggest asset is reinforcing fights: after clearing or roaming into ultimate range, Hero's Entrance can turn a mid skirmish or river contest after its channel completes.

The catch is that he is telegraphed and committal. His dash follows a visible line, his taunt requires melee range, and a well-timed knockback or cleanse can separate him from the target before his team follows.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Stand in front of your carry and charge Shield of Durand when damage is incoming, since it reduces magic damage more heavily than physical damage and can release into a taunt if the enemy walks close. Drop Winds of War on the enemy duo when they line up with the wave to chip them off last hits. Justice Punch is your committed dash, so do not throw it as poke. You do not need a kill in the opening minutes; you need the enemy support respecting the taunt radius whenever you start charging.
gamePlan.midGame: Mid game Hero's Entrance makes Galio relevant to fights within its long range. Watch mid and the river before objectives and begin the channel early enough to reach the fixed landing area; it is not global or instant. Around the first dragon and Herald, use Justice Punch and Shield of Durand to lock down a priority target, and keep the river warded so you can choose a safe channel. Watch your own wave as well, because reinforcing elsewhere can leave your Dragon-lane carry exposed.
gamePlan.lateGame: Late game you are both your team's engage and its safety net. Hold the ultimate for the fight your team actually wants instead of spending it on a single pick, because landing beside a coordinated group is worth more than chasing one runner. Find the angle where Justice Punch and Shield of Durand catch their carry, or stay near your own backline and charge the area taunt to peel a diver; Shield of Durand reduces damage on Galio but does not create a wall between teams. Read which job the team needs before committing.
gamePlan.teamfights: Start it or stop it, and decide before bodies collide. Hero's Entrance shields allies near its chosen area, then Galio lands at that fixed location and knocks enemies back; it does not knock them up or track the targeted ally after cast. Follow the landing with Shield of Durand's taunt, or use Justice Punch when a knockup is needed. If you are not engaging, charge Shield of Durand near your carry to reduce incoming damage on Galio and threaten a taunt on the diver. Justice Punch is telegraphed, so engage on a target that cannot sidestep it.

startingItem.name: Amplifying Tome
startingItem.note: Start Amplifying Tome for early ability power, then build it directly into a Spellslinger's Shoes rush. The fast magic penetration sharpens Winds of War, Shield of Durand, Justice Punch, and Colossal Smash before Galio begins his tank core.
