primaryRunes.desc: After taking damage from a champion, the next 3 instances of champion damage are reduced.
primaryRunes.note: She is the softest target in the lane, and this covers the engage aimed at her rather than her carry.

primaryRunes.name: Revitalize
primaryRunes.desc: Healing and shielding are stronger, especially on low-health targets.
primaryRunes.note: It strengthens Eye of the Storm and Monsoon's healing field, upgrading the protective half of her kit even though Howling Gale and Zephyr remain damage and control tools.

secondaryRunes.name: Transcendence
secondaryRunes.desc: Gain ability haste, then reduce a basic ability's cooldown after it hits at level 9.
secondaryRunes.note: Ability haste means more shields, which is the only stat that really changes her impact.

spells.name: Flash
spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

goodAgainst.note: Her whole game is the all-in and yours is canceling it: a stored tornado interrupts her stun follow-up, and Monsoon sweeps her off your carry the instant she lands her engage.

Dredge Line gives Nautilus a predictable entry path, and Janna can charge Howling Gale through that line before Monsoon pushes him off the carry after he lands. Save the tornado for the hook follow-up rather than lane poke, shield the first impact, and cast Monsoon after Depth Charge reaches its target so the remaining crowd-control chain loses its damage follow-up.

Howling Gale can interrupt Rell's Crash Down approach, and Monsoon removes her from the group before Magnet Storm gathers multiple targets. Stand outside the initial leap radius, keep one disengage spell for the committed landing, and punish the long window where Rell is dismounted and has no clean exit.
Alistar's kill threat is his knockup and headbutt combo, and a well timed tornado or monsoon interrupts the follow-up that makes it lethal, so he burns his cooldowns for nothing.
His root into dive is exactly the engage your kit cancels: monsoon resets the fight his sapling combo opens, and the tornado zones the angle he wants to root from.

weakAgainst.note: Light Binding reaches beyond Eye of the Storm and roots Janna before she can reposition for Monsoon, while Lucent Singularity repeatedly taxes her short shielding range. Keep the carry offset so one binding cannot catch both of you, shield before Final Spark rather than after the root, and trade only while Binding is on cooldown.
Zyra's plants ignore your peel, and her root into burst out-ranges and out-damages a support with no health to spare, so you lose the poke war she forces.
Your tornado disengages an all-in, not a cage that drops on top of you with a stun behind it, and he out-ranges you and bursts your carry before your shield matters.

Sona usually wins through poke and sustain rather than a melee dive, so Janna has fewer obvious knockback targets. She can still engage or counter-engage with Crescendo and hold an empowered Song of Celerity slow or Diminuendo damage reduction; pressure her fragile lane and save Monsoon for the follow-up formation, not the first chord alone.
There is no all-in to peel, just steady chip: her poke out-ranges your shields, her heals undo what your duo trades back, and every soul she collects makes the long game worse for you.

gamePlan.overview:
Janna is a pure disengage support. Her whole kit exists to cancel the enemy's engage and keep her team alive. She can store two tornadoes that automatically launch after a short delay, Eye of the Storm shields Janna, the nearest turret, and the most wounded nearby ally while granting bonus attack damage, and Monsoon instantly knocks nearby enemies away before leaving a healing field. Where most supports look to start a fight, Janna ends the enemy's.

In the Dragon lane she plays a long, patient 2v2. She will not out-trade much on her own, so she stays close enough for Eye of the Storm to protect the most wounded ally and uses Zephyr when enemies enter its range. Howling Gale is not manually charged: each cast places a whirlwind that matures over 0.75 seconds and then launches in the chosen direction, and Janna can hold up to two charges. Her passive movement speed also helps both her and nearby allies rotate quickly.

Her weakness is the other side of that kit. She is frail, her brief tornado knock-up is unreliable as an offensive catch tool, and hooks or poke mages who attack from outside her protective range can get past what she does. She keeps allies alive better than almost anyone, but contributes little damage herself.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Lane patiently and play near your carry so Eye of the Storm can select them when they are the most wounded nearby ally. The shield grants bonus attack damage while it holds, so trade while the absorb and offensive buff are active, then back off. Keep at least one Howling Gale charge ready and place the whirlwind along the route an engager must take; it launches automatically after 0.75 seconds, so lead the target instead of waiting to release it manually. Ward the river entrances early, because with a frail body and no dash, a gank you did not see is difficult to survive.
gamePlan.midGame: Mid game is when your roaming matters most. Tailwind speeds both Janna and nearby allies, while Zephyr sends air elementals to the three nearest champions; speeding allies and damaging enemies; so moving with teammates improves both abilities. A tornado placed from fog can interrupt the enemy's approach, while Monsoon peels your jungler out of a lost duel. Around dragon and herald, keep the river warded and save a Gale charge to deny the first engage into the pit.
gamePlan.lateGame: Late game Janna is the counter to the enemy's engage. One Monsoon at the right second instantly scatters the attackers, then leaves a three-second field that heals allies who remain inside it. Stay glued to your backline, hold a tornado charge for the diver instead of spending both on poke, and position near the ally you need Eye of the Storm to protect; the spell automatically chooses the most wounded nearby ally rather than a manually selected target. Press Monsoon once enemies have committed, then fight inside the healing field instead of treating it as a channel.
gamePlan.teamfights: Read the enemy's engage before it lands and place Howling Gale through the diver's path. Use Monsoon once attackers commit inside your backline, and stand close enough for Eye of the Storm to protect the focused carry. An early Monsoon can give the enemy time to re-engage, while a cast after the dive commits both displaces them and creates a healing zone. Protect the space your carry needs and stay outside the control that would interrupt the channel.

goodAgainst.note: Graves reaches early river fights with End of the Line and armor from Quickdraw, while Shyvana wants uninterrupted camps until Dragon's Descent unlocks her reliable engage. Invade with lane priority, use Smoke Screen to deny her straight auto-attack duel, and take the first objectives before dragon form and passive stacks turn the farming lead into combat power.

True Grit adds armor during Graves's dash pattern, and a point-blank End of the Line plus shotgun attacks can out-damage Kha'Zix after his isolated Taste Their Fear opener. Fight beside a camp to disable isolation, save Quickdraw for the Leap landing, and use Smoke Screen on his exit before he can reset through Void Assault.
Lee Sin contests your early game, but your shotgun burst and True Grit armor out-trade his combo when you stand your ground. Your point-blank damage finishes the skirmish his combo cannot.

weakAgainst.note: Lillia drifts out of your short shotgun range while her burn stacks on you from a safe distance. You cannot catch her without burning Quickdraw, and her sleep sets up a burst before you can close.
Rammus turns your shotgun against you: Defensive Ball Curl reflects the autos your burst relies on, and his taunt drags you into your own damage. Your AD barely touches a champion built to punish it.

Nunu's percent-health bite chunks you faster than your burst dents his health bar. He sustains through your damage, blocks your shotgun angles with his size, and his snowball catches you when Quickdraw is down.

gamePlan.overview:
Graves is the jungler who dominates the early game with a shotgun. His clear is among the fastest in the jungle, his autos fire a spread of shells that shred camps and chunk anyone standing close, and his smoke grenade blinds them to everything outside it before he steps in to finish the kill. He is a brawler who wants to fight point blank, where every pellet lands.

He wins by being ahead before anyone else is ready to fight. A clean first clear and a won scuttle get him rolling, and from there he power farms, invades, and shows up at every early objective with more gold and more damage than the enemy jungler. True Grit makes him tankier the longer a brawl runs, so he happily sits in long fights while his resists climb. Snowballed, he becomes a marksman with a dash, an escape, and bruiser durability.

His weakness is the flip side of that aggression. He wants to fight up close, so hard engage, point-and-click crowd control, and assassins who jump on his cooldowns all punish him hard. He also depends on getting ahead early: a Graves who falls behind does not have true hypercarry scaling to bail him out.
gamePlan.earlyGame:
Your first clear is your whole identity, so clear fast. Use shotgun knockback to limit damage from non-champion monsters, cast End of the Line into nearby terrain so its return explosion happens after 0.25 seconds, and use Quickdraw to reload a round while repositioning. Smoke Screen only deals a small burst when it lands and does not keep damaging camps, so do not treat it as the spell that clears the buff or monsters behind it. Take the full clear instead of breaking off early for a lane; finishing the rotation puts you at the river on tempo with ammunition and Quickdraw ready.

That tempo is what wins scuttle, and scuttle is where your early game is decided. You out-duel almost everything that contests the crab, so path to it and take the fight when it comes. Keep True Grit stacked through the skirmish: every Quickdraw dash gives you a stack, dashing toward an enemy champion gives two, and attacking anything that is not a minion refreshes them. Fully stacked that is a large chunk of armor, so a Graves who keeps them up walks out of a river fight the enemy jungler expected to win.

Scuttle also puts you on level five, and from there the game settles into a loop: gank while your camps respawn, clear them the moment they are back, and go again. Use the river brush to set up a smoke ambush if their jungler paths toward you.
gamePlan.midGame:
Let lane priority decide which first objective receives your damage and tempo. Place Smoke Screen on the enemy jungler so nearsight limits what they can see outside the cloud; it does not silence them or directly reduce their damage, and targets inside their reduced vision can still be attacked. Fight close enough for multiple pellets to connect, and use Quickdraw to reload or reposition as the contest changes. With a first item and an early lead, contest when your team can support the fight; when it is even, trade toward the objective your composition values more.

Between objectives, invade the enemy jungle on the side away from their team, take their camps, and turn a counter-gank attempt into a duel you usually win through burst and True Grit. A Graves who is not actively pressuring the map at this stage is wasting his lead.
gamePlan.lateGame: Late game Graves is not a split pusher and not a scaling monster who out-damages a finished crit carry in a long fight. He is a flanking executioner. Stick with your team near Baron and the late dragons, take camps on the way so your damage stays current, and look for the angle that deletes one priority target rather than the one that puts you in the middle of their frontline. Smoke is your survival tool as much as your damage tool: drop it to break line of sight with whoever is chasing you, dash out, and re-enter once their engage is spent. If you fell behind, your job shrinks to clearing waves and punishing picks. If you are ahead, you are the reason their carry never gets to cast a spell.
gamePlan.teamfights: Wait for the front lines to commit, then collapse on the squishiest target you can reach without walking through their whole team. Smoke the carry so they cannot see out of the cloud, dash in through the gap, and dump the full spread at point-blank range where every pellet connects, because that is where Graves does the damage that ends fights. True Grit lets you survive the dive longer than the enemy expects, but you still cannot take a full lockdown chain, so time your jump for after their key crowd control is used, not before. If the dive is not there, play the flank: hold smoke to peel a diver off your own carry or break a chase, and let your dash keep you firing from the side, never from the front.

goodAgainst.note: A long-range poke war where your hits are heavier. Trading fourth shot for headshot wins you the math, and your root catches her when she walks up to poke.
Twitch is a non-threat until he scales, and your range and burst never give him the room. His squishy frame cannot answer your damage in the early 2v2.
Draven's axe-catch spots are predictable, which creates a good root angle once he has been marked, but you still have to aim and land the skillshot. The duel goes to whoever lands their setup first.

weakAgainst.note: Tristana jumps straight onto your immobile frame, and the all-in arrives faster than your reload can answer. Her burst out-trades you the moment she lands, and a reset kill snowballs the lane.
Vayne tumbles out of your fourth-shot windows, Condemn stuns you against walls you cannot dash away from, and her true damage out-duels you once she has items. Early is yours; the long game is hers.

Bio-Arcane Barrage eventually outranges Jhin's basic attacks and supplies continuous percent-health damage during the reload after his fourth shot. Win before that spike by using Dancing Grenade and Deadly Flourish to control the wave, then avoid a stationary damage race while Barrage is active and save Curtain Call for Kog'Maw's immobile retreat.

gamePlan.overview:
Jhin fires four shots, and the fourth is the core of the kit: a guaranteed critical that deals extra damage based on the target's missing health, followed by a reload window the whole lane is played around. No carry punishes a single mistake harder.

The kit is built on setups. His root catches anyone recently hit by his damage, his traps cover the lane and river, and every critical hit speeds him up, which is how an immobile carry keeps repositioning between shots. Curtain Call opens a large fixed cone and fires four long-range rounds, but it is not a global or cross-map ultimate.

The costs are real: he has no dash, and disciplined enemies can trade into his reload. The fourth shot creates his strongest short window, but he still needs crowd control, spacing, or allied pressure to reach the target safely.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Trade on your terms. Start trades with the fourth shot loaded, follow with the root the moment your damage tags them, and back off during the reload. Put traps in the river brush and behind your own position. Every exchange should begin with your fourth shot ready, because enemies trading into a loaded fourth shot is the most reliable mistake in the lane.
gamePlan.midGame: Your damage comes as burst, not sustained DPS, which makes you the best skirmish-starter on the dragon side of the map. Root the first mispositioned enemy at dragon standoffs and let the fourth shot turn the pick into a fight your team starts ahead. Curtain Call opens or closes objective fights from a screen away, and the traps you keep planting make the river unsafe to walk.
gamePlan.lateGame: You are the pick threat. Fights revolve around your root: land it on a carry and the fourth shot plus your team ends them before the engage really starts. Stay behind your frontline, count your shots into the fight, and move to a safe angle for your ultimate when the fight turns into a chase. Reload windows matter more than ever, so never start a duel you cannot finish in four shots.
gamePlan.teamfights: Play around the four-shot cycle. Open from range, save the fourth shot for whoever your team commits onto, and root the diver who comes for your backline: your crowd control peels as well as it picks. When the fight turns into a rout, Curtain Call finishes the runners. You are not sustained DPS, so do not fight like it. Pick your shots and make the fourth one land on a target it can kill.

goodAgainst.note: Accelerated Shock Blast outranges Overload and punishes Ryze whenever he walks up to spread Spell Flux, giving Jayce control before Ryze's mana and scaling are online. Vladimir's early game is weak, and his sustain only matters if he gets to heal in peace, which your constant poke denies. The lane is yours until his late-game scaling arrives.
You massively out-range her, so every step she takes toward a minion costs health, and she never gets the kills her snowball depends on. Your knockback can even interrupt her ultimate channel.

Wind Wall blocks Shock Blast, including the accelerated projectile that carries Jayce's poke, so it matters greatly in Cannon stance. Hammer abilities bypass the wall, but entering melee exposes Jayce to Yasuo's dash chain; bait the wall before spending the empowered shot.
Kassadin's early game is helpless against your poke range, and he pays for every last-hit before his ultimate comes online. The catch is timing: a farmed Kassadin blinks through your poke late.

weakAgainst.note: Irelia dashes through the wave to close the range your game depends on. Your poke hurts before her items, but once she spikes, one gap-close puts her on top of you.

Lissandra has targeted lockdown through her ultimate and area control through Ring of Frost, so Jayce should use ranged spacing rather than entering the W radius for free. Her self-stasis also cancels your Hammer all-in, and her waveclear shrugs off your poke priority.
Swain heals through the poke that beats most mids and grows too tanky to burst. His long root pulls you into his combo, and his drain refills whatever you chip away.

Vel'Koz can contest Jayce at comparable artillery range, and Organic Deconstruction's true damage ignores resistances. Jayce does have a targeted gap closer in To the Skies!, but using it requires entering the range of Vel'Koz's knockback and full combo.

gamePlan.overview:
Jayce switches between two weapons, and that switch is the whole champion. In Cannon stance he pokes from very long range with a charged shot and drops an Acceleration Gate to make it hit harder. In Hammer stance he is a melee brawler with a knockback, a damage aura, and the burst to finish what the poke started. A good Jayce pokes you down from range, then swaps to Hammer the moment you are low enough to kill.

In mid he is a lane bully who plays for tempo, not the late game. His plan is to win the early levels outright: shove with cannon poke, chunk you every time you walk up to farm, then turn that lead into roams and objectives. He is one of the few mids whose poke alone creates tower pressure, and he can fire a charged shot through his own gate to start a fight from very far away.

The catch is that he falls off. Once everyone has items and health bars, his burst stops one-shotting and his sustained damage is ordinary. To the Skies! is a targeted leap toward an enemy, not a free escape; Jayce usually disengages with Acceleration Gate's movement speed or Thundering Blow's knockback. He has to turn an early lead into a closed game.
gamePlan.earlyGame: The first few levels are where you make the game. Start in Cannon stance, place Acceleration Gate, and fire Shock Blast through it for the empowered projectile. When a target drops low, use the Gate's movement speed before transforming to Hammer stance, then leap with To the Skies! and save Thundering Blow either to knock the target toward allies from the correct side or to disengage. You cannot cast Gate while already in Hammer stance.
gamePlan.midGame: Once you have lane priority, spend it on the map, because mid pressure is worth more than another wave of poke. Shove, then walk to river: gate a teammate onto a scuttle fight, lob a cannon shot over the wall to zone enemies off dragon or herald, or roam to a side lane where your poke and knockback turn a close skirmish into a clean pick. This is your best stretch of the game, so play it aggressively; a Jayce who sits in lane farming wastes the exact window where he is strongest. Help your jungler take the early objectives your lane lead opened up, and watch for side lanes you can reach with gate speed. The tempo you build now is the lead you carry into the phase where your damage falls off.
gamePlan.lateGame: Late game you have to accept your limits. Your burst no longer one-shots a fed carry, so stop hunting picks and play as a poke and tempo tool. Soften the enemy backline with cannon shots before fights start, shove a side lane and rotate, and use the gate to peel for your carries or escape a collapse rather than dive into one. You can still hold a side lane and threaten poke against anyone who steps up, but you lose a straight duel against the hypercarries you used to bully. Be useful by controlling space and starting fights on your terms, not by pretending the burst stance still one-shots people.
gamePlan.teamfights: Your fight starts before the enemy commits. Open from max range in Cannon stance and send Shock Blast through Acceleration Gate to increase its speed, range, radius, and damage. When the fight begins, use the Gate to speed allies or retreat, and use Thundering Blow to knock a diver away. To the Skies! only leaps toward a target and cannot hop Jayce back out, so do not spend it as though it were a reversible engage.

She has to walk through constant Shock Blasts to touch you, and your knockback throws her one gap closer right back out. If she cannot start the fight on her terms, she cannot start it at all.
Your boosted Shock Blast out-ranges his darts, and his blind only affects autos you barely use, so you win the poke war against a champion with very little health.

weakAgainst.note: That dash covers exactly the gap you thought was safe, and his stun ends your kiting on the spot, so one mistake per wave can decide the lane.

Warrior Trickster can make Shock Blast hit the clone, and Wukong can keep Cyclone spinning even after Thundering Blow displaces him. Identify the real Wukong and save the knockback to create distance rather than expecting it to cancel his ultimate.
Armor and his shield blunt the Shock Blasts you live on, and his ultimate closes the distance from a range your spacing cannot answer. Once his ult is online, your spacing no longer protects you.

Sion's charged Decimating Smash does not out-range an accelerated Shock Blast, so Jayce should keep poking from beyond it. The danger is Sion's durability and Unstoppable Onslaught closing from long range; once Sion reaches melee, a charged knockup can punish Jayce's limited escape.

gamePlan.overview:
Jayce brings a ranged laning phase to a lane full of melee fighters, and that is the whole pitch. In cannon form he fires Shock Blasts through his Acceleration Gate from huge range, punishing every last hit the enemy dares to take. In hammer form he becomes a burst bruiser with a knockback for anyone who closes the distance.

His power arrives at level one and never waits for an ultimate, because his stance swap is the ultimate. In most melee matchups the plan is simple: chunk them at range until they cannot contest, then zone them off the wave or swap to hammer and finish the kill.

The catch is that Jayce is a lane bully on a timer. He is squishy, his damage flattens out as enemies itemize, and he offers less in teamfights. If he does not turn his lane into towers and a gold lead, he spends the late game as a poke threat behind his real carries.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Use cannon form to pressure last-hits, but avoid firing every accelerated Shock Blast through the minion wave and pushing without vision. Hold the Baron wave where ranged poke can land without exposing Jayce to a long chase. Save mana when the target stays behind minions and keep Thundering Blow available for a gap closer or gank. Crash before recalling so the opponent must choose between matching the reset and losing farm to the turret.
gamePlan.midGame: Crash the Baron wave before moving to Herald or dragon, then use fog and terrain to hide the accelerated Shock Blast angle. Poke before either team enters the pit and keep Acceleration Gate available to help allies reposition. Swap to hammer form when a target is already reachable or a diver must be knocked away, not simply because the first projectile lands. Return to the side wave after the objective window so the early lead continues producing turret pressure.
gamePlan.lateGame: Clear a side wave only when Baron or Elder cannot be started during the rotation. In the setup, stand behind vision and fire accelerated Shock Blasts through objective entrances before the enemy engages. Keep hammer form ready to knock away a diver or finish a target already separated from peel. If the enemy reaches Jayce with full cooldowns, retreat behind the frontline and rebuild the poke angle instead of continuing the melee trade.
gamePlan.teamfights: Soften, zone, survive. Before the fight, your boosted Shock Blasts chunk the enemy frontline, and a well-placed gate controls where the fight can happen. In the fight, stay cannon, stay far, and swap to hammer only when something jumps you: knock it back, walk away, keep firing. Jayce wins teamfights before they start by chunking the enemy to half health on the way in.

spells.name: Flash
spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

goodAgainst.note: Soraka has no kill pressure, so your poke chunks her and her carry faster than her heals can refill, and you decide when the all-in happens.
Yuumi is only a real target when she detaches, and your poke and root make every detach window dangerous while her host eats your chip alone.
Braum only threatens when his carry gets in range, and your speed and shields keep that moment from coming, so he eats poke while waiting for a brawl you never give him.

Veigar is immobile and vulnerable to Inner Flame, and repeated poke can force him away from minions he wanted to stack. The spell does not remove stacks he has already earned, so deny future farm rather than expecting to reverse his scaling.

weakAgainst.note: Her lockdown lands whether you shield or not, since a shield stops damage and not a stun, so once she reaches engage range your lack of an escape decides the fight.
Nautilus brings a hook, a targeted ultimate, and a knockup, all lockdown your shields cannot answer, and his whole kit exists to erase the distance you rely on.
His mobility beats everything you do: he dashes past the tether, dives your immobile frame, and shields his own carry through your poke, so you never trade on your terms.

Rell's chain crowd control goes through shields and can hold Karma through Inspire's movement speed. Rell's resistance reduction makes the affected target take more allied damage; it does not reduce Karma's outgoing poke, though Rell's stolen defenses make Karma easier to kill.

gamePlan.overview:
Karma is a support who cycles empowered basic abilities. Every ability cast adds a Mantra stack, and at three stacks her next basic ability is enhanced. Mantra Inner Flame creates a slowing field that ruptures for a second hit. Mantra Focused Resolve extends the root and adds another tether between targets. Mantra Inspire gives the primary target a larger decaying shield and speed boost, then grants the same effects to only the nearest allied champion already in; or first allied champion to enter; the ring, not every ally standing nearby.

Her ultimate, Transcendent Embrace, is a separate teamfight button: a ring of spirit energy that detonates after a second for damage and a slow, dragging anyone caught on the outer edge toward the middle. Casting it also fills Mantra instantly, so the ult and an enhanced spell arrive together.

In the Dragon lane she pokes and protects at the same time. Empowered flame chunks the enemy duo every time they walk up, her shield keeps your carry healthy through trades, and the speed attached to it turns a bad spot into a clean exit or a quick collapse. She punishes every step the enemy takes toward her.

Her weakness is that she has no dash and no real escape once her speed is spent. A hook that lands ignores every shield she owns, and a lockdown chain kills her before her shields matter. She protects everyone except herself.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Play the early lane like a poke mage carrying a shield. Lead with empowered flame when the enemy duo lines up with the wave, mix in the basic version to keep the chip going, and use your speed shield to turn your carry's trades into wins. You want the enemy walking into your range to farm or engage, because both cost them health they cannot get back as fast as you deal it. Watch your mana, since an empty Karma is just a slow target, and respect the all-in supports: once they have engage range on you, your lack of an escape is the whole problem.
gamePlan.midGame: Mid game Inspire becomes a roaming tool. Around dragon and Herald, poke before the fight and use Focused Resolve on one or two nearby enemy champions, staying in range until its delayed root. Basic Inspire affects only its selected target; Mantra Inspire can share the larger shield and speed with one additional nearest or first-entering ally in its ring, not the whole team.
gamePlan.lateGame: Late game you are utility first and damage second. Mantra Inspire shields and speeds the primary target plus one additional ally who qualifies through its ring; it does not cover three allies at once. Stay near your carry, hold the enhanced shield for the enemy's commitment, and use Focused Resolve to tether nearby divers long enough for the delayed root.
gamePlan.teamfights: Open with Inner Flame from range, then hold Mantra Inspire for the enemy's engage so its primary shield and one shared ring shield reach the right allies. Focused Resolve can tether the two nearest enemy champions and root them if the tethers hold. Transcendent Embrace adds delayed area control: it damages and slows everyone in the ring, knocks enemies on the outer ring inward, and immediately fills Mantra. The ultimate is not Karma's only hard control because Focused Resolve roots as well, and neither spell directly knocks a diver away from the carry.

startingItem.name: Tear of the Goddess
startingItem.note: Start it to accelerate his scaling. It gains mana as he casts, so the lane he is supposed to lose is already building the mana that becomes ability power on his staff.

boots.name: Spellslinger's Shoes
boots.note: Magic penetration keeps his blink rotation lethal once his stacks make it repeatable.

coreItems.name: Malignance
coreItems.note: Finish this before the staff. Ultimate haste means more blinks, and each one burns the ground where he lands, which is what turns his first item spike into kill pressure instead of just scaling.

coreItems.name: Archangel's Staff
coreItems.note: Complete the Tear second, once Malignance is already giving him blinks. It turns his mana pool into ability power, and the refund pays for the rising cost of stacking his ultimate.

coreItems.name: Rabadon's Deathcap
coreItems.note: Multiplies his ability power. His burst lands in a single blink rotation, so all of it goes up at once.

coreItems.name: Void Staff
coreItems.note: Cuts the magic resist that turns his arrival into a chunk instead of a kill. Choose it over Cryptbloom when enemies are stacking magic resist and maximum personal damage matters more than ability haste and team healing.

coreItems.name: Zhonya's Hourglass
coreItems.note: Stasis covers the window right after he blinks in with his rotation spent. Buy Seeker's Armguard early, since the armor and ability power already help before the full item.

situationalItems.name: Oceanid's Trident
situationalItems.note: Build this when the enemy has shields that keep absorbing the rotation he blinked in to land.

situationalItems.name: Infinity Orb
situationalItems.note: Build this when his rotation keeps leaving targets alive at a sliver, since the crit against low health finishes them.

situationalItems.name: Rod of Ages
situationalItems.note: Build this when the lane is beating him up before his stacks arrive. The health, mana and sustain all turn into damage on a champion who scales through his mana bar.

situationalItems.name: Banshee's Veil
situationalItems.note: Build this when the enemy has crowd control ready for his blink, which is when he is most reliably caught.

situationalItems.name: Armored Advance
situationalItems.note: Boot swap against heavy physical damage, which is what carries him through the levels before he scales.

situationalItems.name: Chainlaced Crushers
situationalItems.note: Boot swap against heavy magic damage and crowd control, which is what punishes his weak early game hardest.

situationalItems.name: Cryptbloom
situationalItems.note: The alternative to Void Staff. Less penetration, but the ability haste and healing on takedown help when his blinks chain through a fight. Choose it when enemies have not built much magic resist, so trading Void Staff's extra damage for more ability haste and an area heal after takedowns is worthwhile.

keystoneRune.name: First Strike

primaryRunes.desc: Empower your spell-focused burst with extra damage and scaling for ability-heavy champions.
primaryRunes.note: He casts his ultimate more than anything else once he is online, so both the damage increase and the takedown cooldown cut apply over and over.

primaryRunes.name: Transcendence
primaryRunes.desc: Gain ability haste, then reduce a basic ability's cooldown after it hits at level 9.
primaryRunes.note: His ultimate is his whole game plan, and ability haste means more blinks per fight.

primaryRunes.name: Gathering Storm
primaryRunes.desc: Gain increasing adaptive force every few minutes as the game goes on.
primaryRunes.note: He is the definitional scaling mid, so a rune that grows over the game matches what the pick is for.

secondaryRunes.name: Sudden Impact

secondaryRunes.note: His ultimate is a blink, so it adds bonus true damage when he arrives.

spells.name: Flash

goodAgainst.note: Event Horizon is a stun on its boundary rather than a slow cage. Riftwalk can blink across the edge without walking through it, but Kassadin must still avoid appearing inside Veigar's follow-up burst.
Brand's whole game is landing his stun chain and letting the burn tick, and none of that survives your silence and magic shield. Once you can Riftwalk onto him, he has nowhere to go.

Ziggs pokes Kassadin from extreme range early, so the opening is rough, but his mobility is limited to one Satchel Charge hop. Repeated Riftwalks can force that cooldown, cross the minefield, and remove the safety of his artillery range.
His long-range skillshots and true damage make the early lane a chore, but he cannot move, your shield absorbs his magic damage, and your silence cuts his combo short.

Vladimir's lane damage is magic, so Void Stone's periodic shield can absorb part of a trade after Kassadin casts. It is temporary rather than permanent spell resistance, and Vladimir can keep sustaining between shield windows, so do not dismiss the early poke entirely.

weakAgainst.note: His Wind Wall blocks Null Sphere outright, his mobility matches your hops, and his early all-in arrives long before your scaling does, while his passive shield shrugs off the chip you land.

Yone has no Wind Wall and cannot block Null Sphere that way. He still wins the early lane through mixed sustained damage, repeated Mortal Steel pressure, and Soul Unbound's engage range before Kassadin has enough mana and ranks in Riftwalk to answer.
She dashes through the wave onto you with a stun your kit cannot reliably interrupt, and her resets turn one mistake into a snowball. Early Kassadin simply cannot duel her.
Zed's AD burst ignores your magic shield, his shadows chase your hops, and his all-in beats yours at every stage until you are full build.

Accelerated Shock Blast deals physical damage that Null Sphere's magic shield cannot absorb, and Thundering Blow removes Kassadin after he spends Riftwalk to approach. Give up early priority, use Force Pulse to secure grouped minions, and wait for repeated Riftwalk ranks and items before contesting the lane Jayce is built to control.

gamePlan.overview:
Kassadin is a scaling anti-mage assassin. Null Sphere damages and silences the first enemy hit, while Void Stone periodically grants a 1.5-second shield after Kassadin casts any ability. He has no separate passive spell-resistance stat. Riftwalk blinks and damages around the landing point, then stacks up to three times so later casts deal more damage at sharply higher mana cost.

None of this exists when the game starts, though. Early Kassadin is a short-range melee with weak waveclear and no way to fight back against poke, so his laning phase is about patience. He soaks farm, eats harass, and waits for the moment everything flips: ultimate online and first item bought. After that, the lane he was losing becomes a lane he leaves, because a Riftwalking Kassadin can assassinate whoever overextends in a side lane.

His core weakness is the front half of every game. Anyone who can shove him in and run him down before his ultimate matters (the AD assassins, Yasuo and Yone, the early all-in skirmishers) can end the game before Kassadin's begins. Survive that window and you become the problem; lose it and you spend the match a level behind.
gamePlan.earlyGame: The opening is about survival. Use Null Sphere to last-hit or silence a key channel, and time any ability cast so Void Stone's periodic shield absorbs part of an AP trade. Null Sphere does not create the shield itself, and the shield will not be available after every cast while Void Stone is on cooldown. Against an AD bully, farm near safety because the magic shield does not absorb physical damage.
gamePlan.midGame: Everything changes when your ultimate is up and your first item is bought, and that first item is Malignance, not the staff. Buy Tear early so it stacks through the lane, then rush Malignance for the ultimate haste, and only finish the Tear into Archangel's Staff after it. Stop farming the lane and start leaving it: shove the wave, then Riftwalk to river or a side lane and turn someone's overextension into a kill they never saw coming. You go from barely holding on to dictating the map, because a Kassadin who can blink onto a target forces the enemy mid to follow you into bad fights or watch you snowball other lanes. Help your jungler on scuttle, contest dragon and herald with the tempo your hops give you, and keep your mana topped up, since an out-of-mana Kassadin has no kill threat at all. This is where the weak opening pays off.
gamePlan.lateGame: By late game Riftwalk can cross a fight in several casts, with each stack increasing both damage and mana cost. Push a side lane, then look for isolated targets while preserving enough mana for the exit. Void Stone can absorb part of one magic-damage window, but it does not grant permanent spell resistance or make enemy magic damage negligible. Hold the dive until the enemy formation cracks.
gamePlan.teamfights: Your job is the enemy backline, but do not open the fight. Let your frontline commit, then Riftwalk in and use Null Sphere to silence a caster's follow-up. Each Riftwalk stack raises the next cast's damage and mana cost; it does not reset a separate escape. Void Stone's shield can blunt part of a magic rotation when available, but crowd control and sustained damage still punish an early entry, so preserve mana and a path for later Riftwalk casts.

situationalItems.name: Cryptbloom

Choose it when enemies have not built much magic resist, so trading Void Staff's extra damage for more ability haste and an area heal after takedowns is worthwhile.

keystoneRune.name: First Strike
keystoneRune.desc: Deal bonus damage for the first 3 seconds of combat with champions and gain gold.
keystoneRune.note: She opens by blinking onto a target, so she reliably lands the first hit.

primaryRunes.name: Sudden Impact
primaryRunes.desc: Deal bonus true damage after using mobility or exiting stealth.
primaryRunes.note: Her E is a blink, giving her an easy way to trigger the bonus true damage as she enters a fight.

primaryRunes.name: Chain Assault
primaryRunes.desc: Reward chained attacks and abilities on the same target with stronger combo pressure.
primaryRunes.note: Her rotation pours into one target at a time, which is what this rewards.

primaryRunes.name: Eyeball Collector
primaryRunes.desc: Gain adaptive force by collecting takedown stacks from enemy champions and epic monsters.
primaryRunes.note: Her passive runs on takedowns, so the stacks build faster on her than on almost anyone.

secondaryRunes.name: Second Wind
secondaryRunes.desc: After taking damage from a champion, regenerate health over time.
secondaryRunes.note: She has to farm at range before her daggers come online, and this keeps her on the wave while she does.

spells.name: Flash
spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

goodAgainst.note: A slow, immobile mage whose whole kill setup is a cage you can blink straight out of. He scales hard if left alone, but he rarely survives long enough to get there against you.

A missed Light Binding removes Lux's hard crowd control, but Lucent Singularity still slows and automatically detonates when Katarina enters it, while Prismatic Barrier can shield both ways. Shunpo around E's area and commit only when enough damage remains to finish through the shield.
Her ball control and shield make her hard to chip, but she is immobile, and one clean commit kills her before she can reposition the ball for the shield.

Vel'Koz is immobile and becomes stationary only while channeling Life Form Disintegration Ray; his basic abilities do not root him in place. Shunpo can cross his skillshot angles, but save it to avoid the knockback that would interrupt Death Lotus.
Her shroud breaks targeting, but your daggers hit the ground she stands on and Shunpo can target the blade, so the trick that saves her elsewhere fails, and you out-reset her in skirmishes.

weakAgainst.note: He scales past the snowball you are trying to build: his ultimate gives him a blink to dodge your dive and chase your retreat, and his magic shield blunts the burst you live on.
The moment you Shunpo in, she shields the burst, drops her crowd control, and all-ins you back with better defenses than yours, while her own resets snowball off your death.
At melee range she simply out-duels you: she out-sustains your daggers, her minion resets snowball faster, and her stun punishes any dive with lockdown you have no answer to.

Glacial Path is Lissandra's projectile and recast blink, not her root. Ring of Frost roots Katarina when she Shunpos into melee, while Frozen Tomb can stun Katarina or put Lissandra in self-stasis through the follow-up.

Galio has a periodically refreshed magic-damage shield and damage reduction from Shield of Durand, but his passive does not grant magic resistance. Justice Punch can interrupt Death Lotus with a knockup, and Shield of Durand can taunt Katarina after she blinks in.

gamePlan.overview:
Katarina is a reset assassin. Retrieving a ground Dagger slashes nearby enemies and reduces Shunpo's current cooldown by 78% to 96% of its total cooldown depending on rank; it is not automatically a completely free dash. Shunpo can blink to a location near a unit or Dagger. Death Lotus channels daggers at up to three nearby champions, applies 60% Grievous Wounds, and lets Katarina move at half speed during the channel.

She wins through snowballing, not lane dominance. A champion takedown within three seconds of Katarina damaging them reduces her current ability cooldowns by 15 seconds; an unrelated nearby death gives no reset. One legitimate takedown can still return her basic abilities quickly enough to continue the fight, which makes roaming and cleanup central to the pick.

Her weakness is that the kit needs a window, and a smart team refuses to open one. She has no defense once her dash is spent, hard crowd control catches her mid-channel and ends both the ultimate and her life, and the early levels before her first item are a thin melee stretch where any ranged laner can shove her in and chip her down. She earns her lead by finding the one mistake the enemy was not supposed to make.
gamePlan.earlyGame: The opening is the part you survive rather than win, because you are a short-range melee against people who mostly out-poke you. Use Bouncing Blade to last-hit and chip the wave, drop a dagger near the enemy and Shunpo to it for a quick burst, then step back before they answer; a clean dagger trade is your only real pressure before items. Do not facetank ranged harass trying to force something. Soak the farm, hold your dash for the gank that is probably coming, and track the enemy jungler constantly. Keep the wave moving so you can leave on your timing, not theirs, and once your full combo comes together, the lane stops being a problem and your roaming game begins.
gamePlan.midGame: Crash the mid wave before moving toward an extended side lane or a river fight your jungler can support. Enter after the first enemy control spell is used and place Shunpo around a Dagger that gives both damage and an exit route. A takedown can shorten Katarina's cooldowns and open the next target, but do not chase the reset beyond allied vision. If the roam has no target, return for the next wave rather than waiting in a side lane where the enemy can collapse.
gamePlan.lateGame: Late game you are the answer to whichever enemy carry got greedy with positioning, and almost nothing else. You do not split push into duels you can lose, and you do not stand in front trading hits. You hover at the edge of the fight waiting for the dagger field and the angle to line up. At full build your blink chain crosses most of a teamfight in seconds, and a clean Death Lotus on a grouped backline removes them. The flip side is that one missed read ends you, since you have no defensive button to save a bad commit. Let their crowd control get spent on someone else first, then enter from the angle nobody is watching. A Katarina who walks out of fights alive wins games; one who dives on cooldown into a waiting stun just respawns.
gamePlan.teamfights: Your job is killing their carry from a flank. Wait for the enemy to spend key lockdown, then blink to a unit or prepared Dagger and collect Daggers to damage nearby targets while reducing Shunpo's cooldown. Death Lotus lets Katarina move at half speed rather than rooting her in place, but any interrupt still ends the channel, so save it until the relevant controls are down. A takedown reduces current cooldowns by 15 seconds; use that real reset to continue or escape rather than assuming every Dagger pickup fully refreshes Shunpo.

startingItem.name: Long Sword
startingItem.note: Simple early attack damage. She applies a Plasma stack with every attack, so stacking starts from the first trade.

boots.name: Gunmetal Greaves
boots.note: Attack speed means Plasma stacks arrive faster, and the fifth stack is where her damage lives.

coreItems.name: Magnetic Blaster
coreItems.note: Build this first. The energized attack's extra range helps Kai'Sa trade without exposing her short base range, while its chain damage improves waveclear so she can crash waves and create more tempo for recalls, rotations, and objectives.

coreItems.name: Guinsoo's Rageblade
coreItems.note: On-hit magic damage that compounds with the rest of the build, since Blade of the Ruined King, Terminus and her own Plasma ride the same attacks.

coreItems.name: Blade of the Ruined King
coreItems.note: Percent current health damage on every attack, landing alongside the Plasma stacks she is already applying.

coreItems.name: Terminus
coreItems.note: Stacking penetration and resistances the longer she attacks, which suits a champion who has to stay on target to detonate anything.

coreItems.name: Runaan's Hurricane
coreItems.note: The bolts apply on-hit effects, so her Plasma spreads to extra targets rather than sitting on one.

situationalItems.name: Kraken Slayer

Smolder spends the early game stacking, and that is exactly the window your all-in owns: his frame is immobile, and until the stacks pile up his range and damage are not there yet.

Xayah punishes your dive directly: when you dash in she goes untargetable with Featherstorm and roots you with her feathers, and her feather zoning controls the ground your all-in needs.

Piercing Arrow and Hail of Arrows control the early wave from beyond Kai'Sa's range, while Blighted Quiver stacks make every farm walk-up vulnerable to a charged detonation. Preserve health until Supercharge is evolved, use Void Seeker to mark him from range, and commit with Killer Instinct only after Chain of Corruption or his peel support is unavailable.

gamePlan.overview:
Kai'Sa is a carry whose upgraded items evolve her basic abilities. Evolved Icathian Rain doubles its missile count, evolved Void Seeker applies an extra Plasma stack and refunds much of its cooldown on a champion hit, and evolved Supercharge makes Kai'Sa briefly invisible during the charge. Plasma itself does not evolve, although its damage scales with level and ability power.

Her Plasma is the signature: Kai'Sa's attacks and Void Seeker apply it, while nearby allied immobilizing effects and polymorphs add stacks to enemy champions. At five stacks it deals bonus magic damage based on missing health. Killer Instinct shields Kai'Sa and dashes her to a chosen location near a visible Plasma-marked champion within range rather than directly to any marked target anywhere.

The cost is the early game. She is short-ranged and squishy, gets bullied by longer lanes, and needs farm badly. Her games are about reaching the evolutions intact, then hunting the fights her finished form wins.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Respect the range gap and farm toward your item spikes. Use Icathian Rain when the enemy carry is separated from the wave so more missiles reach the champion, and avoid pushing with it when you need the wave near your tower. Most lanes out-range you, so take short trades after your support applies crowd control and adds Plasma. Do not chase the fifth stack through the enemy support's return damage. Preserve Supercharge for an all-in or gank unless its movement speed creates a clearly safe trade.
gamePlan.midGame: Your item spikes and evolutions turn isolated targets into real opportunities. Clear the wave before moving, use Void Seeker to reveal and mark a target from range, and let allied crowd control add Plasma before deciding whether Killer Instinct has a safe landing. Around the first objectives, follow the side with lane priority rather than diving the first marked champion you see. Herald is usually the stronger even trade, while a strong teamfighting composition can stay on dragon and build toward soul.
gamePlan.lateGame: You are a carry with an assassin's entry tool, not an assassin who must dive every fight. Start at normal attack range, build Plasma on the closest safe target, and use evolved Supercharge to change angle or drop vision when threatened. Killer Instinct is strongest after the enemy spends key control and a Plasma-marked carry becomes isolated. Check the landing circle before casting, because its shield buys time but does not provide a return dash.
gamePlan.teamfights: Stack, pop, reposition, and dive only when the fight has already created the opening. Layer Plasma onto the closest safe target while watching for allied crowd control on the backline. Use Killer Instinct only when a visible marked carry is in range and the chosen point avoids enemy control, then isolate the target so Icathian Rain does not split across the whole team. The ultimate has no return dash or reset, so keep Supercharge, Flash, or allied protection available for the exit.

gamePlan.overview:
Kayle is a pure bet on the late game. She starts as the weakest champion in the lane, a melee fighter with half a kit, and each level threshold transforms her further: ranged, then faster, then a flying hypercarry who ends games herself. No power curve climbs steeper, and everyone in the lobby knows exactly when it happens.

Her survival tools are just enough if used well. Q poke slows and shreds, her blessing heals and speeds her out of trouble, and Divine Judgment makes her or a teammate briefly invulnerable, which removes the enemy's best burst window entirely.

The whole pick is a bet that her team can survive her weak phase. Every lane bully sees Kayle as a free lane, and they are right: her early game is genuinely terrible. Win the waiting game and she takes over completely.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Your first job is reaching level 5 with enough health to use the ranged form. Farm with Radiant Blast and Starfire Spellblade when walking into melee range would cost a full trade, and use Celestial Blessing's movement speed to disengage rather than healing after every small hit. Keep the wave near your tower against bullies, but punish opponents who waste their main cooldown or take several turret shots to reach you. Do not spend all your mana contesting one minion when the next wave is safer.
gamePlan.midGame: Ranged attacks and first items let you contribute, but farming levels remains important. Push a side wave only when the enemy cannot freeze you away from safety, then rotate before Herald or dragon begins. Divine Judgment can protect you or the teammate carrying the fight, so decide whose uninterrupted damage matters more before the engage lands. If the first objective is an even trade, Herald usually gives the stronger immediate conversion. Join dragon when your team is built to win repeated five-versus-five fights, not simply because it spawned.
gamePlan.lateGame: At level 13 and with several items, Kayle becomes a powerful ranged carry, but she still needs a protected firing line. Keep side waves managed without arriving late to Baron or Elder, then position behind the teammate who can absorb the first control spell. Attack the closest target until a safer route opens to the backline, and use Celestial Blessing to maintain spacing. Divine Judgment should deny the enemy's highest-value burst, whether it lands on Kayle or another fed carry.
gamePlan.teamfights: Begin behind the frontline with Zeal ready to stack through continuous attacks. Divine Judgment prevents damage but does not remove crowd control, so cast it before lethal burst while continuing to respect the enemy's displacement and lockdown. Use it on yourself when staying alive preserves the most damage, or on another carry when Kayle can keep attacking safely during their protection. Do not lead into fog or step past the frontline for one target. Your advantage comes from sustained area damage that remains active throughout the fight.

Orianna controls the lane from outside your reach, poking your soft early form while denying the priority your scaling needs. Her shield blunts your trades and her shockwave catches a carry who cannot sidestep it.

gamePlan.overview:
Kayle is the hardest-scaling pick in mid: weak melee early, ranged hypercarry later, nearly unstoppable at full build. She starts as a short-range melee laner, gains range and waveclear as she levels, and ends as a long-range attacker whose empowered autos splash damage across the fight while her ultimate makes a teammate (or herself) briefly immune to all damage. Almost nobody is weaker at level one or stronger at full build.

Winning takes more patience than most laners are willing to play with. Early on you farm carefully, dodge trades you cannot win, and count levels until your form changes. Ranged autos let you push waves and answer poke, and your ultimate makes you a threat on the map, but the real Kayle shows up late, when your attacks splash area damage and your invulnerability turns a lost fight into a won one. The plan is a countdown: survive the weak phase, then win the strong one.

The weakness is the flip side of the scaling. For a long stretch you are a slow melee target with no reliable escape, so lane bullies and roaming assassins can make your early game miserable. If the enemy denies your farm, dives you, and ends the game before you spike, the payoff never arrives. Kayle does not steal games early; she waits for them.
gamePlan.earlyGame: The early lane is damage control. Kayle gains attack speed with each Zeal stack, but the movement-speed bonus appears only while she is Exalted at five stacks; one isolated attack does not grant it. Use Radiant Blast's slow and Celestial Blessing's movement speed to disengage, farm near safety, and reach the level-five ranged form.
gamePlan.midGame: Use the level-five ranged form to farm the mid wave without walking into melee trades, then move only after the wave is secured. Items increase damage and attack speed, while the base attack range changes at Divine Ascent's level-five and level-thirteen thresholds rather than with every purchase. Keep farming toward level nine's Exalted fire waves and level thirteen's permanent Zealous effects plus 575 range. Join dragon or Herald when Divine Judgment can protect the teammate carrying the skirmish, and avoid isolated river routes that give an assassin the first hit.
gamePlan.lateGame: This is the game you were always playing toward. At full build your attacks splash damage over groups, your range lets you stand behind everything and still hurt people, and your ultimate cancels a kill attempt on whoever needs it most. Late Kayle does not split push into a 1v1 she might lose; she groups, sits behind her frontline, and wins long fights because nobody can survive ranged area damage they cannot shut down. Hold the invulnerability for the moment it matters, whether that is saving yourself from a collapse or denying the kill their whole comp was built around. Keep your positioning disciplined, because you still have no dash to bail you out, but if you reach this point with items, you are the strongest champion on the map.
gamePlan.teamfights: Your teamfight job is ranged carry with a built-in damage veto. Use Divine Judgment just before lethal damage reaches yourself or an ally. The target remains targetable and can still be crowd-controlled during the 2.5-second invulnerability, so it prevents damage rather than erasing the enemy's entire engage. Position at maximum range and keep attacking while the swords prepare to fall.

Her damage comes from stacked autos, which Counter Strike dodges, and she needs a big early lead to stay relevant because you out-scale her for free.
The rare scaling race you win. Her melee phase cannot answer your leap-stun trades, and even late your dodge blunts her attacks while your stun interrupts her carry windows.
Mini Gnar cannot kite your leap, and Counter Strike eats his auto trades while your stun ends him before the rage bar saves him. Only Mega Gnar near a wall is a real threat.

Shotgun knees out-trade you early because Counter Strike dodges his autos but not his spells, and his execute punishes any fight you take at low health. You only win with completed items.

Mundo just will not die fast enough for the dodge to matter, and his cleavers tax your approach all lane. Your burst barely dents a health pool that size, so the long duel he wants is the one you cannot finish.

Ornn's spell damage and knockups bypass Counter Strike's attack dodge, although Jax still gets its 25% champion-damage reduction and can dodge the basic attack that would consume Brittle. Ornn remains hard to burst and can punish a telegraphed Leap Strike with crowd control.

gamePlan.overview:
Jax scales into a strong late-game duelist, so his early decisions should protect farm without giving away avoidable deaths. Counter Strike dodges non-turret basic attacks and abilities that apply on-hit effects, reduces other champion damage by 25%, and ends in an area stun. His attacks build attack speed, while his ultimate's active damages nearby enemies and grants resistances based on how many champions it hits.

The cost is his early game. Before items Jax is weak, easy to poke, and easy to gank, and everyone knows lane is where to stop him. His job early is to farm safely, dodge the worst trades with Counter Strike, and wait for his item spike.

Once it hits, the plan is simple: leap in, dodge their answer, stun, and out-fight whoever stayed. Past two items he barely needs a team.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Farm patiently until Counter Strike can remove the opponent's main attack pattern. Against attack-reliant champions, start the dodge before their empowered attacks land, stun near the end, and use Leap Strike toward your wave or ward if the return trade continues. Against spell-heavy poke, Counter Strike does not solve the whole matchup, so keep the wave close and use Leap Strike mainly for safety. Build Grandmaster's Might's passive third hit on minions before a short trade, but do not push without river vision just to prepare it.
gamePlan.midGame: Your first item and ultimate create side-lane pressure, but only vision turns that pressure into a safe play. Push when you know which champion can answer, keep a ward or allied unit available for Leap Strike, and leave before several missing enemies close the exits. At six minutes, crash and move first toward Herald when your team can contest it. If two opponents answer the side lane, ping the opposite objective and disengage rather than assuming your team will convert automatically. Enter grouped fights from a side angle where Counter Strike can reach a carry without crossing every control spell.
gamePlan.lateGame: Late game, push the lane opposite the next objective only when there is enough time to rotate or threaten a structure before it falls. Jax can beat many isolated defenders, but crowd control and coordinated collapses still punish a blind split push. Use Counter Strike against the defender's attack window and Grandmaster-at-Arms for the damage that follows. If the enemy refuses the side lane, join your team from a flank and choose between stunning the carry or peeling the diver threatening your own backline.
gamePlan.teamfights: Come in from the side only after checking which spell can stop Leap Strike. Use Counter Strike to avoid incoming attacks and time the stun when nearby enemies can no longer step out, then cast Grandmaster-at-Arms where its area hit catches multiple champions for more armor. Counter Strike does not prevent spell damage or most crowd control, so do not treat it as permission to enter five champions alone. When a backline dive is not available, stay near your carry and stun the first attack-reliant threat that commits.

primaryRunes.note: More attack speed stacks the minigun faster, which is the tempo her damage depends on.

goodAgainst.note: Samira has to reach melee range to do anything, and your Flame Chompers plus rocket splash make that trip expensive. Her kit only gets going if you make mistakes.

Fishbones rockets and Zap! damage Vayne before she reaches Silver Bolts range, while Flame Chompers restrict the Tumble route she needs to enter or leave. Push with rockets, place Chompers between Vayne and the carry she wants to condemn, and use the safer range to reach items without giving her an isolated duel.

Fishbones rockets let Jinx punish Kai'Sa's short early range before Icathian Rain and Supercharge are evolved, and Flame Chompers cover the direct Killer Instinct landing. Push her off early last-hits, place Chompers on the marked target before she ults, and use the item lead to start resets before Kai'Sa reaches her evolution breakpoints.

weakAgainst.note: Smolder's stacks upgrade Super Scorcher Breath with area damage, percent-health burn, and eventually an execute, but they do not increase his attack or Q cast range. Jinx retains the longer rocket range, while Smolder threatens grouped teams if allowed to reach his late stack thresholds.
Ezreal pokes your immobile frame from spell range and blinks away from the Flame Chompers and rockets you would catch him with, all while farming safely behind his minions.
Miss Fortune bullies the exact early game you have to survive: her bounces chip you constantly, her strut outpaces your slow movement, and her ultimate punishes a carry with no way to sidestep it.

gamePlan.overview:
Jinx is a scaling carry with two weapons. Her minigun ramps attack speed for close fights, her rocket launcher splashes groups from long range, and swapping between them is the core of the champion. Get Excited! triggers when Jinx scores a takedown on an enemy champion, epic monster, or turret within three seconds of damaging it; a nearby death she did not help damage gives no reset.

Her plan is to farm safely with rockets from a distance and grow into late-game fights, where splash damage and Get Excited! resets let her chase a winning fight. Flame Chompers are her main disengage tool, and Super Mega Death Rocket can finish low-health targets across the map.

The downside is the usual hypercarry package: no dash, a weak early game, and heavy reliance on her team keeping her alive until she no longer needs them.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Prioritize farm because Jinx needs items before her sustained damage takes over fights. Rockets let you clear and poke from outside many trade ranges. Use them when the enemy duo crowds the wave, and swap to the minigun when your support starts a fight you can safely follow. Save Flame Chompers for an engage or gank path instead of spending them as poke. A stable lane with strong farm is enough; do not force an all-in solely to create an early lead.
gamePlan.midGame: Your items arrive and fights start to matter. Rockets splash enemies who stand together and chip them before objective contests. In skirmishes, stay at max rocket range until Jinx earns an eligible takedown after damaging the champion, epic monster, or turret, then use Get Excited!'s movement speed and total attack speed for the cleanup. Super Mega Death Rocket! can contribute from across the map, with damage increasing over travel distance and against a wounded primary champion target.
gamePlan.lateGame: You are the win condition and both teams know it. Siege with rockets, stay behind your peel, and play fights in two stages: careful rocket poke until an eligible takedown triggers Get Excited!, then use the reset to reposition and keep firing. Flame Chompers take 0.75 seconds to arm, so place them in a diver's path before contact rather than expecting an instant root. Do not chase so far that the reset separates you from your peel.
gamePlan.teamfights: Rockets first, minigun when a safe closer target lets you use its attack speed. Start at rocket range, splash their frontline and anyone clumped behind it, and place Flame Chompers early enough to arm in a diver's path. Get Excited! triggers only from a champion, epic-monster, or turret takedown within three seconds of Jinx damaging that target, not from every death in the fight. Survive the opening, then use a real reset to clean up.

Martial Poise hops around Void Ooze and lets Kalista stack spears while Kog'Maw is immobile, but Bio-Arcane Barrage reverses the damage race once his items arrive. weakAgainst.note: Tristana's jump lands faster than your hops can escape, and her burst and bomb out-trade you once she arrives. Your mobility is sideways, not away, so her direct dive ignores it.
Lucian's burst rotation lands inside one hop cycle, faster than your stacks can answer, and his mid-game spike punishes your hop pattern harder than any other lane bully.
Draven's axes hit harder than your spears stack, and his early all-in ends trades before your stacks build up. This is the one bully your mobility does not answer.

gamePlan.overview:
Kalista never stands still. A movement command during her attack windup or Pierce cast makes her dash in that direction, with dash speed and distance scaling from her boots tier. Attacks and Pierce lodge Rend spears, and the active rips all nearby stacks out for damage and a slow; if Rend kills any target, it resets its cooldown and restores mana rather than applying a separate execute threshold.

Her other signature is the Oathsworn bond. Fate's Call cleanses the nearby bonded ally, makes them invulnerable and untargetable while pulling them into Kalista, then the Oathsworn chooses where to launch and knocks back enemies on arrival. Kalista starts the save or engage, but the ally controls the launch destination.

The costs are real. Her damage depends heavily on attacks and Rend timing, while immobilizing effects, grounding, and polymorph prevent or knock down Martial Poise dashes. Attack-speed slows reduce how often she attacks and can hop, but they do not independently disable the dash. Without the Oathsworn nearby she loses Soul-Mark and Fate's Call access, not her basic attacks, Pierce, or Rend.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Trade early and collect spears. Your hop-weave wins long trades against most duos because half their answers miss a target that never stops moving. Stack spears through the exchange and Rend when the math turns lethal. Coordinate your ultimate with your support: a launched engage at level five catches duos who thought the lane was quiet. Respect crowd control above everything, because one stun is the only way most lanes can hold you still long enough to kill you.
gamePlan.midGame: Attack speed items create more attack windups, hop opportunities, and Rend stacks. Around dragon, remember Rend deals only 50% damage to epic monsters; it can still secure an objective in range through terrain, but calculate the reduced damage. Keep the Oathsworn within tether range when Fate's Call may be needed, and coordinate the ally-controlled launch before starting a play.
gamePlan.lateGame: If your rhythm holds, weave along the fight's edges, stack spears into whatever your team focuses, and Rend at the moments that matter. Hold Fate's Call as a safety net when the Oathsworn is within tether range, and coordinate whether the ally should launch back in or disengage. Position most carefully around roots, stuns, grounding, and polymorph, which directly stop Martial Poise; attack-speed slows reduce her output and hop frequency without disabling the dash by themselves.
gamePlan.teamfights: Weave at the fight's edge, putting spears into the closest safe target while Martial Poise repositions each attack. Rend when its damage secures a kill, triggers a reset, or wins an objective rather than spending all stacks too early. Fate's Call can retrieve the Oathsworn, but that ally; not Kalista; chooses the launch location and can knock enemies back on arrival. Immobilizing or polymorphing Kalista during a hop knocks her down, so do not dash predictably into crowd control.

gamePlan.overview:
Kog'Maw is an artillery carry the enemy team has to kill first. Bio-Arcane Barrage grants bonus attack range for eight seconds and adds percent maximum-health magic damage to every attack, making him exceptionally efficient into high-health frontlines. Late game, standing behind a good frontline, he is a major siege and sustained-damage threat.

Before that, he is one of the weakest laners in the game: slow, immobile, mana-hungry, and mostly just surviving bullies until his items arrive. Even his death deals damage, since his corpse sprints at someone and explodes.

His ultimate lobs artillery from a screen away, poking sieges and finishing runners. The whole champion asks one question: can your team keep something this valuable and this slow alive long enough to matter?
gamePlan.earlyGame: Farm from the edge of the enemy's engage range and let the matchup decide whether you can pressure. Bio-Arcane Barrage creates a strong trading window, but its downtime leaves your short range exposed, so back away before it ends. Use Caustic Spittle's resistance reduction before the attacks when a target is reachable, and place Void Ooze across the route a diver must take. Living Artillery can secure a distant minion or finish a short trade, but repeated casts increase its mana cost, so do not empty the bar before a gank or all-in.
gamePlan.midGame: Items make Bio-Arcane Barrage a real front-to-back threat. Clear the wave before rotating and approach objectives with the teammate who can peel, because arriving first alone only gives divers an easy target. Use Living Artillery to check or soften choke points, then activate the barrage after the frontline creates a safe firing line. If the map offers an even first-objective trade, Herald is usually the stronger immediate conversion. Commit to dragon when your composition can protect you through repeated teamfights and build toward soul.
gamePlan.lateGame: Late game, Kog'Maw can melt high-health frontliners if he is allowed to keep attacking. Arrive early with your team, choose a position that has both peel and a retreat path, and use Living Artillery to reveal or pressure enemies before they enter. Activate Bio-Arcane Barrage when targets will remain in range long enough to use the full window. Do not step through the frontline to reach a carry, since percent-health damage means the tank in front is already a productive target.
gamePlan.teamfights: Start behind your frontline with Living Artillery and Void Ooze controlling the approach. Apply Caustic Spittle's resistance reduction to the target your team can safely hit, then activate Bio-Arcane Barrage as the lines meet and maintain maximum range. Reposition during downtime rather than following a low target into fog. Icathian Surprise can trade damage after a death, but walking forward to make use of it is never the plan. Your contribution comes from uninterrupted attacks while allies force divers to cross the slow field.

Pressure Nasus's early last hits with Q marks and empowered attacks; pulling him away from a minion can deny that Q stack, but it never removes stacks he already earned. Wither still cripples K'Sante's attack speed and movement in All Out, so do not assume isolation guarantees the late duel.

Path Maker reduces Volibear's incoming burst and cannot be interrupted while charging, but his Thundering Smash stun still applies even though K'Sante ignores displacement. Use the charged dash or third Q to reposition him and avoid giving him a second Frenzied Maul on the same target.

Mundo has no hard crowd control to interrupt Path Maker, and K'Sante's passive gains target-max-health damage in All Out. Mundo's passive can block the first immobilizing effect and drop a canister, so break it with Q3 or Path Maker before relying on All Out to carry him through terrain.

Renekton's empowered stun and early Fury trades punish K'Sante outside Path Maker. He cannot interrupt Path Maker's charge, however, so use its damage reduction through the burst instead of treating the stun as a universal answer to the ability.

Ranged poison poke taxes K'Sante's patient lane and mushrooms punish predictable approaches. Path Maker still reduces all incoming damage while charging, not only one large hit, but spending it on steady poke can leave no charged displacement for the actual disengage.
Percent-health true damage skips your armor and grows with the health you stack, her Condemn answers your pull, and her rolls keep her out of wall range, so every entry you try she simply leaves.

gamePlan.overview:
K'Sante is two champions in one: a frontline tank who soaks engages, and a duelist who gives up much of that safety when his ultimate decides someone needs to die. All Out always roots and displaces its target, and if valid terrain is behind them it carries both champions through the wall for a much longer isolation. K'Sante then enters a 15-second form capped at 65% health with reduced defenses in exchange for attack speed, armor penetration, omnivamp, free basic abilities, and stronger target-max-health damage.

In lane he plays the long game. His Q stacks twice so the third cast pulls and stuns, Path Maker charges with 30% damage reduction and displacement immunity, and Footwork shields K'Sante while gaining extra range, speed, and terrain crossing when cast toward an ally. Path Maker's charge cannot be interrupted by crowd control, though non-displacement disables can still affect K'Sante while he finishes it.

The price is complexity and a thin early game. Misuse the W or mistime the ultimate and you are a squishy duelist standing where a tank should be.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Play patiently. Stack Q on the wave and the enemy, then use the empowered third cast to pull and stun. Weave a basic attack after an ability to consume Dauntless Instinct's mark, and spend Path Maker's charge through a predictable burst or displacement. Your kill pressure before items is modest, so trade for small advantages and use Footwork toward an allied champion or minion when its longer dash offers a safe exit.
gamePlan.midGame: Fix the Baron wave before moving to Herald, then frontline until a target steps close enough to useful terrain. Use the third Q or Footwork to create the angle and cast All Out only when the isolated duel is winnable and your team can survive without its tank. If no removal angle appears, keep Path Maker for the enemy engage and protect the river entrance. Return to the side wave after the objective so the opponent cannot take the turret while K'Sante waits for another skirmish.
gamePlan.lateGame: Push a side wave only when K'Sante can return before Baron or Elder is contested. In the fight, begin in tank form and use Path Maker to reduce the enemy engage while Q controls the frontline. Cast All Out through terrain when an important target is isolated and the lower defenses will not cause K'Sante to lose the duel. If the carry remains protected, stay with your own backline and peel instead of forcing the transformation.
gamePlan.teamfights: Two phases, one champion. Phase one: be the tank, reduce the engage with Path Maker, stack Q through the cluster, and pull divers off your backline. Phase two: when a key target is positioned in front of useful terrain, go All Out and take them through the wall. Entering All Out resets Q's stacks; if K'Sante had two stacks, Q's cooldown is refreshed but the empowered third cast is not carried into the new form. Path Maker also refreshes, gains 75% damage reduction and bonus true damage, but loses its normal knockback and stun. The transformation caps health and lowers defenses, so choose a duel the offensive bonuses can actually finish.
