coreItems.name: Amaranth's Twinguard
coreItems.note: Build this when you are fighting in the middle of the enemy team and need both armor and magic resist, which his ultimate commits him to.

situationalItems.name: Kaenic Rookern
situationalItems.note: Build this against one large magic burst when Malphite can choose the engage. The shield preserves his health while he waits for an Unstoppable Force angle instead of being poked out first.

situationalItems.name: Randuin's Omen
situationalItems.note: Build this when the enemy team has multiple crit champions. Malphite already wants to dive their marksman with Unstoppable Force, and the armor also strengthens the physical-damage protection built into his kit.

situationalItems.name: Chainlaced Crushers
situationalItems.note: Boot swap against heavy magic damage and crowd control, which lands on him before his ultimate does.

keystoneRune.name: Grasp of the Undying
keystoneRune.desc: Every 4 seconds in combat, your next attack against a champion deals bonus damage and heals you.
keystoneRune.note: Permanent health growth, which also grows a passive shield that is a percentage of maximum health.

primaryRunes.name: Unshakeable
primaryRunes.desc: Gain bonus armor and magic resist, increasing further when surrounded by enemies.
primaryRunes.note: His ultimate lands him in the middle of their team, which is when this gives the most.

primaryRunes.name: Second Wind
primaryRunes.desc: After taking damage from a champion, regenerate health over time.
primaryRunes.note: His shield blocks one hit, and this handles the steady chip that wears him off the wave instead.

primaryRunes.name: Overgrowth
primaryRunes.desc: Gain permanent maximum health when nearby minions or monsters die.
primaryRunes.note: He engages into the whole team, and the health is what lets him live past the knockup.

secondaryRunes.name: Manaflow Band
secondaryRunes.desc: Hitting an enemy champion with an ability permanently increases your maximum mana.
secondaryRunes.note: His trades are mana-hungry early, and a permanent pool increase lets him keep shoving and poking.

spells.name: Flash
spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

goodAgainst.note: Your E cuts the attack speed his whole champion runs on, your armor blunts his crits, and your Q steals the movement speed he chases with.

Counter Strike dodges Malphite's basic attacks but not Seismic Shard, Ground Slam, or Unstoppable Force. It still reduces incoming champion area damage by 25%, so Jax takes reduced damage from E and R while it is active; Ground Slam's cripple remains valuable after the dodge ends.
Windwall cannot block your slam or your ultimate, and your E strips the attack speed his crits depend on. His mobility answers none of it.

Most of Jayce's sustained damage is physical, so armor is efficient, but his Mercury Hammer transformation adds magic damage and no amount of armor makes careless ranged poke literally harmless. Preserve Granite Shield and engage after his acceleration gate or knockback is spent.

Fiora's Vital damage is percent-maximum-health true damage, so armor does not blunt it. Riposte can also block Unstoppable Force's damage and knockup even though Malphite has displacement immunity during the dash; bait the parry or engage another target.

Renekton's Fury combo is mostly physical, so armor reduces it, but Cull the Meek heals him; more when it hits champions; so he does have lane sustain. Trade around Granite Shield and avoid letting an empowered stun set up his full rotation.

weakAgainst.note: Granite Shield absorbs Darius's bleed like other damage; the bleed does not bypass shields. The problem is that repeated ticks delay Granite Shield from refreshing, while Apprehend pulls Malphite back before he can reset the trade.
The silence interrupts your trade pattern, his regen refunds your poke, and the spin grinds down your small early health pool.

Mundo's regeneration wins long poke wars, and his passive can block Unstoppable Force's knockup by consuming the canister effect. Malphite has no other immobilize to remove that passive himself, so coordinate with an ally before spending the ultimate on Mundo.

Spirit's Refuge blocks Malphite's basic attacks, including Thunderclap's empowered hit, but it does not block Q or E. Shen's taunt forces attacks and prevents spell use during the disable, while Stand United can turn a quiet lane into a cross-map numbers advantage.

Sion's health stacking and shield can outlast Malphite's lane poke, but Decimating Smash does not out-range Unstoppable Force. The real threat is Sion's long-range ultimate engage and his ability to keep scaling health through a quiet tank lane.

gamePlan.overview:
Malphite is built around the reliable engage from Unstoppable Force. Before level 5, protect health and manage the Baron wave so the opponent cannot build a lead. Once the ultimate is available, grouped enemies must respect his ability to cross distance and knock up several targets.

His lane is sturdier than it looks. Granite Shield refreshes to 11% of maximum health after Malphite avoids damage for several seconds. Seismic Shard slows a target and grants Malphite movement speed equal to the raw amount removed. Thunderclap passively grants bonus armor and empowers attacks in a cone when activated, while Ground Slam deals magic damage and cripples nearby enemies' attack speed. Armor investment improves his defenses and armor-scaling damage, but health and magic-resist items do not all add damage automatically.

His weaknesses are just as clear. He is slow outside Seismic Shard's stolen movement speed and leans heavily on armor against physical attackers. True damage ignores armor, but percent-health physical or magic damage is still reduced by the corresponding resistance; it is dangerous because it scales against his health, not because all percent damage bypasses armor.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Trade while Granite Shield is available and back away while it recharges. Use Seismic Shard when the opponent steps up for a last-hit, then add Ground Slam only if the wave and enemy jungler make the closer position safe. Against ranged lanes, preserve health and farm near the turret rather than spending all mana on poke. Reach level five without giving away a large wave, because Unstoppable Force creates the first reliable all-in and roam window.
gamePlan.midGame: Crash the Baron wave before moving to Herald or dragon, then approach through fog instead of showing the engage from the front. Use Unstoppable Force on a valuable cluster when allies are close enough to follow, and add Ground Slam immediately to reduce the attack speed of nearby carries. If the enemy spreads, hold the ultimate and frontline rather than using it only to reach one tank. Return to the side wave after the objective window so grouping does not give away the turret.
gamePlan.lateGame: Clear side waves early enough to join the Baron or Elder setup before vision is contested. With Unstoppable Force available, hold a fog or flank angle that makes the enemy carries respect grouping together. Without it, stay beside your carry, absorb damage, and avoid presenting a false engage that the team cannot follow. Use the ultimate when its knockup creates a clear damage window, not simply because several health bars appear in range.
gamePlan.teamfights: You have one job: land the ultimate on the most valuable cluster and let your team follow the knockup. Lead with it from fog when you can, follow with the slam, and Q whoever tries to leave early. If their team spreads out to deny you, that spacing is already a win, since five people standing apart fight worse than five standing together. Hold the ultimate until it matters; spending it on one tank throws the fight away.

startingItem.name: Long Sword
startingItem.note: Simple early attack damage. Three basic attacks build Double Strike stacks, then the following attack consumes them to strike twice; the second hit deals 50% AD and applies on-hit effects.

boots.name: Gunmetal Greaves
boots.note: Attack speed is the stat his whole kit converts into damage, since everything he has rides on-hit.

coreItems.name: Blade of the Ruined King
coreItems.note: Percent current health damage on every attack, stacking with the true damage his E already adds.

coreItems.name: Guinsoo's Rageblade
coreItems.note: On-hit magic damage that compounds with the rest of the build, since Blade of the Ruined King, Terminus and his own E ride the same attacks.

coreItems.name: Terminus
coreItems.note: Stacking penetration and resistances the longer he attacks, which suits a champion whose plan is to never stop attacking.

coreItems.name: Death's Dance
coreItems.note: Spreads burst damage out over a few seconds, which gives his W time to heal it back mid-fight.

coreItems.name: Guardian Angel
coreItems.note: Revives him once after dying. His ultimate keeps him moving but does not keep him alive.

situationalItems.name: Wit's End
situationalItems.note: On-hit magic damage and magic resist, with healing below half health that suits a champion who wins fights he is already losing.

situationalItems.name: Randuin's Omen
situationalItems.note: Build this when multiple crit carries can burst Master Yi after Alpha Strike. The crit reduction buys time to use Meditate and secure a takedown; Highlander then extends by seven seconds while his current basic cooldowns are reduced rather than fully reset.

situationalItems.name: Kraken Slayer
situationalItems.note: Every third attack lands missing-health damage. Double Strike follows a different four-attack cycle; three attacks build stacks and the next attacks twice; so the two effects periodically align rather than sharing the same cadence.

situationalItems.name: Mercurial Scimitar
situationalItems.note: Build this when one stun is what stops him. His ultimate ignores slows but not stuns.

keystoneRune.name: Lethal Tempo
keystoneRune.desc: Attacking champions grants attack speed. At maximum stacks, also gain attack range.
keystoneRune.note: Ramping attack speed, and his damage is entirely how many attacks he lands in a fight.

primaryRunes.name: Brutal
primaryRunes.desc: Attacks deal bonus adaptive damage to enemy champions.
primaryRunes.note: Bonus damage on every autoattack, scaling with his attack damage. His attack speed is among the highest in the game, so he procs it more often than anyone.

primaryRunes.name: Coup de Grace
primaryRunes.desc: Deal bonus damage to low-health enemies.
primaryRunes.note: His plan is finishing targets so Highlander's passive reduces current basic-ability cooldowns and its active duration extends. This helps secure the takedown that starts that chain.

primaryRunes.name: Legend: Alacrity
primaryRunes.desc: Gain permanent attack speed by taking down champions, monsters, and minions.
primaryRunes.note: More attack speed is more on-hit procs, which is the only scaling that matters to him.

secondaryRunes.name: Overgrowth
secondaryRunes.desc: Gain permanent maximum health when nearby minions or monsters die.
secondaryRunes.note: Permanent health from camps suits a melee carry who gets focused the moment he commits.

spells.name: Flash
spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

spells.name: Smite
spells.note: Required for Jungling. Secures objectives and sustains through camp clears.

goodAgainst.note: Xin Zhao wins the early skirmishes with his knockup and poke, but his power fades right as yours arrives, and late game your true damage and Highlander resets out-duel him easily.
One dive is Nocturne's whole plan, and you outscale it: Alpha Strike's untargetable window dodges his burst, and a fed Yi shrugs off his combo while Meditate and your resets finish the duel.
Kha'Zix can catch you out early, but once Highlander and your items are online you win the straight duel: Alpha Strike dodges his leap burst and your resets punish him for committing.

weakAgainst.note: Jarvan exists to answer champions like you: his flag-and-lance knockup cancels Alpha Strike the moment you leap, and his ult cage traps the chase so Highlander cannot bail you out.
Point-and-click lockdown ruins your dive: Vi's knockups cancel Alpha Strike mid-leap and her ultimate suspends you no matter how fed you are, and Highlander cannot save you while you are in the air.

Rammus punishes auto-attackers, and you are the purest one in the jungle: Defensive Ball Curl reflects your hits back at you, his taunt freezes you mid-combo, and no amount of scaling out-damages a tank who profits from your attacks.

gamePlan.overview:
Master Yi is the jungle's purest scaling pick: he farms quietly for the first stretch of the game, then walks into a teamfight and deletes the carries who were ahead of him. Alpha Strike blinks him between targets and makes him untouchable mid-leap, Wuju Style adds true damage that ignores armor, Meditate heals him between camps, and Highlander slashes his other cooldowns and speeds him up on every takedown. He is not a ganker who happens to scale; he is a farmer who becomes the win condition.

His plan is simple: power-farm, hit your item spikes, and turn into a champion nobody can peel off their carry. His early ganks are weak because his only slow comes from Wuju Style and he has no hard crowd control, so pre-five pressure needs a shoved lane or a target with no escape. Win one fight in the mid game and Highlander turns it into three.

His weakness never changes: crowd control switches him off. A stun lands the moment Alpha Strike ends, a knockup interrupts the leap, and one root cancels the Highlander chase. Fall behind early or get invaded and the scaling never arrives.
gamePlan.earlyGame:
Your first clear is about speed, not fighting. Alpha Strike hits several monsters at once and its cooldown ticks down as he attacks, so keep the route moving, keep Wuju Style up for the true damage, and use Meditate between camps. Take the scuttle on the side your team can support, but pick your fights, since Yi loses a straight crab duel to most early bruisers. The crab brings you to level five and Highlander, which is the first point a gank is worth walking for.

Even then, ganks are a favor to your lanes more than a real threat, because you have no crowd control and need a target that is already pinned or out of mobility. Look for lanes that are shoved in or enemies with their escape down, and otherwise clear, take the camps as they respawn, and bank the time. Above all, do not get caught invading: a Yi who loses his early camps to a predator never gets to play his game.
gamePlan.midGame:
Master Yi takes an exposed objective quickly but dislikes entering a prepared control chain. With no other nearby targets, Alpha Strike can mark the same monster repeatedly, but later marks deal 25% damage. Choose between Herald's immediate tower pressure and progressing toward a Dragon Soul based on lane priority and which side can move first.

Between objectives keep power-farming and gank while the camps respawn, since every camp sharpens your next spike. Commit Highlander when a takedown is realistic so its seven-second extension and basic-cooldown reductions pay you back, and never burn it walking into a fight where their crowd control is still up.
gamePlan.lateGame: At full build, wait for a route to the backline. Wuju Style's true damage ignores armor, and a takedown reduces current basic cooldowns while extending active Highlander. Alpha Strike is targeted at an enemy and returns Yi behind the primary target, so it is a gap closer and dodge; not a general escape unless a valid target creates a safe endpoint. Baron and Elder are where the monster damage matters most, but hard control at the reappearance point still ends the attack chain.
gamePlan.teamfights: Your job in a teamfight is to kill their carry, and the trick is patience. Do not be the engage. Wait on the flank while the enemy spends their stuns and knockups on your tank, then leap in with Alpha Strike, whose untargetable window can dodge a re-aimed spell, and put Wuju Style true damage into the squishiest target you can reach. The moment they drop, Highlander resets and you are already moving to the next one with bonus speed. That is how Yi chains kills in a single fight. The fights you lose are the ones where you jump first, get chain-stunned, and die before a single reset triggers, so let the fight start without you and end with you.

startingItem.name: Relic Shield
startingItem.note: Turns the wave into gold and health for an enchanter who is not last-hitting anything herself.

boots.name: Crimson Lucidity
boots.note: Ability haste shortens Lulu's shield, polymorph, and Wild Growth cooldowns. It is especially valuable, though ability power and heal-and-shield power also improve her protection and damage.

coreItems.name: Bulwark of the Mountain
coreItems.note: Quest income. Every point of gold turns into a bigger shield on her carry.

coreItems.name: Ardent Censer
coreItems.note: Her shield goes out on a short cooldown, so the attack speed and on-hit damage stay running on her carry.

coreItems.name: Knight's Vow
coreItems.note: She is already glued to one carry, so picking that champion means she takes their damage and heals off their output.

coreItems.name: Mikael's Blessing
coreItems.note: A cleanse she can hand her carry mid-dive, which her W could only answer by turning the diver off instead.

coreItems.name: Harmonic Echo
coreItems.note: Harmony builds from the moving and casting she does anyway, so the bonus healing is charged when her shield goes out.

situationalItems.name: Frozen Heart
situationalItems.note: Build this when the enemy team has a lot of attack speed dependent champions, which is what she is peeling off her carry anyway.

situationalItems.name: Staff of Flowing Waters
situationalItems.note: Shielding an ally gives her ability haste and ability power, which on her means more shields.

situationalItems.name: Shurelya's Battlesong
situationalItems.note: Team-wide speed on top of the move speed her buffs already grant, so a disengage takes everyone out at once.

situationalItems.name: Redemption
situationalItems.desc: Active AoE heal and enemy true-damage burn
situationalItems.note: Build this when Lulu must help a fight outside her direct cast range. Redemption can stabilize several allies after Wild Growth interrupts the dive, covering health bars her single-target shield cannot all reach.

keystoneRune.name: Aery
keystoneRune.desc: Your attacks and abilities send Aery to a target, dealing damage to enemies or shielding allies.
keystoneRune.note: Aery follows her shield as well as her Q, so it pays out on the button she presses most.

primaryRunes.name: Font of Life
primaryRunes.desc: Damaging enemy champions heals you and the lowest-health nearby ally after a short cooldown.
primaryRunes.note: Her Q and ultimate can hit enemy champions, healing her and the lowest-Health allied champion nearby when the rune is ready.

primaryRunes.name: Bone Plating
primaryRunes.desc: After taking damage from a champion, the next 3 instances of champion damage are reduced.
primaryRunes.note: Assassins go through her to reach the carry she is shielding, and this keeps her alive long enough to spend the ultimate.

primaryRunes.name: Revitalize
primaryRunes.desc: Healing and shielding are stronger, especially on low-health targets.
primaryRunes.note: This strengthens Help, Pix!'s shield, especially on a low-health ally. Heal-and-shield amplification does not increase Wild Growth's bonus health because bonus health is not a heal or shield.

secondaryRunes.name: Transcendence
secondaryRunes.desc: Gain ability haste, then reduce a basic ability's cooldown after it hits at level 9.
secondaryRunes.note: Ability haste means more Help, Pix! shields, Whimsy casts, and Wild Growth saves across a long fight.

spells.name: Flash
spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

goodAgainst.note: Attached Yuumi contributes a guided projectile, Zoomies' shield and attack speed, passive healing, and Final Chapter's heals and stacking slow; not only chip and a shield. Lulu can still pressure detach windows and save polymorph for the host's committed engage.

Lulu can add Pix damage and Whimsy attack speed to short trades, but Janna's tornado knockup and Monsoon knockback are hard disengage, not soft peel. Avoid fighting through both cooldowns and use polymorph on the carry Janna is trying to enable.

Polymorphing Milio himself prevents him from casting Breath of Life during that disable, but he can cleanse crowd control from allies when free to act. Force the ultimate first or control Milio directly before committing to his carry.

Help, Pix! can absorb part of Dark Binding's magic damage but does not prevent or cleanse its root. Whimsy can limit Morgana's follow-up only if Black Shield is absent, because the magic shield can block polymorph while it holds.

Place Whimsy's faerie ring on the ally Pyke wants to reach so it polymorphs him as he enters, but do not assume it cancels a dash already in motion or removes Death From Below's execute. Shields and Wild Growth bonus health can keep an ally above the execute threshold before it lands.

weakAgainst.note: His combo chains past your single polymorph, and once he ults he shrugs off the crowd control your peel relies on, so one save cannot answer his whole engage.

Zenith Blade reaches through Lulu's short poke range, Shield of Daybreak adds a second disable, and Solar Flare can begin the chain before Whimsy reaches the diver. Polymorph the enemy carry rather than the already-committed tank, save Wild Growth for the first focused target, and avoid trading forward while Leona holds the full engage.
Hook, knockup, and a root that triggers off his autos give him more engage tools than you have saves, and each one lands on a champion with no way to dodge.

Thresh layers Death Sentence's stun and pull, Flay's displacement, and The Box's heavy slow. Whimsy can disable one champion, while Dark Passage can shield and extract his ally after polymorph ends, so Lulu must avoid being the hook target herself.

gamePlan.overview:
Lulu turns one carry into a much harder target to reach. Pix fires three small bolts with Lulu's attacks, or with an allied champion's attacks after Help, Pix! transfers him; each bolt stops on the first enemy hit. Glitterlance fires one bolt from Lulu and one from Pix, with subsequent hits dealing reduced damage. Whimsy places a five-second faerie ring that enchants the first champion entering it, prioritizing enemies: foes are polymorphed, disarmed, and slowed, while an allied quick-cast grants attack and movement speed. Help, Pix! shields an ally but grants no speed trail. Wild Growth grants bonus health, knocks up nearby enemies, and leaves a seven-second slowing aura around the enlarged ally.

In the Dragon lane she combines poke with targeted protection. Glitterlance pressures the enemy duo, while Help, Pix! changes the spell's origin and shields the ally taking the trade. Whimsy and Wild Growth can interrupt a single committed diver, but layered threats may force Lulu to split those defensive cooldowns.

The catch is that her strongest protection is targeted and cooldown-dependent. She can combine an E shield, W polymorph, and Wild Growth in one fight, and the ultimate can disrupt several nearby enemies, but layered threats can force those tools onto different targets. Lulu herself is slow, squishy, and has no dash.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Use Help, Pix! deliberately to change Glitterlance's origin: shielding an advanced ally moves Pix to them, allowing the two bolts to cross different angles. Enemy-casting E instead reveals the target for four seconds and positions Pix behind them for the second Q line, but gives up the shield. Whimsy can be quick-cast on an ally for speed or planted as a ring to catch the first entering champion. Ward before stepping up because Lulu has no dash.
gamePlan.midGame: Mid game, use ally-cast Whimsy's movement speed; not Help, Pix!; to rotate or reposition. At objectives, place the faerie ring where a diver must enter, shield the carry through poke, and hold Wild Growth for the committed engage. Remember that the ring prioritizes an enemy champion if both teams enter it, which can turn a choke into reliable polymorph rather than accidentally spending the buff on an ally.
gamePlan.lateGame: Late game, stick to whichever carry the enemy wants dead most and shield them through poke. Wild Growth is strongest as divers enter its knockup radius, before all of their damage lands. It grants bonus health rather than healing, so Grievous Wounds does not reduce that health gain, and the enlarged ally keeps a slowing aura for seven seconds. Hold polymorph for the threat that remains after the knockup.
gamePlan.teamfights: Pre-shield the carry so Pix also fires with their attacks, then choose Whimsy's mode: ally-cast it for attack and movement speed when safe, or plant/target it on the diver for polymorph. Cast Wild Growth as enemies enter the ally's knockup radius, gaining both bonus health and interruption before its lingering slow helps kite. Lulu can use all three protective tools in one fight; the challenge is assigning each cooldown to the right target.

startingItem.name: Long Sword
startingItem.note: Simple early attack damage. His passive fires a second shot with its own scaling after every ability, so it pays twice.

boots.name: Immortal Treads
boots.note: The omnivamp keeps him healthy through the aggressive short trades his passive rewards.

coreItems.name: Essence Reaver
coreItems.note: Ability haste means more casts, and every cast arms another double shot, so it directly multiplies his passive.

coreItems.name: Galeforce
coreItems.note: A second dash next to his own, which suits a marksman whose pattern is dashing in for a double shot and back out.

coreItems.name: Magnetic Blaster
coreItems.note: The energized hit fits a champion already firing extra shots, and the range makes his short trades safer.

coreItems.name: Lord Dominik's Regard
coreItems.note: Build this against armor stackers, since his burst is a handful of shots rather than sustained fire. Choose it over Mortal Reminder when enemies are stacking health rather than healing, since Giant Slayer increases Lucian's damage against high-health targets.

coreItems.name: Infinity Edge
coreItems.note: Both shots of his passive can crit, so a crit spike pays out twice per ability he casts.

situationalItems.name: Mortal Reminder
situationalItems.note: Build this against armor stackers or enemies who heal through his short burst window. Choose it over Lord Dominik's Regard when enemy healing is the bigger problem, since Grievous Wounds stops targets from recovering Lucian's damage.

situationalItems.name: Guardian Angel
situationalItems.note: Revives him once after dying. His dash is short and usually spent aggressively.

situationalItems.name: Mercurial Scimitar
situationalItems.note: Build this when one removable disable stops his rotation or interrupts The Culling. Lucian can normally move and cast Relentless Pursuit during the ultimate channel, so crowd control; not the channel itself; is what prevents the dash.

keystoneRune.name: Empowerment
keystoneRune.desc: Build pressure in combat to enhance your burst and follow-up damage during trades.
keystoneRune.note: His trades are sharp burst windows opened by a dash rather than long fights.

primaryRunes.name: Brutal
primaryRunes.desc: Attacks deal bonus adaptive damage to enemy champions.
primaryRunes.note: Bonus damage on attacks is what makes his aggressive lane pattern work.

primaryRunes.name: Cut Down
primaryRunes.desc: You deal bonus adaptive damage (except true damage) to enemy champions above 60% health.
primaryRunes.note: His double shots come fast, and this is what makes that volume matter against a tank.

primaryRunes.name: Legend: Bloodline
primaryRunes.desc: Gain permanent omnivamp by taking down champions, monsters, and minions.
primaryRunes.note: Sustain for a marksman who has to step forward into range to land his double shots.

secondaryRunes.name: Sudden Impact
secondaryRunes.desc: Deal bonus true damage after using mobility or exiting stealth.
secondaryRunes.note: His E is a dash, so the bonus true damage lands on the double shot that follows.

spells.name: Flash
spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

goodAgainst.note: Your weave cancels her strut and out-bursts her bounce poke in every committed trade. Her big damage is a channel and yours is a rotation, and rotations win duels.

Piercing Light is a non-projectile line attack and is not destroyed by Blade Whirl. The wind wall does block Lucian's basic-attack projectiles, Lightslinger's additional shot, Ardent Blaze, and The Culling shots, so bait it before committing the projectile-heavy part of the rotation.

Piercing Light and Lightslinger front-load damage before Twitch has enough Deadly Venom for Contaminate, while Relentless Pursuit avoids the cask slow or his reveal angle. Push the early wave, dash sideways when Ambush opens, and force short burst trades before Spray and Pray turns the later fight into a range and uptime contest.

weakAgainst.note: Caitlyn punishes your walk-ups from a range your dash cannot bridge for free, and she controls the lane until her power curve dips into your mid-game spike.
Jhin punishes the exact aggression your kit wants: his root catches you mid-weave, his fourth shot out-trades your burst at a range your double-shot cannot answer, and Curtain Call zones your all-in.

Smolder's stacks upgrade Q with area damage, burn, and eventually an execute, but they do not increase his attack or Q cast range. Punish his weaker early lane before those damage upgrades outscale Lucian's short burst windows.

gamePlan.overview:
Lucian is a short-range marksman built around weaving abilities and attacks. After each ability, his next basic attack fires one additional shot for reduced AD damage; that second shot applies on-hit and on-attack effects and is affected by critical-strike modifiers. Relentless Pursuit resets his attack timer, and each Lightslinger attack reduces the dash's remaining cooldown, so clean ability; attack sequencing creates both damage and mobility.

Vigilance makes support pairing especially important. When a nearby ally immobilizes an enemy, or an ally heals or shields Lucian, his next two shots gain bonus magic damage, with up to four shots stored. Ardent Blaze adds another team interaction: Lucian gains movement speed whenever he or an ally damages its marked target, and an ally triggering the mark also grants Vigilance.

The trade-off is real, though. His range is short, his mana drains fast, and his late game flattens while hypercarries keep climbing. Lucian wins by turning early dominance into a lead the late game cannot take back.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Trade by casting once, consuming Lightslinger, then casting again instead of overlapping abilities before the empowered attack. Piercing Light targets an enemy but damages through the full line, so target a minion to reach a champion behind it. Watch mana between rotations: basic attacks remain available when empty, but no abilities means no extra Lightslinger shots or active dash. Coordinate with your support's heals, shields, and immobilizes so Vigilance is stored before the all-in.
gamePlan.midGame: Spend your lead while it is biggest. The Culling fires at the first enemy in its path, so a tank or minion wave can body-block shots rather than the channel shredding an entire clustered corridor. Use its three-second moving channel to pressure one line, and cast Relentless Pursuit during it to adjust the angle as enemies reposition.
gamePlan.lateGame: The hypercarries have arrived, so fight around single windows instead of long trades. Your burst still deletes squishy targets, but you get one rotation to prove it: dash in when their cooldowns are spent, burst the carry, and slide out before the answer lands. Position as the second-strike carry rather than the frontline damage, and use the Culling for zone control. Protect the lead you built, because it is the reason you still matter.
gamePlan.teamfights: Fight in burst windows. Stay at the fight's edge, weave each ability into a Lightslinger attack, and remember that those attacks refund Relentless Pursuit's cooldown by one second; or two on champion hits. The Culling can move and dash during its channel but every shot stops on the first enemy, so find a clear line to the priority target or use it to force movement. Allied control, healing, and shielding can load Vigilance during the fight for extra magic damage on the next shots.

startingItem.name: Long Sword
startingItem.note: Simple early attack damage, which speeds up the clear he needs to reach his transformation.

boots.name: Armorcrusher Boots
boots.note: Early lethality, since his whole pre-transformation window depends on chunking squishy laners.

coreItems.name: Youmuu's Ghostblade
coreItems.note: Momentum builds while he walks through walls between lanes, so the move speed and penetration are both active when he arrives.

coreItems.name: Manamune
coreItems.note: Turns his mana pool into attack damage, which matters because constant casting while clearing and skirmishing drains mana.

coreItems.name: Serylda's Grudge
coreItems.note: The slow holds a target still while his ultimate channel finishes, and the armor penetration keeps his burst lethal.

coreItems.name: Edge of Night
coreItems.note: The spell shield blocks the lockdown that catches him leaving a wall, which is the only moment his escape is unavailable.

coreItems.name: Guardian Angel
coreItems.note: Revives him once after dying. His ultimate attaches him to a target inside their team, so the exit does not always go to plan.

situationalItems.name: Duskblade of Draktharr
situationalItems.note: Bonus damage and a slow on the first hit against an unseen target, which is what an assassin opening on a backline needs.

situationalItems.name: Serpent's Fang
situationalItems.note: Build this when the enemy has shields that absorb the burst he came out of a wall to land.

situationalItems.name: Eclipse
situationalItems.note: His dash and sweep are two quick hits, which is all this needs to trigger. Gives max health damage and a shield.

keystoneRune.name: First Strike
keystoneRune.desc: Deal bonus damage for the first 3 seconds of combat with champions and gain gold.
keystoneRune.note: He chooses when to come out of a wall, so he always opens the fight.

primaryRunes.name: Sudden Impact
primaryRunes.desc: Deal bonus true damage after using mobility or exiting stealth.
primaryRunes.note: His dash and his ultimate both count, so the bonus true damage lands right as he arrives.

primaryRunes.name: Tyrant
primaryRunes.desc: Strengthen your damage output when brawling aggressively at close range.
primaryRunes.note: His snowball runs through picking off isolated laners, which is what this rewards.

primaryRunes.name: Eyeball Collector
primaryRunes.desc: Gain adaptive force by collecting takedown stacks from enemy champions and epic monsters.
primaryRunes.note: His ganks are built to convert into takedowns, so the stacks build faster than on a farming jungler.

secondaryRunes.name: Celerity
secondaryRunes.desc: Gain bonus movement speed and enhance other movement speed effects.
secondaryRunes.note: He spends the early game moving through terrain between camps and lanes, so move speed is his most-used stat.

spells.name: Flash
spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

spells.name: Smite
spells.note: Required for Jungling. Secures objectives and sustains through camp clears.

goodAgainst.note: Master Yi farms slowly and cannot defend his camps early, so your wall invades starve him, and once you transform you out-skirmish him cleanly before his item spikes arrive.

Shyvana's predictable full clears give Kayn time to cross walls with Shadow Step, steal camps, and create champion damage for his transformation before Dragon's Descent improves her ganks. Track her camp respawns, use Blade's Reach to slow her exit, and trade resources rather than taking the dragon-form duel once her Fury bar is ready.
Nunu is an objective bot with a weak personal duel, so you win the straight skirmish, and your wall-hops reach contested pits faster than his snowball setups arrive.

weakAgainst.note: Lee Sin is the early predator your pre-form window dreads: he wins scuttle fights, invades your camps, and bullies you before your form lands. Once you transform the matchup flips, but the early map is his.
Isolation is his whole game, and your weak pre-form body alone in the jungle is exactly the target he hunts. He leaps in, bursts you before you transform, and leaves before you collect your orbs.

Graves clears quickly, gains armor through Quickdraw, and lands multiple shotgun pellets when base Kayn uses Reaping Slash into melee before transforming. Avoid the first isolated river duel, enter through terrain after Smoke Screen or Quickdraw is spent, and reach form through safer ganks before contesting his camps directly.

gamePlan.overview:
Kayn is the jungler who transforms into one of two completely different champions, and damaging enemy champions builds progress toward each form. He starts every game as a weak base form waiting for its upgrade. Damage melee champions and tanks to become Darkin, a drain-tank bruiser who walks through walls and heals off whole teams. Damage ranged carries and mages to become Shadow Assassin, who deletes a backline and leaves before anyone reacts.

Until that transformation lands, he is a slippery skirmisher with one signature trick: Shadow Step lets him move through any wall on the map, which turns ganks into ambushes from angles nobody wards and makes escaping easy. Reaping Slash helps clear camps, while Blade's Reach slows targets during early ganks. The knockup only becomes available after choosing Rhaast. The whole early game is a countdown to the form that wins the match.

The catch is the wait. Pre-transformation Kayn is ordinary, and he has to survive the window where dedicated early junglers want to fight him for scuttle and push him out of his own jungle. Pick the wrong form, fall behind on orbs, or get bullied off camps, and the champion who should take over the map spends it catching up.
gamePlan.earlyGame:
Your first clear is about reaching level five safely and creating champion interactions for form progress. Use Shadow Step to approach a lane through terrain, then land Blade's Reach's slow and keep dealing damage to build progress toward the matching form. Base Kayn has no knockup until he becomes Darkin.

Scuttle is worth contesting only when the matchup and nearby lanes allow it. Damaging melee or ranged enemy champions provides the corresponding Darkin or Shadow form progress.
gamePlan.midGame:
Your chosen form determines how you approach the first major objective fights. Which one you want depends on your form: Darkin is happy to brawl over either, while Shadow Assassin would rather find the carry walking to it alone. Contest when your team is ahead on early fights, and in an even game take Herald and give up the dragon, unless your team fights well enough to play for soul.

Between objectives your tempo is the loop plus the walls: clear, gank while the camps respawn, and use Shadow Step to invade from angles nobody expects and steal a camp the enemy jungler is walking toward.
gamePlan.lateGame: Late-game Kayn follows the chosen form. Darkin heals from post-mitigation ability damage dealt to champions and adds max-health damage plus a knockup, while Shadow Assassin gains bonus magic damage during the first three seconds of champion combat and longer Umbral Trespass range. Takedowns do not reset Shadow Step; Shadow Assassin instead sets its cooldown to 10 seconds at all ranks, so use Umbral Trespass, terrain, and a later E cast to plan the exit.
gamePlan.teamfights: Your teamfight job depends on your form, and you should know it before the fight starts. Shadow Assassin opens from a flank nobody warded: Shadow Step through the wall, land on their carry, burst them, and leave through terrain before their team answers. Darkin plays the opposite way, walking in second through a wall onto the squishies, eating the crowd control your team would rather not, and out-healing the return fire while your spin damages the whole cluster. In both cases the wall is your weapon, so flank wide, pick the angle their peel is not watching, and enter once their lockdown is already spent. Walk in early and get chained, and you die instead of deciding the fight.

startingItem.name: Amplifying Tome
startingItem.note: Early ability power improves her spells, Searing Brilliance bolts, and the damage Overwhelm stores. The first Overwhelm stack stores a larger base amount; later stacks add smaller amounts rather than storing a fixed share of each hit.

boots.name: Spellslinger's Shoes
boots.note: Magic penetration improves her spell damage and the post-mitigation damage represented by Overwhelm's stored execute check.

coreItems.name: Luden's Echo

coreItems.name: Infinity Orb
coreItems.note: Crits against low health targets, which pushes enemies into the range where her stored damage pays out.

coreItems.name: Rabadon's Deathcap
coreItems.note: Multiplies her ability power, and every stack she stores scales with it.

coreItems.name: Cryptbloom
coreItems.note: Cuts the magic resist that would blunt a payload she spent the whole fight storing up. Choose it when enemies have not built much magic resist, so trading Void Staff's extra damage for more ability haste and an area heal after takedowns is worthwhile.

coreItems.name: Zhonya's Hourglass
coreItems.note: A second defensive window next to Rebuttal. Rebuttal surrounds Mel rather than covering one direction, makes her invulnerable to non-turret damage for 0.75 seconds, and reflects hostile champion projectiles that collide with it. Buy Seeker's Armguard early for armor and ability power.

situationalItems.name: Oceanid's Trident
situationalItems.note: Build this when the enemy has shields that keep absorbing the damage she was storing.

situationalItems.name: Morellonomicon
situationalItems.note: Build this when the enemy heals faster than she accumulates stacks. Buy Oblivion Orb early, since the anti-heal works from the component.

situationalItems.name: Stormsurge
situationalItems.note: Her stacked damage can trigger the mark, and the movement speed helps a mage with no dash. Rebuttal is an all-around barrier, not a directional shield.

situationalItems.name: Horizon Focus
situationalItems.note: Her bolts land from range, so the reveal and amplification trigger on the poke already building her stacks.

situationalItems.name: Blackfire Torch
situationalItems.note: Her bolts touch several enemies at once, so the stacking bonus counts multiple champions while she stacks on all of them.

situationalItems.name: Void Staff
situationalItems.note: The raw penetration alternative to Cryptbloom. Build it when a magic resist frontline is what blunts her payout. Choose it over Cryptbloom when enemies are stacking magic resist and maximum personal damage matters more than ability haste and team healing.

keystoneRune.name: Arcane Comet
keystoneRune.desc: Damaging a champion with an ability calls down a comet, dealing bonus damage.
keystoneRune.note: Her root and slow set up a target who cannot dodge it, so Comet lands almost every time.

primaryRunes.name: Manaflow Band
primaryRunes.desc: Hitting an enemy champion with an ability permanently increases your maximum mana.
primaryRunes.note: Her damage comes from casting constantly to build stacks, so more mana is directly more damage.

primaryRunes.name: Transcendence
primaryRunes.desc: Gain ability haste, then reduce a basic ability's cooldown after it hits at level 9.
primaryRunes.note: Ability haste means more casts, which is literally more stored damage for her ultimate.

primaryRunes.name: Scorch
primaryRunes.desc: Your next ability hit sets champions ablaze, dealing bonus magic damage.
primaryRunes.note: Her poke is a volley and back off, and Scorch adds damage to that trade.

secondaryRunes.name: Bone Plating
secondaryRunes.desc: After taking damage from a champion, the next 3 instances of champion damage are reduced.
secondaryRunes.note: She has to hold position to land her damage, and this blunts the burst thrown at her for standing there.

spells.name: Flash
spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

goodAgainst.note: Rebuttal can reflect Ahri's projectile Charm and Orb while making Mel invulnerable to non-turret damage for 0.75 seconds, but it does not reflect Spirit Rush itself. Time the barrier for the projectile portion instead of treating her entire dash combo as one reflected spell.

Rebuttal only copies hostile projectiles that collide with its barrier; it does not generically reflect every part of Syndra's sphere-and-Scatter combo. Use the invulnerability through non-projectile damage and reflect only the actual projectile components.

Mel gives Vex no Gloom mark from dashing because she has no dash, but Looming Darkness also applies Gloom on hit even when the target never moves. Track Doom's fear and do not assume Vex's passive is inactive simply because Mel stays still.

weakAgainst.note: Irelia resets Bladesurge when it kills the target or consumes a mark applied by her E or ultimate; she does not automatically reset merely for dashing to Mel. She can still chain marked minions around Solar Snare and wait out Rebuttal's 0.75-second window.
Once his ultimate is online he blinks past your snare over and over, and your reflect is on too long a cooldown to answer that, so he trades between windows.

Viktor out-ranges your volley and out-scales you, his shield soaks your poke, and his sustained laser gives your reflect nothing clean to catch, while his gravity field controls the ground you need to stand on.

Aurelion Sol's Singularity drags champions inward but does not root them, while Breath of Light is a sustained non-projectile beam that Rebuttal cannot reflect. Mel can use the brief invulnerability and movement speed to leave the area, but the scaling zone control remains difficult.

gamePlan.overview:
Mel is a patient long-range mage who builds Overwhelm on every damaging hit. The first stack stores a large amount of magic damage and each later stack adds a smaller amount; once the stored post-mitigation total exceeds a target's current health plus shields, Mel's next stack consumes them for that stored damage. Separately, each ability cast grants a Searing Brilliance stack, up to three, and her next basic attack consumes them to fire three extra bolts per stack.

Rebuttal surrounds Mel for 0.75 seconds, grants decaying movement speed, and makes her invulnerable to non-turret damage. Hostile champion projectiles that collide with it are destroyed and copied back with part of their original damage converted to magic, while non-projectile damage is prevented but not reflected. Golden Eclipse can be cast only when an enemy champion has Overwhelm and damages every Overwhelm-marked enemy globally; it does not damage a neutral objective itself.

The catch is that she has no dash or blink. The snare and the reflect are her only ways out of trouble, and she burns mana fast early. Anyone who gets past the snare or bursts her after the reflect window closes runs her over, so positioning and patience are the whole champion.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Lane carefully and watch your mana. Use the volley to keep the wave shoved and farm from max range, but do not throw every spell at the enemy or you will be empty when the jungler shows up. Land snares from distance to set up your own ganks, and hold the reflect for the moment an aggressive laner commits their combo. Against anything mobile, stay away from river bushes you cannot see, because with no escape every gank is a real threat.
gamePlan.midGame: With the wave under control, Mel can globally damage enemies who still carry Overwhelm, but she must first have applied those stacks and an enemy champion must be marked before Golden Eclipse is castable. Keep poking with Radiant Volley, save Solar Snare for choke points, and weave the Searing Brilliance attack after up to three ability casts instead of wasting its nine possible bolts.
gamePlan.lateGame: Range and global reach make Mel a constant background threat. Sit behind your frontline, build Overwhelm on champions, and use Golden Eclipse to damage those marked enemies globally. It cannot hit or secure Baron, Dragon, or Herald directly, though damaging the enemy jungler can affect the contest. Save Rebuttal for the most dangerous damage window or projectile volley rather than describing it as a one-direction answer.
gamePlan.teamfights: Position is everything. Use Solar Snare's root and expanding slow area to control the dive, build Overwhelm through repeated damage, and time Rebuttal for either a dangerous projectile or a non-projectile burst that the invulnerability can absorb. Track which enemies still carry Overwhelm before Golden Eclipse, and weave the Searing Brilliance attack after ability casts for the extra bolts.

coreItems.note: Physical vamp that increases on critical strikes helps her sustain through jungle skirmishes where she cannot always fight behind a frontline.

situationalItems.name: Mortal Reminder
situationalItems.note: Build this against armor stackers or enemies who heal long enough for her mark to expire. Choose it over Lord Dominik's Regard when enemy healing is the bigger problem, since Grievous Wounds stops targets from recovering Kindred's damage.

situationalItems.name: Kraken Slayer
situationalItems.note: Every third attack lands missing health damage, which suits a champion already stacking attacks on one target.

situationalItems.name: Infinity Edge
situationalItems.note: A crit spike for a champion whose late game is kiting from a range nobody can close.

keystoneRune.name: Empowerment
keystoneRune.desc: Build pressure in combat to enhance your burst and follow-up damage during trades.
keystoneRune.note: Her trades are burst windows created by her dash rather than long fights, which is what this rewards.

primaryRunes.note: Bonus damage on every autoattack, which sharpens the early duels her range already wins.

primaryRunes.name: Cut Down
primaryRunes.desc: You deal bonus adaptive damage (except true damage) to enemy champions above 60% health.
primaryRunes.note: Her attacks are percent-health already in spirit, and this stacks with that against the biggest target in the fight.

primaryRunes.name: Legend: Alacrity
primaryRunes.desc: Gain permanent attack speed by taking down champions, monsters, and minions.
primaryRunes.note: Attack speed means faster stacks on a marked target, so Wolf's pounce comes out sooner.

secondaryRunes.name: Sudden Impact
secondaryRunes.desc: Deal bonus true damage after using mobility or exiting stealth.
secondaryRunes.note: Her Q is a dash, so the bonus true damage lands on the arrows that follow.

spells.name: Flash
spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

spells.name: Smite
spells.note: Required for Jungling. Secures objectives and sustains through camp clears.

goodAgainst.note: Warwick only wins if he catches you with your dash down, since your kiting keeps his chase from ever connecting and Lamb's Respite turns his suppress dive into a free reset.

Dance of Arrows and Mounting Dread let Kindred kite Shyvana before Dragon's Descent gives her a reliable gap closer, while early Hunt marks reward invading her predictable farm route. Contest the marked camp with lane priority, save the dash for Burnout's approach, and leave once her Fury bar is full because dragon form reverses the spacing advantage.

weakAgainst.note: Hecarim's speed and rampage knockback let him close on you no matter how you kite, and a Kindred who cannot create distance is just a squishy with a bow.
Rammus rolls at you faster than you can make space, and once Powerball connects his taunt freezes you in place while your own attacks chunk you through his spikes.
Lee Sin spikes a full tempo before you, and his early kit erases the space your kite needs: Safeguard closes the gap, Resonating Strike sticks to you, and the kick flings you into his team.

gamePlan.overview:
Kindred is a ranged carry jungler who scales through marks instead of waves. Mark of the Kindred calls a hunt on a jungle camp or an enemy champion, and every mark you collect makes your attacks reach farther and hit harder. Wolf clears the camps while Lamb repositions with Dance of Arrows, so your pathing is quick, your range is unfair, and your early game is about collecting marks across the map before the enemy jungler catches you doing it.

You win by snowballing that hunt into a lead nobody can claw back. A fed Kindred kites entire teams from a screen away, and Lamb's Respite turns the worst moment of a fight into a free reset: drop the zone and for a few seconds nothing inside it can die. The fantasy is a marksman who jungles, picks her fights, and refuses to be caught, and the payoff is a backline carry who happens to own a smite.

The catch is that you are a squishy ranged champion with no hard crowd control, and your clear leans on Wolf doing most of the work. Deny your marks and you are a below-average duelist on a body that folds to one good engage. Kindred games are decided by whether you stack marks early or spend the whole match getting denied them.
gamePlan.earlyGame:
Begin your normal clear while watching the first monster Wolf marks; you cannot choose Wolf's target or mark your own opening camp. The first eligible target is a Rift Scuttler, the pool of enemy-jungle monsters changes as your stack count rises, and at eight or more marks Wolf can select an epic neutral objective. Weave Dance of Arrows inside Wolf's Frenzy to use its reduced cooldown, and contest a marked target only when your lanes can move first. Select a realistic enemy champion hunt before a gank, remembering that the mark takes eight seconds to apply and warns the target.

Ward your entrances and track lane priority, because Kindred cannot damage or remove Wolf's monster mark and enemies can use its public location to predict an invade or set a trap.
gamePlan.midGame:
The first objective rotation tests whether your marks and lane pressure have created enough room to contest. Lamb's Respite can delay both teams' Smite attempts by protecting the monster at 10% health, but it protects enemy champions in the zone too, so contest when your team can control the expiry. In an even game Herald may be the safer trade, though a Wolf mark on the dragon side can justify contesting that dragon when your lanes have priority.

Between objectives, choose the enemy jungler as Lamb's champion hunt when you expect to meet them, then use Wolf's independently selected monster mark to plan the counter-jungle fight. Invade only with lane priority; the marked camp is visible to both teams and is often bait. Keep ganking lanes that bring reliable lockdown, because Kindred supplies a slow rather than a stun.
gamePlan.lateGame: By late game a heavily marked Kindred is a second carry the enemy has to respect, kiting from greatly extended attack range. Play the backline, deal damage from the edge of every fight, and hold Lamb's Respite for the exact moment it flips the math: during a Baron contest, as your carry gets dived, or as your team trades into a losing fight. Do not chase a single mark into a death this late, and remember that the zone also protects enemies standing inside it. Group for objectives and let your range do the work a tankier jungler would do with their body.
gamePlan.teamfights: Fight from maximum attack range and keep Dance of Arrows available to create space from a diver. Place Wolf's Frenzy where the fight will remain long enough to benefit from its area. Use Lamb's Respite when lethal damage is about to land, then prepare your next attack and Smite timing for the zone's end. Remember that enemies inside are protected as well, so an early cast can delay your own team's damage and objective secure.

coreItems.note: Revives her once after dying. Her channel commits her completely.

situationalItems.note: Build this against armor stackers or enemies who heal, since they stand between her and the targets she wants.

situationalItems.name: Magnetic Blaster
situationalItems.note: Extra range for a champion who has to hold a position while channelling.

situationalItems.name: Serpent's Fang
situationalItems.note: Build this when the enemy has shields that absorb a channel she cannot repeat for another minute.

situationalItems.name: Immortal Treads

situationalItems.name: Mercurial Scimitar
situationalItems.note: Build this against removable crowd control that prevents Miss Fortune from beginning or maintaining her positioning. Bullet Time can also be ended by other cast-inhibiting control, displacement, death, or her own recast; not only a stun.

keystoneRune.name: Conqueror
keystoneRune.desc: Gain stacks by damaging enemy champions. At maximum stacks, gain bonus damage and healing.
keystoneRune.note: Stack it with attacks, Q and E before channeling her ultimate. The adaptive damage and vamp then strengthen her full damage window.

primaryRunes.desc: Attacks deal bonus adaptive damage to enemy champions.
primaryRunes.note: Bonus damage on every autoattack, which sharpens the poke her lane is built on.

primaryRunes.name: Cut Down
primaryRunes.desc: You deal bonus adaptive damage (except true damage) to enemy champions above 60% health.
primaryRunes.note: Her ultimate hits everyone in front of her, and this makes the biggest of them actually take it.

primaryRunes.name: Legend: Bloodline
primaryRunes.desc: Gain permanent omnivamp by taking down champions, monsters, and minions.
primaryRunes.note: Sustain for a marksman who holds a fixed position through her most important cast.

secondaryRunes.name: Bone Plating
secondaryRunes.desc: After taking damage from a champion, the next 3 instances of champion damage are reduced.
secondaryRunes.note: Her ultimate is a channel, and this is what keeps her standing through the burst thrown to interrupt it.

spells.name: Flash
spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

goodAgainst.note: Your bounce poke reaches her through the minions her headshot game hides behind, and your strut dodges the trap zones that anchor her control. Her range punishes passive farmers, and you are not one.
Draven has to juggle axes inside your bounce range, and every catch he walks toward eats a Double Up. Your strut keeps your spacing while he is locked into his axe rhythm.

Jinx is vulnerable to early Double Up bounce angles, but Bullet Time is a fixed directional cone she can walk out of or interrupt indirectly with zoning. Use Make It Rain or allied control first instead of treating the channel as undodgeable.

weakAgainst.note: Tumble leaves Double Up's bounce line, Silver Bolts punish Miss Fortune in any extended duel, and Condemn interrupts Bullet Time before the channel pays off. Win through early wave pressure and Make It Rain poke, cast Bullet Time only after Condemn is spent, and avoid the isolated side-lane fight once Vayne has items.
Ezreal pokes from a range your bounces cannot answer, and his blink slips the ultimate you would zone him with. Your strut does nothing about damage that arrives from outside your reach.
Lucian's dash rotation bursts you between your bounce cooldowns and cancels the strut speed that wins you other lanes. His early game beats yours by a real margin.

gamePlan.overview:
Miss Fortune's attacks and abilities build up to three Love Tap stacks on enemy champions and epic monsters. The third stack deals bonus physical damage, and all attacks and abilities deal increased damage while the target remains at maximum stacks; one ability cannot add stacks more than once per second. Double Up hits the first enemy, bounces behind them with priority for units directly in line, applies on-attack effects to the first target, on-hit effects to both, and immediately gives the second target maximum Love Tap stacks.

Strut gains movement speed after avoiding non-persistent damage, grants that speed immediately when activated, and adds attack speed for four seconds. Damaging a maximum-Love-Tap target reduces its cooldown. Make It Rain grants sight and repeatedly slows in an area, while Bullet Time channels a fixed cone for up to three seconds and each wave can critically strike for reduced bonus critical damage.

Her weaknesses are the classic ones: no dash or blink, no hard crowd control of her own, and a channel that cast-inhibiting control or displacement can interrupt. Make It Rain still provides a meaningful slow, so she is not literally without crowd control.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Trade from the first wave, but keep the bounce angle separate from the enemy support's engage range. Aim Double Up through a minion so the prioritized bounce reaches the carry behind it; the second hit gains maximum Love Tap stacks and its built-in critical strike without needing the first target to die. Follow with an attack or ability to exploit the maximum-stack damage amplification, then disengage before the return trade. Taking non-persistent damage removes Strut's passive movement speed, so do not rely on it to escape after stepping too far forward.
gamePlan.midGame: Your first items and Bullet Time make grouped river fights your best window. Clear the wave, rotate with your support, and search for a channel across a choke after allied control lands. Do not force the first dragon simply because your ultimate is ready. Herald is usually the stronger even trade, while a composition with reliable setup and strong five-versus-five fighting can use your area damage to take all three dragons and claim soul. Infernal soul is the strongest payoff when it is available, but lane priority still decides whether the first contest is safe. Before either call, use Double Up and Make It Rain to soften the entrance without exposing the channel.
gamePlan.lateGame: Late game, your sustained attacks still matter, but the clean Bullet Time angle is what separates you from other carries. Hold the fight's edge, track the enemy spells that interrupt channels, and wait for their movement to be restricted before casting. Use Make It Rain to slow an approach or protect your firing line, then continue attacking after the channel rather than treating your job as finished. A hidden flank can create the best angle, but only if vision confirms that reaching it will not get you caught.
gamePlan.teamfights: Find the firing line before bodies collide. Open with Double Up bounce pressure and Make It Rain on the choke, then hold Bullet Time until allied control lands or the enemy's interrupt is committed elsewhere. Firing from behind your frontline into a fixed formation is safer than opening the fight with an exposed channel. If no full channel exists, keep attacking from range and wait, because several seconds of normal damage are better than an ultimate cancelled immediately.

startingItem.note: Support income for an enchanter who spends the lane buffing rather than farming.

boots.name: Crimson Lucidity
boots.note: Ability haste is what changes his impact, since his value is how often his shield and range buff are up.

coreItems.note: Quest income, which funds the enchanter items his kit is designed around.

coreItems.name: Ardent Censer
coreItems.note: His shield has two charges, so the attack speed and on-hit damage stay running on his carry almost permanently.

coreItems.name: Harmonic Echo
coreItems.note: Harmony builds from the moving and casting he does anyway, so the bonus healing is charged when his W goes down.

coreItems.name: Mikael's Blessing
coreItems.note: A second cleanse next to his ultimate, so he can answer two lockdown attempts in one fight instead of one.

coreItems.name: Staff of Flowing Waters
coreItems.note: Shielding an ally gives him ability haste and ability power, which on him means more shields.

situationalItems.name: Locket of the Iron Solari
situationalItems.note: A team-wide shield for the fights where area damage rather than one target is killing his team.

keystoneRune.name: Aery
keystoneRune.desc: Your attacks and abilities send Aery to a target, dealing damage to enemies or shielding allies.
keystoneRune.note: Aery follows his shield as well as his Q, so it pays out on the button he presses most.

primaryRunes.desc: Damaging enemy champions heals you and the lowest-health nearby ally after a short cooldown.
primaryRunes.note: Ultra Mega Fire Kick can trigger Font of Life while peeling from range, healing Milio and the lowest-health nearby ally before his shields and healing zone continue the trade.

primaryRunes.name: Bone Plating
primaryRunes.desc: After taking damage from a champion, the next 3 instances of champion damage are reduced.
primaryRunes.note: He has no escape and stands in range to heal, so the engage aimed at him is what this cuts down.

primaryRunes.desc: Healing and shielding are stronger, especially on low-health targets.
primaryRunes.note: This strengthens Cozy Campfire's healing, Warm Hugs' shield, and Breath of Life's heal. His Q and Fired Up damage are not heals or shields.

secondaryRunes.name: Transcendence
secondaryRunes.desc: Gain ability haste, then reduce a basic ability's cooldown after it hits at level 9.
secondaryRunes.note: Ability haste means more shields, campfire uptime, kick peel, and Breath of Life casts; ability power and heal-and-shield power also affect his impact.

spells.name: Flash
spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

goodAgainst.note: Seraphine brings more than poke: Beat Drop can root or stun under the right conditions, and Encore charms a line of champions. Breath of Life can cleanse those non-airborne disables if Milio is free to cast, while Campfire sustain helps against her ranged damage.

Breath of Life can cleanse Leona's root and stuns from nearby allies, but Milio cannot cast it while he himself is disabled. Position outside Solar Flare and Zenith Blade so the cleanse remains available after Leona commits.

Zilean can slow with Time Warp and a double Time Bomb can stun, so he does have pick setup. Breath of Life cleanses those non-airborne effects, but Chronoshift can still revive the target Milio's team commits to.

Milio's kick is itself a knockback and stun that can start a pick, while Janna can punish with Zephyr and tornado. Breath of Life cleanses slows but not airborne crowd control, so it cannot remove Howling Gale's knockup or undo Monsoon's displacement.

Morgana also brings Tormented Shadow, Black Shield, and Soul Shackles; not only Dark Binding. Breath of Life can cleanse a nearby ally's root or tether stun if Milio remains free to cast, but it cannot be used while Milio himself is under cast-inhibiting crowd control.

weakAgainst.note: His hook removes the spacing your game depends on, one pull on your immobile frame skips the cleanse entirely, and while a heal does lift a target back over his execute threshold, your healing is a trickle next to the burst that puts them under it.
A landed Death Sentence drags you out of position past anything your cleanse can fix, his lantern undoes the dive you peel, and his flay interrupts the moments you need to react.
Senna wins the attrition mirror on raw numbers: she out-ranges your poke, heals nearly as well while adding real damage, and brings almost no crowd control for your cleanse to answer.
You are his easiest target: one hook through a wave gap deletes an enchanter with no escape, your cleanse does not undo the pull, and his threat range alone zones you off your poke spots.

gamePlan.overview:
Milio extends a carry's attack range while layering healing, shields, and peel. Ultra Mega Fire Kick knocks back and stuns the first enemy hit, then bounces forward into an explosion that slows; kicking a non-champion sends the ball farther and makes the explosion larger. Cozy Campfire self-cast creates an aura for Milio and nearby allies, while ally-cast tethers only Milio and that champion. Both versions grant attack range, periodic healing, and Fired Up at cast and every three seconds.

Warm Hugs has two charges, and its shield and movement speed can stack twice. Breath of Life heals and cleanses Milio and nearby allies of non-airborne crowd control, then grants 65% tenacity for three seconds. It cannot be cast while Milio is affected by cast-inhibiting crowd control, and it cannot cleanse knockups, so his positioning determines whether the team-saving button exists.

The catch is that everything he does is reactive and his own body is easy to kill. Slow, fragile, no escape: a hook or flank that reaches him is not cleansed, it is a kill. Roams punish him because he cannot answer a pick across the map, and if he gets caught, the carry he was protecting is suddenly alone.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Play the early lane patiently. Cozy Campfire grants attack range and healing and applies Fired Up at cast and every three seconds; the enchanted ally's next attack or ability hit adds bonus magic damage and a burn, not a slow. Use Ultra Mega Fire Kick directly on a champion for the knockback and one-second stun, or kick a minion to create the farther, larger slow explosion behind it. Stack Warm Hugs' two charges when the shield and movement speed are both needed.
gamePlan.midGame: Leave Dragon lane only after the wave is safe, then move with the carry or jungler to establish river vision. At objectives, cast Cozy Campfire on yourself to affect nearby teammates or tether it to the ally who needs the range and healing. The tether can move to a new ally after one second, and Warm Hugs or Breath of Life cast on Milio or the tethered ally mirrors the effect to the other. Use that link to protect two positions while staying outside the enemy's engage range.
gamePlan.lateGame: Before Baron or Elder, rotate with teammates and ward from behind the frontline rather than checking brush alone. Hold Breath of Life for nearby non-airborne control and stay far enough back that Milio is not disabled before he can cast. It heals, cleanses, and grants follow-up tenacity, but it cannot undo displacement that already moved the team. Use both Warm Hugs charges between larger cooldowns and keep the tether on the carry the enemy is preparing to dive.
gamePlan.teamfights: Extend the carry's range with Cozy Campfire and move the tether if another ally becomes the focus. Use the fire kick's knockback and stun on the first diver, with its later explosion slowing enemies behind them. Breath of Life should follow non-airborne control only while Milio remains free to cast; it cannot cleanse knockups. Warm Hugs' two stackable charges provide the movement speed and shields needed between those larger cooldowns.

gamePlan.overview:
Morgana is a control jungler who turns one binding into a kill and one shield into a stolen teamfight. Her clear runs on Tormented Shadow, a pool of magic damage she drops on a camp and leaves ticking while she moves to the next, so she farms at a comfortable pace without brawling the monsters. The rest of her kit is for people: Dark Binding is a long root, Black Shield puts a bubble on an ally or herself that eats the next crowd control, and Soul Shackles chains everyone near her and stuns them if they cannot get away in time.

She wins by deciding whether a fight happens at all. Early on, her threat is the bind: a gank into a pushed lane is a root, a pool on their feet, and a laner walking up to finish. She is not a duelist and her clear is not fast, so the opening minutes are about landing that one skillshot and farming safely between attempts. Once she has her first item and her ultimate, she becomes a control engine: root the carry, shield her own out of the enemy's engage, chain a whole huddle into a stun.

Dark Binding is her only ranged hard control, and missing it gives mobile opponents time to enter or leave. Morgana has no dash, so stronger early junglers can punish her during that cooldown. Use vision and allied lane priority to choose entrances where the target has less room to sidestep.
gamePlan.earlyGame:
Center Tormented Shadow under the large monster and keep it damaging the camp while you reposition, which lets Morgana clear without spending much health. That reliable route is usually worth finishing, but a lane with guaranteed allied control can justify an earlier Dark Binding visit. Do not race an early duelist into an unsupported river fight just because your camps fell quickly.

Approach a gank from an angle that puts the target's escape behind the minion wave, land Dark Binding, then place Tormented Shadow for the full root duration. Black Shield is often more valuable in a counter-gank, where it can deny the enemy's opening control and let your laner turn. Track the opposing jungler and keep Binding available near contested entrances, because Morgana has no dash when that spell misses.
gamePlan.midGame:
Soul Shackles turns a crowded objective entrance into a choice between scattering and being stunned. Set vision at dragon and Herald, then choose between Herald's immediate tower pressure and progressing toward a Dragon Soul based on which lanes can move first.

Between objectives you out-utility most slow farmers: shield a teammate through their gank and turn it around, or chain an invading duo with your ultimate. Keep clearing between plays so you stay on the item curve, since your value is the cooldowns you bring to a fight.
gamePlan.lateGame: Late game your job is control, and your damage is the least interesting thing about you. Your solo kill pressure has not improved, so stop hunting picks alone and use your tools: a bind on the carry who steps forward, a shield on your own carry the moment the enemy assassin commits, and a chained stun when the teams collide. Black Shield wins late games on its own by eating the one piece of crowd control a fight is built around. Around Baron and Elder you are both the disengage and the lockdown: root the initiator before they reach the pit, or shield the teammate they were about to delete. Patience is the skill here. Hold your bind for the body that matters, because a root wasted on a tank is a fight handed back.
gamePlan.teamfights: You are the controller: you either start the fight with a pick or decide it by blanking theirs. The clean opener is a bind on a priority target that your team folds onto before the root ends, with your pool dropped underneath. Soul Shackles is your engage and your zone at once: walk or flash into the cluster, chain everyone, and force them to scatter or eat the stun, which buys your carries a free damage window. The button that actually wins the fight is Black Shield. Read the enemy's engage, find the ally they are about to lock down, and bubble them just before the crowd control lands, because an engage that hits a shielded target achieves nothing. Never spend your bind on the frontline just because the fight started; hold it for the carry, the assassin, or the initiator.

Black Shield can prevent Nautilus's hook displacement, passive root, or ultimate knockup while it holds, but his magic damage can break the shield and expose the target to later control. It is a timed health-limited immunity, not free protection from his whole kit.

Rakan has Grand Entrance's knockup as well as The Quickness charm, and Battle Dance lets him dash back to an ally rather than forcing a fixed return timer. Black Shield one engage layer while it holds, then aim Binding at his actual exit path.
