Black Shield deletes the Concussive Blows stun his trades build toward, so he cannot peel your picks, and his defensive kit loses the poke war yours forces.

weakAgainst.note: Zyra's repeated magic damage can break Black Shield, after which her root or ultimate knockup can affect the target. The shield can block more than one control effect while it still has health; the problem is Zyra has enough spell and plant damage to remove it first.
Her healing refunds every trade you win, and her silence lands on your cast animations, cutting off the binding and shield in the exact fights you saved them for.
Senna pokes from beyond your binding range and scales off every soul the lane gives her, while your shield blocks crowd control she barely uses.
His ultimate cleanses the binding your whole game is built to land, his poke matches yours with sustain attached, and his range buff keeps his carry outside your root line.
Her trade pattern beats yours: she heals back the poke she loses while your chip stays lost, and her Tidecaller damage stacks up while your shield waits for crowd control worth blocking.

gamePlan.overview:
Morgana is a support who can deny a crucial engage. Black Shield absorbs magic damage and grants its allied target crowd-control immunity for up to five seconds while the shield health holds. It can block multiple control effects if it survives, while physical damage passes through without reducing the magic shield; enough magic damage removes the immunity before later control arrives.

Her own offense is poke and picks. Tormented Shadow clears waves and chips anyone standing in it, and Dark Binding is a long-range snare that holds a target long enough for your marksman to secure the kill. Soul Shackles tethers nearby enemies and stuns them if they cannot break the leash, which turns her into a second engage when the fight clumps up.

The catch is that she is slow with no escape. The bind is her whole pick threat and it can be dodged, so a miss leaves her with just poke and a shield. Mobile supports walk away from the root and the tether, and dive comps and assassins line up against her squishy frame.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Play beside or behind the wave so minions block hostile skillshots without blocking every Dark Binding angle. Use Tormented Shadow to pressure a last-hit or complete the support quest, but avoid pushing automatically when the enemy jungler is missing. Hold Dark Binding for a clear line or for the support who commits onto your carry. Pre-cast Black Shield when the enemy engage is telegraphed; spending it on minor poke can leave the carry exposed to the next control spell.
gamePlan.midGame: At dragon or Herald, a pre-emptive Black Shield can deny the first control spell, but watch its remaining health because magic damage may break it before the next disable. Use Binding for picks and Soul Shackles when several enemy champions are nearby; the ultimate is a three-second tether rather than a channel and continues in Zhonya's, provided Morgana stays close enough for the stun.
gamePlan.lateGame: Late game you have two decisions that swing teamfights, and the question is who gets each one. Black Shield goes on whichever ally the enemy wants to lock down, the hypercarry their picks aim at or the frontline their engage wants to chain, and one well-timed bubble can block the ability their whole team is built around. Your bind either starts the pick or peels the diver off your backline, so stand on the flank or just behind your frontline, where the snare is a threat their squishies have to respect. Soul Shackles is your second engage when their team clusters, but diving into the middle on a slow champion gets you killed before the leash pops. Commit it with your team on top of you, not ahead of them.
gamePlan.teamfights: Your job is to cancel their game plan and start yours. The key play is reading the enemy's crowd control and dropping Black Shield on the target a half-second before it lands, which wastes the engage their whole fight was built on. Open with a bind onto a high-value target if the angle is clean, then let your team fall on the rooted body. Soul Shackles turns fights when bodies clump: tether into the cluster, hold the leash, and the stun hits everyone who could not escape. Spend it where your frontline can protect you, because a dead Morgana means a backline with no shield and no peel. The best fights end with their engage wasted on a bubble and your carry never touched by their crowd control.

gamePlan.overview:
Morgana is a control mage built around a long Dark Binding root and Black Shield. The shield absorbs magic damage and grants crowd-control immunity for up to five seconds while its shield health holds; it can block multiple control effects if unbroken, but enough magic damage removes the immunity and physical damage passes through. Tormented Shadow deals increasing damage as targets lose health, and Soul Siphon heals Morgana for 20% of post-mitigation ability damage against champions and eligible large units.

A bind into Tormented Shadow holds a target through several ticks while its damage ramps with missing health. Soul Shackles initially damages, reveals, and slows nearby enemy champions, then stuns only those who remain tethered for the full three seconds. It is not a channel and continues during Zhonya's, but Flash alone does not make the delayed stun automatic.

The catch is that everything she does is a skillshot or a commitment, with no escape attached. Miss the bind and she is a stationary mage holding cooldowns, exactly the target every dasher punishes. Mobility dodges her, range out-spaces her, and physical damage goes straight through the shield she leans on.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Lane patiently and play everything around the bind. Keep the wave near your side so an enemy step-up has nowhere to hide from the root, then chain Dark Binding into your shadow pool for a trade that actually hurts. Do not throw the bind at the minion line on cooldown, since a miss removes most of your kill pressure for several seconds. Hold Black Shield for the gank everyone aims at an immobile mage, because one well-timed shield wastes a whole jungle trip. Against mobile mids, mostly farm and respect their dash windows; against immobile ones, bully freely whenever your bind is up.
gamePlan.midGame: Clear the mid wave before moving into river with vision. Dark Binding from fog can start a pick when allies are already in range, while Black Shield can protect the teammate who must cross enemy control to engage. If no side lane is extended and no objective is close, return for the next wave instead of waiting for a low-percentage bind. Around dragon and Herald, hold the choke and punish the first isolated target rather than walking into the pit alone.
gamePlan.lateGame: You provide both lockdown and protection. Black Shield can invalidate crucial control while it holds, but it does not cancel physical damage or guarantee that later magic control is blocked after the shield breaks. Use Soul Shackles as a Flash engage or counter-engage, remembering the stun occurs only after a three-second tether rather than instantly. Tormented Shadow on chokes adds damage that ramps as enemies lose health.
gamePlan.teamfights: Your job is to take two enemies out of the fight and keep one ally in it. The clean opener is flash into Soul Shackles on their grouped cluster, chained into the bind and the shadow pool so nobody walks free of the second stun. If your team already has the engage, save your spells to answer instead: shield the ally about to eat the enemy initiation, and bind the diver who slips past your front. Stay at the edge and throw binds into the cluster rather than diving in, since you contribute nothing while dead. Pick the shield target the fight actually needs, and let your roots and zone damage do the rest.

situationalItems.note: Build this against healing. The Grievous Wounds applies from his own damage as well as when they attack him, so his withering slow and strikes keep it on the target.

situationalItems.name: Force of Nature
situationalItems.note: Build this into repeated magic damage. The movement speed compounds with Wither's slow to help Nasus reach Siphoning Strike range instead of being kited by mages.

situationalItems.name: Warmog's Armor
situationalItems.note: Health and regeneration, so he can keep farming stacks through a lane trying to push him off the wave.

situationalItems.name: Mercurial Scimitar
situationalItems.note: Build this when a root or stun wastes the Wither window Nasus needs to reach his target. Cleansing it lets him close and begin repeated Siphoning Strikes.

keystoneRune.name: Fleet Footwork
keystoneRune.desc: Moving and attacking builds Energy. At 100 stacks, your next attack heals you and grants movement speed.
keystoneRune.note: Heals him through the early lane he is supposed to lose, which is the only obstacle between him and his stacks.

primaryRunes.name: Demolish
primaryRunes.desc: Charge up a powerful attack against turrets.
primaryRunes.note: His stacked Q shreds a tower quickly, so a farming lane still converts into an objective lead.

primaryRunes.name: Second Wind
primaryRunes.desc: After taking damage from a champion, regenerate health over time.
primaryRunes.note: He only needs to survive to stack, and this is what keeps him on the wave to do it.

primaryRunes.name: Overgrowth
primaryRunes.desc: Gain permanent maximum health when nearby minions or monsters die.
primaryRunes.note: Overgrowth increases Nasus's maximum health on top of the fixed bonus health Fury of the Sands grants. The ultimate does not scale its health grant from his existing maximum health.

secondaryRunes.name: Transcendence
secondaryRunes.desc: Gain ability haste, then reduce a basic ability's cooldown after it hits at level 9.
secondaryRunes.note: Ability haste is stacking speed, which is the only thing that matters to an early Nasus.

spells.name: Flash
spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

goodAgainst.note: Her melee phase is easy to bully off the wave, and even when she out-scales, Wither turns her ranged carry form into a stationary target.

Wind Wall cannot block Wither, and its movement-speed and attack-speed reductions remove the mobility and rapid Steel Tempest casts Yasuo needs for an extended duel. Cast Wither after he has dashed through the nearby wave, place Spirit Fire under his exit for the armor reduction, and take the Siphoning Strike trade while he has no targets left to dash through.
His whole kit is critical strikes and chasing, and a single Wither guts both at once, even during his undying ultimate. He cannot fight while he can barely move or attack.
Wither switches off the attack speed and stickiness his whole duel runs on, his dodge means little when one empowered Q is your trade, and your stacks out-scale him.

weakAgainst.note: Blinding Dart makes an empowered Siphoning Strike miss and denies the stack, while Toxic Shot taxes every last-hit Nasus must walk up to take. Farm difficult minions with Spirit Fire, use Wither only when the wave position allows a real chase, and sweep mushrooms before committing once Teemo's blind expires.
The silence interrupts your Wither timing and his regen erases your trade attempts, so he owns the early lane. His burst falls behind once your stacks and tank items grow.
Ranged poke punishes the one thing you must do, walking up to last-hit, and he stays out of the range your whole kit depends on.
He is strongest exactly when you are weakest, and his fury combo plus stun denies the stacks your game is built on. His strength fades later while yours keeps growing.

gamePlan.overview:
Nasus plays a different game than his lane opponent. Every minion killed with Siphoning Strike makes that hit permanently stronger, so while everyone else trades health bars, Nasus builds permanent damage. Give him twenty quiet minutes and his Q one-shots squishies while his tank items soak whatever they answer with.

Wither is his other signature: a slow so heavy it basically removes an auto-attacker or a diver from a fight while everyone else keeps playing. Add an ultimate that makes him bigger and far tankier, and late-game Nasus is very hard to stop.

The cost is one of the worst early games in the lane. He is slow, low on damage, and every bully in the roster wants to punish his pick. Nasus games are about surviving the first minutes while keeping his stacks going.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Stack Siphoning Strike without letting one last-hit cost most of your health. Keep the wave near your tower against bullies, use Spirit Fire when you must secure several minions from range, and hold Wither for the champion or jungler committing to an all-in. Against a weaker lane, a Wither into a short Q trade can earn enough space to keep farming, but chasing through the full wave defeats the purpose. Track the enemy's anti-heal and armor purchases early so your first item answers the lane you actually have.
gamePlan.midGame: With a defensive item and useful stacks, you can pressure the side lane and join nearby skirmishes. At the first objective spawn, do not abandon a large wave for a fight your team cannot reach first. Herald is usually the better even trade, and your stacked Q helps take it quickly when Baron-side priority is secure. Activate Fury of the Sands after enemies commit, place Spirit Fire under the target your team is hitting, and use Wither on the champion whose attack speed or movement matters most.
gamePlan.lateGame: Late game, side-lane pressure remains useful only when you can reach the next major objective on time. Large stacks threaten structures and isolated defenders, but mobile carries can still kite Nasus and coordinated teams can collapse before he reaches them. In grouped fights, Wither the enemy whose attacks or movement decide the fight, place Spirit Fire where your physical damage dealers can use its armor reduction, and attack the closest valuable target. Continued stacking helps, but map position matters more than another wave when Baron or Elder is exposed.
gamePlan.teamfights: Open with Wither on the enemy whose attack speed and movement are most important, often a marksman or a diver entering your backline. Activate Fury of the Sands as the teams commit so its bonus health and repeated damage cover the part of the fight when you are focused. Stand in Spirit Fire while attacking targets inside its armor reduction, and do not walk past a dangerous frontline if doing so exposes your carry. Nasus wins grouped fights by controlling one threat and staying in range, not by chasing a mobile target through the whole formation.

startingItem.name: Spectral Sickle
startingItem.note: This item works well for Nami, as she is great at poking and harassing the enemies in lane. For harder matchups where you are forced to play much safer in lane, I recommend taking Relic Shield for the extra health and easier activation of the item.

boots.name: Crimson Lucidity
boots.note: Most games, you will want to rush Boots of Lucidity and upgrade them into Crimson Lucidity. This gives Nami a large power spike for the lane phase, as the cooldown reduction allows her to buff her allies and poke more, and the mana regeneration gives her great sustain in lane. It also reduces summoner spell cooldowns, which is very helpful for enchanters who need to use them to survive.

coreItems.name: Black Mist Scythe
coreItems.note: The Spectral Sickle upgrade. It gives ability power and ability haste, both of which are important stats for Nami, and her poke finishes the quest quickly.

coreItems.name: Harmonic Echo
coreItems.note: Harmonic and Mandate are Nami's best items. I go Harmonic first in most games now, since the extra mana and healing is perfect at keeping you and your ADC alive for longer, and it is the safer buy when the lane is passive or you need higher sustain.

coreItems.name: Imperial Mandate
coreItems.note: Built second after Harmonic. If you are in a very aggressive lane (e.g. having a Lucian ADC), build Mandate first, as the extra damage and move speed the item gives rewards being aggressive and crowd controlling your opponents.

coreItems.name: Ardent Censer
coreItems.note: Ardent is another item you will almost always want to build on Nami. It benefits your allies by enhancing their attack speed, so it is a must buy when you have a hypercarry ADC. Consider building Ardent even earlier when multiple allied champions rely on high attack speed, or if your ADC is snowballing an early lead.

coreItems.name: Staff of Flowing Waters
coreItems.note: Staff is a great general item to have that gives ability haste and ability power to you and an ally whenever you heal / shield them. Since it synergizes so well with AP champions, consider building it earlier if you have multiple AP caster champions on your team.

situationalItems.name: Relic Shield
situationalItems.note: Build this into hard matchups. Against engage tanks and hook supports you are forced to play much safer in lane, so I start Relic Shield over Spectral Sickle for the extra health and the easier activation from behind your minions.

situationalItems.name: Mikael's Blessing
situationalItems.note: Mikael's is crucial to buy when enemies rely on specific crowd control abilities to lockdown your team. You can also use it to cleanse your carry of a debuff or status effect. When it is needed, I will usually buy Mikael's second or third.

situationalItems.name: Shurelya's Battlesong
situationalItems.note: Shurelya's is great for boosting the tempo of your team. It can be used for chasing, running away, or just in teamfights to give your team more engage and sidestepping capabilities. I like pairing this item with champions who rely on movespeed for their combat, like Jinx, Jhin, and Hecarim.

situationalItems.name: Banshee's Veil
situationalItems.note: Veil is a super powerful item that blocks the next enemy ability outright. Nami has no dash and no escape, so buy it when the enemy has a hook or a point and click stun that would end your fight before it starts.

situationalItems.name: Locket of the Iron Solari
situationalItems.note: Locket provides a shield to all nearby allies, so it is most valuable when against high AOE damage or teamfight focused games.

situationalItems.name: Knight's Vow
situationalItems.note: When you have a single carry that you really need to protect at all costs, Knight's Vow can be bought to help funnel your carry to make them even stronger. This is even more useful against AD teams because of the armor it provides.

situationalItems.name: Oceanid's Trident
situationalItems.note: If you are against multiple champions that rely on high shielding to survive, Trident will make it easier for your team to take them down. If your teammates are getting anti-shield, you won't need to.

situationalItems.name: Morellonomicon
situationalItems.note: Against champions with high healing, buy the Oblivion Orb component early in the game, but only upgrade to Morello once you have finished all your other items.

keystoneRune.name: Aery
keystoneRune.desc: Your attacks and abilities send Aery to a target, dealing damage to enemies or shielding allies.
keystoneRune.note: Nami's best keystone is Aery. Aery provides extra poke against enemies in lane and shielding for your allies. It is very consistent and is the default keystone for Nami.

primaryRunes.name: Font of Life
primaryRunes.desc: Damaging enemy champions heals you and the lowest-health nearby ally after a short cooldown.
primaryRunes.note: Ebb and Flow can damage an enemy and bounce into an allied heal; Font of Life adds another heal for Nami and her lowest-health nearby ally on that same trading pattern.

primaryRunes.name: Bone Plating
primaryRunes.desc: After taking damage from a champion, the next 3 instances of champion damage are reduced.
primaryRunes.note: Bone Plating reduces the next three hits when an engage support reaches Nami, buying time to cast Ebb and Flow, land Aqua Prison, and move away with her passive speed.

primaryRunes.name: Revitalize
primaryRunes.desc: Healing and shielding are stronger, especially on low-health targets.
primaryRunes.note: Revitalize amplifies Ebb and Flow's healing and the shields Aery adds to Nami's allied casts, so both halves of her poke-and-sustain pattern scale from one rune.

secondaryRunes.name: Manaflow Band
secondaryRunes.desc: Hitting an enemy champion with an ability permanently increases your maximum mana.
secondaryRunes.note: Ebb and Flow is powerful but mana-hungry because Nami wants to cast it every trade. Manaflow Band increases the pool that keeps her bounce healing and poke available through lane.

spells.name: Flash
spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

gamePlan.overview:
Nami is the enchanter who fights back. Aqua Prison suspends enemies for 1.5 seconds and speeds allies near its landing area, Ebb and Flow alternates between enemies and allies for up to three total hits, and Tidecaller's Blessing empowers an ally's next three basic attacks with bonus magic damage and a slow. Tidal Wave knocks enemies up, then slows them for longer the farther it travels; allies it touches receive a stronger burst of Surging Tides movement speed. She sets the terms of the fight instead of waiting for one, which makes her one of the most aggressive enchanters in Wild Rift.

In the Dragon lane she plays a forward, threatening 2v2. Land the bubble and the lane becomes a kill: your ADC walks onto a stuck target while Tidecaller's Blessing adds damage and slows to their follow-up. The same kit flips to defense in an instant. The slow peels a diver, Ebb and Flow tops your carry up through a trade, and the wave breaks a collapse that went wrong. She is poke, all-in, and peel in one squishy body.

What she lacks is instant mobility. She has no dash or stealth and dies quickly when focused, though Surging Tides movement speed, Tidecaller's Blessing slows, Aqua Prison's suspension, and Tidal Wave's knockup all help create distance. Missing the delayed bubble removes her strongest single-target setup, and careless spell spam empties her mana before the next engage.
gamePlan.earlyGame:
Nami is a lane bully with strong poke, sustain, and crowd control. Use Ebb and Flow when the enemy carry walks up to farm. The stream can bounce twice after its first target, but it must alternate between unaffected enemies and allies and cannot hit the same champion twice, so stand close enough to your carry to create a full three-hit chain. Once the enemy duo is worn down, Tidecaller's Blessing into Aqua Prison gives your carry a clean all-in. At level 5, Tidal Wave can start the engage or cut off the retreat.

Aqua Prison suspends enemies for 1.5 seconds even at level 1 and grants Surging Tides movement speed to allies near its landing area. Holding it can deny an engage without casting, while missing it leaves Nami without her strongest control for 12 seconds. Use Tidecaller's Blessing to slow a target before the bubble, or save Aqua Prison for peel when an aggressive support or jungler commits to your carry.

Aggressive trading often pushes the wave, which leaves you open to the enemy jungler and mid laner. Watch the minimap, track which side the jungler showed on, and ward the river before you walk forward. If you do not know where the jungler is, keep Aqua Prison available and stop contesting the far side of the wave.

Look for roams only after your duo crashes the wave or your carry recalls. Check whether the enemy mid laner is extended, help your jungler contest river, and return before your carry is exposed to a long two-versus-one lane. When the first objectives approach at six minutes, establish river vision early instead of arriving after the enemy support has already claimed the entrances.
gamePlan.midGame:
During the mid game, move with the teammate who can safely convert your buffs into damage rather than following one lane by habit. If your Dragon lane carry is ahead, protect their farm and keep them connected to objective fights. If another teammate is the win condition, use the space between waves to link up with them and your jungler. Ward river entrances, sweep the routes your team wants to use, and never walk into dark jungle alone just to place deeper vision.

Set up vision before objectives spawn and hold the choke with Aqua Prison rather than face-checking it. Herald is usually the stronger first conversion when the map is even, while dragon becomes more valuable when your composition is built to win repeated five-versus-five fights and pursue soul. Nami can support either call: Tidal Wave controls a narrow pit entrance, and Ebb and Flow keeps your frontline healthy through the standoff.
gamePlan.lateGame: Late game, stay one step behind the ally the enemy must kill. Tidecaller's Blessing belongs on the teammate who can keep attacking, while Ebb and Flow should begin on the side that produces the useful bounce rather than automatically starting as a heal. Save Aqua Prison for a predictable target, such as a diver finishing a dash or an enemy slowed by Tidal Wave. Your utility remains strong, but your margin for error shrinks, so rotate with teammates and vision instead of taking shortcuts through fog.
gamePlan.teamfights: Position behind your frontline but close enough for Ebb and Flow to complete a useful chain. Against heavy engage, send Tidal Wave through your own team so it interrupts the dive and gives allies Surging Tides movement speed. When your team has the cleaner initiation, cast it down a choke and follow the knockup with Aqua Prison while enemies are slowed. Keep Tidecaller's Blessing on the ally who can use all three empowered attacks, watch both flanks, and reposition before an assassin reaches casting range.

startingItem.name: Ruby Crystal
startingItem.note: Early health, which survives the lane and also feeds a shield built from a share of the damage he takes.

boots.name: Armored Advance
boots.note: Armor and health, which let him win the extended trades his shield mechanic is designed for.

coreItems.name: Riftmaker
coreItems.note: Ramping bonus damage and Omnivamp during long fights, and his ultimate forces the long duel he wants.

coreItems.name: Zeke's Convergence
coreItems.note: His ultimate is a fixed cast that starts a duel, and this turns that same cast into a blizzard on whoever he dragged away.

coreItems.name: Bloodletter's Curse
coreItems.note: His passive already carries magic penetration, and shredding magic resist on top compounds the aura damage he deals constantly. It is best when Mordekaiser has other magic-damage allies who can exploit the team-wide shred; if Mordekaiser is the team's only significant magic threat, build Void Staff instead for stronger personal penetration.

coreItems.name: Unending Despair
coreItems.note: Damages nearby enemies and heals him for it. He is either surrounded or in a forced duel, so it is always active.

coreItems.name: Amaranth's Twinguard
coreItems.note: Build this when you are fighting in the middle of the enemy team and need both armor and magic resist. His passive and Realm of Death force extended combat, giving Twinguard time to activate before the duel is decided.

situationalItems.name: Cryptbloom
situationalItems.note: Cuts the magic resist that blunts his aura. The healing on takedown also helps the team that followed his engage. Choose it when enemies have not built much magic resist, so trading Void Staff's extra damage for more ability haste and an area heal after takedowns is worthwhile.

situationalItems.name: Hextech Rocketbelt
situationalItems.desc: AP engage item with a dash
situationalItems.note: A gap closer for a champion whose only way to start a fight is walking at someone.

situationalItems.name: Thornmail
situationalItems.note: Build this against healing. The Grievous Wounds applies from your own damage as well as when they attack you, so the carry he banished cannot heal through the duel.

situationalItems.name: Oceanid's Trident
situationalItems.note: Build this when the enemy has shields that keep absorbing the aura damage he grinds out.

situationalItems.name: Randuin's Omen
situationalItems.note: Build this when the enemy team has multiple crit champions. Realm of Death can force Mordekaiser into a duel with their marksman, and crit reduction makes that isolated fight much safer.

situationalItems.name: Rylai's Crystal Scepter
situationalItems.note: The slow keeps enemies inside his aura, which is the only way a damage-over-time pattern works.

situationalItems.name: Liandry's Torment
situationalItems.note: His aura never stops ticking, so the max health burn is permanently applied to whoever is near him.

situationalItems.name: Zhonya's Hourglass
situationalItems.note: Build this for fights where he has to survive rather than win, since his shield alone is not always enough. Buy Seeker's Armguard early for the armor and ability power.

situationalItems.name: Chainlaced Crushers
situationalItems.note: Boot swap against heavy magic damage and crowd control. Tenacity prevents a disable from consuming too much of Realm of Death, where every lost second delays his passive and shield.

situationalItems.name: Void Staff
situationalItems.note: The raw penetration alternative to Cryptbloom. Build it when a magic resist frontline is what turns off his aura. Choose it over Cryptbloom when enemies are stacking magic resist and maximum personal damage matters more than ability haste and team healing.

keystoneRune.name: Conqueror
keystoneRune.desc: Gain stacks by damaging enemy champions. At maximum stacks, gain bonus damage and healing.
keystoneRune.note: His aura keeps him damaging enemies continuously, so he stacks fast and the healing compounds with his shield.

primaryRunes.name: Unshakeable
primaryRunes.desc: Gain bonus armor and magic resist, increasing further when surrounded by enemies.
primaryRunes.note: He fights in the middle of the enemy team by design, which is when this gives the most.

primaryRunes.name: Second Wind
primaryRunes.desc: After taking damage from a champion, regenerate health over time.
primaryRunes.note: His shield builds from damage dealt, and this covers the poke he takes when he has nothing to hit.

primaryRunes.name: Overgrowth
primaryRunes.desc: Gain permanent maximum health when nearby minions or monsters die.
primaryRunes.note: He wins by outlasting one target in his ultimate, and the pool is what decides that duel.

secondaryRunes.name: Last Stand
secondaryRunes.desc: Deal more damage to champions while you are low on health.
secondaryRunes.note: His shield absorbs the damage that would kill him, so he spends the decisive part of every fight in this health range.

spells.name: Flash
spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

goodAgainst.note: Darkness Rise supplies sustained percent-health damage after Ornn's short Brittle trade, and Realm of Death removes the tank from allies who would normally capitalize on his crowd control. Sidestep Searing Charge away from terrain, pull him back with Death's Grasp after Bellows Breath ends, and reserve the realm for the objective fight where isolating Ornn removes his engage.

Armor does not reduce Mordekaiser's magic damage, but Malphite still has a recurring maximum-health shield, a movement-speed swing on Q, and Ground Slam's attack-speed cripple; not only his ultimate. Build passive stacks with abilities when the cripple slows your attacks.

Blind prevents Mordekaiser's basic attacks, which normally add Darkness Rise stacks and carry his AP on-hit damage, so it can delay the passive aura. Use Q and E to build stacks during blind, and remember Teemo can kite with movement speed even inside the realm.

Counter Strike dodges Mordekaiser's basic attacks and on-hit damage and reduces other incoming champion area damage by 25%, including much of the passive aura and Q. It does not dodge Q or E outright, so build stacks with abilities and wait out the returning stun before committing the shield.

weakAgainst.note: Riven's combo happens between your slow wind-ups and she dashes out before your burn pays off, though she falls off later while you do not.
The mist makes her untargetable from outside while her percent damage shreds your big health bar, so she duels you on her terms and out-scales you too.
Her dashes slip your Q sweep and E pull, and she trades in quick bursts before your burn pays off. You cannot stick to someone who keeps repositioning.

gamePlan.overview:
Mordekaiser punishes extended fights. Damaging attacks or basic abilities against enemy champions or large monsters add Darkness Rise stacks, as do takedowns; minion hits and arbitrary damage do not. At three stacks he gains movement speed and a nearby target-maximum-health magic-damage aura. He also has innate magic penetration and AP-scaling bonus magic damage on his basic attacks.

Indestructible stores 35% of post-mitigation damage Mordekaiser deals and 7% of pre-mitigation damage he takes, with much smaller values from non-champions. Casting W converts that resource into a shield; recasting consumes only the remaining shield and heals for a portion, so absorbed damage leaves less healing. Realm of Death then slows and reveals one champion during its cast before banishing both for seven seconds.

He has real weaknesses. He is slow, has no dash, and is weak before his first item, so ranged poke and early bullies hurt him, and kiting teams can keep him out of fights. Mordekaiser games are about reaching the brawl, because once it starts, he wins it.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Make every trade last longer than the enemy wanted. Obliterate has no special center hit; it deals increased damage when only one enemy is struck, so angle it away from the minion wave for isolation damage. Death's Grasp pulls and then slows, helping land the next attack or Q needed for three passive stacks. Cast W after filling Potential Shield, and recast for healing only when preserving health matters more than keeping the remaining shield.
gamePlan.midGame: Crash the Baron wave before leaving for Herald or a river skirmish, then choose the Realm of Death target based on cooldowns and position. The cast heals Mordekaiser for 8% of the target's maximum health and transfers 8% of several current combat stats for seven seconds. Mobile duelists can still win inside and the realm can be dispelled, so do not use it only because a non-tank enters range. Removing the enemy jungler or main damage dealer is valuable only if Mordekaiser's team can handle the remaining fight.
gamePlan.lateGame: Push a side wave only when you can rejoin before Baron or Elder is contested. A carry is often the best Realm of Death target, but banishing the enemy jungler can remove Smite during an objective secure. Check whether the isolated duel is favorable and whether your team needs Mordekaiser to frontline outside. If the target can dispel the realm or win the duel, hold the ultimate and keep applying passive pressure in the grouped fight.
gamePlan.teamfights: Choose the Realm of Death target before entering the fight. Use Death's Grasp to pull a reachable threat into Obliterate and build the passive, then cast the realm when removing that champion improves the outside fight and the duel is winnable. At Baron or Elder, prioritize the enemy jungler when denying Smite matters more than reaching a carry. If your team needs a frontline, remain outside and zone with the passive instead of isolating yourself immediately.

startingItem.name: Amplifying Tome
startingItem.note: Early ability power for her portals and bolts, which are her only way to contest the wave.

boots.name: Spellslinger's Shoes
boots.note: Magic penetration keeps her burst lethal, since her damage arrives in one banished-and-caught window.

coreItems.name: Luden's Echo
coreItems.note: The mana pays for constant portal placement, and Echo adds damage to the first ability of every rotation.

coreItems.name: Horizon Focus
coreItems.note: Her charged bolt lands from long range, so the reveal and amplification trigger on the poke she was already throwing.

coreItems.name: Rabadon's Deathcap
coreItems.note: Multiplies her ability power. Her damage lands in one caught rotation, so all of it goes up at once.

coreItems.name: Void Staff
coreItems.note: Cuts the magic resist that lets a banished target survive the follow-up she set up. Choose it over Cryptbloom when enemies are stacking magic resist and maximum personal damage matters more than ability haste and team healing.

coreItems.name: Infinity Orb
coreItems.note: The low-health crit helps Norra finish targets after her portal control and banish setup have delivered the team’s damage, converting a long setup into a kill.

situationalItems.name: Oceanid's Trident
situationalItems.note: Build this when the enemy has shields that keep absorbing the rotation her portal sets up.

situationalItems.name: Morellonomicon
situationalItems.note: Build this against a drain champion who heals back what her banish window sets up. Buy Oblivion Orb early, since the anti-heal works from the component.

situationalItems.name: Zhonya's Hourglass
situationalItems.note: Build this against assassins who reach her once her portals are spent. Buy Seeker's Armguard early for the armor and ability power.

situationalItems.name: Stormsurge
situationalItems.note: Her caught rotation already does enough damage to trigger the mark, and the move speed helps her reposition between portals.

situationalItems.name: Cryptbloom
situationalItems.note: The alternative to Void Staff. Less penetration, but the ability haste and healing on takedown help when her ultimate anchors a teamfight. Choose it when enemies have not built much magic resist, so trading Void Staff's extra damage for more ability haste and an area heal after takedowns is worthwhile.

keystoneRune.name: First Strike
keystoneRune.desc: Deal bonus damage for the first 3 seconds of combat with champions and gain gold.
keystoneRune.note: Her portals let her open a fight from range on her own terms, so she reliably lands the first hit.

primaryRunes.name: Sudden Impact
primaryRunes.desc: Deal bonus true damage after using mobility or exiting stealth.
primaryRunes.note: The recoil on her fully charged bolt counts as mobility, letting her trigger the bonus true damage on a follow-up hit.

primaryRunes.name: Tyrant
primaryRunes.desc: Strengthen your damage output when brawling aggressively at close range.
primaryRunes.note: Her pattern is banishing someone and converting that into a kill, which is the snowball this rewards.

primaryRunes.name: Eyeball Collector
primaryRunes.desc: Gain adaptive force by collecting takedown stacks from enemy champions and epic monsters.
primaryRunes.note: Her portal roams turn into takedowns, and each one adds adaptive force to the next burst.

secondaryRunes.name: Bone Plating
secondaryRunes.desc: After taking damage from a champion, the next 3 instances of champion damage are reduced.
secondaryRunes.note: She needs time to set up her portal pressure, and this covers the assassin who arrives before it is placed.

spells.name: Flash
spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

goodAgainst.note: A charged Memory Surge reaches Annie before her short spell range, and its recoil helps Norra stay outside Flash-Tibbers distance while Pyromania is loaded. Track the passive stacks, use the bolt on each farm approach, and hold Journey to Nowhere for the moment Annie commits rather than spending the banish on routine wave control.

Memory Surge can be charged beyond Veigar's early spell range, while its recoil helps Norra leave Event Horizon without walking across the cage edge. Punish him during the cage cooldown, use Journey to Nowhere to deny his burst follow-up, and turn the resulting priority into river control before his passive stacks catch up.
She has to place and gather her spheres to do real damage, which means walking into range your bolt already controls, so her setup costs her health every time.

Memory Surge can be charged beyond Orianna's ball leash, while Portalpalooza attacks from two endpoints and forces her to choose which angle to shield. Fire when the ball is committed to the wave, recoil away from Command: Dissonance, and use Journey to Nowhere before Shockwave can convert her setup into a full rotation.

Mel has no dash, but Rebuttal can make her invulnerable to and reflect Memory Surge and Beloved Trinket projectiles. Journey to Nowhere and Threads of Homecoming bypass projectile interception, so use that control to draw her 0.75-second defense before releasing the charged bolt.

weakAgainst.note: Ekko dashes through your poke, shields the chip you do land, and his ultimate undoes the one good combo you finally hit, so the matchup only gets worse after his first item.

Akali's dashes close the gap Norra wants to preserve, but Twilight Shroud does not make her immune to aimed area effects. Place Threads of Homecoming or Journey to Nowhere over the shroud, then use the enlarged hitbox from Threads to make the next Memory Surge easier to land.

Living Shadow lets Zed change angles around Memory Surge, and Norra's conditional recoil is not a dependable escape from Death Mark. Save Journey to Nowhere to remove him during the all-in or deny his follow-up, while tracking the shadow he can return to.
His pole vault goes untargetable straight through your poke and your ultimate, and once he is on you he can wait out the hop, so his all-in beats yours every time he reaches melee.

Wind Wall blocks Memory Surge and Beloved Trinket projectiles, but Journey to Nowhere and the ground-targeted Threads of Homecoming bypass projectile interception. Force the wall with a projectile, then use the portal control while he dashes through the wave.

gamePlan.overview:
Norra is a yordle who fights through portals. Memory Surge charges for up to 2.5 seconds, gaining range and damage during the first 1.5, then fires through enemies until it hits a champion and explodes. A full charge also primes nearby Beloved Trinkets and recoils Norra 300 units. Journey to Nowhere banishes enemies into a separate Spirit Realm for 2.25 seconds, where they are heavily slowed and silenced and cannot interact with units outside. Threads of Homecoming marks enemies between two portals, doubling their hitbox for four seconds and adding maximum-health damage to Memory Surge. Portalpalooza creates a ten-second rift that Norra can recast four times to fire projectile yarn balls from both ends; the fourth shot deals 140% damage.

She wins through poke and position. Hold the lane at the edge of your range, farm with the bolt, chip the enemy mid every time they walk up, then turn that pressure into objectives. She is not a hard-shove roamer; she controls the river, sets up on the map, and waits for the enemy to group at dragon or herald so her ultimate has a cluster to catch. Her trinkets and threaded portals cover the ground around her, so she punishes angles a single straight-line caster cannot.

Her weakness is dependable mobility. A fully charged Memory Surge recoils her, but the direction and charge requirement make it a conditional spacing tool rather than an on-demand dash. Once someone is on top of her, Journey to Nowhere and Flash are her reliable ways to buy separation.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Lane at the range your bolt allows and make every last hit cost the enemy health. Farm with the charged bolt, timing the release so it lands on the enemy mid rather than dying to a minion, and hold the banishing portal for the moment they overextend instead of spending it on the wave. Against short-range or immobile mages, push the tempo and punish them for contesting minions. Against anyone with a dash or longer reach, sit back, farm at max distance, and keep the banishing portal strictly for the dive, because spending it as poke leaves you defenceless for the gank. Ward the river early, since an immobile mid on open ground is exactly what the enemy jungler wants.
gamePlan.midGame: Your ultimate coming online changes what the map is worth to you. A grouped fight at scuttle or a contested dragon is where Portalpalooza can send all four recasts through the same choke. Push the wave with Memory Surge, then use mid priority to move to the river and pressure objectives instead of chasing kills you cannot reach. Journey to Nowhere can remove a target for 2.25 seconds, but neither team can interact across the two realms, so time the return for your jungler or sidelaner to be ready rather than wasting their damage into the banishment.
gamePlan.lateGame: By now the poke does real damage and the ultimate decides fights, so the job is getting your range onto the right target without dying to reach the angle. Hold the ultimate until their team stacks on an objective or a choke, and chip from the back of your group the rest of the time. Vision is your mobility: wards and brush lines are what let you hold a safe poke angle at all, so a warded flank is the difference between a free rotation and a death. The danger never changes. You are a long-range mage in a fight full of people who want to stand next to you, so the skill is patience, spacing, and waiting for their formation to bunch tight enough for one ultimate.
gamePlan.teamfights: Norra does not brawl in a teamfight; she works from the edge and then closes it. Before the teams meet, use Memory Surge and basic-ability hits to cycle Beloved Trinkets, then apply Threads so its doubled hitbox makes the next bolt and trinket detonations easier to land. Portalpalooza lasts up to ten seconds, but the damage only comes when you aim its four recasts; sweep the paired yarn balls through the choke and protect the 140%-damage fourth shot. Journey to Nowhere can peel a diver or temporarily remove a straggler, but the target is unavailable to your teammates until it returns from the Spirit Realm.

boots.name: Spellslinger's Shoes
boots.note: Magic penetration sharpens both her spear and her cougar burst, keeping her relevant in both forms.

coreItems.name: Lich Bane
coreItems.note: Nidalee casts constantly while rotating through two forms, creating frequent Spellblade windows. In Cougar Form, weave the empowered attack from Takedown between casts so Lich Bane lands inside the same burst.

coreItems.name: Rabadon's Deathcap
coreItems.note: Multiplies her ability power, raising both long-range Javelin Toss poke and Cougar Form Takedown's missing-health finisher damage.

coreItems.name: Infinity Orb
coreItems.note: Crits against low health targets, and her cougar Q already scales with missing health, so both pay on the same enemies.

coreItems.name: Void Staff
coreItems.note: Cuts the magic resist that turns a landed spear from a kill setup into a chunk. Choose it over Cryptbloom when enemies are stacking magic resist and maximum personal damage matters more than ability haste and team healing.

coreItems.name: Zhonya's Hourglass
coreItems.note: Build this for when she lands in cougar form with her pounce spent. Buy Seeker's Armguard early for the armor and ability power.

situationalItems.name: Oceanid's Trident
situationalItems.note: Build this when the enemy has shields that keep absorbing the burst her spear set up.

situationalItems.name: Hextech Rocketbelt
situationalItems.desc: AP engage item with a dash
situationalItems.note: A gap closer that does not cost her a pounce, so she arrives with her mobility still available to leave.

situationalItems.name: Banshee's Veil
situationalItems.note: Build this when the enemy has crowd control that catches her mid-dive.

situationalItems.name: Cryptbloom
situationalItems.note: The alternative to Void Staff. Less penetration, but the ability haste means faster form swaps and the healing on takedown helps her team. Choose it when enemies have not built much magic resist, so trading Void Staff's extra damage for more ability haste and an area heal after takedowns is worthwhile.

keystoneRune.name: Dark Harvest
keystoneRune.desc: Damaging low-health champions harvests a soul and empowers your next harvest proc.
keystoneRune.note: Her cougar Q hunts low health targets, so the souls come from kills she was already set up to take.

primaryRunes.name: Sudden Impact
primaryRunes.desc: Deal bonus true damage after using mobility or exiting stealth.
primaryRunes.note: Her pounce is a dash, so it triggers the bonus true damage as she reaches her target in cougar form.

primaryRunes.name: Hubris
primaryRunes.desc: Champion takedowns after damaging an enemy grant a temporary burst of adaptive force.
primaryRunes.note: Her picks convert into kills, and stacking power off takedowns builds the snowball her spears are meant to start.

primaryRunes.name: Eyeball Collector
primaryRunes.desc: Gain adaptive force by collecting takedown stacks from enemy champions and epic monsters.
primaryRunes.note: Takedowns are the point of her ganks, so the stacks build faster than on a farming jungler.

secondaryRunes.name: Transcendence
secondaryRunes.desc: Gain ability haste, then reduce a basic ability's cooldown after it hits at level 9.
secondaryRunes.note: Ability haste means more spears and faster form swaps, which is her poke and her dive frequency.

spells.name: Flash
spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

spells.name: Smite
spells.note: Required for Jungling. Secures objectives and sustains through camp clears.

goodAgainst.note: Javelin Toss outranges Bandage Toss, and Pounce lets Nidalee sidestep the only engage Amumu has before Curse of the Sad Mummy. Once the bandage misses, Takedown punishes the immobile tank before Despair can win a long fight.

Javelin Toss punishes Shyvana's predictable Burnout path between camps, and Pounce avoids the landing zone of Dragon's Descent. Nidalee can mark, invade, and leave before Twin Bite turns the encounter into Shyvana's preferred extended brawl.
Graves only hurts you up close where his shells hit hardest, and his short range has no answer to max-range spears, so he arrives at every fight already chunked.

weakAgainst.note: Rengar erases the spacing your whole game depends on, leaping from a brush to burst your fragile cat before a single spear matters. Poke is worthless against an assassin you never see coming.
Vi punches straight through your spears and sticks to you with her slow, and your fragile frame has no way to peel a point-and-click gap-closer once she commits.
Diana's shield shrugs off your poke, and once she reaches you Moonfall drags the cougar back in before you can leap away, so one gap-close flips the whole fight.

gamePlan.overview:
Nidalee is a poke assassin who clears at a frightening pace and pokes the whole map from long range. In human form she throws Javelin Toss, a spear that gains range and damage the longer it flies, so a throw from fog or over a wall can chunk an enemy before they ever see her. Her traps mark targets, and cougar form leaps onto anything marked with bonus damage that decides early skirmishes.

Cougar form is a fast brawler with a pounce gap-closer and a low-health execute on Takedown. It is also the engine of her clear, letting her finish her route faster than almost any other jungler.

The payoff is tempo: she hits her timings early, snowballs off the leads she creates, and shows up in three lanes while a slower jungler is still clearing. The catch is that the spear has to land. A cat that whiffs is fragile and out of cooldowns.
gamePlan.earlyGame:
Rotate all three Cougar Form abilities through camps, reset an attack with Takedown, and use Primal Surge's attack-speed buff and missing-health heal between form swaps. The resulting clear speed gives Nidalee choices: reach river first, invade a tracked slow starter with lane priority, or gank a lane whose crowd control can guarantee Javelin Toss. Do not spend that tempo throwing low-percentage spears at a neutral lane.

At scuttle, hold space with a maximum-distance spear rather than standing on top of the crab, because its damage comes from travel distance and cannot be charged. A spear or Bushwhack mark extends Pounce's reach, so enter Cougar Form only after the mark lands and the enemy's return control is accounted for. Nidalee's early lead comes from making the map respond to her faster clear, not from forcing every encounter into melee range.
gamePlan.midGame:
Nidalee pressures the first objectives from outside the pit before deciding whether Cougar Form can enter safely. Contest with spears from across it and force the enemy jungler to fight on your terms or give the objective up. If your team cannot contest safely, trade for the other objective or convert your tempo into camps and a tower instead of forcing a bad pit dive.

Between objectives, farm only as much as you need and visit every lane with a gankable angle: a heal keeps your laner topped up while a marked pounce ends an overextended enemy. Counter-jungling works well too, because your clear speed lets you steal a camp and leave before anyone arrives.
gamePlan.lateGame: The longer the game goes, the harder you have to work, because the spear that once deleted a carry now only chunks a full-build team. Stop forcing fights and play the picker: hunt sidelaners and stragglers with traps and spears from fog, and snipe anyone who walks through river without vision. Around Baron you are the threat that makes the enemy afraid to start it, throwing spears over the wall and pouncing on anyone who strays from the group. Keep your heal for yourself and your most fragile teammate, and never commit your pounce into a five-man group with no way out, because a cat caught in the open with cooldowns down does not walk back out.
gamePlan.teamfights: Work from the edge of the fight and use Javelin Toss or Bushwhack to mark a reachable target before entering Cougar Form. Pounce only after the enemy's immediate control is accounted for, then use Takedown on the wounded target and leave through a route your team controls. Place traps in chokes and flank routes, and use Primal Surge on the ally who can keep dealing damage. If no marked target separates from peel, remain at range instead of diving through the frontline.

startingItem.name: Ruby Crystal

boots.name: Armored Advance
boots.note: Armor and health for a lane she wins by absorbing trades rather than winning them outright.

coreItems.name: Heartsteel

coreItems.name: Sunfire Aegis

coreItems.name: Thornmail
coreItems.note: Build this against healing. The Grievous Wounds applies from your own damage as well as when they attack you, so it lands on whoever she has pinned to a wall.

coreItems.name: Force of Nature
coreItems.note: Build this when the enemy team has two or more AP champions. The move speed also helps her close on a mage.

coreItems.name: Amaranth's Twinguard
coreItems.note: Build this when you are fighting in the middle of the enemy team and need both armor and magic resist. Steadfast Presence and Heroic Charge keep Poppy in close combat long enough to activate both Twinguard defenses.

situationalItems.name: Randuin's Omen
situationalItems.note: Build this when the enemy team has multiple crit champions. Poppy has to enter melee range for Heroic Charge, and reducing crit damage keeps her alive while she pins and peels the carry.

situationalItems.name: Chainlaced Crushers
situationalItems.note: Boot swap against heavy magic damage and crowd control, which lands before her charge does.

situationalItems.name: Gargoyle Stoneplate
situationalItems.note: The shield scales with maximum health and grows for each nearby enemy champion, covering the seconds after she charges someone into a wall inside their team.

situationalItems.name: Unending Despair
situationalItems.note: Damages nearby enemies and heals her for it. She is standing in the middle of them by design.

situationalItems.name: Frozen Heart
situationalItems.note: Build this when the enemy team has several attack-speed carries. Heroic Charge and Steadfast Presence keep Poppy close enough for the aura to weaken the carry she is peeling.

situationalItems.name: Mantle of the Twelfth Hour
situationalItems.note: The lifeline gives bonus max health when she drops low, which also enlarges her percentage-based shield.

keystoneRune.name: Grasp of the Undying
keystoneRune.desc: Every 4 seconds in combat, your next attack against a champion deals bonus damage and heals you.
keystoneRune.note: Permanent health growth, and her lane is repeated short walk-up trades. It also grows her shield.

primaryRunes.name: Demolish
primaryRunes.desc: Charge up a powerful attack against turrets.
primaryRunes.note: Her wall stun buys free time on the tower, so a won trade turns into plates.

primaryRunes.name: Second Wind
primaryRunes.desc: After taking damage from a champion, regenerate health over time.
primaryRunes.note: Her kit answers dashes, not chip, so this handles the poke that grinds her down instead.

primaryRunes.name: Overgrowth
primaryRunes.desc: Gain permanent maximum health when nearby minions or monsters die.
primaryRunes.note: She holds a choke and eats the engage, and the health is what lets her keep standing there.

secondaryRunes.name: Transcendence
secondaryRunes.desc: Gain ability haste, then reduce a basic ability's cooldown after it hits at level 9.
secondaryRunes.note: Ability haste means her charge and her dash-denial aura are up more often, which is her whole utility.

spells.name: Flash
spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

goodAgainst.note: Your W shuts her dash resets down completely, and an Irelia who cannot Bladesurge has no trade pattern left. Denying the first dash usually denies the whole fight.
His poke stings, but his whole escape plan is one dash and your W owns it, so every overextension near a wall risks the stun.
Fiora's Q is a dash, so your W interrupts the dueling pattern her whole champion is built on. This is one of the few lanes where her mobility works against her.
Her entire combo is dashes and your W deletes them mid-air, so her burst pattern falls apart without the mobility it assumes.
Shen's only gap closer is the taunt dash, and your W grounds it into nothing, leaving a Shen who cannot reach you and has no kill pressure without it.

weakAgainst.note: Steadfast Presence stops dashes, but Darius uses Apprehend to pull Poppy without dashing and then extends the fight with Crippling Strike and Hemorrhage. Trade with Hammer Shock and the buckler shield at the edge of his range, save Heroic Charge for a real wall angle or escape path, and never remain in melee long enough for five bleed stacks.
Garen's engage is a walk-up, not a dash, so your anti-mobility kit has nothing to deny, while his regen out-grinds your poke and his silence breaks your trade pattern.
Two tanks with no kill threat on each other, and his armor blunts your hammer, so the lane comes down to whose ultimate shapes fights better.
There is no dash to ground and his health pool shrugs off your modest damage, while his shield soaks the buckler trades and his charged Q engages on his terms.

gamePlan.overview:
Poppy is the Baron lane's anti-mobility specialist: a small tank with a big hammer whose kit exists to shut down mobile champions. Steadfast Presence grounds dashes mid-flight, Heroic Charge carries people into walls for a long stun, and her ultimate launches the enemy's most important champion out of the fight entirely.

In lane she is sturdier than she looks. The buckler from her passive gives her ranged poke and a free shield when she picks it back up, her Q chunks anyone close, and laners who rely on a dash to engage or escape find that button no longer works.

Her limits are clear: she needs walls for her best stun, her solo kill pressure is modest, and ranged kiters who never dash give her nothing to deny.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Trade around Iron Ambassador without crossing the whole wave just to recover the buckler. When the shield is safe to collect, use it to cover Hammer Shock's delayed second hit and leave before the return trade. Heroic Charge becomes dangerous near a wall, so control the lane brush and angle the wave to make that threat visible. Hold Steadfast Presence for the dash that begins the opponent's all-in. Against dashless ranged champions, farm patiently and save Heroic Charge for a wall angle or jungle setup rather than forcing contact in open lane.
gamePlan.midGame: Group after fixing the Baron wave, because your kit is more valuable in a river skirmish than an isolated damage race. At six minutes, Herald is usually the stronger first conversion, and the walls around its pit give Heroic Charge reliable stun angles. Steadfast Presence can deny a normal dash through the choke. Charge Keeper's Verdict when removing the enemy jungler or frontline secures the objective, or release it before 0.5 seconds for the short knockup when your team wants to keep fighting the target nearby.
gamePlan.lateGame: Choose between protecting the carry and removing an objective threat before the fight begins. Stay near your backline against dash-heavy divers, hold Steadfast Presence for their entry, and use Heroic Charge only when nearby terrain gives a reliable stun. At Baron or Elder, charge Keeper's Verdict to remove the enemy jungler or strongest frontliner when your team can finish during the absence. Move with allies through jungle corridors and avoid checking the wall angle alone.
gamePlan.teamfights: Start near the ally the enemy wants to dive and hold Steadfast Presence until a meaningful dash begins. Follow the grounded target with Hammer Shock or Heroic Charge when the wall angle is safe. Keeper's Verdict is a displacement, so an unstoppable or displacement-immune target cannot be launched while that immunity holds. Charge it to remove a threat from the fight, or tap it for the short knockup when your team can immediately follow. Do not send a nearly defeated enemy to safety unless removing them protects a more important objective or carry.

startingItem.name: Relic Shield
startingItem.note: Turns the wave into gold and health for a support who is walking at people rather than farming.

boots.name: Armored Advance
boots.note: Armor and health, which let him survive the trade his own hook starts.

coreItems.name: Bulwark of the Mountain
coreItems.note: The quest upgrade strengthens the health behind Nautilus's shield, helping him absorb the return damage after Dredge Line and his passive root commit him.

coreItems.name: Warmog's Armor
coreItems.note: The large health pool strengthens Nautilus's shield, and out-of-combat regeneration lets him absorb poke, miss a hook, and reset for another engage without recalling.

coreItems.name: Frozen Heart
coreItems.note: Build this when the enemy team has a lot of attack speed dependent champions, which his chain of crowd control is already holding still.

coreItems.name: Force of Nature
coreItems.note: Build this when the enemy team has two or more AP champions. The move speed also helps him close before his hook is up.

coreItems.name: Thornmail
coreItems.note: Build this against healing. The Grievous Wounds applies from your own damage as well as when they attack you, so the carry he hooked stays cut off from it.

situationalItems.name: Yordle Trap
situationalItems.note: His hook, his passive root and his ultimate all displace or immobilize, so the shred triggers on nearly every ability.

situationalItems.name: Randuin's Omen
situationalItems.note: Build this when the enemy team has multiple crit champions. Dredge Line and his passive root hold Nautilus beside the carry, so crit reduction protects him while he chains the rest of his crowd control.

situationalItems.name: Chainlaced Crushers
situationalItems.note: Boot swap against heavy magic damage and crowd control, which lands on him before his own does.

situationalItems.name: Amaranth's Twinguard
situationalItems.note: Build this when you are fighting in the middle of the enemy team and need both armor and magic resist. Nautilus's layered crowd control keeps him engaged long enough to activate Twinguard before his shield and second rotation arrive.

keystoneRune.name: Ice Overlord
keystoneRune.desc: Immobilizing an enemy champion creates icy beams and a frozen zone that slows enemies inside.
keystoneRune.note: Dredge Line, his passive root, Riptide's slow, and Depth Charge give him crowd control on three basic parts of a normal engage, making Ice Overlord easy to trigger while its durability helps him survive beside the target.

primaryRunes.name: Courage of the Colossus
primaryRunes.desc: Immobilizing enemy champions grants a defensive shield for frontline engages.
primaryRunes.note: His hook immobilizes, so the shield arrives on the same button he opens the fight with.

primaryRunes.name: Second Wind
primaryRunes.desc: After taking damage from a champion, regenerate health over time.
primaryRunes.note: He holds hook range through poke, and this pays that health back before the next attempt.

primaryRunes.name: Overgrowth
primaryRunes.desc: Gain permanent maximum health when nearby minions or monsters die.
primaryRunes.note: He is the frontline in every fight, and the health is what keeps his chain crowd control coming.

secondaryRunes.name: Hexflash
secondaryRunes.desc: While Flash is on cooldown, it is replaced by Hexflash.
secondaryRunes.note: Flash into hook is the engage everyone respects, and Hexflash keeps a version of it while Flash is down.

spells.name: Flash
spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

goodAgainst.note: Lux has no dash, so sidestepping Light Binding creates a clean Dredge Line window. Her binding passes through and damages minions in Wild Rift, however, and Lucent Singularity still slows you, so do not treat the wave as complete safety on the approach.
Fragile and slower than she looks, her auras mean nothing once she is the one rooted and knocked up, and her thin early health costs her every time she steps up to cast.

Soraka has no dash, and Dredge Line plus your passive root can keep her from repeatedly casting Astral Infusion. She does not spend health or root herself to heal in Wild Rift, so engage when Equinox is unavailable or from an angle where its silence zone cannot stop your follow-up.

Pyke plays the same pick game with much less durability. Dredge Line can punish him while he charges Bone Skewer, and your passive root or targeted Depth Charge can catch him after Phantom Undertow before his grey-health recovery begins.

weakAgainst.note: Howling Gale can interrupt your approach and Monsoon knocks you away from the target before healing Janna's team during its channel. Make her spend one disengage tool before committing Dredge Line, or use Depth Charge to force movement and follow after the knockback.

Black Shield grants crowd-control immunity while its magic shield holds, so it can deny Dredge Line's displacement or Depth Charge's knockup. Your magic damage can break it, however, and Dredge Line still pulls Nautilus toward a shielded target; track its remaining strength instead of assuming either engage is automatically wasted.

Death Sentence contests the same pick angles, Flay can push you away after Dredge Line brings you in, and Dark Passage can extract Thresh's carry unless your root lands before they use it. Pressure the lantern landing point rather than spending every disable on the first body.
The engage mirror goes her way: her dismount crash lands faster than your walk-up hook, her W bulk out-trades your shield, and her shred strips the armor your tank plan leans on.

Unbreakable intercepts Dredge Line for Braum's carry, while Concussive Blows punishes the extended melee trade after you arrive. The hook still connects to Braum himself, so choose whether pulling onto the frontline is useful before throwing it through his shield.

gamePlan.overview:
Nautilus forces the fight whether the enemy wants one or not. Dredge Line stops on the first enemy or terrain hit: an enemy pulls both sides together, while terrain pulls Nautilus to it and refunds half the mana and cooldown. His first attack roots each target on its own cooldown, Titan's Wrath shields him and adds area damage to his attacks while it holds, and Riptide sends out three slowing waves. Depth Charge pursues one chosen champion and knocks up every enemy caught in its path before erupting under the target. He is one of Wild Rift's heaviest engage supports, and also one of its slowest.

In Dragon lane, Nautilus turns one catch into an extended control chain. Dredge Line starts the approach, the first attack roots, and Depth Charge can continue the lockdown after a target uses mobility. The threat changes how the enemy duo can approach the wave, but each engage still needs allied follow-up and a safe route through the opposing support.

The catch is that all his range lives on the hook, and everyone can see it coming. Miss it and he is a slow melee tank with no escape and a long wait before his threat returns. A Nautilus who whiffs is a Nautilus the enemy simply walks past.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Lane for the hook, not the farm. Stand so a wall sits behind your target and the enemy duo cannot tell who you are aiming at, then pull, root with your first attack, and let your ADC unload while they are stuck. Your shield and Riptide let you step into these trades first and eat the return fire. Respect the matchups where stepping into hook range means stepping into poke: against artillery and disengage, wait out their cooldowns instead of throwing yours away. Keep the river warded, because your engage is the perfect setup for your jungler, and a hook into a gank is two kills instead of one.
gamePlan.midGame: Your pick threat now covers the map. Shove the wave, then hunt: a hook from a brush onto the enemy mid or jungler near dragon wins the fight before it starts. Your ultimate reaches across a skirmish to lock the most important target, so save it for their carry instead of the nearest body. Set up dragon and herald by warding ahead of the timer and engaging onto whoever comes to contest, because one rooted body in a pit fight usually decides the whole thing. Roam with intent: your kit lands ganks that have no business landing.
gamePlan.lateGame: One hook decides whole fights now. You are the opener, so your timing is the team's timing: go when your damage is grouped behind you, and never throw the first hook into a wall of bodies that just eats it. Your ultimate locks the enemy carry from long range, and every fight asks whether to start with it or hold it to peel a diver off your own carry. If their backline is exposed, hook yourself onto it and crack the fight open. If it is not, sit on your carry and be the peel their assassin has to get through.
gamePlan.teamfights: Pick a target, not a direction. The best case is a hook from the flank onto their carry, your root holding them while your team folds in, with your ultimate ready for whoever tries to peel. If the enemy is grouped tight and no clean angle exists, the job flips to peel: body-block for your ADC, throw the hook at the diver instead of the carry, and knock up whatever jumps your backline with your ultimate. Your shield and Riptide punish anyone standing near you, so stand where it does the most good. The best Nautilus fights end with the enemy carry spending the whole thing rooted or airborne, never allowed to play.

startingItem.name: Long Sword
startingItem.note: Simple early attack damage, which feeds the empowered attack his passive keeps giving him.

boots.name: Armorcrusher Boots
boots.note: Early lethality, since he is built around bursting one target down after his ultimate lands.

coreItems.name: Duskblade of Draktharr
coreItems.note: Bonus damage and a slow on the first hit against an unseen target complement Duskbringer: the ability's trail grants Nocturne movement speed and attack damage but does not slow enemies by itself.

coreItems.name: Sundered Sky
coreItems.note: Paranoia delivers Nocturne directly into the first-hit crit, and the heal keeps him fighting after the spell shield absorbs the enemy's first answer.

coreItems.name: Serylda's Grudge
coreItems.note: The item slow adds sticking power before Unspeakable Horror completes its two-second tether. Duskbringer itself creates a movement-speed trail rather than slowing the target.

coreItems.name: Edge of Night
coreItems.note: A second spell shield next to his own, covering the crowd control aimed at his ultimate dash.

coreItems.name: Guardian Angel

goodAgainst.note: Taliyah fights through her spells, so your shield eats the Seismic Shove or poke she leads with, and a fragile mage with no escape left is exactly the target your dive deletes.
Your kit turns Zed off: the spell shield eats his opening shuriken, and Paranoia's nearsight stops him from lining up the shadow swap his whole kill pattern depends on.
Lee Sin's whole combo hangs on landing Crescent Strike to dash in, and your spell shield eats it clean, leaving a skirmisher with no way to reach you.

weakAgainst.note: Rammus is an armor wall your auto-reliant damage bounces off, his taunt locks you mid-dive, and your shield only saves you if it eats that taunt with perfect timing.

Amumu carries two pieces of hard crowd control and your shield only blocks one: even if you eat the bandage, his point-blank ultimate still chains you mid-dive while his tankiness outlasts your burst.
A health-stacked yeti is a dive your burst cannot resolve: his knockup interrupts your commit, his bulk and bite outlast your damage, and he peels the carry you actually came for.

gamePlan.overview:
Nocturne is a dive assassin whose ultimate darkens the whole enemy team's vision. His kit is three tools: a spell shield that eats the first ability thrown at him, a trail of dusk that speeds him up while he runs on it, and Paranoia, which nearsights the entire enemy team and launches him at a target from across the map. He duels like a bruiser and ganks from anywhere, and once his ult is up, nobody wants to walk alone.

He wins with tempo into kills. His clear is fine rather than fast, but he does not need to win the farm race; he needs to win the fights. The shield wastes the enemy's best ability, the slow pins fleeing targets, and Paranoia starts fights anywhere on his terms. A good Nocturne snowballs off one early pick, then uses his ult on cooldown to keep making them.

His weakness is everything before that comes online. His early clear leaves him low, he has no escape once the shield is down, his nearsight can be cleansed or soaked by tanks, and ranged junglers can kite him forever. Survive his dive windows and he is a melee champion with spent cooldowns.
gamePlan.earlyGame:
Lead with Duskbringer so its attack-damage and movement-speed trail follows a large monster, then position the empowered Umbra Blades attack through as many camp units as possible for area damage and per-target healing. Basic attacks reduce Umbra Blades' cooldown by three seconds against monsters. Hold Shroud of Darkness for an invader's important spell rather than spending it on routine camp damage. Once Paranoia is learned, ganks stop needing a normal lane approach as long as the target is inside the dash's actual cast range.

The scuttle fight is winnable if you bait their key spell into your shield first, then slow them and stick; lose that exchange and you limp home. Keep an eye on the enemy jungler's start, because before your ultimate you are not a fight to take blind, and an early invade from a faster clearer can put you truly behind.
gamePlan.midGame:
Every early objective creates a long Paranoia lane toward someone rotating alone. Nearsight the enemy team as they collapse, but only dash when your team can follow. Play the cooldown like a clock: when it is up, look for the pick or objective; when it is down, farm, reset, and reposition. If a direct contest is poor, trade for the opposite objective rather than forcing a dive into a grouped team.

Between objectives, treat the minimap like a target list and counter-jungle the slower farmers while your ultimate is up, since catching a jungler alone in his own quadrant is the cleanest kill in the game.
gamePlan.lateGame: Late game, use Paranoia against a target your team can reach or to deny vision during an objective contest. Avoid isolated duels with full-build bruisers and wait for a carry to separate from peel or spend a defensive cooldown. Hold Shroud of Darkness for the control spell most likely to stop the dive, and check that allied damage can follow before taking the second cast. If the backline remains protected, use the nearsight to disrupt the enemy engage instead of arriving alone.
gamePlan.teamfights: Your teamfight job is one thing: dive. You are not the frontline and you are not there to peel; you fly through the dark, land on their backline carry, and remove it before the fight develops. Time Paranoia for the moment your team can follow, because the nearsight that gets you to the carry also blinds their team to whatever your side does next. Drop your trail on the squishy you want dead so they cannot simply walk away, shield the crowd control aimed at you on the way in, and commit fully: a Nocturne who hesitates mid-dive dies in the open. If their carry is already dead or unreachable, use the ult and the blind purely as an engage on their next-best threat and let your team clean up.

goodAgainst.note: Wukong's dash-and-burst combo cannot drop your health bar, your bite heals through the trade, and his clone trick does nothing against a point-blank knockup that answers his engage.
Warwick's pickoff hangs on his suppress leap, and your knockup snaps him out of the air before it lands, while your health bar outlasts what his drain can chew through.
