Evelynn ignores your bulk by bursting it with magic once her charm holds you, and her camouflage means the fight starts before you can ever land the knockup.

gamePlan.overview:
Nunu and Willump clear the jungle by eating it. Consume bites a chunk out of any large monster, healing a lot and clearing camps faster than almost anything in the game, so your first lap ends with a head start nobody else has. Biggest Snowball Ever! builds into a rolling tackle that knocks up whatever it hits, Snowball Barrage hails down snowballs that slow and then root, and Absolute Zero is a channeled blizzard that slows everyone in reach before detonating. The plan is simple: build the snowball, gather speed, and crash it into a lane.

You win by being everywhere first. Clear speed becomes tempo, tempo becomes ganks and objectives, and the bite that heals off camps also rips chunks off dragon and Baron, so you bully every pit. You are not a duelist: you show up before fights are fair, land the knockup, and stall the enemy team inside a blizzard while your carries do the damage.

The catch is that everything strong about you is loud. The snowball ramp is visible from across the screen, the blizzard channel dies to any stun, knockup, or silence, and your early damage is mediocre until you have some health and resists. Pick this champion to set the pace of the map and start fights, not to win the lonely duel at scuttle.
gamePlan.earlyGame:
Route Consume through the large monster in each camp and use its healing to leave the jungle ready to gank. Nunu can roll Biggest Snowball Ever! into a lane after only a few camps when the wave is extended or an ally has crowd control, then return to the remaining route without losing much health. When every lane is neutral, keep clearing and use the earlier river arrival instead of forcing a snowball the enemy can simply sidestep.

Your early value is setup rather than raw dueling. Charge the snowball through fog, steer it along the target's escape line, then layer Snowball Barrage while your ally deals the damage. Contest scuttle with lane support and combine Consume with Smite when it matters; do not turn a champion built for ganks and secure into a stationary duel against an early fighter.
gamePlan.midGame:
Consume plus Smite makes Nunu unusually strong at starting, threatening, and securing early objectives. Contest freely when your team is ahead. When the game is even, still lean dragon, and take Herald only when your team can actually use the tower it buys.

Between objectives, take a dragon then immediately look for the next gank while the enemy resets. A long snowball roll out of fog onto a mid laner or marksman creates the pick that wins the next objective fight before it starts.
gamePlan.lateGame: Use Consume and Smite as an objective-secure combination, but start Baron only after tracking the enemy jungler and the lanes that can collapse. Threaten Biggest Snowball Ever! from a side route and steer it toward a target your team can reach. Save Absolute Zero for a choke, a layered engage, or a peel situation where enemies cannot simply leave the channel. Build enough durability to frontline, then disengage when the secure tools are unavailable instead of dying before the next objective attempt.
gamePlan.teamfights: Your teamfight is engage and area control. Roll a snowball into the densest part of their formation for the knockup, then drop Absolute Zero on the pile so the whole enemy team crawls through the slow while your damage dealers work. The snowball's ramp means you want to start it from a flank or from fog, not from a spot they can sidestep, and the blizzard should land where it catches two or three enemies rather than chasing one. Protect the channel: it is a long cast and a single stun ends it, so commit once their key crowd control is spent or your team stands between you and the danger. Done right, you are the wall their backline cannot walk through.

Ragnarok walks straight through the knockup that is his way into and out of fights, and your true damage shreds any armor he stacks. His clone buys a second, but he has no way to escape your chase.

Spear poke from a range you cannot answer wears you down, and in cougar form she slows you while you swing at nothing. She takes scuttle and objectives at range and kites you around every wall.

gamePlan.overview:
Olaf is a sustained-damage jungler who becomes more dangerous as his health drops. Undertow slows and can be picked up to reduce its cooldown, while his passive increases attack speed and healing at lower health. Ragnarok grants immunity to most control effects during its active window, allowing Olaf to keep moving through the spells that would normally stop a diver. It does not remove the need to track damage, spacing, and the duration of the immunity.

In the jungle his clear is fast, his ganks come online early thanks to the axe slow, and he wins most duels over scuttle and invades. He wants to play forward: clear, gank, fight for the early objectives, and snowball a lead before the enemy carries matter.

The catch is that he is melee with no dash, and he needs his axes to land. Kite him, slow him while his ult is down, or refuse to fight and he runs out of targets. He also scales worse than the hypercarries and tanks he beats early, so he has to end the game while his fights are still unfair.
gamePlan.earlyGame:
Your first clear is fast, so turn that into pressure the slow scalers cannot match. Path toward a scuttle you plan to fight over, because repeated Undertow axes, low-health physical vamp, and Reckless Swing's true damage make Olaf a strong early duelist. Once the clear is done, land Undertow's slow and armor reduction before using Reckless Swing to close the last short gap; Tough It Out is not the source of his slow.

Invade junglers with weak clears and take their camps, and do not be afraid to turn a counter-gank around, since your low-health passive means fights that start badly often still end well. The early game is your strongest phase, so use all of it.
gamePlan.midGame:
Olaf can take early objectives quickly, but the surrounding lane control still decides whether he should. Use Ragnarok to ignore control during the pit fight rather than assuming it protects against damage, and trade for the opposite objective when your lanes cannot contest safely.

Between objectives, hunt the enemy jungler in their own camps, keep ganking lanes that can follow up your slow, and take every skirmish you can while your power still peaks.
gamePlan.lateGame: Late game you stop being the duelist and become the diver aimed at the enemy backline. Your 1v1 starts losing to scaled hypercarries and full tanks, so stop looking for fair fights in the side jungle. Baron fights suit you: your sustain lets you control the pit, and your ult makes you almost impossible to peel off the objective or off their carry once you commit. Build some durability so you survive the walk in, then trust your true damage, which ignores armor but still has to chew through shields, once you reach the target. Group, find the flank, and use your lead to end the game before enemy scaling catches up.
gamePlan.teamfights: Your job in a fight is simple: turn on Ragnarok and walk straight at the enemy carry, immune to every stun and root they use to save it. If you can, wait until their key crowd control is spent elsewhere, then cross the gap. Throw an axe to slow the target before you reach it so it cannot slip away, and let your passive speed up your attacks as your health drops. Do not burn your ult just to start the walk if a slow or an approach through fog gets you there clean; save the immunity for the moment they actually try to lock you down.

Zed needs items before he can one-shot anyone, and your level-three burst arrives long before his does. Aegis blocks his shuriken poke, and his squishy frame cannot trade back into your stun-leap.

weakAgainst.note: His armor eats your physical burst, Defensive Ball Curl turns your spear combo back on you, and his taunt locks you down the moment you commit. He only gets tankier as the game runs.
Stacked health means your burst cannot finish him, his knockup interrupts your dive, and he snowballs objectives while your closing window expires.
Her tankiness and sustain survive your all-in, and once dragon form and her items arrive she wins on raw stats against a Pantheon past his window. She only needs to reach her spike.

gamePlan.overview:
Pantheon is a jungle bully built to make the first ten minutes miserable and cash the lead in before the enemy scales. His spear hits from range or stabs up close, Shield Vault leaps onto a target and stuns it, and Aegis blocks the attacks and abilities that punish other melee junglers for diving, though turret shots still land through it. None of it scales into a late-game monster, and that is the point: he wants the game decided while his early kit is still the scariest thing on the map.

He wins by turning tempo into kills. His clear is quick and Aegis eats the camp damage, so he reaches his first gank early. A Shield Vault stun into his spear combo usually kills, and from there he presses the lead into towers, dragons, and the enemy jungle. Grand Starfall lets him drop into a fight two lanes away, so one snowball spreads across the whole map.

The catch is the timer. He is frontloaded burst with no real sustain, and once enemies stack some health and resistances his damage stops deleting anyone. Lose the early skirmishes and there is no scaling plan to fall back on.
gamePlan.earlyGame:
Path toward the lane you want to influence and check it as soon as Shield Vault is available. Pantheon's point-and-click stun makes a level-three visit worth breaking the clear for when the target is extended and your laner can follow; open with the stun, weave the empowered attack, then aim Comet Spear along the retreat. Its critical strike now requires the target to be below 25% health, so do not hold the spear waiting for the old, higher execute window. If the lane is not ready, finish your route instead of revealing for harmless poke.

Use Aegis Assault to block the enemy champion's return damage during a gank or river fight, not as a reason to stand in a camp longer. You can contest scuttle and invade a slower starter when a nearby lane has priority, but leave when that support disappears. Your early strength should buy a lane lead or enemy camps before the map begins scaling past you.
gamePlan.midGame:
Pantheon should spend his strongest map window creating a numbers advantage before an objective begins. Grand Starfall can turn a distant fight into a temporary numbers advantage, but its landing is telegraphed, so aim the initial spear slow across the target's escape path. If your lanes cannot contest directly, trade for the opposite objective or use the pressure to take a tower rather than forcing a late arrival into a prepared team.

Between objectives, keep counter-jungling the enemy who cannot fight back and look for picks on anyone walking through river without vision. Every kill and objective you take now covers for the late game where you fall off.
gamePlan.lateGame: By late game, defensive items make it harder to burst a protected carry in one rotation. Use Grand Starfall as a flank or a fast rotation that creates a temporary numbers advantage, then convert the pick into Baron, Elder, or a turret. In grouped fights, stun a reachable damage dealer or peel a diver so your better-scaling teammates can finish the target. Avoid landing behind the enemy team unless allied follow-up is already in range.
gamePlan.teamfights: Your job is to reach the enemy carry and shut them down, not to trade in the front line. Look for a flank or a Grand Starfall angle that puts you next to their backline, then Shield Vault the highest-value target, stun them, and dump your spear combo before their team can peel. Aegis is what keeps you alive on the way in, so use it against the burst and crowd control aimed at you when you commit. If their carry is too well protected, do not throw yourself away: hold your leap, use the stun to peel a diver off your own carries, and poke with your spear until an opening appears.

startingItem.name: Amplifying Tome
startingItem.note: Early ability power, which her passive already adds to every attack she lands.

boots.name: Spellslinger's Shoes
boots.note: Magic penetration keeps her Ball hurting in a lane she wins by chipping rather than bursting.

coreItems.name: Archangel's Staff
coreItems.note: Turns her mana pool into ability power, and she casts constantly to keep the Ball where she wants it.

coreItems.name: Blackfire Torch
coreItems.note: The Ball hits several enemies at once, so the stacking bonus counts multiple champions in a fight.

coreItems.name: Rabadon's Deathcap
coreItems.note: Multiplies her ability power, which raises her poke, her shield and her ultimate together.

coreItems.name: Cryptbloom
coreItems.note: Cuts the magic resist that lets a target survive being pulled into her ultimate. The healing on takedown also helps her team. Choose it when enemies have not built much magic resist, so trading Void Staff's extra damage for more ability haste and an area heal after takedowns is worthwhile.

coreItems.name: Zhonya's Hourglass
coreItems.note: Build this for when her ultimate is spent and their team is still on her. Buy Seeker's Armguard early for the armor and ability power.

situationalItems.name: Morellonomicon
situationalItems.note: Build this when enemies heal through Orianna's teamfight damage. The Ball's area spells apply Grievous Wounds to several targets before Command: Shockwave's follow-up lands; Oblivion Orb provides the effect early.

situationalItems.name: Oceanid's Trident
situationalItems.note: Build this when the enemy has shields that keep absorbing the damage her ultimate gathered everyone for.

situationalItems.name: Banshee's Veil
situationalItems.note: Build this when the enemy has a hook or point-and-click stun, since she has no mobility of her own.

situationalItems.name: Cosmic Drive
situationalItems.note: Haste and move speed for a champion who has to keep repositioning to keep the Ball useful, since spacing is her only defence.

situationalItems.name: Void Staff
situationalItems.note: The raw penetration alternative to Cryptbloom. Build it when a magic resist frontline is what blunts the Ball. Choose it over Cryptbloom when enemies are stacking magic resist and maximum personal damage matters more than ability haste and team healing.

keystoneRune.name: Conqueror
keystoneRune.desc: Gain stacks by damaging enemy champions. At maximum stacks, gain bonus damage and healing.
keystoneRune.note: Her damage is steady chip from the Ball rather than one burst, so she stacks across a fight and the healing pays for holding her line.

primaryRunes.name: Axiom Arcanist
primaryRunes.desc: Empower your spell-focused burst with extra damage and scaling for ability-heavy champions.
primaryRunes.note: Her ultimate is the cast the whole fight is built around, and takedowns inside it cut the cooldown for the next one.

primaryRunes.name: Transcendence
primaryRunes.desc: Gain ability haste, then reduce a basic ability's cooldown after it hits at level 9.
primaryRunes.note: Ability haste means the Ball moves more often, which is how much space she controls.

primaryRunes.name: Nimbus Cloak
primaryRunes.desc: After casting a summoner spell, gain movement speed and slow resistance.
primaryRunes.note: Move speed after a summoner spell helps a mage with no dash reposition to where the Ball needs to be.

secondaryRunes.name: Bone Plating
secondaryRunes.desc: After taking damage from a champion, the next 3 instances of champion damage are reduced.
secondaryRunes.note: Take this against assassins who can reach Orianna before the Ball controls the fight.

spells.name: Flash
spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

goodAgainst.note: Command: Protect can absorb part of Lux's poke and its attached defenses help while the Ball remains on you, but Light Binding passes through and damages minions in Wild Rift, Lucent Singularity slows before automatically detonating, and Final Spark is global. Pressure her between cooldowns instead of treating Q as her only threat.

Orianna can control the wave outside Annie's short basic-spell range, but a loaded Pyromania stun into Tibbers can exceed one shield. Track Annie's passive stacks, keep the Ball attached for its armor and magic resistance when she can Flash engage, and punish while the stun is unprepared.

Veigar has no dash and needs time to scale, so Ball poke and wave control can build priority early. Event Horizon still controls a large area without having to hit first, and walking into its edge stuns; keep the Ball in range without stepping inside the cage for a trade.

Orianna never dashes, so she does not create free Gloom marks. Mistral Bolt and Looming Darkness are telegraphed, but Personal Space hits immediately around Vex and any basic ability can carry a prepared Doom fear; track the fear bar before stepping into Shockwave range.
Galio wants you inside his taunt range and your kit never needs to go there, though his tankiness and magic resist mean you deny his priority rather than kill him.

weakAgainst.note: Living Shadow changes the angle of Razor Shuriken around Orianna's ball, and Death Mark places Zed behind her after she has spent Command: Protect on poke. Keep the ball attached when his ultimate is ready, place Command: Dissonance on the return shadow, and hold Shockwave for his reappearance instead of using it to start the trade.
Katarina dashes through minions onto you and resets off kills, and your slow ball cannot catch a champion who is constantly blinking, so one pick on you starts her snowball.
You bully his weak early lane, but once his ultimate spike arrives he blinks onto you and out-scales everything you do, so an even long game slips away from you.

Zyra's plants create repeated pressure from several angles and Grasping Roots can hold Orianna inside Stranglethorns. Roots do not prevent spell casts, so shield immediately and use Dissonance's ally speed field to leave before the delayed knockup rather than assuming you cannot respond.

gamePlan.overview:
Orianna's abilities originate from the Ball, so its position determines her damage, shield, and control angles. Command: Attack damages enemies along its path and at the destination, with reduced damage after hitting multiple enemies. Dissonance pulses around the Ball and leaves a three-second field that slows enemies while speeding Orianna and allies. Command: Protect grants armor and magic resistance to whichever champion holds the Ball; casting it flies through enemies, then shields the allied champion it reaches for 2.5 seconds. Shockwave damages, stuns for 0.75 seconds, and pulls nearby enemies 325 units.

She wins mid by owning the wave and the tempo around it. Her clear is clean enough that she rarely loses priority to another mage, and once she has priority she can shove, look at the river, place the ball on a flank, and set up her jungler or a dive. She does not delete you from full like an assassin. She chips, she zones, her shield tilts every trade her way, and she scales toward a teamfight where one button decides everything.

The catch is that the Ball is her whole defense and she has no dash or blink. If Orianna moves too far from it, the Ball snaps back to her and Shockwave is put on a 0.75-second cooldown, so crossing the leash at the start of an engage can briefly remove her best response. Dissonance's speed and Protect's shield help her kite, but neither is instant terrain-crossing mobility.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Lane around the Ball's position, not only Orianna's. Send it through the wave with Command: Attack, then return it through the enemy mid with Protect when an allied-champion target creates that line. Use Dissonance's enemy slow and allied movement speed to control the short trade. Protect's attached defenses matter before the damage lands, so keep the Ball on yourself when an all-in is imminent rather than assuming the shield alone covers a full combo.
gamePlan.midGame: This is where priority becomes objectives. Shove the wave, ward the river, and put the ball on a choke or a flank so your jungler can start dragon or Herald inside your zone. Both first objectives spawn at six minutes, so move toward the side your lanes can control. Herald is usually the stronger even conversion, while dragon is worth prioritizing when your composition can keep winning grouped fights toward soul. Your roams are not assassin roams, but Command: Dissonance and Command: Shockwave can hold a side-lane target long enough for allies to finish. Take side-lane tempo when the map allows, but return before the objective setup begins.
gamePlan.lateGame: Full items and you become the most important non-engage button on the map. Your poke chunks from range, your shield can save a diving teammate or your own life, and your ultimate can decide an entire fight the moment the enemy clusters. Position behind your frontline like the squishy you are, because dying without casting your ultimate is the one way to lose a fight you were winning. Keep the ball where it threatens the most enemies at once and let your team play around the zone you control. One well-placed Shockwave late ends games that were not otherwise close.
gamePlan.teamfights: You start the fight without stepping forward when the Ball is already attached to an allied champion diving into their formation or resting at a location set by Command: Attack. Command: Protect cannot attach it to a minion. When enemies clump, Shockwave's 0.75-second stun and 325-unit pull set up your team's damage; follow with Dissonance so its damage and slow field cover the gathered targets. Keep track of the Ball leash, because letting it snap back puts Shockwave on a brief cooldown at exactly the wrong moment.

coreItems.name: Kaenic Rookern

keystoneRune.desc: Every 4 seconds in combat, your next attack against a champion deals bonus damage and heals you.
keystoneRune.note: Permanent health growth, and his passive amplifies every point of health he collects.

primaryRunes.desc: Charge up a powerful attack against turrets.
primaryRunes.note: He shoves waves with his Q and can buy items without recalling, so a lane he holds turns into towers.

primaryRunes.note: He farms through poke rather than answering it, and this covers the cost of holding the wave.

primaryRunes.note: He is built to hold the front, and extra max health is the stat that job runs on.

secondaryRunes.name: Transcendence

secondaryRunes.note: Ability haste means more pillars and charges, which is how he controls space.

spells.name: Flash
spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

goodAgainst.note: Renekton is strongest early, while Ornn's defensive multiplier and remote purchases scale with levels. Empowered Ruthless Predator destroys damage shields but Ornn has no innate shield to remove; the real danger is its longer stun before Ornn can use Bellows Breath's displacement immunity.

Sett builds Grit from damage taken and can answer a long trade with Haymaker. Use Bellows Breath's displacement immunity against a predictable Facebreaker or The Show Stopper, then apply Brittle before Searing Charge so the terrain knockup consumes it for bonus damage and longer control.

Counter Strike dodges Ornn's Brittle-consuming basic attack and reduces champion area damage by 25%, so Bellows Breath and Searing Charge are not free damage into it. Wait out the stance before using the attack knockback, while keeping terrain ready to stop Jax's follow-up.

weakAgainst.note: Riposte can deny the knockup from Searing Charge or the Brittle crowd control that completes Ornn's trade, while Fiora's Vitals deal maximum-health true damage that ignores his tank build. Bait Riposte with Bellows Breath pressure, avoid charging into a wall while it is ready, and disengage rather than extending the side-lane duel after she exposes Grand Challenge.

Hookshot lets Camille cross the pillar angle before Searing Charge connects, while Tactical Sweep and the readied Precision Protocol punish Ornn's large health pool with percent-health and true damage. Hold Searing Charge for Camille's landing point instead of opening with it, and take short Brittle trades before her second Precision Protocol is ready.
Percent-health true damage against a champion made of health, and she kites your slow combo from range. You were never going to win the duel.

Ambessa's repeated dashes let her move around the delayed pillar and Searing Charge line, while Ornn has no innate shield to absorb her short trades. Aim Volcanic Rupture behind her likely exit, and do not rely on Bellows Breath's displacement immunity to prevent her ultimate suppression.

gamePlan.overview:
Ornn can buy items without recalling by channeling Living Forge for two seconds; enemy champion or turret damage interrupts the channel. He also gains a level-scaling percentage increase to all bonus health, armor, and magic resistance. At levels 7, 10, and 13, his next forge grants the closest allied champion five Living Forge stacks, up to fifteen, and each stack lets that ally purchase from anywhere once. Wild Rift Ornn does not create PC-style masterwork item upgrades.

In lane he is patient with a terrain combo. Volcanic Rupture slows, then raises an impassable pillar after 1.125 seconds. Bellows Breath makes Ornn displacement immune while he marches and applies Brittle with its final, double-damage flame. Searing Charge only produces its 1.25-second knockup and stun when Ornn collides with terrain, including his own pillar, and can destroy some champion-created terrain.

Call of the Forge God is the payoff. The first ram pass deals magic damage, slows, and applies Brittle but does not knock enemies up. Ornn must recast and collide with the ram to redirect it; only that return pass knocks up and stuns, with the duration reduced to 0.5 seconds after the first enemy champion hit.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Farm, forge, and punish mistakes. A reliable control sequence is Volcanic Rupture to create the delayed pillar, Bellows Breath to apply Brittle, then Searing Charge into that terrain so the knockup consumes Brittle for maximum-health magic damage and 30% longer crowd control. If you attack a Brittle target instead, the empowered attack knocks them back and consumes the mark. Forge only after creating safety, because champion or turret damage interrupts the channel.
gamePlan.midGame: Fix the Baron wave before moving toward Herald or dragon, then arrive early enough to line Call of the Forge God through the river entrance. The incoming ram slows and applies Brittle, while the redirected pass supplies the knockup and consumes the mark. Between fights, use Living Forge near the ally receiving the next remote-purchase stacks so both of you can remain on the map. The purchase saves a recall but does not improve the item's stats, so do not delay an objective setup just to wait for more gold.
gamePlan.lateGame: Clear the side wave early and group before Baron or Elder so the enemy cannot interrupt the ultimate recast from fog. Hold Call of the Forge God for an angle that crosses priority targets and leaves a safe line to redirect the ram. Use Living Forge between objective windows to help allies avoid a recall, not while the team is already contesting vision. The purchases cost normal gold and grant normal stats, so their value is map tempo rather than extra combat power at equal gold.
gamePlan.teamfights: Start it or stretch it. The dream opening is the incoming ram slowing and making the backline Brittle, followed by a successful recast that redirects it for the actual knockup. Volcanic Rupture's pillar can cut a retreat, while Searing Charge into terrain supplies a separate knockup. For peel, apply Brittle with Bellows Breath, then consume it with your attack knockback, Searing Charge, or an ally's immobilizing effect.

startingItem.note: Support income, and his gold from roams and picks is what funds a full assassin build.

boots.name: Armorcrusher Boots
boots.note: Early lethality, since he is built around bursting a squishy target below his execute threshold.

coreItems.name: Black Mist Scythe
coreItems.note: Charged hooks and quick attacks complete the quest without taking lane farm, and the offensive upgrade supports the burst that moves targets toward Death from Below's execute line.

coreItems.name: Youmuu's Ghostblade
coreItems.note: Momentum builds while he roams between lanes, so the speed and penetration are active when he arrives for a pick.

coreItems.name: Duskblade of Draktharr
coreItems.note: Bonus damage and a slow on the first hit against an unseen target, which is what a roaming assassin support wants when opening a pick.

coreItems.name: Serpent's Fang
coreItems.note: Build this when the enemy has shields. A shield does not raise their health, so it never lifts them past his execute threshold, but it does absorb the damage he needs to push them down to it in the first place.

coreItems.name: Edge of Night
coreItems.note: The spell shield blocks the crowd control aimed at him mid-hook, which is his only committed moment.

situationalItems.name: Guardian Angel
situationalItems.note: Revives him once after dying. Pyke cannot increase maximum health through items, but armor, magic resistance, damage-delay effects, shields, and revives still provide durability; Guardian Angel is not his only defensive option.

situationalItems.name: Stridebreaker
situationalItems.desc: Juggernaut bruiser item with a dash
situationalItems.note: Build this when landing the hook is the problem. The dash and slow help him reach the target he missed.

situationalItems.name: Death's Dance
situationalItems.note: Spreads burst damage out over a few seconds, which buys time for the grey health healing his passive gives him out of vision.

situationalItems.name: Maw of Malmortius
situationalItems.note: Build this against heavy magic burst, which matters more on a champion who cannot itemize health.

keystoneRune.name: Ice Overlord
keystoneRune.desc: Immobilizing an enemy champion creates icy beams and a frozen zone that slows enemies inside.
keystoneRune.note: His hook and his E stun both immobilize, so the zone lands on the target he is setting up to execute.

primaryRunes.name: Courage of the Colossus
primaryRunes.desc: Immobilizing enemy champions grants a defensive shield for frontline engages.
primaryRunes.note: Both his hook and his E immobilize, so the shield lands on the same cast he opens with and covers the walk back out.

primaryRunes.name: Bone Plating
primaryRunes.desc: After taking damage from a champion, the next 3 instances of champion damage are reduced.
primaryRunes.note: He commits to hook range with no health to spare, and this blunts the return fire from the first enemy who answers.

primaryRunes.name: Perseverance
primaryRunes.desc: Gain tenacity and bonus defenses while immobilized.
primaryRunes.note: Take this against teams whose crowd control prevents the champion's key follow-up. Its tenacity shortens most disables and grants temporary defenses while immobilized. The shorter disable helps Pyke slip back into camouflage or dash out before his grey health is permanently removed.

secondaryRunes.name: Sudden Impact
secondaryRunes.desc: Deal bonus true damage after using mobility or exiting stealth.
secondaryRunes.note: His E is a dash, so the bonus true damage lands right as he arrives.

spells.name: Flash
spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

gamePlan.overview:
Pyke is a support built to make kills and gold instead of protection. Bonus health cannot increase his maximum health and is converted to attack damage instead. He stores part of post-mitigation champion damage as grey health; much more when at least two visible enemy champions are nearby; and rapidly heals it only while enemies cannot see him. Armor penetration increases both the stored percentage and several other parts of his kit.

Bone Skewer gains range during the first second of a charge and can be held for up to three. A release within 0.4 seconds instead thrusts through all enemies in front; a charged throw hits the first enemy, pulls, reveals, and slows them by 90% for one second. Ghostwater Dive camouflages and speeds Pyke for five seconds, but nearby enemies receive an alert; including whether Pyke can execute them; and attacking or casting ends it. Phantom Undertow dashes, then a phantom homes back after one second to stun enemies it crosses for a duration that scales with armor penetration.

Death from Below executes champions below its displayed threshold; shields do not add to current health for that check. Targets above the threshold take only half that amount as physical damage. Pyke blinks to the X when it hits a champion, but a free 15-second recast depends on a champion dying inside the X through the execution or an ally's kill, not merely on touching a healthy target. Executions give the assisting ally full kill gold and give Pyke an enlarged personal payout under the listed cap.

The trade-off is that he keeps an assassin's tiny health bar. Hard crowd control kills him before the stealth saves him, and any support tanky enough to walk through his combo and live beats him. He also has to commit to make anything happen, and a whiffed hook means a long, exposed walk back to lane.
gamePlan.earlyGame:
Play aggressively in Dragon lane when the matchup allows it, since small early leads make later roams safer. Control the side brush, threaten Bone Skewer when the enemy carry walks up to last-hit, and use Phantom Undertow only when its stun line and Pyke's exit are both clear. A missed hook removes most of your pressure until it returns, so sometimes holding the charge is more valuable than releasing it into a blocked angle.

Wave timing separates a useful roam from abandoning your carry. Leave after your duo crashes the wave into the enemy turret, when your carry recalls, or when the enemy duo cannot hold a freeze. On early recalls, check mid and your jungler's path before returning to Dragon lane. If no play is available, go back to lane instead of waiting in camouflage while your carry loses the wave alone.
gamePlan.midGame:
This is where Pyke thrives. Use Ghostwater Dive to move quickly and camouflage outside enemy detection range, but do not mistake it for invisibility: nearby champions are alerted, Control Wards and close proximity reveal camouflage, and any attack or ability ends it. Roam through unwarded paths, collapse on isolated rotations, then leave enemy vision so stored grey health can actually convert back into health.

Set up around objectives before the enemy arrives. Pyke is much better at catching a champion in a river entrance than standing in the pit through a front-to-back fight, so sweep a flank, threaten Bone Skewer from fog, and turn a pick into Herald or dragon. When both first objectives spawn at six minutes, prefer the side where your lanes can move first. Herald is usually the stronger even trade, while a team built for repeated five-versus-five fights can justify starting a dragon-soul plan.
gamePlan.lateGame: Your damage is less reliable once carries have defensive tools and teams stop rotating alone. Play for information and cleanup instead of forcing hooks into a grouped formation. Ghostwater Dive lets you scout the edge of a setup, but its warning tells nearby enemies you are there, so approach from swept routes and keep Phantom Undertow available as an exit. Track health bars, shields, stasis, and untargetability before casting Death from Below. One patient execute can still chain through a fight, while one failed blink into the enemy team removes your vision and reset threat entirely.
gamePlan.teamfights: Threaten the side of the fight instead of standing beside your frontline. Bone Skewer can pull a reachable target out of formation, while Phantom Undertow is best when its returning phantom crosses the enemy's escape or your own retreat. Wait for key defensive cooldowns, then dive only when the X is likely to execute or an ally can kill the target inside it. Each successful death condition grants the free recast that makes a chain possible; hitting healthy champions repeatedly does not. A non-executing hit still blinks Pyke to the X, so use it only when that position is survivable.

coreItems.name: Bloodthirster

coreItems.name: Lord Dominik's Regard

coreItems.name: Navori Quickblades
coreItems.note: Critical attacks reduce the remaining cooldowns of her basic abilities, giving Nilah more Slipstream access and more frequent Jubilant Veil windows in extended fights.

coreItems.name: Infinity Edge
coreItems.note: Her passive heals off critical strike damage, so a crit spike is her damage and her survivability at once.

situationalItems.name: Galeforce
situationalItems.note: Situational mobility when Nilah needs another reposition to reach a priority target or adjust her angle before committing Apotheosis.

situationalItems.name: Mortal Reminder
situationalItems.note: Build this against armor stackers or enemies who heal through the fight her ultimate started. Choose it over Lord Dominik's Regard when enemy healing is the bigger problem, since Grievous Wounds stops targets from recovering Nilah's damage.

situationalItems.name: The Collector
situationalItems.note: Executes low health targets. Her ultimate pulls a group in low, so this converts those health bars into kills.

situationalItems.name: Guardian Angel
situationalItems.note: Revives her once after dying. Her ultimate commits her into the middle of everyone.

situationalItems.name: Mercurial Scimitar
situationalItems.note: Build this when a stun lands during her W, since it dodges attacks but not crowd control.

keystoneRune.name: Conqueror
keystoneRune.desc: Gain stacks by damaging enemy champions. At maximum stacks, gain bonus damage and healing.
keystoneRune.note: Nilah stays in melee range through extended fights, stacking bonus damage and healing while Apotheosis holds enemies close.

primaryRunes.name: Brutal
primaryRunes.desc: Attacks deal bonus adaptive damage to enemy champions.
primaryRunes.note: Bonus damage strengthens her repeated attacks during early clears and skirmishes before the critical-strike build is complete.

primaryRunes.name: Cut Down
primaryRunes.desc: You deal bonus adaptive damage (except true damage) to enemy champions above 60% health.
primaryRunes.note: Bonus damage against healthy champions helps her start cutting through the frontline she often has to reach first.

primaryRunes.name: Legend: Alacrity
primaryRunes.desc: Gain permanent attack speed by taking down champions, monsters, and minions.
primaryRunes.note: Attack speed means more critical strikes and more opportunities to reduce basic cooldowns through Navori Quickblades.

secondaryRunes.name: Overgrowth
secondaryRunes.desc: Gain permanent maximum health when nearby minions or monsters die.
secondaryRunes.note: Permanent health helps a melee carry survive the focus that follows Slipstream and Apotheosis.

spells.name: Flash
spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

spells.name: Smite
spells.note: Required for Jungling. Secures objectives and sustains through camp clears.

goodAgainst.note: You both scale, but you win the comparison: your lifesteal heals through his on-hit damage, Veil dodges the burst window Alpha Strike opens, and he has no answer to your dash out of a losing trade.

Jubilant Veil dodges the attacks his suppression sets up, though the suppress itself has to be avoided rather than cleansed, so Warwick needs that one lockdown to land clean, and your lifesteal outlasts his drain the longer the fight runs.
Nocturne commits everything to one dive, and Veil is a strong answer: ride out his ultimate behind the damage reduction and he has nothing left, while your sustain outlasts his single-target burst.

weakAgainst.note: Kha'Zix hunts isolated targets, and early you are one: his leap burst can chunk you before Veil matters, and his evolved reset lets him leave any trade you start.

Devastating Charge outpaces Nilah's Slipstream and knocks her away when she finally reaches melee range, while Onslaught of Shadows fears her out of Apotheosis. Jubilant Veil blocks attacks, not either displacement, so it cannot protect her committed entry.

Defensive Ball Curl turns your crit swings into damage on yourself, and his taunt forces you to keep hitting the spikes; even Veil cannot strip the taunt off you, and he is a tank built to profit from your attacks.

gamePlan.overview:
Nilah is a short-range carry played in the jungle. Formless Blade extends her attack reach after it hits, Jubilant Veil helps her avoid basic attacks and reduce incoming magic damage, and Slipstream supplies targeted mobility. Apotheosis pulls nearby enemies together and supports the sustained healing pattern she wants in a grouped skirmish. Her clear and ganks depend on using that temporary reach and mobility without entering before allies can follow.

She wins by scaling, and the payoff is huge. Early she is not a predator: her clear is average and her ganks lean on a single pull, so you farm, scale, and stay out of reach. Once her lifesteal and crit stack, she heals through everything, dodges the one spell meant to stop her, and out-damages whole teamfights while sustaining through them. Few junglers can solo-carry a fight the way she can if she reaches her items alive.

Her weakness is the early window, where she is just a melee with a slow clear and one dash. Catch her with crowd control before her sustain arrives and she folds. Every Nilah game trades a terrible early game for a terrifying late one.
gamePlan.earlyGame:
Treat the first clear as survival, not a race. Start on the side that lets you path toward a safe scuttle attempt, take your sustain seriously, and use Jubilant Veil to eat a camp's burst rather than wasting it. Contest scuttle against junglers you out-duel and give it up to the predators who would just kill you on the crab.

Your ultimate arrives with the clear and the crab, and it is a pull into your own dueling rather than a chain of crowd control, so the ganks worth walking for are the ones where the enemy is already shoved in and low. Otherwise clear, take the camps as they respawn, and get to your items. Do not get caught invading: this is your weakest stretch, and a single death delays the only thing you care about.
gamePlan.midGame:
Nilah needs teammates around her when the first objectives force a close-range fight. Arrive at dragon or Herald with your team, because your pull and sustain make you the best bridge between the two backlines in a contested pit. Contest when your team is ahead on early fights, and when it is even take Herald, since it converts without needing you to win a long fight you are still building toward. A team that wants soul is the reason to flip that.

Between objectives, power-farm and start invading the junglers you out-scale, stealing camps and forcing duels once your crit healing is online. Spend Veil on a dangerous basic-attack window or incoming magic damage; it does not protect you from a spell-based stun, root, or knockup.
gamePlan.lateGame: Late game is Nilah's whole reason for existing. Critical strikes now supply both damage and Joy Unending healing, while Formless Blade converts critical-strike chance into armor penetration for tankier targets. Around Baron, Apotheosis threatens to pull a clump together and heal Nilah's nearby allies from every damaging hit. Stop farming for its own sake and group up, because a fed Nilah beside her team gets much more value from that shared healing and from extending Jubilant Veil to the nearest ally.
gamePlan.teamfights: Your job is to reach a carry and stay alive while your sustained damage works through the fight. Open with the ultimate when the enemy clumps, pulling their backline into your team, then ride your lifesteal through the chaos as you heal off every target you hit. Veil is the line between a great fight and a dead Nilah: hold it for the stun, root, or burst combo meant to delete you, and dash through it instead. You want to be unkillable in the middle of the fight, not picking at the edges, because your whole identity is sustaining through damage that should have killed you. Use the pull to drag a fleeing carry back into range and let the healing win the fight on sustain.

goodAgainst.note: Master Yi is the purest auto-attacker in the jungle, so every swing of Wuju Style comes back into his own face while the taunt freezes him mid-combo. His own attacks are what kill him, and no amount of scaling fixes that.

Talon relies on a blink-and-auto combo, and the taunt locks him mid-rotation while reflected damage answers every strike. He is too squishy to survive attacking into your armor, so one committed combo gets him killed.
Every shotgun auto Graves fires into Ball Curl comes back harder, and the taunt strips the dash he uses to reposition. His kite-and-reload pattern turns against him when he cannot make space.

weakAgainst.note: Diana deals magic damage from front to back, so your armor means almost nothing, and her pull holds you in place for the full combo. The reflect barely answers her spells.

Lillia's damage is magic that ignores your armor stacks, and her ramping speed keeps her ahead of Powerball all fight. Your reflect needs her to hit you, but she kites and burns you from range instead.
Amumu's bandage stun and multi-target ult lock you out of Powerball, and his percent-health aura damage ignores the armor you stacked. Once you are rooted, your reactive damage never gets going.

gamePlan.overview:
Rammus turns your own aggression into the thing that kills you. He rolls into a ball to engage fast, taunts one enemy into attacking him, and punishes every basic attack thrown at him while Defensive Ball Curl is up: the more they swing, the more damage they take. Few champions punish a team harder for hitting the wrong target.

His jungle plan runs on speed. Powerball crosses the map faster than any other jungler moves, so his ganks arrive from angles that looked safe, and his clear speeds up sharply once he has some armor. He does not assassinate or split push: he picks one target, sticks to it with a taunt and a slow, and stays on it until it dies. Against auto-attackers and ability spammers he is extremely hard to kill.

The catch is that his damage is reactive and his kit does one thing: hard crowd control plus single-target lockdown. Powerball can be interrupted by crowd control, but Soaring Slam gives him a second way to engage or escape. A team that refuses to attack him, or that kites both approaches, leaves him chasing people all game.
gamePlan.earlyGame:
Your first clear is patient. Keep Defensive Ball Curl active while camps are hitting you and weave attacks throughout it, since the reflected damage is what keeps the clear moving. Once Soaring Slam is learned, cast it during Powerball when the center knockup is needed, or preserve it as a crowd-control-immune follow-up after the roll is interrupted.

Gank while the camps respawn. Scuttle fights tilt your way once the ball is up, since it catches whoever contests and the taunt pins them while your laner collapses. You are not an early invader, so avoid duels with junglers who out-damage your raw clear.
gamePlan.midGame:
The first objective fights give Rammus multiple walls, corridors, and attack-based targets to punish. Powerball's collision knocks back, stuns, and slows nearby enemies; it does not knock them up. Cast Soaring Slam during Powerball and land its center on the group when you need the one-second area knock-up, then taunt the priority attacker.

Between objectives, play for tempo: clear a camp, Powerball into a side lane, taunt the carry, and leave with a kill or a Flash burned. Counter-gank with your speed, because arriving second to a skirmish on Rammus usually flips it, and keep stacking armor so every brawl tilts further your way.
gamePlan.lateGame: Late game you are pure engage and lockdown: start fights on your terms and pull one carry out of every single one. Powerball's range and speed let you decide when a teamfight happens, so hunt picks on a backliner walking through river without vision and taunt them into your team. Baron and dragon setups suit you, since you can engage from an unwarded flank and the ball scatters a stacked enemy team off the pit. Be honest about who you dive: against armor-stacking auto-attack teams you are nearly invincible, but against burst mages and percent-health damage you pick your windows instead of tanking everything. Stay armored, stay alive, and treat every fight as one chance to remove the enemy's scariest attacker.
gamePlan.teamfights: Your teamfight is one decision made well: which enemy do you take out of the game. Powerball in from an angle their carry did not expect, use the impact to break their formation, and taunt their highest-value attacker so they spend the fight hitting into your armor and feeding your spikes. Curl up the instant the burst comes, and let your team kill the target you isolated. If their carry has an escape, hold your slow to keep them stuck, and remember that peeling a diver off your own carry is worth as much as diving theirs. The fight you want is a brawl where the enemy keeps hitting you; the fight to avoid is one where they ignore you and kite the ball in circles.

spells.name: Flash
spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

goodAgainst.note: Camille's Adaptive Defenses absorbs matching damage, but an empowered Ruthless Predator dispels damage shields on its first strike before the rest of the three-hit attack lands. Hold 50 Fury for that interaction and avoid trading beside terrain that gives Hookshot its stun.

Riposte can block Ruthless Predator entirely and stuns Renekton if it parries the immobilize, so vary the stun timing instead of treating it as guaranteed. Fiora's vital true damage also punishes health stacking, making the early Fury advantage important but not automatic.

Empowered Ruthless Predator destroys Sett's Haymaker shield if it is already active, but the center punch still deals true damage and cannot be erased by armor. Use a short Slice-stun-Q-Dice trade before he stores large Grit rather than assuming the stun always cancels a committed Haymaker cast.

Riven already has multiple dashes, a stun, a knockup, and a shield in the early lane; she does not need two items to function. Renekton's advantage is a reliable Fury-loaded stun and sustain, but track her Valor shield and avoid wasting the empowered attack on a retreating dash.

weakAgainst.note: Garen's regen erases your chip damage and his silence cuts your combo mid-pattern, so the lazy trades that beat most laners just feed his passive.
The clone baits your fury combo: once your empowered stun hits a decoy, the real Wukong punishes you with everything down, and he only takes the fights he wants.

Malphite's armor reduces most of Renekton's physical rotation, but empowered Ruthless Predator dispels Granite Shield before its strikes finish. Break or dispel the shield, avoid letting Ground Slam's attack-speed cripple drag out the trade, and leave before the armor advantage takes over.

Steadfast Presence stops Slice and Dice and grounds Renekton after the interruption, so do not dash while its field is active. Poppy's buckler shield is not safe from Fury: empowered Ruthless Predator dispels damage shields on the first strike if Renekton reaches her.

gamePlan.overview:
Renekton builds Fury with attacks and abilities, gains 50% more from all sources below half health, and consumes 50 Fury to empower his next basic ability. Cull the Meek heals per enemy hit with a champion multiplier and cast cap; its empowered version increases damage, triples total healing, and raises the cap. Ruthless Predator empowers an attack to strike twice and stun for 0.75 seconds, or three times and stun for 1.5 seconds when empowered; the empowered first strike also dispels damage shields.

Slice is a directional dash that unlocks Dice for four seconds only after hitting an enemy. Empowered Dice deals more damage and reduces armor for four seconds. Dominus grants bonus health, size, attack range, and initial Fury for twelve seconds, then repeatedly generates Fury and deals nearby magic damage; it also enlarges Cull the Meek's radius.

The tradeoff is that his power fades as the game goes on. Once enemies finish items his damage stops scaring them, and a Renekton without an early lead has little left to offer beyond his stun. Win early, win fast, and use the lead to take over the rest of the map.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Build Fury without shoving farther than your vision allows. Use Slice through a unit to unlock Dice, then decide whether the second dash is part of the trade or the retreat before committing. Empower Ruthless Predator when the shield dispel and longer stun create the kill, Cull the Meek when the healing wins a crowded trade, or Dice when the armor reduction matters for the follow-up. At level 5, Dominus gives enough health and Fury generation to extend an all-in, but it does not rescue a bad wave position from a jungle collapse.
gamePlan.midGame: Use your early lead before other champions finish scaling. At six minutes, crash the wave and move first toward Herald, which usually converts Renekton's strong skirmish into more immediate map value than the first dragon. Play for dragon instead when your composition is built to win repeated teamfights and has a realistic soul plan. Enter river with Fury prepared, use Slice and Dice to reach a priority target, and hold the empowered stun long enough for teammates to follow rather than spending it on the first tank in range.
gamePlan.lateGame: Late-game Renekton has less burst relative to enemy health bars, so choose between disruption and peel. A flank can still reach a carry if their defensive cooldowns are down, but a direct charge through the frontline usually wastes both dashes. When your own carry is stronger, stay close enough to stun the assassin or bruiser entering the backline. Keep a side wave managed between objectives, then group early, because Renekton is much better in the first seconds of a fight than arriving after Dominus and Fury would have mattered.
gamePlan.teamfights: Decide before the fight whether you are diving or protecting. For a dive, build Fury in advance, use the first dash to reach the angle, and keep Dice available until you know whether the target can be finished. For peel, stand beside your carry and use empowered Ruthless Predator on the threat that enters. Activate Dominus as damage begins so the bonus health absorbs a real rotation and the Fury feeds another empowered spell. If the backline remains unreachable, control the frontline rather than crossing the whole enemy team alone.

goodAgainst.note: Soraka has no dash, so Grand Entrance can punish her positioning, but Equinox's silence prevents Rakan from casting Battle Dance until he leaves the zone and its delayed root can catch his exit. Make her spend Equinox before committing The Quickness and the knockup.

Yuumi can cast most of her kit while attached and untargetable; she does not need to detach just to use an ability. Engage the host with The Quickness and Grand Entrance, then punish Yuumi only if she voluntarily detaches or the host dies.

Grand Entrance ignores the minion screen Sona uses against linear skillshots, but she has two separate hard-control threats: a 0.5-second stun on her three-stack Power Chord and Crescendo's one-second stun. Track both before spending Battle Dance's return route.

Seraphine has no dash, but Beat Drop can root or stun through its upgraded cast and Encore charms along an extending line. Approach from the side so her projectiles cannot cover both Rakan and his carry, then save Battle Dance to leave after the delayed Grand Entrance knockup.

weakAgainst.note: His hook plucks you out of the air mid-dash and his attacks root whatever he touches, so one caught dash becomes a full crowd control chain you do not survive.
Plants and roots cover the open ground your dashes need, so you engage through vines, arrive rooted, and her ultimate knocks up the exact fight you tried to start.
His taunt can be charged around your landing point and turns the fight around, his magic bulk shrugs off the charm follow-up your combo needs, and his ultimate reaches any skirmish you start.

Twisted Advance follows you and roots on arrival, so he reliably controls you after the movement, saplings reveal the flank angles your engage needs, and his bulk outlasts the burst window your charm opens.

gamePlan.overview:
Rakan is a mobile support with separate tools for entering and leaving a fight. Fey Feathers periodically grants a shield, and champion hits reduce its cooldown. Grand Entrance dashes to a location before its delayed knockup. Battle Dance moves to an allied champion and shields them, with a second cast available during the recast window. Because Battle Dance cannot target enemies, Rakan needs an ally in range when he plans to use it as the exit.

Gleaming Quill damages the first enemy hit. Hitting a champion or epic monster creates a circle around Rakan that heals him and nearby allies after three seconds or immediately when an allied champion enters it; it does not grant a shield. The Quickness grants four seconds of movement speed, and Rakan charms and slows each champion he physically collides with once. The first collision gives another decaying speed burst, and each unique champion collision extends the duration by 0.25 seconds.

The catch is that he is very fragile and his combo needs an exit ally. Gleaming Quill does not make Grand Entrance land more reliably; The Quickness's charm or an ally's control is what can hold someone through the 0.35-second knockup delay. If Battle Dance has no allied target in range; or both casts are spent; Rakan is stranded inside the fight he started.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Laning is about picking dash windows, not spamming them. Hit Gleaming Quill on a champion, then move close enough that your ally can enter the circle and trigger its heal early. Use Grand Entrance for the knockup only when Battle Dance has an allied exit target, ideally saving its free second cast to adjust again. Champion hits also reduce Fey Feathers' cooldown, but Quill's heal and the passive shield are separate mechanics.
gamePlan.midGame: Mid game Rakan becomes a roaming threat, but none of his dashes is map-wide: Grand Entrance covers a targeted location and Battle Dance requires an allied champion. Before objectives, approach through fog, activate The Quickness for the collision charm, then place Grand Entrance under the controlled targets. Use Quill on a champion or epic monster so an ally entering its circle triggers the team heal during the fight.
gamePlan.lateGame: Late game you have two possible jobs, and you pick one as the fight begins. Either you are the opener, flanking wide and charming their backline into your team, or you are the bodyguard, glued to your carry and saving your dashes to peel every assassin and bruiser that comes for them. Read the draft and decide before the fight starts, because trying to be both gets you killed doing neither. Your ultimate is your highest-value button now, so do not waste it as a panic charm on a frontline tank; hold it for the carry or the cluster that decides the fight. An alive Rakan dictates where the fight happens, and a dead one gave away the team's best engage.
gamePlan.teamfights: Commit or cover, and never hover between the two. As the engage, lead with The Quickness from a flank, physically collide with priority targets for the charm and slow, then use Grand Entrance while they cannot dodge its delayed knockup. Battle Dance to an ally for the exit and preserve its free recast when another reposition may be needed. As the protector, shield the carry with Battle Dance and place Grand Entrance under the diver. Keep landing attacks and abilities on champions to reduce Fey Feathers' cooldown; Quill itself provides a separate area heal, not a shield refresh.

goodAgainst.note: Master Yi's first clear and pre-item dueling give Riven room to invade, but Alpha Strike can dodge a telegraphed Broken Wings hit and Meditate can blunt her burst. Hold Ki Burst for the spot where Alpha Strike ends, interrupt Meditate, and convert the early camp lead before Highlander removes the kiting window.
Viego needs a drawn-out duel to heal through and reset off, but your combo bursts him inside one shield window and your dashes dodge his spear, so the fight never lasts long enough.

Valor absorbs Talon's Rake and Noxian Diplomacy opener, while Broken Wings can follow his short combat movement after the first burst is spent. Do not chase Assassin's Path across multiple walls; interrupt the initial commit with Ki Burst, then extend the duel while his Rake and Shadow Assault are unavailable.

weakAgainst.note: Vi punishes the exact window you live in: her charged knockup catches you mid-dash and her lock-on ultimate pulls you out of any escape you planned, so your mobility and shield mean little.
Every dash and auto in your combo feeds Defensive Ball Curl straight back into your own health bar, and his taunt burns your shield while you stand there hitting armor you cannot cut through.

gamePlan.overview:
Riven is a jungler whose clear is one long ability combo and whose ganks commit fully. Her kit is three Q dashes, a stun on W, and a shielded dash on E that doubles as her escape, all with no mana bar to slow her down. Chain the rotation cleanly and camps die fast and ganks end in kills.

She wins by being early. Riven hits her power band the moment her kit is online and her first item lands, and from there she wants to be everywhere: first to scuttle, first to a gank, deep in the enemy jungle stealing camps. The knockup on her third Q plus the W stun locks a ganked laner down long enough to die. Snowball that into objectives and the game closes before the scaling junglers get to scale.

Her core problem is the clock. The shield is her only real defense, and once burst or sustain outpaces it she has no second layer. She is also demanding to play: miss the combo and a winning skirmish becomes a fight she can easily lose. Riven is a snowball, not a scaler, and if the lead stops growing she falls off.
gamePlan.earlyGame:
Use Broken Wings between attacks to clear, and use Valor's shield; not Ki Burst; to absorb camp damage. Only the third Broken Wings cast can cross terrain, so plan wall movement around that cast instead of assuming every Q dash will pass through. Keep Ki Burst ready to stun the laner when the gank begins.

Contest Scuttle when your nearby lanes can move and Riven reaches the river with enough health and cooldowns to duel. Winning the crab gives vision and can open a gank on the adjacent lane. Invade a slow-starting jungler only after tracking their route and preserving a dash for the exit; mobility does not protect Riven from a collapse by both enemy lanes.
gamePlan.midGame:
Riven should convert her strongest skirmishing window before enemy frontlines and carries finish scaling. Collapse on river and take dragon or Herald while few junglers want to fight you, contesting properly when your team is ahead. In an even game take Herald, since a tower converts your tempo immediately and soul asks you to still be relevant much later, which Riven is not.

Between objectives, counter-jungle hard when you know where the enemy is, timing your invade around their clear so you catch them low or absent. Every gank that lands should turn into an objective, or you are spending your best minutes on nothing. A Riven who farms passively through her power spike throws away the only window she gets.
gamePlan.lateGame: Late game you are no longer the strongest jungler on the map, so stop playing like you are. Group with your team, look for picks before the big objectives, and use your dashes to flank rather than facecheck. Baron and Elder fights are where you earn your keep: dive the enemy carry the moment the fight commits, kill them, and trust your team to clean up the rest. You no longer win the open duels you used to own, so skip those fights, and respect that anti-shield tools or heavy burst on the enemy team cut deep into your survivability. Your job is to close the game off your early lead, and if it runs long, fight only where your team can follow.
gamePlan.teamfights: You are a diver, not a frontline. Wait for the fight to start or for the enemy to spend their first round of crowd control, then leap in with E, land the stun, and put the full combo on their carry. Your knockup interrupts channels and key abilities, so time it to cancel an enemy ultimate or a fleeing dash instead of spending it on the tank. Keep moving with your Q dashes once you are in, because a Riven who stands still dies before the kill lands. If you cannot get in from the front, take the flank, since a stun onto the backline from the side ends fights faster. Save E for the way out, not just the way in, once your target drops.

coreItems.name: Death's Dance

coreItems.name: Guardian Angel
coreItems.note: Revives her once after dying. Her combo commits her deep into a fight.

situationalItems.name: Serpent's Fang
situationalItems.note: Build this when shields turn Riven's gank into a survivable chunk. Her Q chain applies the reduction before Wind Slash reaches its missing-health finisher damage.

situationalItems.name: Trinity Force
situationalItems.note: Riven naturally attacks between ability casts, so she can consume Spellblade without changing her combo. The proc has its own cooldown, so rapid Broken Wings casts do not each create a separate hit.

situationalItems.name: Spear of Shojin
situationalItems.note: Ability haste means her combo comes back sooner, which is her damage and her mobility.

situationalItems.name: Maw of Malmortius
situationalItems.note: Build this against heavy magic burst, which punishes her for committing a full rotation.

situationalItems.name: Mercurial Scimitar
situationalItems.note: Build this when one disable breaks Riven's Q and passive-attack sequence. Cleansing it lets her resume animation-cancelling before Blade of the Exile expires.

keystoneRune.note: Her combo lands many hits into one target, so she stacks almost instantly and the healing pays for the all-in.

primaryRunes.note: Her W stuns, so the shield arrives on the same cast she opens a trade with.

primaryRunes.note: Her shield covers one commit, and this handles the chip damage between them.

primaryRunes.name: Overgrowth
primaryRunes.desc: Gain permanent maximum health when nearby minions or monsters die.
primaryRunes.note: She commits her whole rotation up close, and the pool covers the return damage while it plays out.

secondaryRunes.name: Sudden Impact

secondaryRunes.note: Her E is a dash, so the bonus true damage lands as her combo begins.

spells.name: Flash

goodAgainst.note: Nasus has to walk up and spend Siphoning Strike on minions, giving Riven a predictable Broken Wings and Ki Burst punish before he has enough stacks or durability to answer. Freeze early, attack each stacking attempt, and use Valor plus your dashes to leave when Wither starts; if the lane becomes a passive farm race, the matchup has already moved toward Nasus.
His only real threat is the big slam, which is easy to dodge, and a dash escapes his pull, so by the time his death realm hits you are usually ahead on items.

Broken Wings and Valor repeatedly cross Kayle's melee-phase spacing, while Ki Burst stops her from freely farming toward Divine Ascent. Freeze and punish each Starfire Spellblade last-hit, force Divine Judgment before using Wind Slash, and re-engage during the long ultimate cooldown instead of donating the execute into invulnerability.

His combo needs you to stand in the sweet spots, and your dashes simply leave them, so he never lands a clean sweep and loses the early trades. Only the level five World Ender all-in is a real threat.
A squishy yordle you reach in one dash and delete in one combo. The blind only mutes your autos, not the Q dashes, W stun, and ultimate that do the actual killing.

weakAgainst.note: The silence lands mid-combo and locks out the rest of your buttons, his regen erases your chip damage, his W blunts your burst, and he is never not ready.

He matches your early aggression with cheaper tools: a point-and-click stun, built-in sustain, and fury windows that beat your cooldown windows. Your ceiling is higher, but only from the mid game onward.
The clone spends your combo on a decoy, then the real Wukong bursts you while your cooldowns are down. His knockup interrupts your dash chain, and one wasted rotation against him is a lost fight.

Armor stacking against a champion whose whole combo is physical burst. His shield soaks your opener, every armor item softens the rest, and his fast, ground-targeted ultimate is difficult to react to at close range and can catch Riven during a committed combo. Hold Flash or keep enough spacing to react.
Jayce chunks you before your dashes ever connect, and the knockback resets the engage you spent three cooldowns setting up. His poke wins the levels where you want to all-in.

gamePlan.overview:
Riven is pure execution: a manaless burst bruiser whose damage depends on how cleanly you chain her dashes, stun, and attack resets. Played well, she strings Broken Wings, Ki Burst, and Valor into one combo that ends with the enemy dead and Riven untouched. Played sloppily, the same buttons leave a melee champion standing in the open with everything on cooldown.

Her lane threat builds on itself. The third Broken Wings cast knocks enemies back, Ki Burst stuns, and Valor dashes and shields. Blade of the Exile increases her attack range and the ranges of Broken Wings and Ki Burst before unlocking the missing-health Wind Slash; it does not increase every ability's range.

She has two real enemies: crowd control, which interrupts the combo, and time, which lets enemies stack armor against her. Riven games are won in the window where her mechanics matter most and enemy items matter least.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Use short combinations when the wave or matchup cannot support a full commit. Valor provides one dash and a shield, while Broken Wings supplies three separate casts, with only the third crossing terrain and knocking enemies back. Weave Runic Blade attacks between casts, use Ki Burst before the opponent can answer, and preserve at least one movement cast for disengage. A long trade becomes favorable only when the enemy's main control or damage spell is down.
gamePlan.midGame: First item plus Blade of the Exile gives you strong side-lane and river pressure. Crash before moving toward Herald, use terrain to shorten the approach, and enter only when teammates can follow Ki Burst or the third Broken Wings cast. Wind Slash deals up to triple damage as the target loses health rather than using a fixed execute threshold, so save it for later in the combo unless the cone must hit several enemies. Check shields, stasis, and control before committing, since one defensive cooldown can break the burst and leave no movement for the exit.
gamePlan.lateGame: Late game, keep a side wave managed but return before Baron or Elder forces a grouped decision. Enemy armor and defensive tools make a direct front-to-back burst less reliable, so approach from a warded flank and wait for key control to land elsewhere. Wind Slash can hit several champions, but its missing-health scaling often rewards using it after the first part of the combo. If the enemy backline remains protected, use Ki Burst and the third Broken Wings cast to peel rather than crossing the whole formation alone.
gamePlan.teamfights: Approach from the side and track the specific control spell that can stop your combo. Enter after it is spent or when Flash and Valor can avoid it, stun the cluster around a priority target, and weave Runic Blade attacks without delaying the burst so long that peel arrives. The shield absorbs one response, not a full front-to-back fight. If the carry remains unreachable, threaten the flank, peel your own backline, or damage the closest target until a cleaner entry appears.

spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

goodAgainst.note: Varus is immobile artillery, and your whirl can erase his root mid-flight, so once you dive him he has no way to keep the fight at range.
Kai'Sa wants to trade at range and dash out, but your dash reaches her first, your whirl blocks her missiles on the way in, and up close your combo out-damages her weak early game.
Jhin has no escape and reloads after four shots, so your dive catches him helpless, and your whirl spins away the root he needs to peel you off.

weakAgainst.note: Draven's axes out-trade your style-building phase, and at even gold his early all-in beats yours. Your teamfight cleanup out-scales his lane pressure if the game stays close.
Her bounce poke chips you on the way in, her ultimate punishes the clustered brawls your kit wants, and she out-trades you until items even things out.
Every auto Ashe lands slows you, so the dash-and-brawl pattern you need gets kited apart before you reach her. Your whirl blocks her Volley but does not remove the slow applied by her basic attacks.

gamePlan.overview:
Samira is a melee brawler in a marksman's slot. Damaging champions with different attacks and abilities builds her style meter toward S rank, which unlocks Inferno Trigger: a moving barrage of gunfire that can critically strike and apply lifesteal while it shreds grouped teams. No carry turns one engage into a pentakill faster.

Her kit is built to dive: a dash through enemies, a blade whirl that blocks incoming projectiles, and a passive that lets allied crowd control extend her combo. That makes engage supports her best partners.

The downsides are real. She needs style to function, one stun shuts down her whole combo, and a Samira behind on gold threatens nothing. She wins by finding the brawl, hitting S rank, and turning it into a cleanup the enemy cannot stop.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Build Style through short trades, using the gun at range and the blade only when the enemy cannot punish the closer position. Let allied crowd control create the dash target rather than entering first. Blade Whirl destroys hostile non-turret projectiles that enter its area during the cast, so save it for the key projectile that would stop the all-in. At level five, track every control spell that can interrupt Inferno Trigger before committing to the extended fight.
gamePlan.midGame: Your first items and an engage support turn river skirmishes into strong cleanup windows. Clear the wave before rotating, build Style from the edge of the fight, and dash only after allied control creates a target. At six minutes, Herald is usually the stronger even trade. Dragon becomes attractive when your composition can keep forcing grouped fights toward soul, since clustered enemies give Samira better Style and Inferno Trigger access. Track the control spells that can interrupt the ultimate before committing to the pit.
gamePlan.lateGame: Late game, play the first seconds like a short-range carry and the final seconds like a reset champion. Build Style with different attacks and abilities while allied engage draws control, then dash toward a wounded target only when a takedown or safe exit is likely. Blade Whirl should remove the projectile that stops your entry or protects the ultimate channel. Inferno Trigger can restore substantial health through clustered enemies, but Grievous Wounds, hard crowd control, and burst still punish a cast made in the middle of five ready champions.
gamePlan.teamfights: Build Style from the edge with alternating attacks and abilities, keeping Wild Rush for the target whose takedown can refresh it. Enter after the enemy spends the control that interrupts Inferno Trigger, and use Blade Whirl against the most important incoming projectile rather than as a routine Style step. Cast the ultimate where several wounded enemies are in range and allied pressure prevents them from simply focusing Samira. If S rank arrives before the safe opening, hold it and keep attacking instead of treating the meter as a command to dive.

coreItems.name: Radiant Virtue

coreItems.name: Dawnshroud

coreItems.name: Amaranth's Twinguard

situationalItems.note: Build this when the enemy team has multiple crit champions. Crash Down and Magnet Storm leave Rell beside the enemy carry, but current Wild Rift Rell has no special dismounted movement-speed penalty; the value is surviving the committed position itself.

situationalItems.name: Frozen Heart
situationalItems.note: Build this when the enemy team has a lot of attack speed dependent champions, which her ultimate is already holding in place.

situationalItems.name: Chainlaced Crushers

keystoneRune.desc: Immobilizing an enemy champion creates icy beams and a frozen zone that slows enemies inside.
keystoneRune.note: Her stun, her mounted charge and her ultimate all immobilize, so the zone is up on nearly every engage.

primaryRunes.desc: Immobilizing enemy champions grants a defensive shield for frontline engages.
primaryRunes.note: Her knock-up triggers the shield as she enters the fight, helping her survive the focus that follows.

primaryRunes.note: She walks into range to engage and eats poke for it, and this refunds enough to try again.
