primaryRunes.note: Take this against teams whose crowd control prevents the key follow-up. Its tenacity shortens most disables and grants temporary defenses while immobilized, helping Rell continue into Magnet Storm or Mount Up; Crash Down itself does not slow her movement in the current kit.

secondaryRunes.name: Hexflash
secondaryRunes.desc: While Flash is on cooldown, it is replaced by Hexflash.
secondaryRunes.note: Flash into her W is the engage everyone watches for, and Hexflash keeps a version of it while Flash is down.

spells.name: Flash
spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

goodAgainst.note: Yuumi casts most abilities while attached and untargetable, so she does not offer a detach window on every spell. Use Full Tilt to reach the host, then layer Crash Down and Magnet Storm; punish Yuumi only if she voluntarily detaches or the host dies.

Crash Down crosses Sona's short Hymn of Valor range and Magnet Storm keeps her inside the follow-up, while her small shields do not stop a committed two-target engage. Track her three-cast Power Chord stun and Crescendo, then engage after one is spent so she cannot interrupt Rell before the carry is locked down.

Lux has no dash, but Light Binding passes through and damages minions in Wild Rift and Lucent Singularity slows before automatically detonating. Approach from outside the binding line, then use Shattering Strike to destroy Prismatic Barrier's damage shield before stunning.
The engage mirror goes your way: your dismount crash lands before his walk-up hook, your W bulk out-trades his shield, and your shred strips the armor his tank plan leans on.

weakAgainst.note: Janna's tornado interrupts your leap mid-animation and her ultimate blows your whole engage back out of the fight, so the game's cleanest disengage cancels your best button.
He is mobile where you are committed: he dashes out of your lockdown, out-engages your slower leap, and disengages the all-ins you do land.

Black Shield grants crowd-control immunity while its magic shield holds, so it can initially deny Crash Down or Magnet Storm. Shattering Strike destroys champion damage shields before dealing damage and stunning, giving Rell a direct way to remove Black Shield before the rest of her engage.

Event Horizon can stun Rell when Crash Down crosses its edge, but dismounted form grants 15% bonus armor and magic resistance immediately and the leap grants a lasting shield. Bait the cage or use Full Tilt's approach before committing the leap.

gamePlan.overview:
Rell is a pure hard-engage support. Break the Mold makes her attacks and abilities apply up to five stacks, each reducing armor and magic resistance by 3% while granting Rell the total defenses removed. Her attacks also deal bonus magic damage based on 5% of her total armor plus 5% of her total magic resistance; those stats do not become attack damage. Shattering Strike lunges slightly, destroys champion damage shields before dealing damage, and stuns for 0.65 seconds.

Crash Down turns Rell from mounted to dismounted, grants a shield that lasts until broken or she remounts, then knocks up and stuns enemies along the leap and slide. Dismounted Rell has no special movement-speed penalty in the current Wild Rift kit; she instead gains 15% bonus armor and magic resistance, attack speed, and attack range. Mount Up restores mounted form and empowers a charging attack to stun and fling its target over Rell.

Full Tilt targets an allied champion and speeds both that ally and Rell for three seconds, with more speed while they face each other or an enemy. It empowers Rell's next attack or Shattering Strike within five seconds to create a damage explosion; it does not empower the ally's next strike. Magnet Storm pulls nearby enemies inward on cast, then damages and drags them toward Rell for two seconds.

Her problem is commitment, not a forced slow form. Once Crash Down is spent, she must survive on its shield and dismounted defenses until Mount Up returns. She still has Shattering Strike's stun, Full Tilt's speed, and Magnet Storm, but no immediate free-target dash back out.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Laning is a patience game until your engage is online. Put Full Tilt on your ADC before committing so both of you gain approach speed, then use Crash Down's stun and knockup to begin stacking Break the Mold. Full Tilt empowers Rell's own next attack or Shattering Strike, so spend that explosion inside the caught duo. When shields appear, Shattering Strike removes them before its damage and stun. Track the enemy jungler because Crash Down has no immediate free-target return dash.
gamePlan.midGame: Leave Dragon lane after a crash or recall timer and move with your jungler to establish river vision. A pull or knockup on an isolated mid laner or jungler can create a numbers advantage before dragon or Herald, but engage only when allies are close enough to continue the control chain. When no pick is available, return to your carry rather than waiting in fog while the lane becomes a 1v2.
gamePlan.lateGame: You are the fight starter and the body that survives the dive. Group with your team, hold the leap and the pull for the angle that catches more than one target, and let your durability buy the deep position other supports cannot reach. Your shred makes the enemy tanks killable for your carries, and Full Tilt keeps your most important teammate moving through the chaos. The one real mistake is throwing the engage early: a Rell who leaped at nothing is a slow body the enemy walks around, so wait for the clean angle even when you want to force it.
gamePlan.teamfights: Your job is to pick the angle and gather the enemy into one spot for your team to kill. The best case is an ultimate that drags two or more of their backline together, followed instantly by the leap and your shred so your team kills them while they are stacked. If the flank does not exist, frontline straight: peel divers off your carry with the knock-up, body-block the engage, and keep Full Tilt on whoever the enemy most wants dead. You are the difference between a scrappy even fight and a one-sided collapse, so spend your cooldowns on the carry, not the tank in your face.

His ultimate cleanses the charm and root your picks are built on, his range buff lets his carry out-trade your poke, and his sustain matches yours with less mana strain.
Her targeted stun opens a chain she can follow through once she commits, your shield does not cover the gap she crosses, and one root is thin peel against a tank with resists already up.

gamePlan.overview:
Seraphine is a support who mixes long-range poke with heavy sustain. Her Q pokes from very far, she shields and speeds up her carry while healing allies nearby, and her passive turns every third cast into an echo, so one button often does the work of two. Her ultimate is a charm that grows as it passes through bodies and can end a fight before it starts.

In the Dragon lane she plays a slow chip game. Her notes poke the enemy duo off the wave, her shield and speed keep your carry out of all-ins, and her area heal wins long trades. You are not looking for early kills; you win every small exchange, then turn one landed charm into a kill your carry could not set up alone.

The cost is that she has no dash. Surround Sound can shield, heal, and speed her team, Beat Drop can slow, root, or stun depending on the target's existing control, and Encore charms along a long line, but all of those defenses need timing and spacing. Hook supports can drag her out before the protection resolves, and dive comps punish her when the upgraded control and movement-speed window are unavailable.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Throw your note when it hits the enemy carry and the wave at once, let the echo double its value, and shield-speed your ADC the moment a melee support steps up. Your area heal is your biggest edge in long trades, so bait the enemy duo into extended exchanges you out-sustain instead of burst trades you might lose. The whole phase is range and mana management: poke when it is free, hold the charm to punish their engage, and remember a gank hits hard on a champion with no dash.
gamePlan.midGame: Once your support item upgrades and your charm range improves, the lane starts producing picks instead of just chip. Ward the river and the enemy pixel brush before every dragon, since seeing the rotation coming lets you root the front of it instead of eating the engage blind. Roam mid when your wave is shoved, because a charm from fog onto the enemy mid or jungler can win a herald or an early dragon in one cast. Keep shielding your carry through skirmishes, and treat every objective fight as a question of who you can lock down in the choke first.
gamePlan.lateGame: You are now a fight-opener and a peel source at once, and your positioning decides which job you do. Stand behind your frontline, hold the charm for the enemy engage or the diver jumping your carry, and layer shields and heals to keep your damage dealers alive through the burst. Your poke still matters before fights, chipping grouped teams off an objective before anyone commits. The only way to lose from here is walking up for a hero charm and getting collapsed on, so let the fight come into your range and pick it apart from the back.
gamePlan.teamfights: You have two jobs, and the order depends on who moves first. If you have the angle, open with the charm through their stacked frontline so it grows into a multi-person lock and your team crashes the opening. If they engage first, the same cast becomes peel: root the diver off your carry, then cover your backline with shields, heals, and the speed burst so they can kite out. Stay at the edge of the fight where your range reaches but their assassins do not, and keep the area heal ticking on whoever is taking damage. A good fight ends with your carry alive and the enemy engage charmed before it ever connected.

Her burst beats your slow attrition: the root catches you on soul pickups, her full combo chunks harder than your chip trades back, and her shield blunts your poke, though her one-rotation pattern falls off late.

gamePlan.overview:
Senna is a marksman played as a support. Her attacks reach very far, and Piercing Darkness can damage enemies and heal Senna and allies along the same line. She protects and punishes with one cast, so her lane never plays like a normal 2v2.

She wins lane with reach and sustain. You stand at the edge of the fight and chip the enemy carry every time they walk up to farm, while topping off your ADC, so even trades slowly tilt your way. Last Embrace roots enemies who clump together, and her ultimate is a global shield that can save your backline from across the map. She collects souls off dead units to grow her range and crit, so over time she becomes a second carry your team never paid for.

Her problem is that she is fragile once someone reaches her. Last Embrace's delayed root, Curse of the Black Mist's camouflage and movement speed, and Dawning Shadow's shield can buy an exit, but none is an instant dash or guaranteed disengage. Senna punishes enemies who must walk through her range and struggles against fast, layered engage that reaches her before those delayed tools resolve.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Stand at the edge of your range and line up Q through an ally or other target so it can hit the enemy carry and heal your ADC at the same time. Let your lane partner take the minion last-hits whenever possible: minions Senna does not kill have a better chance to leave Mist Wraiths, and collecting those souls grows her range, attack damage, and critical strike chance. Stay out of the enemy support's engage range, because Curse of the Black Mist has to be available before the engage arrives, not after. Win this phase by walking home healthier than the enemy duo, not by chasing kills you cannot commit to safely.
gamePlan.midGame: As the lane opens up, your Q becomes a roaming poke tool and your root becomes a pick tool. Move toward mid before objectives: a Last Embrace from fog onto a grouped enemy mid and jungler hands your team a free dragon or herald, and your global ultimate lets you affect fights you are not even near. Keep collecting souls off every kill and large minion, because your late game depends on the range and crit you build now. Ward the river so your low-mobility frame never gets surprised, and let your ADC push under your poke cover while you set up the next play.
gamePlan.lateGame: By now you are a support in name and a carry in practice. Your range is huge, your autos crit, and your Q still heals the backline mid-fight, so you sit behind your frontline and do two jobs: chip their carries from outside their reach and keep yours alive. Hold your ultimate for the fight that decides the objective, when its global shield and the damage down the line can set up your team from anywhere on the map. Position still matters most, since one hook or assassin can delete you, but an alive late-game Senna out-ranges and out-heals most of what the enemy has.
gamePlan.teamfights: Start from the back and stay there. Land Last Embrace on the enemy frontline or a grouped carry pair to open the fight, then weave long basic attacks with Piercing Darkness lines that damage enemies while healing allies. Save the ultimate for the moment that matters: shielding your whole team as they commit, or shielding a carry through the burst a diver opens with, and keep Curse of the Black Mist as its own answer when you need to slip out. Use your Q slow and W root as peel first, spent on whatever reaches your backline instead of saved for a kill. Your best fights end with the enemy carry chunked from range and your own carry untouched.

gamePlan.overview:
Sivir wins through tempo. Boomerang Blade can hit once outward and once on its homing return, and its champion damage increases with critical-strike chance. Ricochet resets her attack timer, grants four seconds of attack speed, and makes attacks bounce repeatedly through clustered enemies; a critical first hit also makes its bounces crit. Together they create exceptional wave pressure and much better teamfight damage when enemies group.

Spell Shield lasts two seconds. Successfully blocking a hostile effect heals Sivir and activates Fleet of Foot's movement speed; if nothing hits it, half of its remaining cooldown is refunded instead. On the Hunt initially grants Sivir and nearby allies movement speed, reduces Sivir's basic-ability cooldowns, and lets her champion hits stack Morale for bonus attack damage. At eight stacks she rallies again for a larger personal movement-speed boost that stacks with the first and refreshes the duration.

The trade-offs: short range for a marksman, a quiet early trading game, and damage that wants crowds to bounce between rather than duels. Sivir wins by pushing the lane, shielding the one spell that mattered, and arriving everywhere first.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Push first and profit everywhere. Shove the wave with ricochet, force the enemy duo to farm under tower, and use the tempo: your recalls cost less, your support can roam, and the river opens on your schedule. Hold your spell shield for the matchup's key ability; eating their hook or root swings the entire lane phase. You lose most direct trades, so the goal is a lane state that never offers them.
gamePlan.midGame: Tempo turns into objectives. Your push reaches towers quickly, Spell Shield breaks the single picks that start enemy fights, and On the Hunt moves nearby allies into or out of a dragon contest. Keep hitting champions with attacks and abilities during the ultimate: every Morale stack adds attack damage, the ultimate reduces basic cooldowns, and the eighth stack triggers the stronger second rally.
gamePlan.lateGame: You are a utility carry whose damage ramps during the fight. Push safely, shield the hostile effect that would stop you attacking, and spend On the Hunt on a committed engage or disengage rather than a moment with no champions to hit. Use Boomerang Blade and Ricochet to build Morale quickly, then exploit the refreshed duration, extra attack damage, and second movement-speed boost at eight stacks.
gamePlan.teamfights: Speed up the right moment. Open with On the Hunt when your team can commit, then use its reduced basic cooldowns to cycle Boomerang Blade, Ricochet, and Spell Shield while champion hits build Morale. Ricochet's cast resets the attack timer, so weave it immediately after an attack. Stay behind the frontline and save Spell Shield for the hostile effect that would interrupt your damage long enough to lose the eight-stack rally.

gamePlan.overview:
Smolder is one of the hardest-stacking scalers in the Dragon lane. Hitting an enemy champion with an ability or killing a minion or monster with Super Scorcher Breath adds a permanent Dragon Practice stack, so his early game is a farming exercise and his late game is overwhelming. No carry punishes a passive enemy duo harder for leaving him alone.

His kit protects the plan: Super Scorcher Breath upgrades at 25 stacks with an impact explosion, at 100 with an expanding fan of bolts, and at 175 with a stack-scaling maximum-health true-damage burn plus a 6.5%-health execute. Flap, Flap, Flap grants movement speed, terrain crossing, and up to five or more automatic bolts for 1.25 seconds, but casting another ability or becoming immobilized ends the flight immediately.

The cost is a weak, farm-dependent early game in a heavily contested lane. If the stacks never arrive, neither does he.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Stack at every chance. Last-hit with Super Scorcher Breath whenever possible and hit champions with any ability when the trade is safe. Q restores 15 mana when it kills at least one target, rewarding accurate last-hits. Treat Flap, Flap, Flap as gank insurance, and do not cancel its 1.25-second escape early by casting Q or W unless that spell secures safety.
gamePlan.midGame: The stacks start paying off. Super Scorcher Breath gains splash at 25 stacks and a wider fan of explosions at 100, while your ultimate zones dragon standoffs and heals you if the wave passes over Smolder. Keep farming between fights, since the scaling never stops, and use your flight to join fights over walls that other immobile carries have to walk around.
gamePlan.lateGame: This is what you stacked for. A high-stack Smolder spreads true-damage burns through clustered enemies and executes targets pushed below the Q threshold. Stay behind your frontline, cast Q through the nearest safe target for its splash, aim your ultimate through both teams when you need its heal, and fly only when the fight demands the angle or the exit. If they let you stack all game, this is where they lose to it.
gamePlan.teamfights: Poke with Achooo! and use upgraded Q splashes through the nearest safe target, then aim MMOOOMMMM! through both the enemy formation and Smolder so its heal helps him survive the return damage. At 175 stacks, Q's burn executes champions only when your damage would leave them below its low-health threshold, so keep casting and watch the indicator rather than assuming the next hit kills. Save Flap, Flap, Flap for a committed dive or terrain escape unless a forward cast clearly ends the fight.

goodAgainst.note: Blinding Dart only denies Rumble's basic attacks, not Flamespitter, Electro Harpoon, or The Equalizer, so Teemo cannot switch off the damage that drives the lane. Build Danger Zone before the trade, shield the return poison with Scrap Shield, and sweep mushrooms before chasing so Teemo cannot turn a winning burn into a trapped retreat.

Rumble's magic damage bypasses Malphite's armor investment, but Granite Shield still absorbs it and Malphite can itemize magic resistance. Keep Danger Zone Flamespitter pressure between shield refreshes and respect Unstoppable Force's displacement-immune engage.

Darius has no dash, but Apprehend pulls, Crippling Strike slows, and the outer edge of Decimate heals him. Stack Electro Harpoon's slow and magic-resistance reduction from outside the pull range, then use Scrap Shield's movement speed when he tries to close.

Wind Wall does not block Flamespitter, but it can stop Electro Harpoon projectiles and remove the slow and magic-resistance reduction that help Rumble kite. Keep the flame cone on Yasuo while holding a harpoon charge until the wall expires.

Riven has to enter Flamespitter range, but Valor's damage shield absorbs the burn rather than letting it pass through. Maintain Danger Zone without overheating, use stacked Harpoon slows after her dashes, and do not assume she needs an item spike to threaten an early all-in.

weakAgainst.note: Accelerated Shock Blast reaches far beyond Flamespitter, and Thundering Blow knocks Rumble out before his Danger Zone burn can complete. Shield the ranged poke with Scrap Shield, farm with Electro Harpoon, and do not overheat on the approach because Jayce can switch forms and disengage while Rumble's spells are silenced.
Her hookshot crosses your fire line in one motion and her true damage goes straight through your resistances, though your shield still absorbs it, so her all-in beats you once she has items.

Spinning Slash crosses Flamespitter, Mocking Shout slows Rumble's retreat, and Undying Rage lasts through the burn that would normally finish the all-in. Keep Electro Harpoon for his entry, use Scrap Shield to kite the Fury window, and place The Equalizer on his exit after the ultimate expires rather than dumping it into invulnerability.

Sion's Soul Furnace shield can absorb a burn window, but his large health pool is not automatically safe: Liandry's and Rumble's Overheated attacks both add maximum-health magic damage. Stay outside Decimating Smash's charged area and break the shield before Sion can detonate it for percentage damage.

Ambessa's dashes slide straight out of your flame cone and slip the harpoons that would slow her. She closes the spacing your whole kit is built to keep, and once she is on you the mech is too slow to shake her off.

gamePlan.overview:
Rumble drives a junkyard mech that runs on Heat instead of mana. Each basic ability generates 20 Heat. At 50 Heat he enters the Danger Zone, increasing Flamespitter's damage by 50%, Scrap Shield's shield and movement speed by 50%, and Electro Harpoon's slow and magic-resistance reduction by 50%. At 150 Heat he Overheats and loses ability access while Heat returns to zero over four seconds, but gains attack speed and maximum-health magic damage on his basic attacks during that window.

Flamespitter burns in a frontal cone for three seconds. Scrap Shield lasts 1.5 seconds and gives one second of movement speed. Electro Harpoon stores two charges; each hit slows and reduces magic resistance for four seconds, stacking twice. Managing which spell crosses 50 Heat; and whether the next cast causes an intentional Overheat; is the champion's real skill test.

The Equalizer is why teams pick him: a line of fire that cuts battlefields in half, zones whole teams off objectives, and blocks choke points. Rumble games are won by the player who aims that line, and lost by the one who panics and wastes it.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Control the lane step by step. Use the first Harpoon to slow and reduce magic resistance, stack the second when the target remains exposed, then walk Danger Zone Flamespitter across the trade. Use Scrap Shield's brief movement speed to keep the cone aligned. Avoid 150 Heat when you need another spell, but intentionally Overheat beside a committed melee target when the empowered attacks can be used safely.
gamePlan.midGame: Crash the Baron wave before moving toward Herald or dragon, then approach from the side that gives The Equalizer a line across the enemy entrance. Use Electro Harpoon to slow the first target and wait until the formation commits before placing the fire. Enter the fight with enough Heat to empower the needed spells without silencing yourself before the rotation is complete. If the enemy avoids the choke, hold the ultimate and keep pressuring the frontline instead of placing it on one retreating target.
gamePlan.lateGame: Push a side wave only when you can return before Baron or Elder vision is contested. Hold The Equalizer to split the enemy formation, seal an entrance, or cover the pit while your team finishes the objective. Use Flamespitter on reachable frontliners and keep Scrap Shield for the damage window that forces you closer. If no high-value line appears, preserve the ultimate and continue controlling the choke with Harpoons.
gamePlan.teamfights: Divide, then burn. The opening Equalizer should split their frontline from their carries or zone half their team out of the fight, and the rest is cleanup: flamethrower on whoever is trapped on your side, harpoons on the runners, shield through the response. Manage heat going into the fight so the empowered versions arrive when the fight does. A panicked early ult is the main way Rumble loses fights.

goodAgainst.note: You take away Zed's choice of when to fight by leaping on him from brush: full ferocity bursts his squishy frame in one jump, and the leap lands before the shadow swap he would escape with.
Nidalee wants to poke with spears at range, but your leap closes that gap instantly, and she has no bulk to survive your opener and no time to land enough spears to matter.
Before her charm setup comes online Evelynn is weak and clunky, and your brush leap bursts her early frame long before the scaling spike that would flip the matchup.

weakAgainst.note: Committing your combo into Defensive Ball Curl feeds the reflect, and his taunt cancels your leap before your damage lands. You cannot burst that much armor, especially when it hits back.
Wukong drops a clone the instant you commit, so your empowered burst kills a decoy while the real one knocks you up and turns the duel, leaving a squishy assassin stuck in melee with a bruiser.

gamePlan.overview:
Rengar makes any bush dangerous. From brush he can leap onto a target for a burst of empowered damage, so his ganks are ambushes launched from terrain the enemy forgot to ward. His abilities build a ferocity bar, and at full ferocity his next ability becomes a stronger empowered version, which lets him win most duels through ferocity management.

He is an early-game predator who wants the game over before it becomes teamfights. The heal on empowered Battle Roar keeps his camps cheap, his single-target burst is among the scariest in the jungle, and his ultimate reveals the nearest enemy champion and speeds him toward them, with a leap built in. A fed Rengar decides which enemy carry gets to keep playing.

The flip side is that his power lives in the early game and in brush. Control wards remove his leap threat, focus fire kills him before his combo finishes, and grouped late-game fights leave his single-target hunt without clean targets. He is a snowball pick: terrifying when ahead, ordinary when stalled.
gamePlan.earlyGame:
Your first clear is not about setting a speed record, so path toward lanes that can follow up a leap. Normal Battle Roar heals 50% of damage taken in the previous two seconds; empowered Battle Roar replaces that heal with higher damage, a crowd-control cleanse, and movement speed. Use the normal cast for camp sustain unless the empowered utility is actually needed, and arrive at a lane brush with Ferocity prepared.

Contest scuttle when the duel favors you, since Rengar wins most early one-on-ones, but do not spend a losing crab fight when a gank is available instead. Watch your own jungle too, because invaders like Lee Sin, Kha'Zix, and Nidalee want to catch you mid-camp before your ferocity is up.
gamePlan.midGame:
Rengar wants the brush and vision battle around an objective more than the stationary pit brawl. Clear vision in the pit brush so you are the one waiting when the contest starts, but choose the target rather than leaping onto the first tank who appears. If your lanes cannot hold the fight, trade for the opposite objective instead of forcing a grouped engage that denies clean isolation.

Between objectives, treat every squishy on the map as a target: a mid laner pushed up, a carry farming a side wave, a support warding alone. Use your ultimate to start hunts rather than only to finish fights, since the vision on the nearest enemy is half its value, and counter-jungle hard when their jungler is on the far side.
gamePlan.lateGame: Late game you have to be smart instead of just strong, because grouped teams leave no clean targets. Stop diving into five bodies and hunt the edges: a carry stepping to a side wave, a support warding alone, or someone in the fog before the real fight starts. Your ultimate is now a flank tool as much as a finisher, so use its vision and speed to find an angle from a bush the enemy backline cannot see. If you cannot find isolation, you still force the enemy carry to play scared, which has value, but leaping into a grouped fight first just gets you killed. Baron and dragon setups are your best windows, since the brush around those pits is exactly the terrain your kit was built for.
gamePlan.teamfights: Your teamfight is an assassination timed to match one. Sit in a flank bush, wait for their carry to commit or their frontline to step forward, then leap in with full ferocity and burst them before their team can turn. That opening burst buys you the first second, so do not spend it on a tank you cannot kill. If the enemy has hard crowd control saved for you, bait it out or wait, because one stun lands and you die before your combo finishes. When you cannot reach the carry cleanly, your presence still forces their backline to play too safe, which opens angles for your team. You are a single-target assassin, not a brawler: pick one target and commit only when the kill is certain.

goodAgainst.note: Wukong's Cyclone brings his divers together, giving Impale a chance to suppress him and the allies following his engage in one cast. Track the real body through the clone, then use Ixtal's Impact to pin him against terrain after his mobility is spent.

Ixtal's Impact follows Talon's wall routes instead of letting terrain guarantee his escape. Once he commits with Shadow Assault, Impale can suppress him and any nearby teammates trying to follow his dive.
Ixtal's Impact can stun Kha'Zix against terrain and Impale stops his leap or takedown reset. If his team collapses on the isolated target with him, the same ultimate can catch the nearby follow-up.

weakAgainst.note: Javelin Toss and Pounce let Nidalee pressure from outside the reliable range of Ixtal's Impact and Impale. A missed charge leaves Skarner exposed to her ranged poke and repeated repositioning.
Lillia's ramping movement speed makes both Ixtal's Impact and Impale's wind-up difficult to connect. Her sleep then punishes Skarner and any teammates who group behind his slow approach.

Amumu can body-block Ixtal's Impact before it reaches a carry, then answer Skarner's entry with his own area control. If Skarner drags several enemies into one place, Curse of the Sad Mummy can punish the grouped position as soon as the suppression ends.

gamePlan.overview:
Reworked Skarner is a terrain-crossing tank who controls groups rather than removing only one target. Threads of Vibration stacks Quaking through his attacks, Shattered Earth, Upheaval, and Impale, then deals maximum-health magic damage when fully stacked. Shattered Earth empowers three attacks, and the third adds 11% maximum-health physical damage; recast it to throw Upheaval and slow enemies. Seismic Bastion gives a maximum-health shield, damages and slows nearby enemies, while Ixtal's Impact carries Skarner through terrain, grabs the first champion or large monster hit, and stuns the victim when he smashes them into a wall.

Impale is the center of his teamfight, but it is no longer a single-target abduction. After its wind-up, it suppresses and drags up to three enemy champions. Clear with Shattered Earth's area damage and Quaking, use Ixtal's Impact to create gank angles through walls, then fight around chokes where one Impale can move an entire section of the enemy formation. Prepare Shattered Earth before casting Impale so Upheaval automatically fires through the same group.

His weakness is how clearly the engage is advertised. Ixtal's Impact catches only the first champion it reaches, while Impale has a wind-up that can be dodged, spell-shielded, or answered by crowd-control immunity. Ranged champions can kite him before he finds an angle, and missing either engage tool leaves a tank with limited pressure until the cooldown returns.
gamePlan.earlyGame:
Use Shattered Earth as an attack reset, spend its three empowered attacks, and mix Seismic Bastion or Upheaval into camps to reach three Quaking stacks quickly. The passive's percentage-health damage is capped against monsters but still contributes heavily to large camps. Do not wait for level five to gank: Ixtal's Impact can cross a lane wall, grab a champion, and stun them against terrain before Impale is learned.

Enter ganks through terrain with Ixtal's Impact, steer into the target, then drive them into the nearest wall for the 1.5-second stun and cooldown refund. If no wall angle exists, end the charge where Seismic Bastion's slow and a thrown Upheaval can keep them in range. Respect roots and knockups on the approach because they detach the grabbed target before the wall collision.
gamePlan.midGame:
Clustered objective entrances are where reworked Skarner can turn one Impale into control over several champions. Take that trade in an even game and contest both when your team is ahead on early fights. Dragon is worth prioritising only when your team can hold the longer fights that soul asks for.

Between objectives, collapse through terrain and look for clustered champions rather than tunnel-visioning one carry. Prepare Shattered Earth before Impale: casting the ultimate while holding the boulder automatically throws Upheaval in the ultimate's direction, adding the Q finisher's area damage and slow before the suppression attaches up to three champions.
gamePlan.lateGame: Late game you are both initiation and counter-engage. Flank through terrain for an Ixtal's Impact wall stun, or hold Impale until multiple champions enter its trapezoid. Skarner gains 40% movement speed during a successful Impale but the targets remain only 1.5 seconds and are placed a short distance forward when it ends, so turn toward your team immediately rather than expecting a long cross-screen drag.
gamePlan.teamfights: Prepare Shattered Earth before casting Impale so Upheaval fires automatically through the same group. Enter through terrain with Ixtal's Impact or Flash before Impale's wind-up, use Seismic Bastion for the shield and slow, then angle the ultimate across as many champions as possible. Impale suppresses and drags up to three, so a frontline target is not wasted if the same cast also catches a carry or support. Drag the group toward your damage dealers, out of an objective pit, or away from their own backline. A clean two- or three-person Impale is usually worth more than waiting forever for one perfect carry.

primaryRunes.note: He farms through everything thrown at him, and this covers the poke that would otherwise push him out.

goodAgainst.note: His whole champion is autos into a body built to ignore them. He cannot burst through your shield and health, you knock up his commits, and he brings less to teamfights.

Blinding Dart affects Sion's basic attacks but does not stop Decimating Smash, Roar of the Slayer, or Soul Furnace, whose shield absorbs much of Teemo's poison trade. Use Roar's slow before charging the knockup, keep the shield for Toxic Shot rather than the minion wave, and sweep the lane before committing Unstoppable Onslaught through mushroom paths.
Armor stacking does not stop your Q knockup and shield burst, which out-trade his shield poke, and your engage beats his at every stage of the game.

Soul Furnace absorbs the repeated Shuriken and Electrical Surge poke that normally pushes a melee champion out, while Sion's wave clear prevents Kennen from freezing him away from farm. Slow Kennen with Roar before charging Decimating Smash, keep the shield for a marked stun trade, and scale through the lane instead of chasing Lightning Rush.
Her burst opener hits a shield instead of a health bar, and your charged knockup catches the hookshot she engages with. Her percent-health damage only becomes a problem in long duels.

weakAgainst.note: Apprehend can displace Sion during Decimating Smash and put the interrupted ability on its short cooldown, while Hemorrhage grinds through his large health bar. The pull does not remove Soul Furnace's shield, so detonate it before Darius breaks it and avoid telegraphing a full charge in open space.

Every health item increases the value of Gwen's percentage-health damage, and the center of Snip Snip! deals true damage. Hallowed Mist only makes her untargetable to enemies outside it, so step into the mist before releasing Decimating Smash or expect the cast to miss her.
Your big health pool makes her vitals hit harder, and your charged Q is a free parry stun for her. The vitals also shred the shield and tank stats you scale into.
He dashes through the charged Q wind-up and out-skirmishes you at every turn, and his spirit-form trades chip your shield faster than it refreshes.

Silver Bolts punishes Sion's maximum-health stacking, and Vayne can kite Decimating Smash or use Condemn to interrupt its channel. Condemn cannot stop Unstoppable Onslaught while Sion is crowd-control immune, but she can reposition before impact and resume kiting after the charge ends.

gamePlan.overview:
Sion is a scaling tank whose passive permanently gains health from killing units and whose death passive reanimates him after a brief stasis with a full but rapidly decaying health bar. Decimating Smash can charge for up to 1.75 seconds; releasing after at least 0.75 seconds upgrades its short slow into a knockup followed by a stun. Enemy interruption puts the ability on a two-second cooldown.

Soul Furnace shields for up to six seconds and can be detonated after two seconds while the shield still holds. Roar of the Slayer hits the first enemy, slows it, and reduces its armor; hitting a minion or non-epic monster also knocks that unit backward and applies the same effects to enemies it passes through, creating a long-range setup for Decimating Smash.

What Sion lacks is speed. The Q is easy to see coming, the body is slow, and kiting champions can mostly ignore him. His games are not about winning lane; they are about scaling into the engage tank whose ultimate decides where the teamfight happens.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Farm behind the shield and let the lane come to you. Soul Furnace cannot be detonated until two seconds have passed and loses its damage recast if enemies break the shield first. Kick a minion through the opponent with Roar of the Slayer to slow them and reduce their armor, then charge Decimating Smash while their movement is restricted. Release after 0.75 seconds for the knockup and stun; a shorter tap only damages and briefly slows.
gamePlan.midGame: Crash the Baron wave before looking for a clear travel line into Herald or a river skirmish. Unstoppable Onslaught accelerates during its finite charge and cannot turn sharply, so choose the route before leaving lane and ping the target for allied follow-up. After arriving, use Roar of the Slayer to restrict movement before charging Decimating Smash. If terrain blocks a reliable ultimate line, walk with the team instead of starting a long charge that cannot reach the fight.
gamePlan.lateGame: Push the side wave early and group before Baron or Elder so Unstoppable Onslaught has a clear route into the setup. Hold the ultimate for a reachable carry or use it to counter-engage when the enemy dives your backline. Follow with a charged Decimating Smash only while allies can keep targets in the area, and detonate Soul Furnace before the shield is broken. Do not treat the passive as permission to die before the objective is secured.
gamePlan.teamfights: Pick the angle and charge. The dream is an R that hits two or more of their backline, followed right away by the charged knockup and shield burst while they are still getting up. If no flank exists, frontline honestly: body-block, slow the divers with E, and charge Q under their carry's escape paths. Then die, stand back up, and keep swinging; few champions get to keep fighting after death.

startingItem.name: Ruby Crystal
startingItem.note: Early health. His shield is a share of the damage he takes, so a bigger bar means a bigger shield.

boots.name: Armored Advance
boots.note: Armor and health, which let him absorb the trade he is inviting, which is how his Grit fills.

coreItems.name: Heartsteel
coreItems.note: Stacks permanent health from trades. More maximum health raises Sett's Grit cap, so a fully charged Haymaker can grant a larger shield and deal more damage; The Show Stopper instead scales with the grabbed enemy's bonus health.

coreItems.name: Overlord's Bloodmail
coreItems.note: Health that converts into damage, which suits a champion whose kit already scales off the health he stacks.

coreItems.name: Spear of Shojin
coreItems.note: Ability haste means more punches and more pulls, which is his damage and his lockdown.

coreItems.name: Sterak's Gage
coreItems.note: A second shield next to his own, so the moment his Grit is spent he still has something between him and death.

coreItems.name: Amaranth's Twinguard
coreItems.note: The armor and magic resistance protect Sett after he enters the enemy team, buying time to build Grit, cast Haymaker, and keep fighting after its shield expires.

situationalItems.name: Stridebreaker
situationalItems.desc: Juggernaut bruiser item with a dash
situationalItems.note: Build this when you cannot reach anyone. The dash and slow fix the fact that everything he does needs enemies next to him.

situationalItems.name: Chainlaced Crushers
situationalItems.note: Boot swap against heavy magic damage and crowd control. The tenacity lets him finish a pull that would otherwise be interrupted.

situationalItems.name: Hullbreaker
situationalItems.note: Build this when you are taking the side lane rather than grouping. Health, attack damage and move speed, with a heavy fourth attack and armor and magic resist for your nearby siege and super minions, feeding a duel his kit already makes hard to lose.

situationalItems.name: Black Cleaver
situationalItems.note: His punches hit the same target repeatedly, so the armor shred reaches full stacks quickly.

situationalItems.name: Thornmail
situationalItems.note: Build this when Sett needs armor and anti-heal. Entwine applies Grievous Wounds when enemies attack him or whenever he damages them, so Knuckle Down, Facebreaker, and Haymaker keep it on the brawler standing in front of him.

situationalItems.name: Force of Nature
situationalItems.note: Build this into repeated magic damage. The movement speed helps Sett reach Facebreaker range, while the magic resistance preserves health for a larger Grit-backed Haymaker.

situationalItems.name: Titanic Hydra
situationalItems.note: Turns the health he stacks into cleave, for the games decided by side-lane waves rather than a single grab.

situationalItems.name: Mercurial Scimitar
situationalItems.note: Build this when crowd control prevents Sett from spending a full Grit bar on Haymaker. The cleanse protects the brief shield and true-damage timing his all-in depends on.

keystoneRune.name: Conqueror
keystoneRune.desc: Gain stacks by damaging enemy champions. At maximum stacks, gain bonus damage and healing.
keystoneRune.note: His fights are long by design while Grit fills, so he stacks fully and the healing adds to his passive regeneration.

primaryRunes.name: Brutal
primaryRunes.desc: Attacks deal bonus adaptive damage to enemy champions.
primaryRunes.note: Bonus damage on every autoattack, which sharpens the right-hand punches his passive already amplifies.

primaryRunes.name: Last Stand
primaryRunes.desc: Deal more damage to champions while you are low on health.
primaryRunes.note: He spends every fight low by design, since that is when his Grit is fullest.

primaryRunes.name: Legend: Alacrity
primaryRunes.desc: Gain permanent attack speed by taking down champions, monsters, and minions.
primaryRunes.note: Attack speed means his punch alternation cycles faster, which is where his passive damage comes from.

secondaryRunes.name: Overgrowth
secondaryRunes.desc: Gain permanent maximum health when nearby minions or monsters die.
secondaryRunes.note: Permanent health raises the amount of Grit Sett can store, which increases the maximum shield and damage available from a fully charged Haymaker.

spells.name: Flash
spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

goodAgainst.note: Wind Wall blocks none of Sett's punches, Facebreaker, or Haymaker, and Sweeping Blade repeatedly brings Yasuo into the close range Sett wants. Save Facebreaker until Yasuo has dashed beside a minion or champion for the stun setup, then aim Haymaker after his dash is committed so he cannot slide away from the true-damage center.

Fiora can Riposte Haymaker's center damage, Facebreaker's stun, or The Show Stopper's suppression, so vary your timing instead of feeding her an obvious counter. Sett can still absorb her committed burst as Grit and punish her after Riposte is spent.

Blinding Dart stops Sett's alternating punches and Knuckle Down attacks from connecting, but it does not stop Facebreaker, Haymaker, or The Show Stopper. Use Knuckle Down's movement speed to close after the blind expires and avoid chasing through mushrooms.
Riven has to dive into your punch range to start her combo, where your grit shield blunts her burst, the pull breaks her dash chain, and the suplex ruins her all-in.

weakAgainst.note: Malphite stacks armor against your punches and pokes without feeding you meaningful grit, so the brawl never works in your favor, and his level 5 engage out-ranges yours.

Renekton can stun Sett with Ruthless Predator before Haymaker is aimed, then use Slice and Dice to leave before the Grit conversion lands. Keep Facebreaker for his second dash, angle Haymaker toward that exit rather than his entry, and avoid front-loading the shield into an empowered Ruthless Predator that can strip it.

Sion can absorb short trades with Soul Furnace and threaten Sett with a charged Decimating Smash while Haymaker is telegraphed. Haymaker's shield still appears immediately on cast, so use it before the knockup rather than claiming the knockup cancels the strike, and save displacement tools to spoil Sion's charge.
Her dashes slip the pull and slide out of your W radius mid-combo, so she chips you in bursts and never stands in punch range long enough to feed your grit.

gamePlan.overview:
Sett stores post-mitigation damage as Grit, up to half of his maximum health. Haymaker spends all stored Grit for an immediate, decaying shield and a delayed cone whose center deals true damage. Add the alternating left-right punches of his passive; the right punch is much faster and deals bonus damage; and he is strongest when enemies commit to fighting him at close range.

His lane plan is to force close-range brawls: Facebreaker pulls enemies from both his front and back, slowing them normally and stunning everyone only when at least one enemy is caught on each side. Knuckle Down resets his attack timer, guarantees a left-right pair, and briefly speeds him toward enemy champions. At level 5, The Show Stopper suppresses one enemy champion, carries them forward, and creates a slowing impact whose damage is highest near the center.

What he cannot do reliably is reach targets before committing his ultimate. Knuckle Down only grants movement speed while moving toward enemy champions, and The Show Stopper needs an enemy target, so ranged poke and repeated kiting can keep him out of his preferred range.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Brawl on your terms. Use the normal left-right pair, then reset the sequence with Knuckle Down for two empowered attacks. Let return damage build Grit and cash it in with Haymaker before the Grit begins decaying; the shield arrives immediately, while the damaging cone lands after the wind-up. Hold Facebreaker until the champion and a minion are on opposite sides of Sett so it stuns instead of only slowing. In ranged matchups, farm patiently and use Q's movement speed toward the enemy to close only when the trade is favorable.
gamePlan.midGame: Crash the Baron wave before moving to Herald so the opponent must lose farm or follow late. Use fog and the pit walls to approach a target that The Show Stopper can carry into your team, then line up Facebreaker with enemies on both sides for the stun. If no flank exists, frontline and hold the ultimate to remove a diver from your carry. Return to the side wave after the objective window because Sett is too slow to abandon lane pressure without a clear play.
gamePlan.lateGame: Clear the side wave early enough to group before Baron or Elder. Hold The Show Stopper either to carry a reachable damage dealer into allied focus or to remove the diver attacking your backline. Build Grit while frontlining, then aim Haymaker through several enemies without stepping beyond follow-up. Avoid distant late-game duels against scaled carries when Sett's crowd control is needed for the objective fight.
gamePlan.teamfights: Grab the most dangerous enemy and drop them where they are worst off, usually inside your team. Open with the suplex onto a carry when the angle is there, or hold it to peel your own backline. Pull clumped enemies into the stun, face their damage to charge grit, and release the punch through as many bodies as possible, since the true damage ignores however much armor their frontline stacked. You win fights by deciding where the enemy's best champion ends up standing.

coreItems.name: Amaranth's Twinguard

primaryRunes.desc: Immobilizing enemy champions grants a defensive shield for frontline engages.
primaryRunes.note: His taunt immobilizes, so the shield arrives on the same cast he engages with.

primaryRunes.name: Second Wind
primaryRunes.desc: After taking damage from a champion, regenerate health over time.
primaryRunes.note: His shield goes to whoever needs it, and this covers the damage he takes holding the lane himself.

primaryRunes.name: Overgrowth
primaryRunes.desc: Gain permanent maximum health when nearby minions or monsters die.
primaryRunes.note: He is the frontline and the peel, so the pool is what keeps him alive to be both.

spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

goodAgainst.note: He cannot meaningfully hurt you, you can trade into him with empowered autos, and your ultimate answers his teamfight engage by shielding whoever it lands on.

Spirit's Refuge blocks the basic-attack component that triggers Fiora's Vitals, while Stand United lets Shen answer the side-lane pressure her dueling creates elsewhere. Do not send Shadow Dash into a ready Riposte; bait the parry with a short empowered attack, then taunt after it expires and leave before Grand Challenge becomes an extended duel.
Blocking the empowered fury trade collapses his advantage, and the taunt drags him into your minions when he dashes in. After his strong levels he fades while you play the whole map.
Her engage wants autos and a clean combo, and your W blocks the first while the taunt interrupts the second, so her commits accomplish little.

weakAgainst.note: The W punch is an ability your block cannot stop, his grit absorbs your empowered trades, and your taunt does nothing to prevent his pull.

Silver Bolts deals percentage maximum-health true damage, but it only stacks through attacks that connect, so Spirit's Refuge can prevent procs during its 1.75-second window. Vayne remains difficult because she can wait out the zone, kite Shen afterward, and use Condemn to interrupt or displace his approach.
His damage is mace arcs and passive burn, not the autos your W blocks, and the death realm drags you into a 1v1 where your teamfight-and-peel kit is useless.
Her W grounds the dash your taunt rides in on, stranding your whole engage, while her buckler shield blunts your empowered autos and she trades back through your block.

gamePlan.overview:
Shen plays a different map than his lane opponent. Stand United immediately shields any allied champion anywhere on the map, with a larger shield when that ally is missing more health, then teleports Shen and his Spirit Blade to them after a three-second channel. A good Shen turns the enemy's best play into a sudden numbers advantage, but crowd control that interrupts the channel leaves him behind even though the initial shield was already granted.

His laning is sturdy rather than scary. Twilight Assault pulls the Spirit Blade to Shen and empowers his next three attacks; dragging it through an enemy champion also slows that champion while they move away and strengthens the attacks with bonus attack speed and damage. Spirit's Refuge creates a moving zone around the blade that blocks non-turret basic attacks hitting allied champions inside it. Shadow Dash damages and taunts enemy champions and monsters Shen passes through.

Shen usually wins through map impact rather than solo kills. Hold Baron lane without giving the opponent an easy lead, prepare the wave before leaving, and watch for fights where Stand United changes the numbers. If you use the ultimate without managing the wave first, the enemy can take plates or a turret while you are gone.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Trade when the blade is ready and the river is quiet. Position it behind the Baron laner, pull it through them with Twilight Assault, and spend the three empowered attacks while they are slowed when retreating. Cast Spirit's Refuge on yourself or an allied champion to send the blade there, then keep allies inside its moving zone while it blocks attacks. From level 5 onward, watch every allied health bar, but do not abandon a stacked enemy wave for a low-value skirmish. Stand United's shield is immediate, but Shen only arrives if its three-second channel completes.
gamePlan.midGame: Shove the wave before every play window so your absences cost the enemy a tower instead of costing you one. Your ultimate decides dragon fights, dives, and mid lane collapses, so track every lane's health bars constantly. When you arrive, taunt the most dangerous thing and block what you can. Between teleports, set up your jungler with the taunt: Shen ganks in lanes nobody warded for him.
gamePlan.lateGame: Keep the Baron wave pushed only as far as vision allows, then watch allied health bars and the next objective timer. Use Stand United when its immediate shield prevents lethal damage and the three-second channel can complete safely. After arriving, taunt the diver and place Spirit's Refuge where the protected carry can remain inside it. If the ultimate is unavailable, group before Baron or Elder rather than creating side-lane pressure Shen cannot convert into a global response.
gamePlan.teamfights: Protect first, then choose whether the taunt is better for peeling or engaging. Start fights near your carry, dash-taunt the champion diving them, and hold Spirit's Refuge for the enemy's biggest basic-attack threat instead of spending it on stray damage. If a fight starts across the map, check whether the shield saves an ally, the channel is safe, and your arrival creates useful numbers before committing. Shen's value is often measured by the damage his backline avoids, not by his own kill count.

startingItem.name: Ruby Crystal
startingItem.note: Early health for a champion whose whole pattern is being chased while his poison does the killing.

boots.name: Spellslinger's Shoes
boots.note: Magic penetration keeps the poison relevant, since it is a steady tick rather than a burst anyone respects.

coreItems.name: Liandry's Torment
coreItems.note: Poison Trail refreshes its damage while enemies keep crossing the cloud, so Liandry's maximum-health burn stays active on pursuers. The poison is persistent pressure, not an infinite debuff after one touch.

coreItems.name: Dead Man's Plate
coreItems.note: Momentum builds while he runs, which is all he does, and triggers on the fling that starts a kill.

coreItems.name: Rylai's Crystal Scepter
coreItems.note: The slow on his poison keeps chasers stuck in the trail, which is why they die to it.

coreItems.name: Bloodletter's Curse
coreItems.note: His poison touches everyone following him, so the magic resist shred stacks across a whole team.

coreItems.name: Rabadon's Deathcap
coreItems.note: Multiplies the AP scaling on Poison Trail, Mega Adhesive's initial hit, and Fling, turning every second enemies spend in the trail into a more expensive mistake.

situationalItems.name: Morellonomicon
situationalItems.note: Insanity Potion already makes Poison Trail apply 40% Grievous Wounds for its 20-second duration. Build Morellonomicon only when your team needs anti-heal outside that ultimate window or from the rest of Singed's magic damage; an early Oblivion Orb is enough before finishing it.

situationalItems.name: Oceanid's Trident
situationalItems.note: Build this when the enemy has shields that keep absorbing his steady tick damage.

situationalItems.name: Zhonya's Hourglass
situationalItems.note: Build this for when the chase finally catches him, so the poison can finish what it started. Buy Seeker's Armguard early for the armor and ability power.

situationalItems.name: Force of Nature
situationalItems.note: Build this when the enemy team has two or more AP champions. The move speed is also the stat his whole plan runs on.

situationalItems.name: Cosmic Drive
situationalItems.note: Haste and stacking move speed, both of which feed a champion whose survival is staying ahead of people.

situationalItems.name: Armored Advance
situationalItems.note: Boot swap against heavy physical damage, which is what makes the chase survivable.

situationalItems.name: Chainlaced Crushers
situationalItems.note: Boot swap against heavy magic damage and crowd control. The tenacity matters most since he dies the moment he is caught.

keystoneRune.name: Phase Rush
keystoneRune.desc: Hitting an enemy champion with 3 separate attacks or abilities grants movement speed and slow resistance.
keystoneRune.note: Poison Trail and Fling provide two quick champion hits; add an attack or Mega Adhesive to reach the third unique hit and trigger the burst of movement speed for an escape or chase.

primaryRunes.name: Manaflow Band
primaryRunes.desc: Hitting an enemy champion with an ability permanently increases your maximum mana.
primaryRunes.note: His poison trail drains mana for as long as it is running, and no item in the build gives him any, so the max mana is how long he can keep it on.

primaryRunes.name: Celerity
primaryRunes.desc: Gain bonus movement speed and enhance other movement speed effects.
primaryRunes.note: Move speed is not a convenience on him, it is the mechanic his kit is built around.

primaryRunes.name: Nimbus Cloak
primaryRunes.desc: After casting a summoner spell, gain movement speed and slow resistance.
primaryRunes.note: Move speed after a summoner spell is what makes his Flash and Ghost turns actually escape.

secondaryRunes.name: Battle Zeal
secondaryRunes.desc: While in combat with an enemy champion, gain stacking basic ability damage amplification.
secondaryRunes.note: His damage is basic abilities, so the amplification builds across the long chases he creates.

spells.name: Flash
spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

goodAgainst.note: Mega Adhesive grounds Irelia and turns off the Bladesurge resets she needs to cross the wave, while Fling can place her back inside the grounded zone. Drop Adhesive over the low-health minions she wants to dash through, Fling only after she commits, and do not give her a stationary extended fight with Ionian Fervor stacked.

Singed's movement makes Decimating Smash easy to sidestep, and Fling can interrupt Sion before a charged knockup controls the lane. Proxy only with river vision, run across the charge rather than straight away from it, and use Poison Trail to force Sion to choose between chasing you and catching the wave under his turret.
Camille has to catch you to matter, and catching you means standing in your poison with a fling waiting. Her true damage only counts in straight fights you never need to take.

His sweet spots need a stationary target and you never stand still, so the sweeps whiff while your fling breaks his combo. His sustain wants a long brawl that never happens against a champion who keeps running.

weakAgainst.note: Apprehend cancels Singed's escape line, Crippling Strike keeps him in Hemorrhage range, and the bleed continues after Poison Trail has stopped trading. Keep the wave recoverable, save Fling for the moment after Darius pulls, and never circle in melee trying to stack poison while he is stacking toward Noxian Guillotine.
Mini Gnar pokes you at a range you cannot answer and taxes every step of your run, while Mega form has the crowd control, like the wall toss, to actually end your escape.
Decisive Strike is one of the few tools fast enough to catch a running Singed, its silence locks your fling on arrival, and his regen heals back the poison you leave on him.
He out-ranges your whole kit, and the accelerated Shock Blast punishes every step of your run. You cannot fling someone who stays a screen away, and his poke chips you even while you proxy.

gamePlan.overview:
Singed does not play your game; he makes you play his. Poison Trail leaves clouds that linger for 3.25 seconds, while moving near any champion grants Singed a two-second burst of movement speed on a separate cooldown for each champion. Mega Adhesive deals an initial hit, then leaves a three-second slowing and grounding field. Fling now dashes Singed to its target, knocks other enemies aside along the path, and throws the target behind him; landing that target in Mega Adhesive roots them.

His value is map pressure. Proxy farming forces the enemy laner to choose between farming the crashed wave and hunting a champion built to survive being hunted, while the enemy jungler wastes minutes on him. Every chase he survives is two enemies doing nothing while his team plays four versus three.

Insanity Potion turns Singed into a 20-second disruptor by granting ability power, armor, magic resistance, movement speed, health regeneration, and mana regeneration. It also gives 30% of those bonuses to the nearest allied champion and makes Poison Trail apply 40% Grievous Wounds, so activating it beside the ally who will enter with him is a real teamfight optimization.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Use Poison Trail to control the wave without turning every lane into a proxy. A proxy is worthwhile only when the enemy jungler is accounted for and the cleared wave creates time for a recall, roam, or camp. Toggle the trail off between targets because it continuously spends mana. When the opponent commits, place Mega Adhesive where Fling will throw them, then use Fling's short targeted dash to reach and root them in the field. Keep an escape route open and pass near different champions for separate Noxious Slipstream speed bursts.
gamePlan.midGame: Insanity Potion and defensive items turn side-lane pressure into a strong river flank. Clear the wave before the first objectives, then move toward Herald when the map is even or dragon when your team is committed to repeated grouped fights. Activate the ultimate beside the ally who benefits most from receiving 30% of its stat bonuses, ground a choke, and Fling a reachable priority target toward your team. Keep Poison Trail touching healers and drain tanks during the ultimate so its Grievous Wounds continues to refresh.
gamePlan.lateGame: Late game, manage a side wave only when the next objective gives you time to rejoin. Your real value is forcing the enemy formation to turn: activate Insanity Potion, approach from a flank, and use Mega Adhesive to block the carry's escape or the diver's entry. Fling the target your team can actually punish, which may be a frontline engager rather than the most distant carry. Keep moving through several enemies for passive speed and spread Poison Trail without running beyond allied follow-up.
gamePlan.teamfights: Activate Insanity Potion near the allied diver or carry who can use its reduced stat package, then enter along the side of the fight rather than through the full frontline. Mega Adhesive can ground a choke, stop an escape, or protect your carry from a mobile diver. Fling a target toward allied damage or away from your backline, keep Poison Trail across multiple enemies for the ultimate's anti-heal, and cross near different champions for more passive movement-speed bursts. Leave the fight when the ultimate expires instead of staying for a fair stationary brawl.

situationalItems.name: Armored Advance

situationalItems.name: Chainlaced Crushers

keystoneRune.desc: Moving and attacking builds Energy. At 100 stacks, your next attack heals you and grants movement speed.
keystoneRune.note: Movement speed to keep Burnout ticking on a target, and healing on the attacks she lands doing it.

primaryRunes.name: Overgrowth

secondaryRunes.name: Legend: Alacrity

spells.name: Smite
spells.note: Required for Jungling. Secures objectives and sustains through camp clears.

goodAgainst.note: Wukong's dash-in burst does not kill a scaled Shyvana, and once you transform your cleave and Burnout out-damage him in the extended brawl, so his clone buys an escape rather than a kill.
Nocturne bets everything on one dive, and the longer the game goes the less his single combo means against your bulk, since you heal through the burst he commits.
Kha'Zix needs an isolated squishy target to delete, and a dragon-form Shyvana is neither. He can bully your early farm, but once you scale his burst bounces off your bulk.

weakAgainst.note: Her magic damage ignores your armor, and her ramping speed kites your dashless frame around every fight. Lillia also out-clears you, and her sleep flips any pit contest.

Nunu contests the objective race you rely on: his Consume clear keeps pace with yours, his percent-health bite chunks the health bar you scale with, and his ultimate threatens a steal at every dragon.
Rammus reflects the hybrid autos your damage leans on: Defensive Ball Curl sends Twin Bite and your on-hit damage straight back, and his armor cuts your physical damage to almost nothing.

gamePlan.overview:
Shyvana is a farming jungler whose early strength comes from clear speed rather than reliable gank control. Burnout damages nearby monsters and helps her move between camps, Flame Breath marks a camp for bonus damage, and Twin Bite resets her attack. After learning Dragon's Descent, attacks generate Fury toward the next transformation.

Farm toward level five, but take an early gank when an allied lane already has reliable control or the target is far beyond the wave. Contest Scuttle only when nearby lanes can move, because Shyvana has no hard control in Human Form. Large monsters and champion takedowns build Draconic Bloodline, while Dragon and Baron grant larger amounts. Once Dragon's Descent is available, the landing displacement gives her ganks and objective fights a clear entry tool.

Before level five, Shyvana has no hard control or dash, so an invade can force her away from camps before she can respond. Track the opposing jungler, ward entrances, and trade sides of the map when nearby lanes cannot support a contest. Losing one dragon slows Draconic Bloodline but does not stop her from gaining stacks through other large monsters and takedowns.
gamePlan.earlyGame:
Your first clear is the point of the champion, so treat it like a race. Use Flame Breath to mark the camp, keep Burnout ticking while attacking, and reset an attack with Twin Bite; both Twin Bite strikes apply on-hit effects, and subsequent attacks reduce its cooldown. The clear earns Draconic Bloodline from large monsters, but Fury is not available until Dragon's Descent is learned, at which point the ability grants its first 100 Fury automatically.

Path toward scuttle when your lanes can support the contest, then prioritize reaching level five for Dragon's Descent. Before that, only gank lanes that can hold the target for you because Human Form has no hard crowd control or dash. Ward your flanks, watch where the enemy jungler started, and keep collecting large-monster stacks without forcing an unsupported river duel.
gamePlan.midGame:
Dragon is valuable because it grants a large Draconic Bloodline increase, but Herald, Baron, other large monsters, and takedowns also progress the passive. Choose the objective your lanes can reach first instead of forcing every dragon from a losing setup. If the enemy commits several champions to one side, trade for Herald, camps, or turret pressure and keep building stacks elsewhere.

Your clear speed lets you farm one side of the map and still reach the objective on the other side first, so use it to set up vision and arrive before the enemy jungler. You also stop fearing invades once your ultimate is up, so counter-jungle the slow farmers and steal camps from anyone who tried to starve you.
gamePlan.lateGame: Group before Baron and Elder, build Fury in advance, and avoid showing on a distant side wave when the enemy can start the objective. Use Dragon's Descent after the enemy commits or when the landing can displace a priority target toward your team. Damage the closest safe target after entering and use Burnout to stay in range. Against scaled carries, do not remain alone in the pit after allies disengage; leave with the team and rebuild Fury for the next contest.
gamePlan.teamfights: Do not waste Dragon's Descent as an opener unless the leap lands on a clump or a key target and drags them with her. That leap is your engage, your gap-closer, and your only hard crowd control, so spend it where it locks down a carry or splits their backline instead of just adding a body to the fight. Once you are in, Burnout and your cleave punish anyone stacked near you, and Flame Breath marks the target your team should focus. You are tanky and you heal as you fight, so the longer you stay alive in the middle, the more the fight tilts your way. Pick the right target, commit the leap when your team can follow the landing, and let the brawl play out around you.

situationalItems.name: Banshee's Veil

keystoneRune.name: Phase Rush
keystoneRune.desc: Hitting an enemy champion with 3 separate attacks or abilities grants movement speed and slow resistance.
keystoneRune.note: His rotation is many quick hits, so it triggers almost immediately, and the move speed is his only real escape.

primaryRunes.desc: Hitting an enemy champion with an ability permanently increases your maximum mana.
primaryRunes.note: His passive turns mana into damage, so more mana is more damage.

primaryRunes.name: Transcendence
primaryRunes.desc: Gain ability haste, then reduce a basic ability's cooldown after it hits at level 9.
primaryRunes.note: Ability haste means his rotation loops faster, which is how his damage works.

primaryRunes.name: Nimbus Cloak
primaryRunes.desc: After casting a summoner spell, gain movement speed and slow resistance.
primaryRunes.note: Move speed after a summoner spell helps a mage with no dash reposition around a fight.

secondaryRunes.name: Battle Zeal
secondaryRunes.desc: While in combat with an enemy champion, gain stacking basic ability damage amplification.
secondaryRunes.note: All his damage is basic abilities, so the amplification builds through his extended rotations.

spells.name: Flash
spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

goodAgainst.note: Rebuttal can copy Overload if Ryze fires it into the barrier, but its brief window cannot cover the repeated Spell Flux and Overload cycle. Use Spell Flux or movement to draw Rebuttal, hold the next projectile until it expires, then root Mel and continue the low-cooldown rotation while her only invulnerability is unavailable.

Your health pool and mana scaling absorb the burst she commits, and once she dashes in, she is a squishy melee assassin standing next to a targeted prison that roots her outright once Spell Flux has marked her.

Ryze never dashes, so he does not create free Gloom marks. Mistral Bolt and Looming Darkness are telegraphed, but Personal Space is immediate and Shadow Surge gives Vex a real dash; use a Flux-marked Rune Prison after she arrives and track whether Doom is prepared.
His hop dodges one spell, but your damage is a constant stream, and your health pool and sustained output outlast the short window his all-in gives him while he stands in melee range.

weakAgainst.note: This matchup is built to beat you: his silence cuts your rotation mid-combo, his blink steps out of your root, and he out-scales the late game you were counting on.

Aurelion Sol out-ranges Overload and Singularity pulls enemies toward its center while executing units below its threshold; it does not root Ryze. The pull and slow can still hold a predictable caster in Breath of Light while Aurelion Sol scales.
Veigar's cage stuns you from outside your range, his stacked burst kills you through the bulk you build, and he out-ranges Overload, zoning the ground you need to stand on.

gamePlan.overview:
Ryze is a sustained-damage mage who fights in repeating spell rotations. Overload fires faster each time the rest of his combo cycles, Rune Prison slows anyone who steps too far up the lane and roots them outright when Spell Flux has already marked them, and Spell Flux spreads his damage across the wave and any group standing close together. He is not a burst mage who kills in one window; once he starts casting, he keeps going until the target is dead.

In mid lane he plays the standard scaling mage game. The early levels are short on mana and damage, so he punishes walk-ups with Rune Prison and farms while he waits for items. Once those arrive, the lane flips: the combo tears through anyone who holds still, and the root sets up his jungler in every river fight.

His ultimate, Realm Warp, teleports his whole team through walls, into flanks, or onto an objective before the enemy expects it. The cost is the usual mage weakness, only worse: he is squishy, his range is short for a caster, and anyone who can dash or blink onto him kills him before the rotation gets going.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Farm with your spells and punish anyone who steps into the wave. Flux into prison into a loaded Overload is the trade you want: catch a walk-up, land the combo, and step back before they answer. Watch your mana constantly, because a Ryze with an empty bar has no threat at all. Give ground calmly to lane bullies and farm toward your spikes. Against other mages, only trade full rotations when yours is up and theirs is on cooldown. Take wave priority when it is cheap, since the scuttle fight and the first river skirmish are where your prison is useful long before your damage is.
gamePlan.midGame: One or two items in, your damage and wave control begin to matter. Shove before moving into river, then use Rune Prison on a target your jungler can reach rather than chasing through an unwarded entrance. At six minutes, Herald is usually the stronger even conversion, while a composition built for repeated teamfights can choose dragon and work toward soul. Realm Warp can move teammates across a wall, create a flank around vision, or extract them from a collapse, but confirm who is taking the portal before committing the destination. Keep farming between plays so map pressure does not delay the item scaling that makes later rotations stronger.
gamePlan.lateGame: By now you are sustained magic damage with a team-wide teleport attached. Root the diver coming for you, spread Spell Flux through their team, and cast Overloads from behind your frontline, because every uninterrupted second adds damage they cannot afford. The portal decides endgames: a five-man warp onto Baron, a flank that lands your team on their backline, or an exit that turns a lost fight into a regroup. You are still a squishy, short-ranged mage, so never lead with your body and let the rotation do the work.
gamePlan.teamfights: Spread Spell Flux through grouped enemies, root the threat that can reach you, and fire Overload from behind your frontline. Save Realm Warp for a planned entry, a rotation around terrain, or an exit that the team has time to take together. Ryze has no instant escape, so step forward only while the enemy engage is controlled. If a control spell interrupts the rotation, back away and rebuild the spell sequence instead of remaining in range.

boots.name: Crimson Lucidity
