coreItems.name: Black Mist Scythe
coreItems.note: Sona completes the quest with Hymn of Valor and empowered Power Chords, converting her repeated aura cycle into wards, ability power, and haste without taking lane farm.

coreItems.name: Archangel's Staff
coreItems.note: Turns her mana pool into ability power, which matters because cycling all three auras drains mana fast.

coreItems.name: Harmonic Echo
coreItems.note: Harmony builds from the moving and casting she does constantly, so the bonus healing is charged whenever her heal goes out.

coreItems.name: Staff of Flowing Waters
coreItems.note: Healing an ally gives her ability haste and ability power, which on her means every aura back sooner.

coreItems.name: Ardent Censer
coreItems.note: Sona's W aura can shield several allies at once, spreading Ardent Censer's attack speed and on-hit damage across the team every time she cycles the aura.

situationalItems.name: Banshee's Veil
situationalItems.note: Build this when the enemy has a hook or point-and-click stun, since she is the most fragile champion in the game.

situationalItems.name: Frozen Heart
situationalItems.note: Build this when the enemy team has a lot of attack speed dependent champions. The mana also feeds her aura cycling.

situationalItems.name: Zhonya's Hourglass
situationalItems.note: Build this for the dive that reaches her, since Aria of Perseverance heals and shields her too but nowhere near fast enough to cover a full combo. Buy Seeker's Armguard early for the armor and ability power.

situationalItems.name: Mikael's Blessing
situationalItems.note: A cleanse next to her auras, so the carry she is buffing can be pulled out of a lockdown chain.

situationalItems.name: Redemption
situationalItems.desc: Active AoE heal and enemy true-damage burn
situationalItems.note: Lets her heal a fight from outside it, which matters since her auras only reach as far as she can safely stand.

situationalItems.name: Armored Advance
situationalItems.note: Boot swap against heavy physical damage, when surviving the enemy duo matters more than aura frequency.

keystoneRune.name: Fleet Footwork
keystoneRune.desc: Moving and attacking builds Energy. At 100 stacks, your next attack heals you and grants movement speed.
keystoneRune.note: Sona charges Fleet while moving between aura positions. When she spends her empowered Power Chord attack, Fleet supplies the heal and movement speed that help her return behind the carry after poking; the Power Chord itself deals bonus magic damage and stuns.

primaryRunes.name: Font of Life
primaryRunes.desc: Damaging enemy champions heals you and the lowest-health nearby ally after a short cooldown.
primaryRunes.note: Hymn of Valor repeatedly damages enemy champions, letting Font of Life add healing for Sona and her lowest-health nearby ally throughout lane and teamfights.

primaryRunes.name: Bone Plating
primaryRunes.desc: After taking damage from a champion, the next 3 instances of champion damage are reduced.
primaryRunes.note: Sona is extremely fragile and has no dash, so reducing the next three instances of champion damage helps her survive the engage that reaches her.

primaryRunes.name: Revitalize
primaryRunes.desc: Healing and shielding are stronger, especially on low-health targets.
primaryRunes.note: Revitalize strengthens Aria of Perseverance's heal and its aura shield, especially when Sona or her protected ally is already low.

secondaryRunes.name: Transcendence
secondaryRunes.desc: Gain ability haste, then reduce a basic ability's cooldown after it hits at level 9.
secondaryRunes.note: Ability haste means faster aura cycling, which is the only stat that changes what she contributes.

spells.name: Flash
spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

goodAgainst.note: Yuumi remains untargetable while attached, so Sona wins by pressuring the host rather than trying to hit the cat. Use Hymn of Valor and Power Chord to tax that single exposed target, answer Zoomies with Aria of Perseverance, and hold Crescendo for the host's engage so Yuumi cannot carry them through the sustained exchange.
Lulu shields and peels but brings no kill pressure of her own, so the lane becomes a poke contest you have the damage to win, though her peel makes diving her backline late a chore.

Milio can answer Sona's poke with healing and shields, while Ultra Mega Fire Kick can interrupt her forward positioning. Sona can pressure multiple targets with Hymn of Valor, but do not claim Milio is unable to stop poke; win through repeated aura trades and mana efficiency.
In the aura mage mirror you spike first: your Power Chord is the harder-hitting poke in every exchange, so you win the early trades and shoves outright.

Janna can answer Hymn of Valor with Eye of the Storm and punish Sona's short range with Zephyr or Howling Gale. Tag both lane opponents when possible, avoid standing in the tornado line, and do not treat Janna as a champion with no return damage.

weakAgainst.note: Zenith Blade crosses Sona's short aura range, Shield of Daybreak begins a crowd-control chain, and Solar Flare can start it before she is close enough to use Crescendo. Keep the wave near your turret, preserve the empowered Diminuendo Power Chord to reduce the carry's follow-up, and do not step up for poke while Zenith Blade is ready.
One hook ends the trade and probably your life, since you have no dash to dodge it and no escape after, and his pick threat completely out-ranges your poke.
He exists to delete immobile squishies and you are the most immobile squishy in the lane; a single grab pulls you into instant burst your sustain means nothing against.
His hook roots you in place, his shield eats your poke, and his chain of crowd control lasts longer than your fragile frame can survive.
Her crash-and-stun engage was built to punish immobile frames like yours, and your shields barely slow a committed all-in once she binds you.

gamePlan.overview:
Sona's basic abilities each create a three-second aura that tags Sona and nearby allies: Hymn of Valor loads bonus magic damage onto their next attack, Aria of Perseverance shields them after healing Sona and the most wounded nearby ally, and Song of Celerity grants movement speed. Each cast adds a Power Chord stack; at three, Sona's next attack against a champion gains bonus magic damage and a 0.5-second stun. She respawns with all three stacks ready.

In the 2v2 she wins by attrition and careful aura positioning. Hymn of Valor automatically bolts the two nearest visible enemies while prioritizing champions, but allies must enter the aura to receive its attack buff. Her basic casts also impose a brief shared cooldown on the other basic abilities, so cycle deliberately instead of trying to press all three simultaneously.

The catch is that she is extremely fragile and has no dash. Her movement-speed aura, a fully prepared passive stun, and Crescendo can create space, but none of them make an exposed position safe. Sona needs vision and disciplined spacing because being caught before those tools are ready usually removes her from the fight.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Cast Hymn of Valor when one or both enemy champions are among the two nearest visible targets, then move near your carry so its aura tags both of you for an empowered next attack. Cast Aria of Perseverance when the most wounded nearby ally is the intended heal target and step close enough to share its shield aura. Track Power Chord at three stacks and spend the stunning attack when your carry can trade during the 0.5-second opening.
gamePlan.midGame: After Crescendo is available, move from Dragon lane only when the wave is safe and your carry can follow or farm alone. Use Song of Celerity to reach river setups, establish vision with a teammate, and hold Crescendo for a grouped target or the diver that reaches your backline. Arrive before the objective so Sona can poke and cycle auras from a protected position instead of walking through dark river after the fight begins.
gamePlan.lateGame: Late game, Crescendo is both crowd control and an aura steroid. Aim the traveling chord through a route enemies must remain near, then exploit the 20-second 20% aura amplification after it ends. Keep rotating Q for allied on-hit magic damage, W for group shields, and E for movement speed; Sona's passive also reduces her basic cooldowns increasingly with level, making survival throughout that empowered window especially valuable.
gamePlan.teamfights:
Crescendo lasts 3.75 seconds as it travels to the target location and emits a pulse every 0.75 seconds. Enemies damaged for the first time are stunned for one second; later pulses damage and slow them. Afterward, all three auras are 20% stronger for 20 seconds, so do not disengage automatically after the initial stun.

Stay close to the largest safe group of teammates so each ability cycle reaches several allies. Position behind the frontline, close enough to empower attacks, refresh shields, and help teammates reposition. Remain far enough back that one engage cannot remove you from the fight. Move with your carries as the formation changes instead of chasing a low-health enemy alone. Sona wins extended fights by surviving and cycling all three auras through her team.

goodAgainst.note: Swain never dashes, so he does not create free Gloom marks. Mistral Bolt and Looming Darkness are telegraphed, but Personal Space is immediate and Shadow Surge gives Vex a real dash; track the prepared Doom fear before committing to a drain fight.
His whole game is a burst dive, and you are a drain tank built to outlast exactly that: your healing beats his combo, and he is squishy once pinned next to you.

Wind Wall can deny Nevermove's projectile path, but it does not stop the drain from Demonic Ascension once Yasuo has dashed into Swain's range. Bait the wall before using Nevermove, place Vision of Empire on his return path, and extend the fight with the ultimate only after he has consumed nearby minions as dash targets.
Her burst is built for squishies, and your ultimate heals it back while she is stuck in melee next to you; the shroud breaks targeting but not your ground root.
Ahri's charm burst is meant for squishies, and you heal it back, so her all-in feeds the ultimate it was supposed to kill; only her three dashes let her get away.

weakAgainst.note: Syndra out-ranges your root and stun-bursts you from a distance your sustain cannot answer, and her early poke out-paces your drain before your fragments stack.
Brand's stun chain interrupts the engage your whole kit is built around, he out-ranges your reach, and his full combo chunks you faster than your drain heals it back.

Death Ray damages Swain before Nevermove can threaten, Gravity Field controls the ground his ultimate wants to occupy, and Power Transfer shields Viktor's short return trade. Approach from a side angle after the field is used, pull Viktor into Demonic Ascension rather than walking through the zone, and preserve health until an extended fight is actually available.
Vel'Koz pokes from a range your short reach cannot answer, his knockup stops the walk-up your game depends on, and his true damage chips through your sustain faster than you heal it back.

gamePlan.overview:
Swain builds permanent health from Soul Fragments. Enemy champions leave one after dying, Vision of Empire collects one from each champion it hits, and recasting Nevermove collects one from every rooted champion it pulls. Each fragment heals Swain for a percentage of his maximum health and grants 16 permanent health. Nevermove damages on the outward pass, then its returning claw detonates on the first enemy hit to root nearby enemies for 1.5 seconds.

The key combo is Nevermove into Vision of Empire before pulling. Vision deals 50% bonus damage to immobilized targets and collects its own fragment, then Nevermove's recast pulls all rooted champions and collects another fragment from each. Death's Hand fires five bolts and deals reduced damage from additional bolts hitting the same target, making it strongest at close range after the pull.

Demonic Ascension begins with 50 Demonic Energy. Energy decays over time; faster after five seconds; but draining at least one enemy champion generates more every half-second and a champion takedown refills it completely. The form ends at zero Energy, so spacing or crowd control that removes every champion from drain range is often more dangerous than raw damage. Demonflare unlocks after two seconds and can be recast while the form remains active.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Aim Nevermove so its returning claw reaches the champion after the outward pass. When it roots, immediately place Vision of Empire under the immobilized target to gain the 50% damage bonus and its fragment, then recast E before the root ends to pull and collect another. Follow at close range with Death's Hand so multiple bolts connect. Against mobile targets, hold E until their dash is spent instead of throwing the only setup into open space.
gamePlan.midGame: Crash the mid wave before moving to dragon or Herald, then enter the river fight from beside your frontline. Activate Demonic Ascension when at least one champion will remain in drain range, because its initial Energy otherwise decays and begins falling faster after five seconds. Each half-second of champion drain offsets the normal decay, while a takedown refills the resource. Use Demonflare after its lockout to slow enemies back into range, and return to the side wave when no objective or skirmish is available.
gamePlan.lateGame: Clear side waves only when Swain can rejoin before Baron or Elder is contested. In the setup, stay close enough to the frontline to land Nevermove without entering every enemy damage source. Grievous Wounds reduces the healing from Demonic Ascension but not its damage or Energy generation, so keep a reachable champion in range and use Demonflare to prevent an easy disengage. A takedown refills Energy, but do not chase one beyond allied vision and lose the objective position.
gamePlan.teamfights: Activate Demonic Ascension as bodies collide so champion drains replenish Demonic Energy immediately. After two seconds, use Demonflare's 60% decaying slow to keep enemies inside and continue recasting it while the form lasts. Root with Nevermove, land Vision of Empire during the immobilize for its bonus damage and fragment, then pull for another fragment. Zhonya's is especially strong after committing because the drain, healing, and Energy generation continue during stasis while enemies remain nearby.

gamePlan.overview:
Threaded Volley fires five shards over 1.5 seconds and creates Worked Ground for 30 seconds. Casting Q while standing on that ground consumes it for a 10-mana, half-cooldown Boulder: one larger projectile that deals increased primary-target damage and slows its explosion. Unraveled Earth deals initial damage, then slows enemies walking across its stones; only a dash or forced movement over a stone detonates it and stuns that enemy once per cast.

Rock Surfing builds movement speed while Taliyah travels near terrain and is out of champion combat, supporting her shove-and-roam plan. Weaver's Wall creates terrain, knocks champions aside as it forms, and lets Taliyah alone surf after a one-second channel. She can jump off after 0.75 seconds, is forced off by immobilization or silence, and can destroy the completed wall with another recast.

The cost is the usual control-mage weakness: no mobility. Once Seismic Shove is on cooldown she has no escape, her damage wants her standing on worked ground rather than chasing, and her squishy frame makes her the exact target every gap-closer is built to delete.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Use full Threaded Volley from fresh ground to clear and poke, then return to a Worked Ground patch when a cheap, half-cooldown slowing Boulder is more valuable than five shards. Against a dash threat, place Unraveled Earth on its landing route and hold Seismic Shove: W can force the target across stones, causing detonations and the delayed stun. Ward before leaving lane because champion damage locks Weaver's Wall for three seconds and can deny the escape.
gamePlan.midGame: After Weaver's Wall is available, crash the mid wave and check which side has allied follow-up before riding toward a fight. Use the wall to cut off a retreat, divide reinforcements, or reach river before the enemy mid. At dragon and Herald, place Unraveled Earth across the entrance and use Seismic Shove on the first target who steps too far forward. Do not take the wall into an unseen enemy formation; plan where Taliyah will dismount and how she leaves if the target retreats.
gamePlan.lateGame: By late game you are a control mage with long-range personal travel, not a team teleport. Weaver's Wall can split a formation or close a retreat, but it can also block allies and Taliyah is the only champion who can surf it. Once the wall finishes, recast to destroy it early when it obstructs your own team. Use Unraveled Earth's normal slow to hold chokes and its detonation stun specifically against dashes or targets displaced by Seismic Shove.
gamePlan.teamfights: Lay Unraveled Earth on dive paths for its slow, then use Seismic Shove to knock a priority target across the stones and trigger up to five detonations; only the first can stun that target, and later detonations deal reduced damage. Use Weaver's Wall before taking champion damage, split or trap the formation, and destroy it once it becomes more helpful to the enemy than your team.

gamePlan.overview:
Taliyah is a control-mage jungler who shapes where enemies can move. Threaded Volley provides repeated damage, Seismic Shove displaces a target, and Unraveled Earth punishes forced movement and dashes through the field. Weaver's Wall creates terrain and gives Taliyah a long rotation tool. She relies on controlling an area before opponents reach her because her direct dueling and escape options are limited.

She wins through poke, zoning, and map pressure rather than one big all-in. Chip targets at scuttle and on ganks, use Seismic Shove to peel a diver or throw a squishy into your team, and lay Unraveled Earth so the enemy has nowhere safe to stand. Her ultimate is the key tool: a wall that lets her flank from an unwarded angle, cross the river to a fleeing target, or escape a collapse.

The cost is how fragile she is. She is squishy with no real escape once her wall is down, so an assassin who reaches her or an early duelist who catches her mid-clear ends the fight before her zoning matters. All her damage is skillshots, so a missed Seismic Shove or a dodged volley is a wasted window.
gamePlan.earlyGame:
Use full Threaded Volley from fresh ground to hit the whole camp, then step onto Worked Ground and use the Boulder while repositioning for the next cast. Lay Unraveled Earth through the camp and use Seismic Shove to force the large monster across its stones, speeding up the clear while briefly interrupting its attacks. A clean clear comes from cycling these interactions without standing still between casts.

For ganks, cast Unraveled Earth first, then aim Seismic Shove to knock the target across its stones. Forced movement triggers up to five detonations; only the first stuns that target, and later detonations deal reduced damage. Ordinary walking through the field only takes the initial hit and slow.
gamePlan.midGame:
Taliyah approaches objective fights by claiming ground before either team commits. Unraveled Earth denies the ground the enemy needs to stand on, so shove the first person who steps up and let your team collapse on whoever you peeled or threw. Contest when your team is ahead on early fights; when it is even, take Herald and give up the dragon, since your wall converts a tower faster than most, unless your team is built to fight for soul.

Between objectives, clear a camp then ride Weaver's Wall to a lane nobody is watching and turn a gank into a pick from an angle they never warded. Your tempo comes from the wall, not your clear speed, so keep showing up where the enemy is not.
gamePlan.lateGame: Late game, set Unraveled Earth before divers dash and keep Seismic Shove for forcing a priority target across its stones. Weaver's Wall can divide a formation, but it can also obstruct allies and only Taliyah can ride it; once fully formed, recast to destroy it early when necessary. Do not describe it as a panic escape because incoming champion damage locks the cast for three seconds.
gamePlan.teamfights: Stay in the back and shape the fight before it starts. Lay Unraveled Earth on the chokes and dive paths so the enemy front line has to walk through mines to reach you, then poke them down with Threaded Volley as they come. Seismic Shove is your one decisive button: peel the assassin off your carry, or throw their carry into your team and end the fight. Save Weaver's Wall to flank, cut off a retreat, or escape a collapse, and do not waste it on nothing. The mistake that loses fights is greedy positioning, because one dash onto your squishy frame undoes everything your zone set up.

gamePlan.overview:
Syndra is a burst control mage who plays the whole lane from long range and then ends it in one combo. She conjures Dark Spheres as delayed area damage, hurls a nearby or newly generated sphere to slow enemies, and casts Scatter the Weak to knock enemies back. Spheres pushed by Scatter the Weak stun targets they hit; the stun duration does not grow from leaving a sphere in the path. She can cast while repositioning, but she still has no dash or blink when someone gets through that control.

Ability damage to champions grants Splinters of Wrath and restores mana, while each skill point also grants four Splinters. At 40, 60, and 80 stacks Syndra can enhance one basic ability: Dark Sphere can store two charges, Force of Will gains bonus true damage, and Scatter the Weak gains angle and range. At 100, Unleashed Power gains range and executes when its damage would leave the target below 10% health; at 120, Syndra gains 12% ability power.

The catch is built into the kit. She has no dash, no blink, and no escape, so a diver who gets past the stun leaves her with nothing. The stun is a skillshot with a real cast time, and champions who sidestep it or jump through it run her down freely.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Poke with Dark Sphere as the enemy steps up to last-hit; each champion hit adds one Splinter and immediately restores mana, so accurate pressure partly funds the next cast. Keep a sphere near you for Scatter the Weak. Force of Will automatically grabs the nearest sphere, or generates and throws one at 80% damage when none is available, so do not accidentally remove the sphere you intended to push for a stun.
gamePlan.midGame: Your first item turns the poke into real kill pressure, so start spending your priority. Crash the wave with sphere damage, then walk to river: a loaded Syndra contests scuttle hard, and a sphere pushed by Scatter the Weak into Unleashed Power is a clean pick on anyone who face-checks near dragon or Herald. Set up around objectives with a sphere already on the ground, stun whoever steps too far, and end the skirmish before it becomes a fight. Roam to a side lane when the wave is shoved and your stun is up, since an immobile carry hit by your stun-and-barrage sequence rarely lives to call for help. Keep nearby spheres banked before a major fight so the ultimate can collect them.
gamePlan.lateGame: Clear side waves only when Syndra can return before Baron or Elder is threatened, then prepare spheres from behind allied vision. Use Unleashed Power on a valuable target when the barrage can finish or force them out of the fight. The cast creates three spheres and collects up to four recent nearby spheres, then leaves them on the ground for six seconds. Follow with Scatter the Weak through that field to knock back a diver or create several stun lines across the enemy formation.
gamePlan.teamfights: Place spheres before the fight to increase Unleashed Power's count, but track the six-second lifetime so they do not expire before R collects them. Open with Q-E when a carry can be stunned, then barrage; if the first stun is unavailable, R can create and leave three to seven spheres for a follow-up E that threatens several stun lines at once. At 100 Splinters the execute checks whether R would push its target below 10%, and a lethal sphere then explodes onto nearby enemy champions.

gamePlan.overview:
Talon is a jungler who reaches lanes from angles nobody is watching. Rake clears camps fast and slows whatever it touches, and Noxian Diplomacy dashes him onto a target for a burst of damage, with a combo that usually ends the fight before the laner can react. He is an early-game assassin in the jungle role, built to come out of his clear ahead and to keep everyone else behind.

He wins by being everywhere first. His clear is quick, his blink ignores normal spacing, and Shadow Assault shreds camps, checks brush, and doubles as the escape his squishy frame needs. Get ahead early, keep visiting lanes, and steal enemy camps while their jungler is busy. A fed Talon does not really teamfight; he removes one person from the fight and leaves. Left alone for the first few minutes, he decides who on the enemy team is allowed to play.

His problem is the same as every glass assassin's. He commits a blink to reach a target, and if that target lives, he is a melee body with no health bar in the wrong place. Hard crowd control, tanky bruisers who survive his combo, and junglers who match his early aggression all turn his tempo against him. He needs to be ahead, because he has no way to catch back up by farming.
gamePlan.earlyGame:
Lead with Rake so both its outward and returning passes hit large monsters, then use Q as an attack reset and trigger Blade's End with the next attack at three Wound stacks. Close-range Q crits, while kills heal Talon and refund most of its cooldown. Plan the last camp around an unused wall section that opens a gank angle rather than assuming level five is required for pressure.

Contest scuttle when you arrive even, since your duel is strong this early and the vision pays for itself. If the enemy jungler is a slow farmer, walk into their camps and take what you want: you clear faster and duel better, and every stolen camp is one they lose. Just watch your health, because an aggressive path leaves you low and a counter-gank can turn your invade into a death.
gamePlan.midGame:
Talon makes an objective safe by turning the enemy rotation into a temporary numbers disadvantage. That is worth forcing whenever your team is ahead. In an even game take Herald, since your falloff means the tower matters more to you than a soul point you may not be around to use.

Between objectives, keep the gank loop running and farm a camp between visits so your gold keeps coming. Save Shadow Assault primarily for champion kills instead of routinely spending the key invisibility cooldown on camps. In a gank, hit both Rake passes when possible, Q to the target, and attack at three Wound stacks; or cast R during the Q dash and break invisibility with the finishing attack so the blades converge on the victim.
gamePlan.lateGame: Your window shrinks as the game goes long, so play tighter. You can still delete a squishy on command, but the enemy now groups, wards, and stands near their tank, so free kills become rare and you have to create them. Hunt the flanks: move to a side lane, threaten a pick on whoever the enemy sends to answer you, and use Shadow Assault as the reposition that gets you in and back out alive. Around baron, your value is the pickoff that opens the fight, not the brawl itself, because a full five versus five with you committed in the middle makes you the easiest body to focus. If the game stays even this long, your influence is smaller, so make every blink count and never spend your ultimate on a target that will not die.
gamePlan.teamfights: You are not the one who starts the fight or stands in it. Your job is the assassination: wait for the engage to land, then blink past the frontline onto their carry, burst them down before their escape and defensive tools come online, and burst them before anyone peels. Shadow Assault is both your entry damage and your exit, so time it to cover the dive and the retreat rather than spending it on the way in. If their backline has a hard peeler guarding it, do not force it: flank wide, bait a cooldown, and take the kill on the second look. The fight you want removes their damage dealer and gets you out, leaving a clean four versus five. The fight you lose is the one where you commit early, get caught, and die before your combo finishes.

Her ball out-ranges your poison, her shield soaks the chip you land, and your blind does nothing to a mage whose damage is all abilities.
Zed's damage comes from shurikens and his ultimate, not autos, so your blind barely dents his burst, and his shadows close onto your squishy frame the moment your dart is down.
Heimerdinger's turret nest out-damages you in lane and zones you off the wave, your blind does nothing to turrets, and the grenade stun catches you on the walk-up.

gamePlan.overview:
Teemo's attacks deal immediate bonus magic damage and apply a four-second poison. Guerrilla Warfare is an activated camouflage that lasts indefinitely while Teemo is idle or inside brush and only for a limited duration while moving elsewhere; breaking it grants three seconds of attack speed. Move Quick supplies both passive speed and an active dash, so Teemo is mobile even though he remains fragile.

You win with patient, constant pressure. Shove the wave with your damage-over-time, sit at the edge of your range, and dare the enemy mid to commit into a blind they cannot afford. Between waves, seed the map with mushrooms, which give vision and damage at once: they zone the river, guard objectives, and chunk anyone who forgets where they walked.

The weakness is obvious. His attack range is short for a ranged champion, and Move Quick's short dash plus speed often cannot clear a committed engage by itself. Blind only answers attack-reliant damage, so a mage who out-ranges him or an assassin who bursts with abilities can still run through his fragile health bar.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Poke with Toxic Shot when the opponent last-hits and save Blinding Dart for attack-reliant trades. Use Guerrilla Warfare from brush or while idle, then exploit its attack-speed buff after revealing. Move Quick does not interrupt camouflage, so Teemo can dash while hidden and preserve the ambush; its active also doubles the passive movement bonus for three seconds and prevents damage from removing that speed during the window.
gamePlan.midGame: Crash the mid wave before placing mushrooms along the river route, objective entrance, and likely flank rather than stacking every charge in one brush. Mid priority lets Teemo prepare vision and damage before Scuttle, dragon, or Herald is contested. He does not need to force a side-lane roam when no target is extended; hold the wave, deny the enemy mid's movement, and let traps reveal rotations. Keep at least one charge available to rebuild control after a sweeper clears the first line.
gamePlan.lateGame: Late game Teemo is poke and zoning with only a short dash and speed burst for self-peel, so positioning is the entire job. Your shrooms become serious area denial: a fully mined chokepoint around Baron or dragon forces the enemy to eat poison or give up the objective, and a single trap can reveal and slow an engage before it lands. You can split push a side lane on the strength of your poison shove and trap-covered routes, but never get caught alone, because Move Quick does not make his tiny health bar survive a full collapse. Your on-hit poison holds up against tanks and squishies alike, so play around the vision you laid yourself.
gamePlan.teamfights: Your value in a fight is poison and zoning, not a flashy combo. Pre-seed mushrooms across every approach the fight might funnel through, so the enemy takes damage and reveals itself before the engage even lands. Once it starts, stand at the back of your line, pour Toxic Shot into whatever is closest, and save Blinding Dart for their strongest auto-attack carry at the worst possible moment for them. You are not diving anyone and not tanking anything: you are the chip that softens their team, the blind that turns off their marksman, and the traps that make their flank routes dangerous. Stay behind peel, keep your distance, and let the poison and the field do the killing you are too fragile to do in person.

gamePlan.overview:
Teemo's attacks deal immediate bonus magic damage and apply a four-second poison. Move Quick passively grants speed after five seconds without champion or turret damage; activating it dashes and doubles that bonus for three seconds without letting damage remove it. Guerrilla Warfare grants camouflage indefinitely while Teemo is idle or in brush, and breaking camouflage grants three seconds of attack speed.

His lane plan is simple. Melee champions walk up to farm, take poisoned darts, and lose the trade because his blind makes their attacks miss. Against the right opponents, that blind removes an entire trade's worth of damage on a short cooldown.

Everything outside the poke game is a weakness. He is tiny, squishy, and dies to one gap-closer, and in teamfights he sits at max range hoping nobody looks at him. Teemo wins by making the map dangerous and the lane miserable, not by fighting fair.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Pressure last-hits without pushing so far that one gank ends the lane. Use Toxic Shot attacks when the opponent is occupied with a minion, then leave their retaliation range before the poison finishes ticking. Save Blinding Dart for an attack-reliant champion's commit rather than spending it on harmless poke. Guerrilla Warfare in brush can create an ambush, and Move Quick can reposition Teemo without breaking camouflage during its allowed duration. From level 5, place mushrooms on the river approach and the lane route a gank must cross, giving each one time to arm.
gamePlan.midGame: Your power is denial and tempo rather than a direct engage. Push the Baron lane only as far as your vision allows, then place mushrooms on the entrances to Herald, the enemy's likely flank, and your own retreat. Herald is usually the better first conversion when the map is even, and Teemo helps by making the nearby paths costly to contest. Do not spend every charge in one obvious line, since sweepers can erase the whole setup. Keep enough mushrooms to rebuild control around the next objective.
gamePlan.lateGame: Choose the side lane only when your trap network and map information make the push survivable. Before Baron or a late dragon, seed several different approaches and keep one charge for the fight itself. A mushroom in the enemy's retreat or under a diver can matter more than another trap stacked in a swept choke. Poke from the edge of vision, preserve Move Quick for repositioning, and join your team before the objective is already being contested.
gamePlan.teamfights: Begin with the ground already prepared. Bounce or place mushrooms where an engage, retreat, or flank will cross them, then attack from behind the champion who can absorb the response. Spend Blinding Dart on the most dangerous attack-reliant threat when they commit, not on the first target in range. If a diver reaches you, kite through a trap and use Move Quick after incoming damage stops suppressing its passive speed. Teemo wins the fight by stretching it across hostile ground, not by standing still for a damage race.

Featherstorm makes Xayah untargetable and leaves feathers behind, but it does not root by itself. Bladecaller roots only when at least three recalled feathers hit, so track the feather line after landing and preserve a reset or Buster Shot to escape it.

gamePlan.overview:
Rocket Jump moves Tristana to a target location, then damages and briefly slows nearby enemies on landing. It resets from champion takedowns and from detonating a maximum-stack Explosive Charge on a champion. Explosive Charge lasts four seconds; attacks and ability hits against its target add up to four damage stacks, and the fourth stack detonates it immediately.

The safe aggressive sequence is to place Explosive Charge, land Rocket Jump on or near its target for one stack, activate Rapid Fire, and attack until the fourth stack detonates and refreshes W. Buster Shot also counts as an ability hit for the charge and knocks the target plus nearby enemies back, allowing an emergency detonation or peel setup.

The catch: the jump has a real cooldown, and a Tristana who leaps in without it up is a squishy melee champion in the worst spot on the map. She wins by picking the jump that snowballs, never the one that strands her.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Explosive Charge's passive makes attacks against killed units explode around them, so last-hit carefully when you want to preserve a freeze. For an all-in, cast E before W when possible, land the jump's area damage to add a stack, then use Rapid Fire to reach four stacks. The maximum-stack detonation refreshes W even if the champion survives, giving Tristana a planned exit rather than requiring a kill first.
gamePlan.midGame: Items plus passive range make attacking safer. Place E before jumping so W's landing damage contributes a charge stack, and use Buster Shot as another stack only when its knockback will not move the target out of attack range. A four-stack champion detonation refreshes Rocket Jump immediately; a takedown provides another reset, allowing one jump out after the charge and another after the kill.
gamePlan.lateGame: Your range has caught up and your jump still resets, so you are a backline carry who can also leap onto theirs. Deal damage from max range behind your frontline, hold the jump as your escape from divers, and spend the knockback to peel or to knock a key target out of position. The reset means a clean teamfight entry can chain into more kills, but the rule is the same as level one: never jump without a way back out.
gamePlan.teamfights: You have two modes, and the fight picks one. If you are the backline carry, stand at max range, bomb the cluster, and hold the jump purely as your anti-dive escape. If the enemy carry is reachable and low, the jump-bomb-reset chain is the most explosive cleanup in the lane. The knockback ultimate is your peel button and your disengage: kick a diver off your support, or use it to get yourself out of a collapse. Jump into snowballs, never into stacked crowd control.

goodAgainst.note: You can pressure him from outside his preferred melee trade, and your legs win those exchanges, but respect Apprehend and the outer edge of Decimate. His only way in is forcing the gap, and the flip answers exactly that.

Counter Strike dodges Purge shots and the basic attacks that trigger Echoing Flames, so Urgot loses both W and shotgun damage during its window. Use Corrosive Charge to slow Jax, avoid the stun, then activate Purge after Counter Strike ends.
Both his forms have to enter shotgun range, and the spirit's snapback walks him through your legs twice, so his health bar rarely lets him farm, let alone scale.

Wind Wall blocks Purge's ranged projectiles and Fear Beyond Death's drill, though Echoing Flames' cone is not a projectile. Reposition around the wall before casting R; the execute becomes available below 25% health, not below half.
Her dashes deliver her into the one place she should never be: the flip catches the engage, the machine gun shreds the landing, and the execute erases what her sustain saved.

weakAgainst.note: He simply regenerates everything you deal, his health pool sits far above your execute threshold, and his cleavers tax your slow frame all lane. Even anti-heal only slows the stalemate.
She farms outside your range and scales past your relevance, so if she reaches her ranged form healthy, everything you won in lane stops mattering.

Blinding Dart makes Purge miss, and Noxious Traps slow the straight path Urgot needs for Disdain, so Teemo can deny both the sustained damage and the engage. Clear mushrooms before advancing, use Corrosive Charge to slow and mark him, and wait for the blind to expire before activating Purge or committing Disdain.

Decisive Strike's silence interrupts Urgot's ability rhythm, and Garen's regeneration repairs short trades. Fear Beyond Death has a true 25%-health execute threshold; Demacian Justice instead deals point-and-click true damage that scales with missing health, so do not treat the two finishers as the same mechanic.

gamePlan.overview:
Urgot's six legs each hold a shotgun with its own directional arc and cooldown. A basic attack made inside a ready leg's arc fires that shotgun for area physical damage including a percentage of the target's maximum health. Circle around a target to reach fresh legs instead of standing on one side and waiting for the same shotgun to recharge.

Abilities mark one enemy champion at a time. Purge fires up to 13 attacks over four seconds at fixed 3.0 attack speed, prioritizes that marked champion, and can be toggled indefinitely at maximum rank. Its attacks apply on-hit effects at 70% effectiveness and cannot critically strike. Disdain grants its shield before the dash and can activate Purge during the movement, then flips the first champion hit behind Urgot.

What he lacks is speed. He is slow, short-ranged for a shooter, and mana-hungry early, so kiting champions and ranged poke shut his pattern down. Urgot wins by controlling the space he stands in, because nobody wins inside it.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Keep the wave on a side that lets you circle through shotgun legs without stepping into a gank. Slow and mark with Corrosive Charge, use Purge while moving around the target, and disengage after the nearby legs are spent rather than continuing a weak trade. Cast Purge during Disdain's dash when committing so the flipped champion is already marked and prioritized on landing. At level 5, Fear Beyond Death leashes for four seconds and can execute only after the target falls below 25% health, so land it early enough to create pressure without assuming the threshold is already met.
gamePlan.midGame: Your first item and execute threat make narrow river fights much easier to control. Crash the wave before Herald, arrive with several shotgun legs ready, and stand where the enemy must cross your Purge range to contest. Look for a Disdain flip on a reachable target, then cast Fear Beyond Death before they retreat beyond the leash. If your team chooses dragon instead, rotate only after fixing the Baron wave and avoid arriving through an unwarded route, since Urgot has no fast escape from a collapse.
gamePlan.lateGame: Position before Baron or Elder begins, because Urgot cannot quickly change sides of a fight. Cycle shotgun legs through the closest safe target, use Disdain to interrupt a diver or punish someone entering your zone, and fire Fear Beyond Death at a champion your team can push below the threshold. A tank can be the correct execute if the resulting fear reaches several carries. Avoid long chases after Purge locks onto a marked target, and keep the fight inside the area your legs can cover.
gamePlan.teamfights: Stand in front of your carries without walking beyond their damage. Circle through ready shotgun arcs, mark the focus target for Purge, and save Disdain to shield and flip a diver or exposed carry. Hit Fear Beyond Death before or as a useful target approaches 25% health. Once eligible, Mercy suppresses and makes the target untargetable during the pull, and a successful execution fears nearby enemies. Reposition toward the enemy backline before the execute completes when that fear can decide the fight.

goodAgainst.note: She out-ranges your early poke and controls the first part of the lane, but you out-scale her hard, and eventually one cage into your full combo one-shots her.
Her all-in is a dash into your face, which is exactly what Event Horizon punishes. The shroud hides her, but your cage and Dark Matter hit the ground she is standing on.
He wins the early trades, but every kill attempt forces a dash straight into Event Horizon, and his windwall blocks Baleful Strike, not the cage on the ground.
Ahri relies on dashes to engage, so her commit walks straight into your cage, and once she is stunned her thin frame cannot survive your burst.

weakAgainst.note: Zed's shadows let him bait out your cage, dodge it, and reach you the moment it is down, and you are exactly the escape-less squishy his kit deletes.
Her blink jumps her out of your cage radius and her resets snowball off any kill, so once she gets ahead your one stun is not enough to stop her.
Norra out-ranges Baleful Strike with a bounce that hits from angles your cage cannot punish, and her dog drags you out of position while she pokes from outside the stun ring.
His pool dodges your cage, Dark Matter, and even the point-and-click ultimate all at once, and he out-sustains your poke while scaling right alongside you.

Baleful Strike's 9 range now lets Veigar answer Ziggs from farther away, but Ziggs still shoves faster and pressures the wave without entering cage range. Preserve health while farming stacks, and do not rely on Event Horizon alone because Satchel Charge can carry him out of the ring.

gamePlan.overview:
Veigar gains one permanent ability power for each enemy champion hit by an ability and each minion or monster killed with an ability, plus seven stacks per champion takedown. Merely placing a cage or clearing a wave with attacks does not generate stacks.

Baleful Strike now has 9 range and damages only the first two enemies hit, making long poke and aligned double last-hits much safer. Dark Matter lands after 1.2 seconds, and its cooldown becomes shorter as Phenomenal Evil grows. Primordial Burst deals up to 100% increased damage based on missing health but has no fixed execute threshold, so use it after Q and W rather than assuming a marked health line guarantees the kill.

His problem is movement. Veigar has no dash, no blink, and no escape beyond the cage itself. If the enemy baits out the stun or dodges it, a gap-closer runs him down with nothing to stop them. He has to survive the early game, when he is at his weakest, to reach the point where his numbers take over.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Farm and stack, in that order. Every minion you kill with Q adds to your passive, so last-hit with the spell whenever the enemy cannot punish you for it. Hold Event Horizon as a defensive tool early instead of poking with it; throwing it away for chip damage leaves you with nothing when the jungler shows up. Keep the wave near the middle of the lane so you are never pinned under your tower with the cage down. Watch both side bushes for ganks, since you are one of the easiest mids to gank. This phase is about surviving until your numbers take over.
gamePlan.midGame: This is where the cage starts producing kills. Once your first item is done and you have some stacks, a clean Event Horizon into your full combo deletes most squishies, so look for those windows instead of farming passively. Shove the wave with Q, then walk to river or a side lane and threaten a pick: nobody wants to path near a Veigar holding a stun, and one cage on a roaming enemy hands your team scuttle, dragon, or Herald. Use your priority to set up objectives rather than chasing kills, because your roam is slow and a missed cage leaves you stranded in the open. Ward the river and play for the moments your stun creates a numbers advantage.
gamePlan.lateGame: Now you are the biggest single-target threat on the map and the enemy has to plan around you. With full stacks and a couple of items you one-shot any carry you can stun, and your ultimate finishes anyone who left a fight low. Stay behind your frontline and keep the cage ready for the first diver who commits. Your damage no longer needs a long setup: stun plus combo kills a squishy outright. Do not sit in side lanes; you scale to win grouped fights, not to split push, so be where the next objective is contested. The key skill late is patience, saving the stun for the target that matters instead of the first body that walks past.
gamePlan.teamfights: Your job is to land one cage and delete one carry. Sit at the very back, let your frontline take the engage, and watch for the moment the enemy backline steps where Event Horizon can catch them, or a diver jumps at you and the ring stuns them. The cage is both your engage and your only peel, so every fight you choose between offense and self-defense; guess wrong and you are standing still while an assassin kills you. When the stun lands, dump your combo on the most valuable squishy and finish stragglers with your ultimate, which hits harder the lower they are. Your whole value is one full combo, so make sure it lands on the right person.

goodAgainst.note: Sona is extremely squishy with no escape, so one landed cage deletes her before her heal goes off. Your poke also out-ranges her early auras.
Lulu's shields blunt your poke but cannot answer a cage that pins her in place, and once her polymorph is used she is just a squishy enchanter with no escape.
Braum's whole lane is a slow walk toward your carry, and slow walk-ups are exactly what the cage punishes. His shield also cannot block Dark Matter, so your poke lands anyway.

Phantom Undertow can cross Event Horizon's edge and be knocked down, but Ghostwater Dive's camouflage and movement speed do not automatically collide with a wall unless Pyke leaves through it. Hold Primordial Burst until he is low for higher damage; it is not an execute that overrides Death from Below.

weakAgainst.note: His hook out-ranges your cage and pulls one of the slowest supports in the game out of position before the ring is even up. One grab on you usually ends the trade and sometimes the lane.

Thresh's hook out-ranges your cage, his flay interrupts every step forward, and his lantern turns a won skirmish into a two-versus-three before you can react. He dictates the lane until you out-scale him.
All your damage is magic and he stacks magic resist against it, so your burst falls short, his taunt catches you the moment the cage is down, and his bulk wins the fights he starts.
Karma's poke beats your stacking pattern: her empowered flame chips you off every Q you step up for, her speed boosts walk the duo out of your cage, and her tether roots your immobile frame.

Black Shield can deny the edge stun and the burst setup your pick game depends on, though the cage still restricts movement and creates value for your allies. Her binding also punishes a stacking mage who has to stand still to farm.

gamePlan.overview:
Support Veigar gains one Phenomenal Evil stack for each enemy champion hit by an ability and seven for a champion takedown, so he can scale without taking his carry's minions. Ability last-hits also grant one stack but should respect lane farm ownership. Baleful Strike now reaches 9 range and hits the first two enemies, while Dark Matter's cooldown falls as his passive stack total grows.

In the Dragon lane he plays for zone control. You poke the enemy duo off the wave and threaten the cage every time they step toward you. He has no shield or heal, so his protection is the cage itself: a well-placed ring stops a diver outright. The catch is that everything lives on cooldowns you do not get back if you miss.

His weakness is the usual immobile mage problem, made worse. Veigar is slow, squishy, and has zero mobility, which makes him the perfect target for every hook and dash in the support pool. Miss the cage and you are a stationary mage with a great late game and no way to reach it.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Use Dark Matter when the enemy commits to a last-hit or is already controlled, then add Baleful Strike without walking past your carry. Holding Event Horizon can deny an engage even before it is cast. Spend the cage when the enemy support commits, your jungler arrives, or a gank must be stopped. While it is unavailable, stay behind the wave and avoid contesting lane brush without vision.
gamePlan.midGame: Mid game your damage starts to matter, but Event Horizon remains the reason your team controls space. Set up vision before the six-minute objectives and cage the entrance your team already owns rather than walking alone into the pit. Herald is usually the stronger even trade, while dragon is the better commitment when your composition wants repeated grouped fights toward soul. Roam to mid after the Dragon lane wave is secured, and approach with your jungler so a cage from fog becomes a pick instead of a face-check. Keep enough vision around your carry's next route to stop hooks and dashes from finding either of you first.
gamePlan.lateGame: By now you are a control mage who happens to be the support, and your job splits in two. On defense, the cage is the best peel on your team: ring your carry and any diver who jumps in gets stunned the second they cross the edge. On offense, your nuke from the backline deletes whoever you catch, and a stunned target rarely survives the follow-up. Stand behind your frontline, never in front of it, because your damage is huge and your survivability is tiny. Hold the cage for the engage you have to answer instead of throwing it at the first body you see.
gamePlan.teamfights: Event Horizon erects after 0.5 seconds and lasts three seconds. It stuns and knocks down only enemies that collide with an edge, and each enemy can be affected once per cast; targets standing safely inside are trapped but not automatically stunned. Use that control to land Dark Matter's 1.2-second delay, then cast Primordial Burst after other damage so its missing-health scaling is higher.

Spell Shield blocks one spell, not the true damage your Silver Bolts keep stacking onto her, and her short range cannot kite you once you commit to a long fight.

Kalista's hops reposition after attacks but do not make targeted basic attacks miss. Keep Silver Bolts on Kalista rather than switching targets, use Tumble to maintain range, and respect Rend's burst before the third stack lands.

weakAgainst.note: Caitlyn's basic-attack range and Piltover Peacemaker punish Vayne before she can apply Silver Bolts, while Yordle Snap Traps narrow her Tumble angles around the wave. Draven's axes hit harder than anything you have early, and his all-in kills your fragile frame for free. He falls behind once laning ends and your scaling takes over.
Her jump and reset burst beat your fragile early frame before your stacks matter. Once your items arrive, you out-space and out-duel her.

gamePlan.overview:
Silver Bolts stacks from attacks and Condemn, lasts 3.5 seconds, and triggers percentage maximum-health true damage on the third stack. Attacking a different enemy clears the previous target's stacks, so target discipline matters. Activating W grants five seconds of attack speed and 10% omnivamp, creating a defined dueling window rather than only a passive third-hit effect.

Tumble is a fixed-distance dash that cannot cross terrain, resets the attack timer, and empowers the next attack within four seconds. Condemn adds a Silver Bolts stack and knocks the target back; only terrain collision adds bonus damage and a 1.5-second stun. Night Hunter grants movement speed only while Vayne faces a nearby visible enemy champion.

Past that point the game flips. A few items and her ultimate turn her into a tank-melting duelist who out-spaces almost anyone. Vayne games are a race to her item spikes, and both teams know it.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Protect your health while farming at the edge of Vayne's short range. Use Tumble to dodge the spell that starts the enemy trade, then take a second attack only when it does not pull you into the support's control. Save Condemn for a wall stun, diver, or gank rather than spending it as poke. Against bullies, give up a minion before losing enough health to be forced out of lane. Against a weaker short-range duo, Silver Bolts can still reward a three-hit trade when your support controls the return damage.
gamePlan.midGame: Once items arrive, activate Silver Bolts before an extended fight and keep farming until the map gives a safe objective rotation. At six minutes, follow lane priority rather than crossing an unwarded river to contest by habit. Herald is usually the stronger even trade, while dragon is worth committing to when your composition can protect Vayne through repeated fights toward soul. Final Hour adds attack damage, raises Night Hunter's chase speed to 70, and makes each Tumble grant one second of invisibility that ends on attacking or casting. Use that brief stealth to change direction, then look for takedowns that extend the ultimate by four seconds up to its original duration.
gamePlan.lateGame: Three items and Final Hour make Vayne a strong front-to-back carry, but short range still decides which targets are safe. Stay behind your frontline, attack the closest threat, and use Tumble's invisibility to break targeting or change angle instead of rolling deeper by habit. Silver Bolts handles high-health targets without requiring you to cross the frontline. Hold Condemn for the diver or wall stun that preserves your attack uptime, and arrive early enough to Baron or Elder that you are not forced to walk through fog.
gamePlan.teamfights: Stand behind your peel and attack the closest target, since Silver Bolts makes a tank productive damage rather than an obstacle to bypass. Tumble between attacks only when the new position preserves spacing, and use Final Hour's brief invisibility to break targeting before revealing with the next shot. Hold Condemn for the diver who reaches you or a reliable wall stun on a priority target. Do not chase through the enemy formation. Vayne wins the fight by maintaining safe attack uptime while each threat enters her range.

goodAgainst.note: Tumble stays outside Apprehend, Condemn cancels Darius's straight-line approach, and Silver Bolts punish the health he adds for extended fights. Garen's regen erases your early poke, but your bolts scale off his max health and skip his armor entirely, and he has no answer to kiting, which is your whole game.
Mundo's entire champion is a health bar, and your entire champion punishes health bars. Your percent damage out-scales his sustain; the lane phase is the only hard part.

Ornn's armor and maximum-health purchases cannot reduce Silver Bolts' true damage, but Bellows Breath's percentage damage, Brittle control, and Call of the Forge God still threaten Vayne. Wild Rift Ornn does not grant forged item upgrades; he grants allies remote-purchase opportunities at level thresholds.
Volibear has to reach you to do anything, and reaching a Vayne is the hard part. Past the early dive levels, he is just another big health bar for your bolts to shred.

weakAgainst.note: Teemo's blind shuts off your bolts and the poke war is genuinely his, so the lane is uncomfortable even though your late game still wins it.

Malphite's attack speed slow drags down your damage and his poke chips you from behind a free shield, with his level five ultimate a permanent threat. Your true damage still beats his armor eventually.

Accelerated Shock Blast outranges Vayne's early attacks, and Thundering Blow removes her after Tumble tries to enter Silver Bolts range. Farm behind the wave, use Tumble to dodge the empowered projectile rather than to approach, and wait for items before forcing the duel that Jayce's earlier form-switch rotation controls.

gamePlan.overview:
Silver Bolts stacks from attacks and Condemn, lasts 3.5 seconds, and triggers percentage maximum-health true damage on the third stack. Attacking a different enemy clears the previous target's stacks. Activating W grants attack speed and 10% omnivamp for five seconds, so commit that window only when Vayne can stay on the same target.

Tumble resets the attack timer and empowers the next attack but cannot cross terrain. Condemn itself adds a Silver Bolts stack and always knocks back; terrain collision adds the bonus damage and stun. Night Hunter grants movement speed while Vayne faces a nearby visible champion, helping her chase but not flee in the opposite direction.

Once her items arrive, the game flips. Final Hour turns her tumbles into stealth and her duels into executions, and the juggernauts who bullied her at level three start walking to lane in pairs. Every Vayne game is about reaching that point, and the enemy knows it.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Treat health and wave position as the early priorities. Farm at maximum range, use Tumble to dodge the spell that starts the opponent's trade, and save Condemn for a wall stun or disengage. Against melee champions with key cooldowns down, one attack, Tumble attack, and retreat can build a useful health lead without turning into an all-in. Give up a minion when taking it would expose you to a full combo, and keep the wave close enough that the enemy jungler cannot punish your short range and limited escape.
gamePlan.midGame: Items and Final Hour give you real side-lane pressure, but the map still decides whether a duel is safe. Push only when the enemy locations are known, then rotate toward Herald or a tower before several champions can collapse. The ultimate adds attack damage, raises Night Hunter's chase speed to 70, and gives one second of invisibility after each Tumble until Vayne attacks or casts. Use that invisibility to break targeting and change direction, not only to chase. Takedowns extend Final Hour by four seconds up to its original duration, enabling chained fights but not unlimited duration.
gamePlan.lateGame: Late game, you can pressure a side lane or shred the frontline in a grouped fight. Choose the side lane when vision shows a single defender and your team is not about to contest Baron or Elder. Otherwise group, attack the closest safe target, and let Silver Bolts handle tanks without stepping through them toward a carry. Hold Condemn for the diver or wall angle that protects your uptime, and use Final Hour's invisible Tumbles to reposition unpredictably. Your scaling is strong, but crowd control and short range still punish careless entries.
gamePlan.teamfights: Stay behind your frontline and attack the closest target you can reach without Tumble moving you into enemy control. Final Hour's invisible Tumbles break targeting, but attacking or casting reveals you, so use the brief pause to change your angle before the next shot. Save Condemn for the assassin or bruiser who reaches you, unless a reliable wall stun on a priority target ends the fight immediately. Do not chase through the enemy formation. Vayne wins by keeping her damage active while each threat is forced to cross her range.

goodAgainst.note: Jinx is immobile with no escape, and her chompers cannot cover the flank your stealth opens, so you pick her off before her reset snowball ever starts.
Vayne has to fight at short range, and your poison plus your ambush punish every step she takes to get there. Your spray also reaches the backline she tumbles into.
Sivir's wave-clear and tempo do nothing against a flank she never sees, and her Spell Shield blocks a single cask, not poison that is already ticking.

weakAgainst.note: Lucian bursts your fragile early frame long before your stacks come online, and his dash rotation out-trades the one ambush you get. Caught out, you simply die.

Featherstorm makes Xayah untargetable and leaves feathers, but it does not root by itself. Bladecaller roots only if at least three recalled feathers hit, so reposition after opening and avoid standing on the line between Xayah and her feather field.
Caitlyn out-ranges you all lane, her headshots punish your last-hits, and her traps cover the brush you want to ambush from. You have no answer to her range before your items.

gamePlan.overview:
Twitch's attacks apply up to five Deadly Venom stacks, each dealing true damage over five seconds. At maximum stacks on a champion, Twitch gains bonus attack speed. Contaminate can then damage every poisoned enemy whether visible or not, with additional physical damage for each stack, so hold E until stacks are high or a target is about to leave range.

Ambush enters camouflage after a one-second delay. Attacking or casting Venom Cask or Contaminate breaks it; after revealing, attacks apply an extra poison stack for three seconds. Spray and Pray can be prepared without being one of those listed stealth-breaking casts, then the first attack reveals Twitch with bonus range already active. If a poisoned champion dies, Ambush's cooldown resets, creating the escape or second reposition after a kill.

The costs are plain: Twitch is weak and gankable early, fragile, and has no dash after camouflage breaks. He needs an ambush angle that preserves distance from enemy control, because opening beside a diver leaves little room to kite.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Keep the wave near safety until you know where the enemy jungler is. Twitch's short range makes direct trading difficult, so attack when the enemy carry is occupied with a last-hit, add Venom Cask where they must retreat, and cast Contaminate before the stacks expire. Ambush can create a new angle after the enemy loses vision, but its delay makes it unreliable as a last-second escape. Do not abandon a large wave for an early roam unless the target is exposed and your support can protect the lane.
gamePlan.midGame: Use Ambush after pushing a wave to threaten mid, river, or the objective approach from fog. Spray and Pray grants attack damage and 225 attack range for six seconds, and its bolts pierce every unit in a line, but their attack damage falls as they pass through more enemies. Choose an angle that places the priority target early in the line, then use the multi-target poison for a grouped Contaminate. If no ambush appears, remain with your frontline and keep farming rather than circling in stealth while waves die.
gamePlan.lateGame: Late game, decide whether the fight needs a flank or safe front-to-back damage. A flank can line several carries up for Spray and Pray, but only when vision is swept and enemy control cannot catch Twitch as he reveals. Otherwise stay behind your frontline and let the extra range reach through it. Place Venom Cask where its slow keeps the first target in the firing line, secure a takedown on a poisoned champion, and survive Ambush's one-second delay before relying on the reset camouflage.
gamePlan.teamfights: Approach under Ambush only from a route your team has cleared. Line the first bolts through the highest-priority targets because later pierced enemies take reduced attack damage, and build five poison stacks where possible for the passive attack-speed bonus. Cast Contaminate before wounded targets leave range, including poisoned enemies that have moved out of vision. Crowd control pauses attacks rather than cancelling Spray and Pray, so cleanse when the remaining firing window is worth it and use a valid Ambush reset to reposition instead of chasing through the enemy team.

goodAgainst.note: She heals everything except being pulled out of position, and a landed hook drags the team's whole sustain source into your duo before she can cast anything.

You win the hook mirror on utility: his approach is slow and telegraphed, your Flay interrupts his combo, and your lantern undoes whatever he hooks while he has no rescue of his own.

Death Sentence gives Thresh a competing hook, Flay can interrupt Blitzcrank's Overdrive approach, and Dark Passage extracts the ally Rocket Grab catches. Stand near enough to lantern the target but do not body the grab accidentally, then punish Blitzcrank during its cooldown with the Flay into hook sequence.
Her whole defense is one Whimsy while your kit brings three separate threats, so the hook, flay, and box each demand an answer and polymorph cancels only one.

weakAgainst.note: Black Shield's crowd-control immunity prevents Death Sentence's stun and tugs while the shield holds; do not recast expecting to dash to a successfully shielded target. Break or bait the shield first, while respecting Dark Binding's range during the hook wind-up.

Pulling him drags a taunt into your own backline, his magic resist blunts your chip damage, and his counter-engage taunt flips every pick you start into a fight his team wanted.

gamePlan.overview:
Death Sentence stuns and reveals the first enemy hit for 1.5 seconds, tugs them twice toward Thresh, and reduces its current cooldown by two seconds. Recasting stops the tugs and dashes Thresh to the shackled enemy; he can cast Dark Passage and Flay during that dash, enabling hook-then-lantern delivery for an ally or a mid-flight Flay setup.

Dark Passage grants sight and shields Thresh plus the first ally who approaches it. That ally must use the Minion button to dash to Thresh and cannot take the lantern while immobilized, grounded, or silenced, so throw it before crowd control lands. Souls near Thresh or the lantern are collected automatically and grant two ability power and two armor each; unlike most champions, Thresh gains no armor per level.

The weakness is the same as every playmaker who lives on a skillshot. Everything he threatens flows through that first chain, so a missed hook leaves him with no engage and no kill pressure, and disengage or a spell shield can undo even a clean one before your team converts it.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Hold Death Sentence for a clear opening, such as the enemy support stepping away from the carry or a target leaving minion cover. Before recasting, check that your marksman can follow and that the landing point is not inside the enemy wave or jungle path. Use Flay to interrupt the return engage or control the target after the hook. Ward the river and lane brush before holding an aggressive angle, since Thresh has no reliable exit after spending Dark Passage.
gamePlan.midGame: Leave lane after your duo crashes or your carry recalls, then move with the jungler and use Dark Passage to extend a planned gank. Before dragon or Herald, clear vision and threaten Death Sentence from the side of the entrance rather than standing in the pit. Keep Dark Passage available when your carry must cross an unsafe route. If the hook target is a tank with allies behind them, stay at range and use Flay for peel instead of taking the recast automatically.
gamePlan.lateGame: Before Baron or Elder, move with teammates to establish vision and threaten Death Sentence from fog. Keep Dark Passage available when your carry must step forward or a teammate is entering a risky angle. If the enemy has several divers, stand close enough to Flay the first dash and place the lantern behind your carry's retreat path. Do not recast a hook into the frontline unless the position is safe and your team benefits from the entry.
gamePlan.teamfights: Decide before the fight starts whether to engage or peel. The Box creates five walls for four seconds: the first wall an enemy champion breaks deals damage and slows by 99% for two seconds, while later walls deal no damage and slow for only one second. A dash can still cross and break a wall unless another effect interrupts it, so use Flay to stop or redirect the dash rather than attributing that job to The Box itself. Throw Dark Passage before an ally is immobilized, grounded, or silenced so they can still use the Minion button to escape.
