goodAgainst.note: Tristana has to jump onto you to threaten anything, and landing next to a marksman holding a root is how that ends. Before she has items your sustained damage wins the straight trade.
Neither of you can walk away from a trade, which favours the one whose damage ramps with attack speed. Winning those extended trades denies the farm her scaling needs.
Twitch is no threat early and depends on farm you can contest by winning every trade he takes. His only early danger is the stealth flank, and he only wins if he reaches the late game.

weakAgainst.note: He punishes you from a range you have to walk into to deal damage, and his root lands on a frame that cannot dodge it. Survive to your attack speed items and the fight flips, and your chaining ultimate out-values his single shots when teams group.
Her burst trades faster than you can stack blight, and her strut keeps the spacing you need to close to attack range. She punishes your immobile frame until your items even it out.

Caitlyn's basic-attack range and Yordle Snap Traps control the ground Varus needs to charge Piercing Arrow, while 90 Caliber Net preserves her distance if he approaches. Farm with Arrow from outside Headshot range, avoid channeling beside traps, and save Chain of Corruption for grouped fights where its spread can out-value her single-target siege.

gamePlan.overview:
Varus's attacks add up to three Blight stacks for six seconds, and ability hits consume them for bonus magic damage. Each stack consumed on a champion or epic monster removes 13% of his basic abilities' total cooldowns, up to 39% per target. This creates a repeatable attack-three-times, detonate, then quickly rebuild cycle rather than a single on-hit rotation.

Piercing Arrow can charge for up to four seconds while Varus moves at a 20% slow; range, arrow damage, and detonated Blight damage reach full scaling after 1.5 seconds. Activating Blighted Quiver empowers the next Q within 5.5 seconds with bonus magic damage. A fully charged Q can therefore amplify both W's active damage and three consumed Blight stacks in one shot.

The cost is that he is completely immobile. He has no dash and no escape, and he has to stand inside attack range to deal any of his damage. Everything about playing him is about earning that space and then keeping it.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Trade with attacks followed by an ability detonation. Use Hail of Arrows when the enemy heals: its desecrated area lasts four seconds, slows, and applies 40% Grievous Wounds without requiring an anti-heal item. When preparing a stronger burst, reach three Blight stacks, activate W, charge Q for up to 1.5 seconds, and fire through the target; each prior enemy pierced reduces the arrow's own damage, so protect the direct line.
gamePlan.midGame: Your attack speed items arrive and your damage stops being a trade and becomes a fight. Around dragon, look for the ultimate that chains through a grouped duo, then attack into the root and detonate on whatever is closest. Blight scales with the target's health, so their frontline is a target rather than an obstacle. Stay behind your own frontline, because an immobile carry dies the moment a diver reaches him.
gamePlan.lateGame: You are the sustained damage in every fight. Percent health detonations mean you can attack into a full tank and still deal real damage, so the job is to keep attacking something for the whole fight rather than waiting on one big shot. Hold the ultimate for the angle where the root chains through their group, and position like the fragile immobile carry you are: behind everything, flanked by nothing.
gamePlan.teamfights: Chain of Corruption roots its first champion for two seconds and adds maximum Blight stacks over that duration. Nearby champions have two seconds to leave before the tendril infects them and repeats the effect. Time Q or E after all three ultimate-applied stacks arrive, then use the resulting 39% basic-cooldown refund to begin the next detonation cycle. Spread pressure with Runaan's attacks, but keep a safe line because Varus has no mobility.

startingItem.name: Long Sword
startingItem.note: Simple early attack damage. His Fury converts into crit chance, so raw damage and crit scale together.

boots.name: Gunmetal Greaves
boots.note: Attack speed builds Fury faster, and Fury is crit chance, so it feeds his damage and his heal.

coreItems.name: Blade of the Ruined King
coreItems.note: Percent current health damage on every attack, which is what lets a pure duelist kill a frontline.

coreItems.name: Magnetic Blaster
coreItems.note: Extra range on a melee duelist, which closes some of the gap kiting normally opens.

coreItems.name: Lord Dominik's Regard
coreItems.note: Build this against armor stackers, since he has no true damage to fall back on. Choose it over Mortal Reminder when enemies are stacking health rather than healing, since Giant Slayer increases Tryndamere's damage against high-health targets.

coreItems.name: Infinity Edge
coreItems.note: His Fury already supplies crit chance, and he can overcap it, so the excess converts into attack damage rather than being wasted.

coreItems.name: Guardian Angel
coreItems.note: Revives him once after dying. His ultimate delays death by five seconds, and this covers what happens after.

situationalItems.name: Mortal Reminder
situationalItems.note: Build this against armor stackers or enemies who out-sustain his spin-and-slash pattern. Choose it over Lord Dominik's Regard when enemy healing is the bigger problem, since Grievous Wounds stops targets from recovering Tryndamere's damage.

situationalItems.name: Serpent's Fang
situationalItems.note: Build this when the enemy has shields that keep a target alive through his crits.

situationalItems.name: Armored Advance
situationalItems.note: Boot swap against heavy physical damage. Reducing basic-attack damage preserves Tryndamere's health before he has to spend Undying Rage, leaving more time to chase afterward.

situationalItems.name: Mercurial Scimitar
situationalItems.note: Build this when crowd control keeps him away. His ultimate stops him dying but not being kited.

keystoneRune.name: Lethal Tempo
keystoneRune.desc: Attacking champions grants attack speed. At maximum stacks, also gain attack range.
keystoneRune.note: Ramping attack speed builds Fury faster, and Fury is crit chance, so every stack feeds his damage and healing.

primaryRunes.name: Brutal
primaryRunes.desc: Attacks deal bonus adaptive damage to enemy champions.
primaryRunes.note: Bonus damage on every autoattack, which sharpens the levels where his duelling should take over a lane.

primaryRunes.name: Last Stand
primaryRunes.desc: Deal more damage to champions while you are low on health.
primaryRunes.note: His ultimate keeps him alive at a sliver by design, so he spends the decisive seconds in this range.

primaryRunes.name: Legend: Alacrity
primaryRunes.desc: Gain permanent attack speed by taking down champions, monsters, and minions.
primaryRunes.note: Attack speed compounds with a passive that converts every hit into Fury and every point of Fury into crit.

secondaryRunes.name: Second Wind
secondaryRunes.desc: After taking damage from a champion, regenerate health over time.
secondaryRunes.note: Steady regeneration for a melee duelist who walks through poke to reach anyone.

goodAgainst.note: Kayle's early melee form cannot fight a champion who runs her down and refuses to die, and every early kill sets her late-game form further back, usually too far to recover.
Mordekaiser's death realm forces a 1v1, and the 1v1 belongs to the champion who cannot die while his ultimate runs. Your sustain and crits beat his shield and burn.
Riven needs her burst combo to kill you before you ramp, and your ultimate makes that impossible. Once you survive her damage, you out-sustain and out-crit her.
Urgot wants a long grinding trade, but his execute cannot kill you while Undying Rage runs, and he is too immobile to escape once your crits ramp.

weakAgainst.note: Malphite's kit counters yours completely: armor against your crits, an attack speed slow on your whole damage plan, and poke that your sustain keeps paying for.
Sion has more health than your crits can burn through, his charged Q knocks you out of your spin, and the zombie passive keeps swinging after your undying window expires.
Jax's Counterstrike dodges the crit autos your whole champion is built on, and he out-scales the extended duel, so your undying window only delays the loss.
Wukong's clone tricks you into spending your spin and ultimate on a decoy, then the real one bursts you with everything down. His knockup also interrupts your engage.

gamePlan.overview:
Undying Rage can be cast even while Tryndamere is under cast-inhibiting crowd control. It immediately grants Fury and prevents his health from falling below a minimum threshold for five seconds; it does not remove crowd control or make him immune to it, so disables and kiting can consume the entire window.

Fury comes from attacks, critical strikes, and kills. Each point grants critical-strike chance; up to 32; 50% at full Fury based on level; and crit chance above 100% converts one-for-one into bonus attack damage. Bloodlust passively grants attack damage with more at lower health, but activating it consumes all Fury for a Fury-scaled heal, trading immediate sustain for crit chance.

Attacking an enemy champion also grants attack speed based on Undying Rage's rank. Spinning Slash generates Fury for each enemy hit, and critical attacks reduce its current cooldown; twice as much against champions as minions. Bloodlust and Undying Rage can both be cast during the dash, a key escape interaction when damage or crowd control threatens mid-spin.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Build Fury through attacks and kills, then decide whether its crit chance or Bloodlust's heal is more valuable. Bloodlust's passive attack damage increases as health falls even when Q is not activated. In trades, hit the enemy champion to activate Battle Fury's attack speed, use critical attacks to reduce Spinning Slash's cooldown, and preserve enough route to dash away. At level five, remember R can be pressed during a stun or even during E's dash.
gamePlan.midGame: A critical-strike item plus Undying Rage creates real side-lane pressure. Push only as far as your vision and Spinning Slash escape allow, and keep Fury high before challenging the defender. At the first objectives, Herald is usually the stronger even trade and your turret damage helps convert it quickly. If several enemies disappear to answer you, retreat and ping the open objective rather than assuming Undying Rage can survive every collapse. Group when your team lacks time to trade or when a flank can reach the enemy carry.
gamePlan.lateGame: Late game, use the side lane to force a response without abandoning Baron or Elder. Push when the enemy must show a defender, then choose between taking the duel, rotating first, or continuing onto a structure. Undying Rage lets you survive five seconds at minimum health, but it does not prevent control or guarantee the Bloodlust heal afterward. Track Grievous Wounds and the spells that can kite you through the ultimate. When the enemy groups and no structure trade is available, join from a flank instead of leaving your team four-versus-five.
gamePlan.teamfights: Come from a flank after the enemy spends the control that would keep you away from the carry. Mocking Shout reduces nearby enemy attack damage whether they face Tryndamere or not, and slows only targets facing away. Use Spinning Slash to reach the target while preserving a route for the refreshed dash, and let champion critical strikes reduce its cooldown. Cast Undying Rage during crowd control if needed, then disengage or use Bloodlust before the five seconds end when the heal can keep you alive afterward.

startingItem.name: Amplifying Tome
startingItem.note: Early ability power, since his card damage is what makes his roams worth taking.

boots.name: Spellslinger's Shoes
boots.note: Magic penetration sharpens the card and the on-hit damage that follow his gold card stun.

coreItems.name: Dusk and Dawn
coreItems.note: Locking a Gold Card primes Spellblade for the exact attack Twisted Fate uses to start a pick. The extra on-hit repeats Stacked Deck's bonus when it is loaded and Nashor's Tooth's Gnaw, so the two items have especially good synergy on his card attack.

coreItems.name: Nashor's Tooth
coreItems.note: Nashor's attack speed cycles Stacked Deck faster and lets Twisted Fate keep dealing damage after Gold Card lands. Dusk and Dawn repeats Gnaw on the Spellblade card, so the pair adds another ability-power-scaling on-hit to the same pick.

coreItems.name: Rabadon's Deathcap
coreItems.note: Multiplies his ability power, and both his cards and his E scale with it.

coreItems.name: Void Staff
coreItems.note: Cuts the magic resist that lets a stunned target survive the follow-up his gold card sets up. Choose it over Cryptbloom when enemies are stacking magic resist and maximum personal damage matters more than ability haste and team healing.

coreItems.name: Banshee's Veil
coreItems.note: Build this when the enemy has a hook or point-and-click stun, which is how a Twisted Fate dies mid-roam.

situationalItems.name: Oceanid's Trident
situationalItems.note: Build this when the enemy has shields that keep absorbing the burst his gold card set up.

situationalItems.name: Morellonomicon
situationalItems.note: Build this when the enemy heals through his burst. Buy Oblivion Orb early, since the anti-heal works from the component and the full item can wait.

situationalItems.name: Zhonya's Hourglass
situationalItems.note: Build this for when his ultimate drops him into a fight with his cards spent. Buy Seeker's Armguard early for the armor and ability power.

situationalItems.name: Luden's Echo
situationalItems.note: The mana pays for constant wave clearing, and Echo adds damage to the cards he throws before every roam.

situationalItems.name: Magnetic Blaster
situationalItems.note: The energized hit fits a champion whose damage is already an empowered attack, and the range keeps him safe while picking a card.

situationalItems.name: Hextech Rocketbelt
situationalItems.desc: AP engage item with a dash
situationalItems.note: A gap closer after Gate's long-range but finite blink, helping Twisted Fate reach Gold Card attack range without pretending the teleport itself is global.

situationalItems.name: Lich Bane
situationalItems.note: Spellblade triggers on the attack after every card, which is exactly the rhythm his kit forces.

situationalItems.name: Rod of Ages
situationalItems.note: Health and mana for the games where surviving the arrival matters more than the burst that follows.

situationalItems.name: Cryptbloom
situationalItems.note: Choose this when enemies have only moderate magic resist. Compared with Void Staff, Twisted Fate trades some burst for more Gold Card and Destiny uptime plus an area heal after his pick becomes a takedown.

keystoneRune.name: Fleet Footwork
keystoneRune.desc: Moving and attacking builds Energy. At 100 stacks, your next attack heals you and grants movement speed.
keystoneRune.note: Heals him through a lane he farms safely, waiting for a card rather than trading rotations.

primaryRunes.name: Manaflow Band
primaryRunes.desc: Hitting an enemy champion with an ability permanently increases your maximum mana.
primaryRunes.note: He spends mana on Pick a Card and wave clear between roams, and no item in the core build carries mana, so every ability he lands on a champion widens the pool.

primaryRunes.name: Transcendence
primaryRunes.desc: Gain ability haste, then reduce a basic ability's cooldown after it hits at level 9.
primaryRunes.note: Ability haste means more cards and a faster ultimate, which is how often he influences another lane.

primaryRunes.name: Nimbus Cloak
primaryRunes.desc: After casting a summoner spell, gain movement speed and slow resistance.
primaryRunes.note: Move speed after a summoner spell helps him close the last steps after arriving from his ultimate.

secondaryRunes.name: Bone Plating
secondaryRunes.desc: After taking damage from a champion, the next 3 instances of champion damage are reduced.
secondaryRunes.note: He is immobile between gold cards, and this blunts the burst thrown at him while the cards are cycling.

spells.name: Flash
spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

goodAgainst.note: A roam race you win on map presence: Destiny reveals every targetable enemy champion globally, then Gate can move you within its finite cast range while Norra has to rotate on foot.

Destiny reveals Akali even inside Twilight Shroud, denying the invisibility she uses to reposition. Gold Card can then punish a predictable dash arrival, but the shroud itself is not a cooldown-reset mechanic.

Twisted Fate does not dash during ordinary lane trades, so he does not create free Gloom marks. Mistral Bolt and Looming Darkness are telegraphed, but Personal Space is immediate and Shadow Surge is a real dash; win through map pressure while tracking whether Doom is prepared.

Ziggs shoves and pokes from range, while Mega Inferno Bomb can affect fights within its 5,000-unit cast circle. Twisted Fate still roams more directly because Destiny reveals targets globally and Gate can blink him within its own finite range.

weakAgainst.note: He out-trades you with shurikens, then all-ins your squishy frame the moment his ultimate is up, and nothing in your kit stops him from jumping you on cooldown.
Playful Trickster dodges your gold card on reaction, which strips the one tool the matchup depends on, and his burst kills you before you cycle a second card.
Riftwalk answers your whole plan: once it is online he blinks out of your gold card and beats your roams with a shorter-cooldown blink, and he only gets stronger from there.
Black Shield blocks your gold card outright, removing the one tool that locks a target for your burst or your gank, and her bind roots your escapeless frame for trades you cannot walk out of.

gamePlan.overview:
Pick a Card cycles Blue, Red, and Gold for up to 7.2 seconds. Recasting locks the hovered card, resets the attack timer, and empowers the next attack for eight seconds; Blue restores mana, Red deals area damage and slows for three seconds, and Gold stuns. The selection recast can be used while Twisted Fate is under cast-inhibiting crowd control, so locking a needed card is still possible even when he cannot immediately attack.

Stacked Deck passively grants attack speed. Attacks build three stacks, and the next attack consumes them for bonus magic damage; activating E adds more attack speed for three seconds and makes every attack roll Loaded Dice for bonus gold. It does not reduce ability cooldowns. Use its loaded hit together with Pick a Card when possible so one attack delivers the card, Stacked Deck, and item on-hit effects.

The catch is that he is a squishy, slow caster with no escape button. His stun needs him to cycle to the gold card mid-fight, and any assassin or all-in skirmisher who reaches him before it lands runs him over. He scales into decent poke, but his real ceiling is the map, not the duel.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Use Red Card's area hit and Wild Cards to clear, Blue Card to restore mana, and Gold Card for gank setup or defense. Prime three Stacked Deck stacks before locking a card so the empowered attack carries both effects. During safe farm windows, activate E and attack repeatedly because every hit rolls Loaded Dice for extra gold, extending the passive income gained whenever Twisted Fate kills an enemy.
gamePlan.midGame: Shove, lock Gold Card before traveling, then cast Destiny to reveal all targetable enemy champions. After at least 0.5 seconds, recast Gate and channel for 1.5 seconds to blink within its cast range. Only Twisted Fate moves, so select a landing position where allies can follow and enemies cannot immediately interrupt or punish the arrival. The reveal can also expose stealth or verify an objective even when no Gate cast is safe.
gamePlan.lateGame: Push the mid or side wave when Destiny is available and the next Baron or Elder setup leaves time to rejoin. Use Destiny for global information, then choose a Gate landing inside Gold Card range and allied follow-up. The spell moves only Twisted Fate, so do not arrive behind the enemy formation alone. If no safe river pick exists, use the reveal to check flankers or the objective and return to the team for a front-to-back fight.
gamePlan.teamfights: You start the fight and lock down the target; you are not the frontline. The ideal opening is Destiny revealing a flank or an out-of-position carry, then a blink, a gold card, and your team folding onto the target before they react. Once the fight is live, cycle to gold for the most dangerous threat you can reach, fan Wild Cards across their cluster, and let Stacked Deck add up on your autos from the backline. Position like the squishy you are, because the moment a diver reaches you, the stun is the only thing between you and a quick death, and a gold card spent on a tank instead of their assassin wastes the one tool your team was waiting on.

startingItem.name: Spectral Sickle
startingItem.note: Starcall earns support gold from ranged champion poke without taking the carry's minions. Hitting a champion also returns Rejuvenation to heal Soraka and reduces Astral Infusion's remaining cooldown by two seconds.

boots.name: Crimson Lucidity
boots.note: Ability haste, since her value is how often her heal and her zone are available.

coreItems.name: Black Mist Scythe
coreItems.note: Starcall completes the quest from range, and the upgrade's offensive stats strengthen Soraka's poke and self-healing. In the current Wild Rift kit, Rejuvenation stays on Soraka rather than being passed through Astral Infusion.

coreItems.name: Harmonic Echo
coreItems.note: Harmony builds from the moving and casting she does anyway, so the bonus healing lands on top of a heal she was casting regardless.

coreItems.name: Ardent Censer
coreItems.note: Soraka's low-cooldown heal keeps Ardent Censer active on the carry she is sustaining, adding attack speed and on-hit damage throughout the extended fight.

coreItems.name: Staff of Flowing Waters
coreItems.note: Healing an ally gives her ability haste and ability power, which compounds on a champion whose heal scales with both.

coreItems.name: Banshee's Veil
coreItems.note: Build this when the enemy has a hook or point-and-click stun, since she is the squishiest champion on the map.

situationalItems.name: Zhonya's Hourglass
situationalItems.note: Build this for the divers who get through Starcall sustain and Equinox, since she has no dash and can still be burst down before her healing matters. Buy Seeker's Armguard early for the armor and ability power.

situationalItems.name: Mikael's Blessing
situationalItems.note: A cleanse next to her heal, so she can answer the lockdown that would kill the carry she is topping up.

situationalItems.name: Armored Advance
situationalItems.note: Boot swap against heavy physical damage, when surviving the enemy duo matters more than heal frequency.

keystoneRune.name: Aery
keystoneRune.desc: Your attacks and abilities send Aery to a target, dealing damage to enemies or shielding allies.
keystoneRune.note: Aery follows her heal as well as her Q, so it pays out on both halves of what she does.

primaryRunes.name: Font of Life
primaryRunes.desc: Damaging enemy champions heals you and the lowest-health nearby ally after a short cooldown.
primaryRunes.note: Her Q and E can hit enemy champions, healing her and the lowest-Health allied champion nearby when the rune is ready.

primaryRunes.name: Bone Plating
primaryRunes.desc: After taking damage from a champion, the next 3 instances of champion damage are reduced.
primaryRunes.note: She is the primary target of every dive, and this buys her the time to heal through it.

primaryRunes.name: Revitalize
primaryRunes.desc: Healing and shielding are stronger, especially on low-health targets.
primaryRunes.note: Her entire contribution is healing, so a flat increase to it is the most direct upgrade she can take.

secondaryRunes.name: Nimbus Cloak
secondaryRunes.desc: After casting a summoner spell, gain movement speed and slow resistance.
secondaryRunes.note: Move speed after a summoner spell helps the least mobile champion in the game reposition.

spells.name: Flash
spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

goodAgainst.note: He brings poke and a shield but no real kill pressure on you, so the lane turns into a grind your sustain wins while his side runs out of patience and mana.
A disengage mirror that becomes a patience contest: his shields and cleanse blunt your harass, but nothing in his kit can punch through your sustain, and you out-poke him with Starcall.
Nobody out-sustains you in pure attrition. Her disengage saves her from ganks, not from healing that never runs out, so the long game belongs to you.

Black Shield can prevent Equinox's silence and delayed root while it holds, and Dark Binding threatens Soraka's immobile positioning. Place Equinox after the shield is broken or on Morgana before she begins a new cast; silence does not erase projectiles or spells already released.

weakAgainst.note: Leona's targeted stun opens a chain that lands on the immobile healer first, and you cannot heal through a full lockdown combo onto your own face.
His hook drags you out of position and his kit chains crowd control long enough that no amount of healing matters once you are caught.

He is built to make your healing irrelevant: his ultimate executes anyone left under its health threshold, his whole kit hunts squishy backline supports, and a qualifying champion death inside its X grants a recast.
Her engage locks you down hard and arrives whether you are ready or not, so your sustain ends up answering a fight that already ended once she binds you.
A single grab removes you from the fight entirely, and an immobile healer is the easiest hook target in the lane, so one landed hook erases your whole sustain advantage.

You are his prime hook target: immobile, squishy, and worth the whole lane when a hook lands. Flay does not interrupt the instant cast of Astral Infusion, but Thresh's chained crowd control can stop you from reaching or repeatedly healing the ally he catches, while his lantern rescues his own partner.

gamePlan.overview:
Soraka keeps her lane alive through raw healing. Astral Infusion heals an allied champion without spending Soraka's health and converts excess healing into a two-second shield. Every time Soraka heals at least one damaged ally with an ability or Heal, she gains a stack; at three stacks her next Starcall has a larger area and deals 140% damage. Hitting a champion with Starcall slows them, returns Rejuvenation to heal Soraka, and reduces Astral Infusion's remaining cooldown by two seconds.

In the 2v2 she wins by attrition. She has no engage and no burst, so the lane is a slow trade war: poke with Starcall, heal off every bit of harass, and let your ADC farm and trade from a health bar that refuses to drop. Every failed all-in leaves the enemy support out of mana and your carry topped off. Equinox is the one button that makes a dive think twice.

Wish heals Soraka and all allied champions globally, with 150% healing on allies below 35% maximum health. Salvation also grants Soraka 100% bonus movement speed while she runs toward a nearby ally below that threshold. Neither effect is a dash or crowd-control break, so hooks and hard engage still punish her positioning.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Play the long game from the first wave. Heal damaged allies to build three passive stacks, then use the enlarged, 140%-damage Starcall when the enemy steps up. A champion hit gives Soraka Rejuvenation and removes two seconds from Astral Infusion's remaining cooldown, letting Q lead directly into another W. Watch mana rather than health cost; Astral Infusion no longer spends Soraka's health; and hold Equinox for the route a diver must remain in for 1.5 seconds before its delayed root.
gamePlan.midGame: Wish reaches every allied champion, so watch all lanes and wait when possible until endangered allies fall below 35% health for the stronger heal. Do not delay into lethal damage just to chase the threshold. Leave Dragon lane after the wave is safe and move with allies rather than entering river alone. Before objectives, ward from behind the frontline, use healing to charge empowered Starcall, and place Equinox across the choke a diver or enemy jungler must cross.
gamePlan.lateGame: Stand behind your team and away from the flank routes the enemy can use to reach you. Cast Wish when several allies are about to take lethal damage or when its healing changes an important fight elsewhere, not simply when health bars first drop. Keep Equinox for the diver who crosses your frontline, then reposition while the silence interrupts the next cast. Soraka's value depends on surviving long enough to repeat Astral Infusion, so retreat with the carry rather than remaining to deal minor damage.
gamePlan.teamfights: Stay behind the fight and use Astral Infusion on damaged allies to build Starcall stacks. At three, land the larger empowered Q on a champion to deal 140% damage, slow them, heal Soraka through Rejuvenation, and cut two seconds from W's remaining cooldown before healing again. Drop Equinox under a committed diver: the zone silences immediately, but the root happens only when it erupts after 1.5 seconds. Use Wish across all five health bars, prioritizing the below-35% amplification without waiting past a lethal moment.

startingItem.name: Amplifying Tome
startingItem.note: Early ability power, since his lane is landing three separate abilities to trigger his true damage.

boots.name: Spellslinger's Shoes
boots.note: Magic penetration sharpens everything except his passive, which already ignores resistances.

coreItems.name: Blackfire Torch
coreItems.note: His abilities tag several enemies at once, so the stacking bonus counts multiple champions.

coreItems.name: Horizon Focus
coreItems.note: All of his abilities land from long range, so the reveal and amplification trigger on the poke he was already throwing.

coreItems.name: Rabadon's Deathcap
coreItems.note: Multiplies his ability power, and his passive true damage scales with it, so it raises the part magic resist cannot blunt.

coreItems.name: Void Staff
coreItems.note: Cuts the magic resist blunting the two thirds of his damage that is not true damage. Choose it over Cryptbloom when enemies are stacking magic resist and maximum personal damage matters more than ability haste and team healing.

coreItems.name: Zhonya's Hourglass
coreItems.note: Stasis interrupts his beam, so this is not a way to finish the channel safely; it is the button that keeps an immobile artillery mage alive through the dive so he can start the next one. Buy Seeker's Armguard early for the armor and ability power.

situationalItems.name: Morellonomicon
situationalItems.note: Build this when the enemy heals through his poke. Buy Oblivion Orb early, since the anti-heal works from the component and the full item can wait.

situationalItems.name: Oceanid's Trident
situationalItems.note: Build this when the enemy has shields that keep absorbing the poke his passive needs to land.

situationalItems.name: Banshee's Veil
situationalItems.note: Build this when the enemy has a hook or point-and-click stun, since he has no mobility and a channelled ultimate.

situationalItems.name: Liandry's Torment
situationalItems.note: His abilities keep applying, so the max health burn stays refreshed on anyone holding ground against his poke.

situationalItems.name: Luden's Echo
situationalItems.note: The mana pays for poking every cooldown, and Echo adds damage to the first ability of every rotation.

situationalItems.name: Infinity Orb
situationalItems.note: Crits against low health targets, which finishes the group his poke leaves low.

situationalItems.name: Cryptbloom
situationalItems.note: The alternative to Void Staff. Less penetration, but the ability haste and healing on takedown help when his ultimate closes a teamfight. Choose it when enemies have not built much magic resist, so trading Void Staff's extra damage for more ability haste and an area heal after takedowns is worthwhile.

keystoneRune.name: First Strike
keystoneRune.desc: Deal bonus damage for the first 3 seconds of combat with champions and gain gold.
keystoneRune.note: He out-ranges almost every mid laner, so he reliably lands the opening hit.

primaryRunes.name: Axiom Arcanist
primaryRunes.desc: Empower your spell-focused burst with extra damage and scaling for ability-heavy champions.
primaryRunes.note: His ultimate is where most of his damage lands, so raising it raises the cast that closes teamfights.

primaryRunes.name: Transcendence
primaryRunes.desc: Gain ability haste, then reduce a basic ability's cooldown after it hits at level 9.
primaryRunes.note: Ability haste means more casts, and since his passive needs three separate abilities, that is directly more true damage.

primaryRunes.name: Gathering Storm
primaryRunes.desc: Gain increasing adaptive force every few minutes as the game goes on.
primaryRunes.note: He is a scaling artillery mage, so a rune that grows over the game matches the pick.

secondaryRunes.name: Bone Plating
secondaryRunes.desc: After taking damage from a champion, the next 3 instances of champion damage are reduced.
secondaryRunes.note: His damage is a channel and a set of slow skillshots, and this keeps him casting through the first burst.

spells.name: Flash
spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

goodAgainst.note: Annie has to walk into stun range to threaten you, and your reach means she eats a full rotation on every approach, so she struggles to ever close the gap safely.

Plasma Fission and Void Rift reach Veigar before Event Horizon can cage Vel'Koz, and Organic Deconstruction adds true damage once the spell sequence lands. Stay outside the cage edge, punish every Baleful Strike last-hit, and reserve Tectonic Disruption for anyone trying to close the distance after Veigar's setup misses.
Syndra is immobile and her effective range falls short of yours, so she has to walk into your poke for every last hit. The matchup gets tighter once her items come in.
You out-range the ball, so she cannot set up her shield-and-clear rhythm without eating poke, and your range plus true damage wins the long game.

Ryze has to get close to deal real damage while you massively out-range him, and your true damage lands with none of the resistances he builds blunting it, though his health pool still has to be chewed through.

weakAgainst.note: Zed is built to walk through your skillshots and delete you from a shadow before your next rotation lands; once his ultimate is up, one clean combo takes your whole health bar.

Twilight Shroud hides Akali but does not make her immune to Vel'Koz's untargeted area skillshots or a manually steered beam. Her dashes still close his safety range, so place Tectonic Disruption near Vel'Koz for its extra outward knockback and aim through her likely shroud path.
His hop makes him untargetable straight through your rotation, the worst thing possible for a champion made entirely of skillshots, and he dives you the second you mistime a cooldown.
Her blink closes your range instantly, her resets turn one kill into several, and a single missed skillshot from you becomes a free all-in with no way to run.

Norra's charged Memory Surge and Portalpalooza projectiles attack from changing portal angles that Vel'Koz cannot cover with one straight Plasma Fission line. Move before the charge completes, save Tectonic Disruption for her recoil landing, and avoid channeling Life Form Disintegration Ray while Journey to Nowhere can banish and silence you.

gamePlan.overview:
Every Vel'Koz ability hit applies Deconstruction for seven seconds, with basic attacks refreshing the stacks. The third stack consumes them to deal a separate burst of true damage and marks champions Researched for seven seconds. The passive does not convert all ordinary spell damage; its own proc is true damage, and Researched specifically changes Life Form Disintegration Ray's damage to true damage.

Void Rift stores two charges and hits once as it opens and again 0.75 seconds later as it collapses, making it capable of supplying two Deconstruction stacks. Tectonic Disruption can provide the third while holding a target in both Rift phases. Cast close to Vel'Koz, E also knocks enemies slightly away in the cast direction, strengthening his self-peel.

The catch is built into the kit. He has no dash, no blink, nothing but a slow between him and a committed diver. Everything he does is a skillshot, so a miss wastes a full rotation, and mid lane assassins exist to walk through his poke and kill him. Vel'Koz wins from extreme range or not at all.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Use Plasma Fission's manual perpendicular split to bend around minions, and last-hit with it when practical because each enemy it kills restores mana. Track both phases of Void Rift: opening and collapse can each contribute toward the three-stack passive. A target at two stacks is one ability hit from the true-damage proc and Research mark, which turns the ultimate from magic to true damage.
gamePlan.midGame: This is your tempo phase. Once your first item lands, the poke starts doing serious damage, so shove the wave in and use your range across the map: stand back from a contested scuttle or dragon and rain Void Rift and Fission into the pit before your team even arrives. You will not out-roam a Twisted Fate on foot, but mid priority plus your reach lets you decide whether an objective fight happens on good ground. Set up around dragon and Herald by standing where your ultimate threatens the choke, and look for the knockup into a full rotation on anyone who steps too far forward. Always keep minions or a teammate between you and the flank, because a side laner who finds you alone does not need to dodge much.
gamePlan.lateGame: Your passive true-damage bursts ignore resistance, but Q, W, E, and the beam against unresearched targets still deal magic damage and benefit from penetration. Apply three stacks before channeling when possible: Researched lasts seven seconds and is refreshed by attacks or abilities, while the beam then deals true damage and continues applying Deconstruction every 0.7 seconds.
gamePlan.teamfights: You are backline artillery, and your value is range plus the true-damage finish. Open with poke to chunk whoever fronts the fight, knock up the first diver who commits to break their angle, and save the ultimate for the instant their team clumps, because a laser swept across three bodies usually ends the fight right there. Stand behind every teammate you have and assume a flank is always coming, since you have no button to answer a gap-closer who reaches you. Let your frontline hold while you melt everything behind it. A Vel'Koz who lands the clumped ult and walks away alive wins the fight; one who positions greedily dies instantly and contributes nothing.

coreItems.note: Build this against armor stackers, which matters when late fights become front-to-back. Choose it over Mortal Reminder when enemies are stacking health rather than healing, since Giant Slayer increases Viego's damage against high-health targets.

Choose it over Lord Dominik's Regard when enemy healing is the bigger problem, since Grievous Wounds stops targets from recovering Viego's damage.

situationalItems.name: Mercurial Scimitar

keystoneRune.name: Conqueror

keystoneRune.note: Viego stacks Conqueror through repeated attacks and abilities before the first takedown. A possession heals him and supplies another champion's basic kit, letting him preserve a stacked combat rune while moving to the next target rather than resetting onto the same one.

primaryRunes.name: Sudden Impact

primaryRunes.note: His ultimate is a dash, so the bonus true damage triggers as Heartbreaker lands.

primaryRunes.name: Hubris

primaryRunes.note: His whole game is turning one kill into the next, and stacking power off takedowns is exactly that.

primaryRunes.desc: Gain adaptive force by collecting takedown stacks from enemy champions and epic monsters.
primaryRunes.note: His passive needs takedowns to work at all, so the stacks build faster on him than on almost anyone.

secondaryRunes.name: Legend: Alacrity
secondaryRunes.desc: Gain permanent attack speed by taking down champions, monsters, and minions.
secondaryRunes.note: Attack speed lets him consume ability marks faster, since each mark is spent by his next basic attack.

spells.note: Required for Jungling. Secures objectives and sustains through camp clears.

goodAgainst.note: Kha'Zix gets one leap-in combo, and your sustain outlasts it while your Q keeps refreshing, so his squishy frame loses the extended brawl he never wanted.
Lee Sin's pressure is all front-loaded, and once his combo is spent you out-sustain him in the long fight his fading damage cannot win.
Xin Zhao hits hard with his three-talon combo, but he only has one rotation, and your stun plus resets win the drawn-out fight once his early spike fades.

weakAgainst.note: Rammus reflects your attacks back at you and taunts you into the trade, and killing him is so hard that your passive rarely finds a corpse to possess.

Ixtal's Impact can wall-stun Viego before his first reset, while Impale suppresses him and can catch the teammates he needs to start a possession chain. Grouping for the first takedown risks giving Skarner a multi-person ultimate.

Taliyah keeps you off the corpse your kit needs: an empowered Threaded Volley from Worked Ground can slow your approach, Seismic Shove throws you back when you close, and her poke chips you down before you can land a kill.

gamePlan.overview:
Viego is a jungler who keeps fighting as long as someone else is dying. His passive lets him possess the body of anything he kills, borrowing that champion's whole kit for a few seconds, healing on the takeover, and resetting his own abilities. One kill in a teamfight can become a chain of stolen ultimates.

In the jungle he is an aggressive skirmisher who wants the game decided early. Blade of the Ruined King marks enemies hit by his abilities so his next attack strikes twice and heals him, Spectral Maw charges a stun and short dash, and Harrowed Path spreads mist around terrain for camouflage and attack speed. Heartbreaker then dives onto a low target and helps start the possession chain. You win by finding fights with a realistic first takedown, not by entering every skirmish before a body is ready to fall.

The catch is that the plan needs a takedown to start. Without a Mist Wraith to possess, Viego is a melee fighter with a charged stun and limited escape options, easy to kite or burst before Heartbreaker can reset the fight. A disciplined enemy that protects the first low-health champion can keep his passive from taking over.
gamePlan.earlyGame:
Aim to finish the full clear healthy rather than chasing a record time. Path through camps with the ability-mark into double-strike rhythm, and send Harrowed Path into nearby terrain so its mist spreads around the wall and conceals your approach. Take scuttle at the end, which puts you on level five, and Viego is worth fighting for a crab when his cooldowns and health favor the brawl.

With that done, hunt the first gank while your camps respawn: approach outside enemy vision, charge Spectral Maw, and remember its accompanying dash cannot cross terrain. Let the stun plus your marked attack hand your laner an easy takedown, because an early Mist Wraith can start a possession chain that snowballs the map. If you find the enemy jungler alone at a camp, that is your best fight: land the charged stun, earn a qualifying takedown, and consume the resulting Mist Wraith when it is safe.
gamePlan.midGame:
Viego wants an objective skirmish where one realistic takedown can unlock the first possession. Contest whenever your team is ahead on early fights. When it is even, take Herald and trade dragon away, unless your team can hold the fights soul is worth.

Between objectives, cast Harrowed Path toward river terrain so the mist wraps the wall, then use its camouflage and movement speed before attacking. Ambush an isolated target only when allies can help secure the takedown, then check the enemy jungler and lane priority before starting the objective. Invade when the enemy jungler shows on the far side and nearby lanes cannot collapse. Keep farming between real skirmish windows instead of waiting in mist for a target that may never arrive.
gamePlan.lateGame: You are not a side laner late; you are the cleanup threat in every grouped fight, so stay with your team and look for a way to reach a wounded squishy. Hold Heartbreaker until its most-wounded target selection and missing-health damage can secure a takedown, then consume the Mist Wraith to heal and borrow that champion's basic kit. Possession preserves Viego's current health percentage rather than protecting a separate body, so choose forms and exits carefully. Vision around Baron and the dragon pit decides these fights, so ward the flanks and let Harrowed Path hide your approach before you commit.
gamePlan.teamfights: You join the fight second, not first. Let your frontline commit, watch for the first health bar to drop, then ult in, execute, and possess the corpse so your cooldowns reset and you keep fighting on someone else's kit. Every takeover heals you and hands you a fresh ultimate, which is how a fed Viego kills an entire team one body at a time, so always target whatever is already low instead of the tank. Save your W to peel a diver off your carry or to lock the target you are about to execute, and use the E brush to flank the backline from an angle their support is not watching. The whole job is the chain: one clean kill should become the next one, and the next, until nobody is left to possess.

boots.name: Spellslinger's Shoes

coreItems.name: Stormsurge

coreItems.name: Infinity Orb

coreItems.name: Void Staff
coreItems.note: Cuts the magic resist that turns her one burst window into a chunk instead of a kill. Choose it over Cryptbloom when enemies are stacking magic resist and maximum personal damage matters more than ability haste and team healing.

coreItems.name: Rabadon's Deathcap
coreItems.note: Multiplies Vex's fear combo and Shadow Surge damage, raising the chance that the champion marked by her ultimate dies within the six-second takedown window and grants the free recast.

situationalItems.name: Oceanid's Trident

situationalItems.name: Morellonomicon
situationalItems.note: Build this when enemies heal through Vex's burst or survive beyond Shadow Surge's marked-target takedown window. Her area fear applies Grievous Wounds before the ultimate lands; buy Oblivion Orb early and finish the item later.

situationalItems.name: Banshee's Veil
situationalItems.note: Build this when the enemy has a hook or point-and-click stun, since she has no escape before her ultimate mark is placed.

situationalItems.name: Zhonya's Hourglass
situationalItems.note: Build this for the dive that reaches her once her shadow and shield are spent. Buy Seeker's Armguard early for the armor and ability power.

situationalItems.name: Cryptbloom

Choose it when enemies have not built much magic resist, so trading Void Staff's extra damage for more ability haste and an area heal after takedowns is worthwhile.

primaryRunes.note: Her passive fear and her slow mean the target is almost always impaired when her follow-up lands.

primaryRunes.name: Chain Assault

primaryRunes.note: Her whole rotation pours into one marked target, which is what this rewards.

primaryRunes.name: Eyeball Collector
primaryRunes.desc: Gain adaptive force by collecting takedown stacks from enemy champions and epic monsters.
primaryRunes.note: A takedown on the champion marked by Shadow Surge within six seconds grants its free recast, so successful ultimate chains also accumulate Eyeball Collector stacks quickly.

secondaryRunes.name: Bone Plating
secondaryRunes.desc: After taking damage from a champion, the next 3 instances of champion damage are reduced.
secondaryRunes.note: She commits with her ultimate and eats the answer, and this softens what comes back before the reset.

spells.name: Flash
spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

goodAgainst.note: Every dash he makes marks him with Gloom, so your next hit detonates it and refunds part of Doom's cooldown, and his windwall blocks the bolt but not the gloom zone, so his mobility-heavy playstyle plays straight into your kit.
Yone repeatedly dashes as he trades, and each dash can mark him with Gloom, so your detonations keep pulling Doom's fear forward, though his scaling means the lane gets closer as it goes.
His whole kit is shadow dashes, so he arrives marked every time, and if Doom is ready your next ability fears him out of the combo before it lands while the Gloom detonation adds to your burst.
Diana's engage is one committed Lunar Rush dash into your face, exactly the input your passive is waiting for, though she has more health than most assassins, so one combo may not kill her.
Akali is squishy and dash-reliant, so every leap into your gloom marks her, and with Doom ready your next ability fears her out of the combo; the shroud hiding her is the only real annoyance.

weakAgainst.note: Veigar never has to dash, so you never get a Gloom mark to detonate and Doom's fear only ever arrives on its own timer, and his cage out-ranges your short poke while threatening a stun your immobile frame cannot dodge. He also out-scales you.

His bombs arc in from well outside Vex's bolt range, and his only dash is a Satchel Charge hop rather than the repeated mobility her passive punishes best. That hop does create a Gloom mark, but Ziggs can still use it to leave Shadow Surge's landing area if timed before Vex arrives.
Orianna out-ranges your poke, controls the wave with her ball, and never commits a dash for your passive to punish, while her shockwave throws your Surge engage right back out.

Her spheres out-range your bolt and she has no dash to feed your Gloom detonations. Syndra threatens Vex from range with sphere-and-E angles, so track existing spheres and sidestep the projected knockback line.
Norra out-ranges your poke with a bounce that hits from angles you cannot sidestep, her dog drags you out of position, and she never gives your Gloom mark a dash to punish.

gamePlan.overview:
Vex is a burst mage built to punish dashes. She pokes with Mistral Bolt, places Looming Darkness for area damage and a slow, and when an enemy dashes, blinks, or flashes near her, Gloom marks them so her next basic attack or basic-ability hit detonates the mark for bonus damage and refunds part of Doom's cooldown. Shadow Surge marks the first enemy champion hit and lets her dash to them; a takedown on that marked target shortly afterward makes it available again, so one pick can chain into several.

In mid lane she punishes the exact champions other mages dread. Shove the wave, hold Doom for the dash-happy assassin's commitment, and use Looming Darkness to control the space they must cross. Once her ultimate is up she becomes a roam threat: the Surge reaches across the river, and the reset turns a side-lane gank into a snowball. She wants picks and burst, not a slow scaling game.

Her weakness is simple. Her basic kit has no dash, and enemies who refuse to dash deny her the bonus Gloom marks and Doom cooldown refunds she thrives on. Long-range artillery and patient scalers do not give her the mistakes she feeds on, and once her ultimate is spent she has no escape of her own.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Play the early lane around your fear threat. Before level five, farm safely, chip with Mistral Bolt when the enemy walks up to last-hit, and place Looming Darkness where they must stand; it applies Gloom but does not leave a persistent zone. Their first aggressive dash also gives you a mark to detonate and pulls your fear forward. Do not try to win a raw poke war against artillery: trade around Doom and the faster, narrower end of Mistral Bolt instead. Manage the wave so you can shove and deny, and remember you have no basic dash to escape a gank, so ward the river and let the enemy commit first.
gamePlan.midGame: Once Shadow Surge is up, you stop being just a laner and start pressuring the map. Shove with Mistral Bolt and Looming Darkness, then walk to river to mark the enemy jungler at scuttle or start a pick before a dragon fight, since a takedown on the marked target can make Shadow Surge available again. Mid priority unlocks objectives: crash the wave, contest the river, and use the long Surge range to threaten anyone who shows on the Dragon lane side of the map. Your first item turns the fear-into-burst combo into a real kill on squishies, so look for roams onto side laners who shoved too far. Watch your own back though: a Vex with her ultimate already spent is exactly the immobile target the enemy assassin is hunting.
gamePlan.lateGame: Clear side waves only when you can return before Baron or Elder is contested. From fog, look for Shadow Surge on a reachable carry or another low-durability target, but recast only when allies can follow and the enemy's main control cannot stop the landing. Place Looming Darkness on the path a diver or retreating target must cross, then detonate Gloom marks to shorten Doom's cooldown. If the enemy backline remains protected, hold the ultimate and use fear to peel rather than entering alone.
gamePlan.teamfights: Place Looming Darkness where the enemy engage must pass, then detonate Gloom with Mistral Bolt, Personal Space, or a basic attack to shorten Doom's cooldown. Choose a Shadow Surge target that your team can finish, because the recast commits Vex to that position. Enter after the control that can stop her landing is spent, and use the reset only if the next target is reachable without crossing the enemy frontline.

coreItems.name: Amaranth's Twinguard
coreItems.note: Build this when you are spinning in the middle of the enemy team and need both armor and magic resist.

situationalItems.name: Chainlaced Crushers
situationalItems.note: Boot swap against heavy magic damage and crowd control. Tenacity shortens most disables so Wukong can reposition or use the second Cyclone cast sooner; being controlled does not inherently cancel an active Cyclone.

situationalItems.note: The burn scales with bonus health and ticks on everyone caught in his spin.

situationalItems.name: Gargoyle Stoneplate
situationalItems.note: The shield grows when Wukong's dash and Cyclone place him among several enemies, protecting the window between his first knock-up, clone reposition, and second cast.

situationalItems.name: Randuin's Omen
situationalItems.note: Build this when the enemy team has multiple crit champions, so his spin does not end the moment it starts.

situationalItems.name: Mercurial Scimitar
situationalItems.note: Build this when a removable disable catches Wukong before he reaches the backline or between Cyclone casts. Cleansing restores his ability to reposition; it is not needed merely to keep an already active Cyclone spinning.

keystoneRune.desc: Every 4 seconds in combat, your next attack against a champion deals bonus damage and heals you.
keystoneRune.note: Permanent health growth, and his lane is repeated short walk-up trades behind his clone.

primaryRunes.desc: Gain bonus armor and magic resist, increasing further when surrounded by enemies.
primaryRunes.note: His ultimate spins him through a group, which is when this gives the most.

primaryRunes.name: Second Wind
primaryRunes.desc: After taking damage from a champion, regenerate health over time.
primaryRunes.note: His clone covers a commit, not chip, so this handles the poke that wears him down first.

primaryRunes.name: Overgrowth
primaryRunes.desc: Gain permanent maximum health when nearby minions or monsters die.
primaryRunes.note: His ultimate puts him in the middle of everyone, and the health decides how much of it he survives.

secondaryRunes.name: Sudden Impact
secondaryRunes.desc: Deal bonus true damage after using mobility or exiting stealth.
secondaryRunes.note: His E is a dash, so the bonus true damage triggers as he reaches his target.

spells.name: Flash
spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

goodAgainst.note: Nimbus Strike closes Mini Gnar's boomerang spacing, while Warrior Trickster can make him spend Hop or a Hyper attack on the clone instead of Wukong. Commit only while his rage bar is low, save Cyclone to interrupt the escape after Hop, and disengage before Mega Gnar gains the crowd control that reverses the matchup.
Renekton's kill threat lives in one empowered stun, and your clone makes him guess which Wukong to spend it on. Once that combo misses, he has no follow-up.
Darius needs an extended brawl and his pull needs the right target: the clone hands him the wrong one, and your burst is done before the bleed ever stacks up.
His windwall stops projectiles you do not have, and the clone eats his engage, so a committed combo bursts a squishy skirmisher before his crit items arrive.

weakAgainst.note: Sion has more health than your burst can finish: the charged knockup catches your dash-in, his shield soaks the combo, and the zombie passive keeps fighting after he dies.
Malphite's armor stacking and shield are exactly what your burst cannot punch through, and the clone does not fool a ground-targeted charge that can still land on the real you.
Shen's taunt punishes a champion who commits a full combo: the moment you dash in, he pulls you into a trade on his terms, his block eats your autos, and his sustain outlasts your burst.

Volibear tanks your burst and heals through the brawl: his charge stun catches your dash-in and his bite heals mid-fight, so your burst window never quite finishes him. His level three all-in also beats yours.

gamePlan.overview:
Wukong is built around his clone. Warrior Trickster makes him invisible for one second, dashes him to a chosen location, and leaves a clone at the cast position; if Wukong was moving, the clone continues briefly in that same direction. The clone attacks autonomously and mirrors Wukong's other ability casts. It can copy Nimbus Strike and Cyclone damage, but Wukong and the clone cannot knock up the same enemy twice during one Cyclone cast.

His trade pattern is fast: Nimbus Strike to the target, use its attack-speed window and Golden Staff reset, then decide whether Warrior Trickster adds mirrored damage or covers the exit. Stone Skin stacks only when Wukong damages an enemy champion; each of its three stacks grants armor and maximum-health regeneration for five seconds, so repeated champion hits make an extended physical trade sturdier.

His weaknesses are the usual snowballer problems: ranged poke hurts his approach, his power fades against full builds, and with both dashes spent he is a plain melee bruiser with no escape. He wins by turning early kills into a mid game where Cyclone decides every grouped fight.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Trade around Warrior Trickster and the wave position. Nimbus Strike in when the opponent's main response is down, use Golden Staff to reduce armor for the follow-up, and decide before committing whether the clone is adding damage or preserving the exit. Spending W to dodge a key spell is often better than saving it after the damage has landed. Against poke, farm with the extended staff and wait for a jungle setup rather than using both movement tools just to reach the target.
gamePlan.midGame: First item plus Cyclone is a strong river-fight window. Crash the Baron wave before the first objectives, then favor Herald when the map offers an even trade. Use Warrior Trickster from fog, Nimbus Strike toward the priority target, and cast Cyclone while the clone can mirror its coverage. Keep the second cast for the enemy's reposition or for peeling the counter-engage. If the river is dark and your lane is not pushed, do not force a flank that gives away both the wave and your ultimate.
gamePlan.lateGame: Late game, arrive before the objective so you can threaten a flank without revealing which angle is real. Enter with Nimbus Strike or Warrior Trickster, then cast Cyclone while the clone is active for extra damage and coverage. The clone cannot grant a second knockup on a target already hit during that same cast, so move the real Wukong toward a different part of the formation when useful. Choose between disrupting the backline and peeling your own carry based on which side has the stronger sustained damage.
gamePlan.teamfights: If the enemy groups, flank and move the first Cyclone cast through several champions, then use the recast after they reposition. If they spread, reach a priority target with Nimbus Strike and Golden Staff while keeping Warrior Trickster for the response. A clone active during Cyclone widens the disruption but does not repeat a knockup already applied by that cast. Stone Skin's armor and regeneration build from damaging champions, so touch several reachable targets without chasing beyond allied follow-up.

boots.name: Armorcrusher Boots

coreItems.note: Spellblade triggers on the empowered attack his Q already is, which speeds up his clear and sharpens his ganks.

coreItems.name: Sundered Sky

coreItems.name: Serylda's Grudge

coreItems.name: Goredrinker
coreItems.desc: Fighter sustain item with AoE healing
coreItems.note: The active heals more for each enemy it hits, and his ultimate already puts him in the middle of several of them. It pays off most against a team with several melee champions, who stay close enough together for one cast to catch more than one.

coreItems.name: Guardian Angel
coreItems.note: Revives him once after dying. His clone buys one deception, not a second life.

situationalItems.name: Black Cleaver
situationalItems.note: Armor shred for the durable targets his ultimate keeps him fighting through.

situationalItems.name: Serpent's Fang
situationalItems.note: Build this when the enemy has shields that absorb the burst his ultimate opens.

situationalItems.name: Armored Advance
situationalItems.note: Boot swap against heavy physical damage, when armor is what keeps the dive survivable.

situationalItems.name: Chainlaced Crushers
situationalItems.note: Boot swap against heavy magic damage and crowd control, which buys the tenacity his commit needs.

keystoneRune.name: Conqueror
keystoneRune.desc: Gain stacks by damaging enemy champions. At maximum stacks, gain bonus damage and healing.
keystoneRune.note: His attacks and abilities stack it as he enters a fight, and his two ultimate casts help him keep the stacks active through an extended engage.

primaryRunes.name: Triumph
primaryRunes.desc: Champion takedowns restore missing health, max mana or energy, and grant movement speed.
primaryRunes.note: His ganks are meant to convert into kills, and refunding health mid-fight lets him survive the collapse.

primaryRunes.name: Cut Down
primaryRunes.desc: You deal bonus adaptive damage (except true damage) to enemy champions above 60% health.
primaryRunes.note: His spin grinds through whoever is near him, which is usually the frontline this pays out against.

primaryRunes.name: Legend: Alacrity
primaryRunes.desc: Gain permanent attack speed by taking down champions, monsters, and minions.
primaryRunes.note: Attack speed works with Nimbus Strike's four-second attack-speed window and lets repeated attacks reduce Golden Staff's remaining cooldown more quickly.

secondaryRunes.name: Sudden Impact
secondaryRunes.desc: Deal bonus true damage after using mobility or exiting stealth.
secondaryRunes.note: His E is a dash, so the bonus true damage triggers as he reaches his target.

spells.name: Flash
spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

spells.name: Smite
spells.note: Required for Jungling. Secures objectives and sustains through camp clears.

goodAgainst.note: Nidalee only threatens you if the long spear lands, and a fragile cat with her cougar cooldowns spent is exactly what your Cyclone punishes. The clone also baits out her pounce.
Lee Sin commits his whole combo up front, and your clone turns that into a wasted cooldown: he kicks or dashes onto the decoy, then has nothing left when the real Wukong arrives.
Zed has to land a clean combo to win, and your clone makes him spend his shadow and burst on a decoy while your Cyclone knocks him out of the swap he needs to escape.

weakAgainst.note: Nunu shrugs off your combo with his stacked health, and his knockup stops your dive before Cyclone lands, so the clone trick does nothing against a body you cannot kill.
Attacking Rammus hurts you more than him: his taunt drags your committed dive onto Defensive Ball Curl, and every hit you land gets reflected back into your own health bar.

gamePlan.overview:
Wukong is a mobile diver who uses Warrior Trickster to hide his route and leave a clone behind. He clears at a steady pace, closes distance with Nimbus Strike, and uses Cyclone to disrupt several enemies. The clone is useful for changing an approach, absorbing a spell, or widening the area covered by his abilities, not only for fooling an opponent in a duel.

He wins by snowballing the early map. His ganks hit hard because Cyclone is a guaranteed knockup once it gets going, his clone makes invades and counter-ganks hard to read, and his dash plus stealth let him commit and then back out if things go wrong. Get an early lead and he turns it into picks, dives, and stolen objectives, and later his ultimate becomes an area knockup that can decide a teamfight on its own.

The catch is that he is a melee diver with no range and no backup plan once his dash and clone are used. Hard crowd control beats every trick he has, and a champion who locks him down mid-dash kills him before the clone matters. He also depends on his early window: if a faster jungler beats him to tempo, the snowball never starts.
gamePlan.earlyGame:
Use the first clear to reach the side with the best lane setup instead of forcing a fixed route every game. Take Scuttle when lane priority protects the river and use the experience toward level five, when Cyclone makes the next gank much harder to escape. Before that point, gank lanes that already have crowd control or an overextended target. Return to camps when no lane offers a clean angle so a failed visit does not cost both tempo and experience.

Contest Scuttle only when the nearby lanes can move or you have tracked the enemy jungler away from support. Warrior Trickster can absorb the first important spell or cover your retreat. Invade a predictable farmer after confirming lane priority and an exit route; taking one camp is not worth being collapsed on without Nimbus Strike or the clone available.
gamePlan.midGame:
Crash or cover the nearby lanes before starting an objective, then look for Cyclone on the enemy jungler or backline as they enter river. Herald is a useful conversion when it can break a turret, while dragon is stronger when your lanes can arrive first and your composition wants repeated grouped fights. If the enemy controls the entrance, trade for camps, a wave, or the opposite objective instead of using Warrior Trickster to face-check the pit.

Between objectives, gank the lanes that are already pushing and turn every won skirmish into an objective. Keep your income up by mixing ganks with quick camps, and remember the clone works as a vision and bait tool from fog, not just a burst button.
gamePlan.lateGame: Group before Baron and Elder rather than taking a distant side-lane duel. Approach from swept vision and look for a Cyclone angle on several enemies, but keep Warrior Trickster available until the target and enemy control spells are clear. If the enemy backline cannot be reached, use Cyclone to interrupt divers and protect your own sustained damage. A visible flank can still force the enemy away from the pit, so do not reveal yourself early by clearing a ward in their sight.
gamePlan.teamfights: Wait until your team can follow before committing Nimbus Strike and Cyclone. From a flank, use Warrior Trickster to change the entry line or absorb a key spell, then move Cyclone through the carry and nearby peel. Keep the recast for the enemy's reposition or for a second disruption after your team arrives. If the frontline blocks access to the backline, protect your carry and damage the reachable target rather than crossing the entire formation alone.

coreItems.name: Mortal Reminder

coreItems.name: Sterak's Gage

coreItems.name: Guardian Angel

goodAgainst.note: Lee Sin wants the same early skirmishes, but your sustain and knockup win the straight fight: you heal through his front-loaded combo and stay on him after his burst is spent.
Kha'Zix needs to leap in, burst, and reset out, but your knockup catches him mid-jump and your dash keeps you attached, and a squishy assassin who cannot reset loses the extended fight.
Wukong relies on his clone and knockup, but your own knockup answers his, and your sustain lets you heal through his one damage rotation while your repeated hits out-pace it.

weakAgainst.note: Every attack you land on Defensive Ball Curl comes back at you, and his taunt locks your single-target kit onto him while your knockup does nothing to stop him.
Shyvana survives your early aggression and scales past you: your power is front-loaded and hers is back-loaded, so her dragon form eventually lives through your all-in and out-damages you.
Amumu stops your one plan cold: his bandage pins you mid-engage, his ultimate locks you the moment you commit, and his percent-health aura hurts no matter what you build.

gamePlan.overview:
Xin Zhao is an all-in diver who commits fully to one target. He dashes in on his spear, knocks the target up on his third strike, and sweeps everyone else away so he can fight one on one. His clear is fast, his early dueling is among the strongest in the jungle, and his ultimate blocks ranged damage from anyone he has not recently hit.

He wins by ending the game before the scaling junglers come online. Path for an aggressive full clear, gank the moment it is done and your knockup is ready, and turn the early map into skirmishes you usually win. Scuttle is yours, the enemy jungle is open to you, and every early dragon or Rift Herald is a fight you are happy to start.

His weakness is time and kiting. Almost all his power sits in the early and mid game, and full-build carries eventually out-stat him. He also has no way to reach a backline that keeps its distance, so ranged teams with good peel leave his dash with nothing to hit.
gamePlan.earlyGame:
Xin Zhao's third-hit knockup makes level three a real decision point. Path toward a volatile lane or the enemy jungler's likely route, then break off when Audacious Charge can put you on a target your team is ready to finish. Prepare the first two Three Talon Strike attacks on a camp or scuttle when possible, so the gank reaches the knockup sooner. If no target is exposed, complete the clear and carry that pressure into river.

You win many early duels, but an invade still needs lane priority and an exit. Force the opposing jungler away first, then take the camp rather than starting on their resource while enemies collapse. Xin Zhao should use his early stats to create a lead, yet a guaranteed clear is still better than chasing a target through a wave with no allied follow-up.
gamePlan.midGame:
Xin Zhao controls early river fights by marking the target he can reach and using Crescent Guard to split the response. Lead with Wind Becomes Lightning when possible: its thrust marks the farthest champion or large monster hit, revealing them and extending Audacious Charge's range. After you enter, Crescent Guard can knock non-Challenged enemies away and protect Xin from champions who remain outside its radius; enemies close to Xin can still damage him. Contest when your team can follow rather than assuming the guard makes every entry safe.

Between objectives, counter-jungle the slow farmers before they come online and keep turning your tempo into gold, because this stretch decides whether the enemy's late game ever arrives.
gamePlan.lateGame: Be honest about your power: scaled carries now out-stat you, and charging five people alone just gets you killed. Hold your engage until their crowd control is spent, then dive a priority target your team can reach. Crescent Guard buys a window against enemy champions who remain outside its range, but a ranged champion who moves close enough can damage Xin normally. Stay near Baron and the late Dragons as a threat; your job is to start the fight your team finishes, not to win it alone.
gamePlan.teamfights: Choose a target your team can reach, apply the challenge, and use Audacious Charge after the enemy commits their first movement tool. Prepare Three Talon Strike so the knockup lands during allied follow-up. Cast Crescent Guard when ranged damage or nearby enemies would otherwise overwhelm the position, but remember that opponents inside the circle can still damage Xin Zhao. If no carry is reachable, protect your own backline and attack the nearest threat instead of diving alone.

startingItem.name: Ruby Crystal
startingItem.note: Early health for a champion whose lane is committing to level three all-ins.

boots.name: Armored Advance
boots.note: Armor and health, which let him survive the trade his charge starts.

coreItems.name: Heartsteel
coreItems.note: Stacks permanent health from trades, turning lane durability into a mid-game body nobody can move.

coreItems.name: Dusk and Dawn

Thundering Smash or Frenzied Maul primes its empowered attack, the extra on-hit repeats The Relentless Storm's chain-lightning damage, and the attack speed helps Volibear stack his passive and reach a second Frenzied Maul.

coreItems.note: Ramping bonus damage and Omnivamp strengthen repeated attacks, Sky Splitter, and the second Frenzied Maul, matching the main build's focus on extended fights.

coreItems.name: Unending Despair
coreItems.note: Volibear's ultimate commits him among several enemies, where Unending Despair damages them and heals him while he waits to mark the same target with a second Frenzied Maul.

coreItems.name: Amaranth's Twinguard
coreItems.note: Build this when you are fighting in the middle of the enemy team and need both armor and magic resist. Volibear's ultimate starts an extended tower dive or brawl, and repeated Frenzied Maul heals help him reach Twinguard's activation.

situationalItems.name: Trinity Force
situationalItems.note: Build this instead of Dusk and Dawn against squishier champions. Its stronger short burst and movement speed help Volibear reach and finish targets that will not survive long enough for sustained DPS to matter.

situationalItems.name: Force of Nature
situationalItems.note: Build this when the enemy team has two or more AP champions. The move speed also matters since his charge is his only gap closer.

situationalItems.name: Thornmail
situationalItems.note: Build this when Volibear needs armor and anti-heal. Entwine applies Grievous Wounds from his own damage as well as enemy attacks, and his passive lightning can carry it across several champions in an extended fight.

situationalItems.name: Frozen Heart
situationalItems.note: Build this when the enemy team has several attack-speed carries. Volibear's charge and ultimate keep him beside the target, so Frozen Heart slows their attacks while he waits for a second Frenzied Maul.

situationalItems.name: Chainlaced Crushers
situationalItems.note: Boot swap against heavy magic damage and crowd control. Enemy immobilization pauses Thundering Smash rather than consuming it, and tenacity gets Volibear moving toward the target again sooner.

situationalItems.name: Titanic Hydra
situationalItems.note: Turns his health into cleave, for the games decided by side-lane waves rather than surviving a teamfight.

situationalItems.name: Gargoyle Stoneplate
situationalItems.note: The shield scales with Volibear's health and nearby enemies, covering the deepest part of the tower dive after his ultimate lands and before his second Frenzied Maul heals him.

situationalItems.name: Mercurial Scimitar
situationalItems.note: Build this when a removable disable holds Volibear during Thundering Smash. The ability's duration pauses while he is immobilized, and cleansing lets him resume the approach sooner and stay close for the second Frenzied Maul.

keystoneRune.note: Permanent health growth, and his lane is repeated short walk-up trades behind a charge.

primaryRunes.note: He fights through damage rather than around it, and the pool is what that plan needs.

secondaryRunes.note: He often drops low while staying in melee long enough to cast Frenzied Maul a second time, which is when its empowered bite finally heals him.
