primaryRunes.name: Scorch
primaryRunes.desc: Your next ability hit sets champions ablaze, dealing bonus magic damage.
primaryRunes.note: His poke is a bomb and back off, and Scorch adds damage to that trade.

secondaryRunes.name: Cut Down
secondaryRunes.desc: You deal bonus adaptive damage (except true damage) to enemy champions above 60% health.
secondaryRunes.note: His bombs grind through health bars, so bonus damage against high health targets suits the frontline holding his siege back.

spells.name: Flash
spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

goodAgainst.note: Your bombs pressure him from outside Event Horizon, and your waveclear forces him to spend time farming instead of setting up a cage. Do not try to Satchel Charge through the cage wall: touching it still stuns you.
Her kit is built to punish dashes, which you barely use, so the part of her that terrorizes other mids does little to you, and your range beats her gloom poke.
Neither her sphere poke nor her stun setup reaches as far as your bombs, so she has to walk into a siege and pay for it. Her point-and-click ultimate is the only real threat.

An artillery standoff you win: your minefield and siege out-zone her volley, and the snare that is her only peel does not stop your satchel hop. Her reflect only punishes a telegraphed committed cast.

weakAgainst.note: His pole-vault sidesteps your bombs and minefield in one untargetable hop, then he lands on top of you. You cannot out-poke a champion who erases the poke, and his item spike makes every catch lethal.
Dashes and resets carry her through the minefield that should zone her, landing on your immobile frame before the bombs connect. If she snowballs off a pick, the lane is lost.
He walks through your poke behind his shield and bridges the gap with a knockup that ignores your spacing. One satchel hop buys a single disengage, and he wins every duel after two items.
His shadow swaps dodge your bombs, and his ultimate deletes you the moment it comes online, since one satchel hop rarely buys enough distance to survive the burst.

Her three dashes and charm carry her through the bombs and minefield you use to keep distance, and one landed charm sets up a burst your immobile frame cannot survive. Her mobility outpaces your single satchel hop.

gamePlan.overview:
Ziggs is an artillery mage who controls the lane with explosives. Bouncing Bomb arcs in from a range most mids cannot match, his minefield covers the ground in zoning hexplosives, and Satchel Charge both clears waves and launches him out of bad spots. He sits at the back, lobs bombs, and makes standing anywhere near him cost health.

He wins on poke and pressure rather than kills and roams. Shove the wave, chip the enemy laner every time they step up to last-hit, and turn mid priority into objective control. Mega Inferno Bomb has very long 5,000-unit range rather than global range, so it can influence distant river and side-lane fights when they are within its cast circle. His passive also makes him a major siege threat against towers.

The catch is the usual artillery problem: no mobility and no answer to getting jumped. Outside of one satchel hop he has no escape, so any assassin or skirmisher who gets past the minefield lands right on top of him. His games come down to spacing, respecting the gap-closers in the lobby, and staying alive while everyone tries to kill the artillery first.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Establish early that the lane belongs to your range. Land Bouncing Bomb on the enemy whenever it lines up with the wave so you chip and push at the same time, and use Satchel Charge on the casters when you need a hard shove. The minefield is your safety net: drop it between you and the enemy so walking up costs them health, and save some for the jungle paths once you suspect a gank, since you have no clean way to run. Check the enemy jungler before every aggressive bomb, because a Ziggs caught mid-cast with his satchel down is the easiest kill on the map. You will not solo kill many people early, but a poked-down laner cannot contest the wave or trade back.
gamePlan.midGame: This is where the artillery pays off. Your bombs out-range almost everyone, so shove the wave and choose: crash it and siege the tower with your passive, or hold priority and walk to river to bomb the enemy jungler at scuttle. Your ultimate is the big swing tool now, so watch the Dragon lane side of the map and drop Mega Inferno Bomb onto a dragon fight your team is taking without you. Once your first item is done the poke genuinely hurts, and a tower that falls to your passive opens the map for your jungler. Remember that mid is where you are safest: only roam with the wave shoved and a teammate watching for the flank that kills you.
gamePlan.lateGame: By late game, clear side waves from range and return before Baron or Elder can be contested. In objective setups, stay behind your frontline and place Hexplosive Minefield across the entrance the enemy must use. Mega Inferno Bomb can finish a low target or damage several enemies grouped in a pit, but account for its travel time. Preserve Satchel Charge when a flank is possible, because it is Ziggs's only way to create distance after an enemy crosses his range.
gamePlan.teamfights: Make the ground hostile before anyone commits. Lay the minefield across the choke or the objective pit so the enemy frontline has to walk through hexplosives to reach you, then lob bombs into the cluster from a range their carries cannot answer. Open from max distance and keep your satchel for the diver, since its knockback can push an assassin off you or knock an enemy back into your team. Mega Inferno Bomb can start the fight or end it: drop it on a clumped backline to open, or save it for whoever tries to limp away. You bring zoning and damage, not lockdown, so position behind everything and keep the bombs coming.

startingItem.name: Spectral Sickle
startingItem.note: Support income for a champion who is stockpiling experience rather than contesting minions.

boots.name: Crimson Lucidity
boots.note: Ability haste, since his value is how often his bombs and his revive are available.

coreItems.name: Black Mist Scythe
coreItems.note: Time Bomb completes the quest from safe range, and the upgrade's haste helps Zilean cycle double bombs, speed boosts, and his revive more often.

coreItems.name: Harmonic Echo
coreItems.note: Twisted Timeflow shields Zilean and the nearest ally together, giving a charged Harmonic Echo an easy allied target and adding healing to a spell that otherwise only shields.

coreItems.name: Ardent Censer
coreItems.note: Twisted Timeflow automatically reaches the nearest ally as well as Zilean, so using it to accelerate an ADC also gives that carry Ardent's attack speed and on-hit damage.

coreItems.name: Staff of Flowing Waters
coreItems.note: Twisted Timeflow shields an ally while making Zilean's basic cooldowns recover 80% faster. Staff adds more ability haste and ability power to that same high-tempo casting window.

coreItems.name: Banshee's Veil
coreItems.note: Build this when the enemy has a hook or point-and-click stun, since a caught Zilean cannot revive himself.

situationalItems.name: Morellonomicon
situationalItems.note: Build this when the enemy duo heals through his bombs. Buy Oblivion Orb early, since the anti-heal works from the component.

situationalItems.name: Oceanid's Trident
situationalItems.note: Build this when the enemy has shields that keep absorbing his bomb damage.

keystoneRune.name: Aery
keystoneRune.desc: Your attacks and abilities send Aery to a target, dealing damage to enemies or shielding allies.
keystoneRune.note: Aery follows his shield as well as his bomb, so it pays out on both halves of what he does.

primaryRunes.name: Font of Life
primaryRunes.desc: Damaging enemy champions heals you and the lowest-health nearby ally after a short cooldown.
primaryRunes.note: His bombs can hit enemy champions, healing him and the lowest-Health allied champion nearby when the rune is ready.

primaryRunes.name: Bone Plating
primaryRunes.desc: After taking damage from a champion, the next 3 instances of champion damage are reduced.
primaryRunes.note: He is immobile and gets focused first, and this covers the burst thrown before his ultimate is up.

primaryRunes.name: Revitalize
primaryRunes.desc: Healing and shielding are stronger, especially on low-health targets.
primaryRunes.note: His shield and his revive are both protective effects, so a flat increase to healing and shielding suits his kit.

secondaryRunes.name: Transcendence
secondaryRunes.desc: Gain ability haste, then reduce a basic ability's cooldown after it hits at level 9.
secondaryRunes.note: Ability haste means more bombs and a faster revive, which is the only stat that changes his impact.

spells.name: Flash
spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

goodAgainst.note: One hook ends you, but his single telegraphed engage walks straight into your stun, your poke punishes him for stepping up at all, and Chronoshift undoes the one pick his whole kit exists to land.
Veigar is the most immobile thing in the lane, so your shared speed burst sidesteps his cage while your bombs out-range his setup. Even a landed combo on your carry gets undone by your ultimate.

Leona's lane is one long commitment and your kit punishes commitment: the slow makes her engage arrive late, the stun catches her landing, and Chronoshift revives whoever she spent everything to kill.

Unbreakable can intercept a thrown Time Bomb, so aim around Braum or attach the bomb to an ally or minion before it reaches his shield. Chronoshift still punishes the single target his team commits to killing.

Every soul she wants is a walk into bomb range, so your poke punishes the collection all lane long. Her slow attrition plan also collapses against an ultimate that undoes the one kill she works toward.

weakAgainst.note: Thresh's hook, lantern, and flay are all aimed at the slowest support in the lane, which is you. One landed grab pulls you out of position before your bombs or ultimate can answer.
Milio answers your whole kit: his ultimate cleanses the double-bomb stun, his range matches your poke with less mana strain, and his heals mean nobody dips low enough to need your revive.
Her poke comes out faster than your bomb cooldowns, her shield absorbs the chunk you stack two spells to land, and her speed boosts carry the whole duo out of your stun.
Every bomb you land gets healed back, and her silence zone lands on the exact spot you cast from. Your revive is a one-time swing while her healing is constant, and constant wins lanes.

gamePlan.overview:
Zilean is the support who can undo a death. He throws bombs that stick where they land, and a second bomb on the same target detonates the pair early for an area stun. Twisted Timeflow shields him and his nearest ally, increases their movement and projectile speed, and makes his own basic cooldowns recover 80% faster while either buff remains. Temporal Mirage drops a field that slows enemies and drags enemy-champion projectiles down to a crawl, and Chronoshift revives whoever he places it on. His passive also stores experience and, when enough is banked, lets him channel on an ally to level both of them together.

In the Dragon lane he plays a poke-and-revive game. Double-bomb the enemy duo when they walk up for a last hit, run Twisted Timeflow when you and your carry both need the shield and the speed, and drop Temporal Mirage over the skillshots aimed at your duo. Hold the stun for the moment their support commits. Once Chronoshift is up, your carry can take fights they would normally lose, because the worst case is a short setback instead of a real death.

The cost is his body. He is one of the most fragile supports in the role, slow on his feet, and his escape is a shared speed buff that only helps if he is standing near the ally he is saving. Miss the bombs, or get caught by a hook before they arm, and he is a squishy body with long cooldowns and nothing left.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Lead with a single bomb on the enemy carry when they step up to farm, and attach the second to the same unit when you want the immediate area stun. Twisted Timeflow accelerates your two bomb charges and other basic cooldowns while its buff remains, so use that window to cycle another rotation. Save Temporal Mirage for the gank or enemy-champion projectile you see coming. When Time in a Bottle has enough experience stored to level an ally, share it from safety; champion damage interrupts the channel for one second. Hold river vision early, because every jungle path that reaches you is one you cannot run from.
gamePlan.midGame: Chronoshift changes how your carry plays now. With it up, your ADC can step into fights and contest objectives knowing one death gets undone, so plan the aggressive timings together instead of waiting them out. Around dragon and herald, your bomb stun is the setup that lets your team collapse, and Twisted Timeflow gets your duo to the pit first or out of a bad one. Bomb the chokes the enemy has to walk through, and watch for the roam: your stun landing on an enemy mid or jungler in the river starts a pick before they know the fight began. Shove the wave before you wander, since you have nothing to defend the lane with once you leave.
gamePlan.lateGame: Before Baron or Elder, stay near the ally most likely to be engaged and avoid checking vision alone. Hold Chronoshift until the enemy commits enough damage to threaten a kill, but cast before control prevents you from responding. Use Twisted Timeflow and Mirage to move the carry away from the first threat, then place the double bomb where pursuers must cross. If the enemy refuses to dive, use the speed to help your frontline enter or leave instead of forcing a risky walk-up.
gamePlan.teamfights: Your job runs in two layers: stun the engage, then cover the carry. Read who steps in first and drop the double bomb on the clump so the stun catches more than one body. Put Chronoshift on your ADC before the fight, not after they are already dead, since it is far stronger cast early than as a panic reaction. Spend Twisted Timeflow to pull your carry out of a flank or to chase down the runner once your team commits, and lay Temporal Mirage between your backline and whatever is walking at it. Beyond the stun, the shield, and that field you have no hard peel and no real escape, so stay behind your frontline and treat every cooldown as your carry's lifeline rather than your own.

startingItem.name: Amplifying Tome
startingItem.note: Early ability power, since her lane is landing one star from maximum range.

boots.name: Spellslinger's Shoes
boots.note: Magic penetration keeps her one-rotation burst lethal, which is all a pick mage gets per fight.

coreItems.name: Luden's Echo
coreItems.note: First item. Fixes her mana and gives her the wave clear her kit does not have, so she can shove the lane and then go hunting for a pick.

coreItems.name: Lich Bane
coreItems.note: Every ability primes both Spellblade and More Sparkles. After Paddle Star wakes the target, Zoe can add one empowered non-projectile basic attack for both effects instead of wasting the sleep on the attack first.

coreItems.name: Rabadon's Deathcap
coreItems.note: Multiplies her ability power. Her damage arrives in one sleep window, so all of it goes up at once.

coreItems.name: Void Staff
coreItems.note: Cuts the magic resist that lets a slept target survive, since a resisted burst leaves her defenceless. Choose it over Cryptbloom when enemies are stacking magic resist and maximum personal damage matters more than ability haste and team healing.

coreItems.name: Banshee's Veil
coreItems.note: Build this when the enemy has a hook or point-and-click stun, which is how a mage with no escape dies.

situationalItems.name: Infinity Orb
situationalItems.note: Build this against squishy teams, where her rotation already leaves targets at a sliver and the bonus damage to low health enemies finishes them.

situationalItems.name: Oceanid's Trident
situationalItems.note: Build this when the enemy has shields that keep absorbing her one-rotation burst.

situationalItems.name: Morellonomicon
situationalItems.note: Build this against a drain champion who outheals her combo. Buy Oblivion Orb early, since the anti-heal works from the component.

situationalItems.name: Zhonya's Hourglass
situationalItems.note: Build this against assassins who dive her the moment her bubble is spent. Buy Seeker's Armguard early for the armor and ability power.

situationalItems.name: Horizon Focus
situationalItems.note: Her star lands from long range, so the reveal and amplification trigger on the poke between rotations.

situationalItems.name: Cryptbloom
situationalItems.note: The alternative to Void Staff. Less penetration, but the ability haste and healing on takedown help when she picks alongside her team. Choose it when enemies have not built much magic resist, so trading Void Staff's extra damage for more ability haste and an area heal after takedowns is worthwhile.

keystoneRune.name: Fleet Footwork
keystoneRune.desc: Moving and attacking builds Energy. At 100 stacks, your next attack heals you and grants movement speed.
keystoneRune.note: Heals her through a lane where she has to hold a forward position to land a star at all.

primaryRunes.name: Manaflow Band
primaryRunes.desc: Hitting an enemy champion with an ability permanently increases your maximum mana.
primaryRunes.note: She throws Paddle Star on cooldown and no item in the core build carries mana, so the permanent max mana is what keeps her poking.

primaryRunes.name: Absolute Focus
primaryRunes.desc: While above 70% health, gain bonus adaptive force.
primaryRunes.note: Her range means she should be at high health while poking, which is when this pays out.

primaryRunes.name: Nimbus Cloak
primaryRunes.desc: After casting a summoner spell, gain movement speed and slow resistance.
primaryRunes.note: Move speed after a summoner spell helps a mage whose only mobility is a brief portal jump.

secondaryRunes.name: Sudden Impact
secondaryRunes.desc: Deal bonus true damage after using mobility or exiting stealth.
secondaryRunes.note: Her ultimate is a blink, so the bonus true damage lands on the star that follows.

spells.name: Flash
spells.note: Must take. Essential for repositioning, escapes, and aggressive combos.

goodAgainst.note: Paddle Star and Sleepy Trouble Bubble reach Veigar without entering Event Horizon, but Portal Jump always returns Zoe to a visible point the cage can cover. Draw out Event Horizon before using the jump, attack his Baleful Strike stacking from long range, and save the bubble for the cooldown window rather than returning into a guaranteed stun.
Vladimir's early game is weak and you out-range everything he has, so you can bully him all lane before his sustain comes online. His pool dodges one bubble combo, nothing more.

His plan is a quiet lane to collect Stardust, and channeling Breath of Light gives you a predictable bubble angle. Respect Singularity's pull and his ability to fly away with Astral Flight instead of assuming he is trapped.
You out-range her ball harassment, and your burst on a landed sleep goes straight through the single shield she banks. An immobile control mage who has to come to you loses the poke war.

weakAgainst.note: She dashes through your minions straight onto you, and once she is on top of you the bubble is far too slow to save you. Her resets only make the lane worse as she stacks.
Early he just eats your poke, but once his ultimate is online his blink dodges the bubble and dives you on repeat, closing the gap faster than your tools come back.
Her shield soaks your poke, and her dash plus pull turns one landed engage into your whole health bar. The bubble travels too slowly to stop her once she commits.

Wind Wall blocks Paddle Star and Sleepy Trouble Bubble, denying Zoe's main setup and burst from that direction, but it does not erase More Sparkles attacks or Spell Thief casts. Attack from a different angle, wait out the wall, and keep Portal Jump's return point away from Yasuo's minion-dash route.
His shadow swaps dodge the bubble and force an all-in you cannot escape, and once he has items his combo kills you faster than yours kills him.

gamePlan.overview:
Zoe punishes a single positioning mistake with a kill. Paddle Star hits harder according to the distance it travels, Sleepy Trouble Bubble puts whoever it touches to sleep, and Spell Thief lets her pick up an enemy summoner spell or boot enchantment; or a spell shard dropped by certain minions; and cast it once. Land the bubble, redirect Paddle Star along a long path, and most squishy mids are dead before they wake up.

In lane she plays poke and punish from max range: chip with stars, threaten the bubble, and take the kill when someone walks a straight line or hugs a wall. She does not want to shove and brawl. When the lane stalls she roams, since a bubble thrown from fog onto a side lane sets up the same kill with far less warning.

Her problem is that everything she does is a slow skillshot, and she has no real escape when it misses. Portal Jump is a short hop on a leash, not a Flash, so once a mobile assassin or all-in skirmisher closes the gap she is a fragile mage with her tools on cooldown. Land the combo and the fight is over before it starts; miss the bubble and she is the squishiest target on the map.
gamePlan.earlyGame: Laning is a patience test. Use Paddle Star to last-hit from range and chip the enemy mid whenever they step up for a minion, but do not throw the bubble at random, since missing it leaves you defenseless for the whole cooldown. The kill pattern is bubble first, then a redirected, long-travel star into the sleeping target; against immobile mids you can set the bubble up through a wall or from brush. Watch your positioning constantly: Portal Jump always returns you to its original cast point after one second, so it can extend a star angle or dodge a brief moment but cannot carry you away from a gank. Ward the river and keep Flash for the escape Portal Jump cannot provide.
gamePlan.midGame: Once you have your first item, a clean bubble into star leaves squishy enemies dead instead of scared. This is your roaming window: shove the wave with a star or two, then look for a bubble onto a side lane or onto an enemy mid who stepped out to ward. A pick in fog is worth more than poke in lane, so drift toward objectives and let your sleep start the fight your team finishes. Mid priority matters here, because a shoved wave frees you to walk to dragon or herald, and the threat of your bubble at a contest is often enough to make the enemy back off without a fight.
gamePlan.lateGame: Your damage scales to the point where a single landed combo erases a carry, so the whole late game is about finding that one angle. You cannot duel anyone who reaches you, so you live on the edges of the map and at the back of every fight, fishing for a bubble through a choke or onto someone who strayed from their team. The flip side is fragility: you have less escape than almost any mid, so one caught Zoe usually means a lost fight. Position like the artillery you are, and treat every long-distance redirected star as a possible pick on a backliner who thought distance kept them safe.
gamePlan.teamfights: Start from the back or an unwarded side angle and look for Sleepy Trouble Bubble on a carry or another reachable threat. Build Paddle Star distance while the target sleeps, but do not Portal Jump from a return point the enemy can immediately engage. If the frontline blocks the angle, hold the bubble or use it to stop a diver instead of spending the cooldown on a tank your team cannot finish.
